trips.title: Carp Country — Cycling the Třeboň Ponds and the Vltava

bestPeriod.note: Late October is the carp harvest, when the ponds are drained and the dams are working roads; midsummer brings mosquitoes to the bog margins.

trips.gatewayAirport: Prague (PRG)
trips.summary: Flat dam-top gravel through a 700-year-old fishpond landscape, linked to the Vltava cycle path and the climb into Český Krumlov.
trips.hook: The Třeboň basin is a machine built in the sixteenth century and still running: 500 ponds, hand-dug canals, and dams wide enough to ride two abreast, all engineered by men whose names are still on them. It is the flattest interesting cycling in Central Europe. Then, on Day 6, the land finally tilts and drops you into Český Krumlov.

snapshot.Base(s): Třeboň (3 nights) → České Budějovice (2 nights) → Český Krumlov (2 nights)
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx 330 km, roughly 1,900 m cumulative gain; asphalt on the Vltava corridor, crushed limestone and packed sand on the pond dams, short grass and forest-track sections
snapshot.Getting There: Prague (PRG) → bus or metro to Praha hl. n., ČD express to České Budějovice (approx 2h20), local line to Třeboň
snapshot.Who It Suits: Riders who want long flat days, birdwatchers, families, and anyone who thinks a fish dinner is a legitimate reason to travel

itinerary.title: Into the basin, around Svět
itinerary.morning: Train from Prague to České Budějovice, then the regional line east to Třeboň. ČD charges a bike ticket of roughly CZK 45–65 (approx €2.00–2.60), plus a compulsory bike seat reservation of about CZK 35 on express services with a marked bike wagon.
itinerary.afternoon: A gentle first loop around Svět, the pond that Třeboň sits on. The circuit is 12 km of packed dam-top gravel and asphalt, past the Schwarzenberg family tomb at Domanín — a neo-Gothic mausoleum in a wood, open in season for approx CZK 120.
itinerary.evening: Třeboň's Masarykovo náměstí is an unbroken Renaissance square with arcades on both sides. Eat carp: Šupina a Šupinka near the Svinenská gate has been serving pond fish for decades and does a fried carp and a carp soup that justify the trip.
itinerary.dayStats: 28 km, +90 m, half packed gravel dam-tops, half asphalt.

itinerary.title: Rožmberk, the largest pond in the country
itinerary.morning: North to the Rožmberk dam, built 1584–1590 by Jakub Krčín of Jelčany for the Rožmberk lords. It holds 489 hectares of water behind an earth wall planted with 400-year-old oaks. The dam top is a wide grass-and-gravel road, closed to cars.
itinerary.afternoon: Follow the Zlatá stoka — the Golden Canal, 45 km of hand-cut channel finished in 1520 and still feeding the whole system — to Stará Hlína, then back past the Nová řeka diversion canal. Reed beds, herons, eagles.
itinerary.evening: The Třeboň spa houses, Bertiny lázně and Lázně Aurora, both sell peat baths and swim access to non-residents. After 70 km on gravel, take the peat bath.
itinerary.dayStats: 68 km, +140 m, roughly 40 km of crushed limestone and packed sand.

itinerary.title: Novohradské foothills and the Greenway
itinerary.morning: South on the Greenway Praha–Vídeň, the marked Prague–Vienna corridor, through Chlum u Třeboně and its glassworks village toward Nové Hrady. The land rises for the first time.
itinerary.afternoon: Nové Hrady has a Rožmberk castle, an Empire-period chateau and the Terčino údolí landscape park with its artificial waterfall. Return north on quiet asphalt through Borovany, whose Augustinian monastery has been restored as a cultural centre.
itinerary.evening: Last night in Třeboň. Walk the town walls and the Rožmberk brewery courtyard; the beer is Regent, brewed here since 1379.
itinerary.dayStats: 74 km, +410 m, mostly asphalt with 8 km of forest gravel.

itinerary.title: West to České Budějovice via Hluboká
itinerary.morning: Leave Třeboň westward on quiet field roads through Lomnice nad Lužnicí and Veselí nad Lužnicí, then pick up the Vltava corridor. Bags go ahead: Top Bicycle and AVE Bicycle Tours both run luggage transfer across South Bohemia for roughly €12–18 per bag per stage.
itinerary.afternoon: Hluboká nad Vltavou is a Windsor-style neo-Gothic pile rebuilt by the Schwarzenbergs in the 1840s; approx CZK 350, tours timed, so buy the slot on arrival. The Alšova jihočeská galerie in the old riding school is quieter.
itinerary.evening: Roll into České Budějovice on the riverside path. Náměstí Přemysla Otakara II is one of the largest medieval squares in Central Europe, 133 metres a side.
itinerary.dayStats: 62 km, +230 m, asphalt with 6 km crushed limestone along the Vltava.

itinerary.title: Holašovice and the Blanský les edge
itinerary.morning: West out of Budějovice through Dubné on lanes to Holašovice, a UNESCO-listed village of rural Baroque farmhouse gables around a green with two ponds. Twenty-two protected homesteads, still lived in.
itinerary.afternoon: Loop south under the Blanský les hills to Křemže and back along the Vltava. This is the first day with sustained rolling, and the return along the river is fast.
itinerary.evening: Budvar's brewery runs English tours at fixed times, approx CZK 250; the beer at source is noticeably softer. Otherwise the Masné krámy beer hall in the old butchers' arcade.
itinerary.dayStats: 58 km, +480 m, asphalt with 5 km gravel.

itinerary.title: Up the Vltava to Český Krumlov
itinerary.morning: The Vltava cycle path south from Budějovice is the prettiest riding of the week: a mostly asphalt riverside route through Boršov and Zlatá Koruna, where the Cistercian abbey of 1263 keeps one of the best-preserved Gothic cloisters in Bohemia (approx CZK 180).
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to Český Krumlov, arriving over the meander with the castle tower directly above. Push the last cobbled climb into the old town rather than riding it; the setts are polished and steep.
itinerary.evening: Krumlov after 18:00, when the day coaches have left, is a different place. The Baroque theatre in the castle is one of only a handful in the world with original stage machinery; tours are strictly limited and sell out.
itinerary.dayStats: 42 km, +360 m, asphalt with cobbles in the old town.

itinerary.title: Lipno approach and the train home
itinerary.morning: Ride the Vltava upstream toward Zlatá Koruna's opposite bank or push on to Rožmberk nad Vltavou, a compact valley castle 25 km south. Turn where the legs say.
itinerary.afternoon: Return to Český Krumlov and take ČD line 194 north to České Budějovice. The line runs a bike wagon through the summer and it fills on Sunday afternoons — reserve, or take an earlier train.
itinerary.evening: Connect at České Budějovice for Prague. Bikes need a ticket and, on express services, a reserved bike slot.
itinerary.dayStats: 40 km, +320 m, asphalt with 4 km gravel.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Bílý koníček
accommodationStrategy.description: The oldest house on the square, Renaissance-gabled, with an interior courtyard where bikes are locked overnight. Three nights here is the structural decision of the trip: the pond basin is a wheel with Třeboň at the hub, so you ride unloaded every day and the spa is a five-minute walk.
accommodationStrategy.booking: two months ahead; the October carp harvest weekends sell out in spring.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: CZK 1,900–2,600 (approx €78–105) per night for two with breakfast

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Budweis
accommodationStrategy.description: A restored malt house on the Malše with a secure garage, a bike-wash point in the yard and a lift to the rooms. It is 300 metres from the main square and directly on the Vltava cycle route, so Day 5 and Day 6 both start without touching city traffic.
accommodationStrategy.booking: six weeks ahead.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Dvořák
accommodationStrategy.description: Inside the loop of the Vltava under the castle, with locked storage and a terrace over the water. Sleeping inside the old town rather than in the modern outskirts is what makes the empty early-morning Krumlov possible, and it saves the cobbled climb twice a day.
accommodationStrategy.booking: three months ahead for June–September.

logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European; in Czechia 155 for ambulance and 158 for police both work directly and are often faster.
logistics.money: Czechia uses the koruna, not the euro. Roughly CZK 24–25 to the euro in 2026. Pay in crowns — euro-accepting tourist businesses use punitive rates. Cards are near-universal; village pubs and pond-side stalls are cash.

other.label: Bikes on ČD
other.text: A bike ticket costs roughly CZK 45–65 per journey. On express (R) and fast services with a marked bike wagon the seat reservation, about CZK 35, is compulsory and capped — on the Český Krumlov line 194 and the Prague–Budějovice line 220 the summer slots go early. Regional Os trains take bikes without reservation, space permitting.

other.label: Rental
other.text: České Budějovice has both Rekola and Nextbike station-based bikes for city hops. For touring bikes and e-bikes, the Třeboň spa complexes Bertiny lázně and Lázně Aurora run guest fleets, and Top Bicycle and AVE Bicycle Tours deliver hire bikes and e-bikes anywhere in South Bohemia with a one-way drop.

other.label: Luggage transfer
other.text: Top Bicycle and AVE Bicycle Tours both move bags between South Bohemian towns for roughly €12–18 per bag per stage; book at least two weeks out.

other.label: Navigation
other.text: Czech cycle routes are signed with yellow route numbers on white; the Greenway Praha–Vídeň and EuroVelo 7 carry their own logos. KČT paper maps at 1:60,000 cost around CZK 130 at any information centre.

other.label: Pond dam access
other.text: Dams are working infrastructure owned by Rybářství Třeboň. Cycling on marked routes is fine; riding onto an unmarked dam during a harvest, when heavy machinery is on it, is not.

other.label: Protected area
other.text: Třeboňsko is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a Ramsar site. Stay on tracks, keep out of reed beds, and do not fly a drone — Czech law requires registration and the reserve zones are restricted.

other.label: Opening traps
other.text: Czech castles close entirely November to March and on Mondays year-round. Visits are guided, timed and capped; buy the slot on arrival, not when you are ready.

proTips: Come in the last week of October for the výlov, the carp harvest. Rožmberk and Svět are drained on announced dates, the dams turn into a working festival and the fish goes straight from net to grill.
Book the Český Krumlov Baroque theatre tour the day you arrive in Třeboň, not the day you arrive in Krumlov. Visitor numbers are capped at a few dozen per tour to protect the machinery.
Order kapr na černo or a carp soup in Třeboň rather than at the Prague end of the trip. The fish comes from the pond you rode around that morning.
Use the Zlatá stoka towpath rather than the parallel road between Stará Hlína and Třeboň. It is traffic-free, packed sand, and the reason the canal exists is visible the whole way.
Buy your KČT map at the Třeboň information centre on the square on arrival. Czech route numbering does not always match what a phone app thinks the network looks like.

raw.Total Distance / Terrain: approx 330 km, roughly 1,900 m cumulative gain; asphalt on the Vltava corridor, crushed limestone and packed sand on the pond dams, short grass and forest-track sections
raw.Who It Suits: Riders who want long flat days, birdwatchers, families, and anyone who thinks a fish dinner is a legitimate reason to travel

typeSpecific.surface: approx 330 km, roughly 1,900 m cumulative gain; asphalt on the Vltava corridor, crushed limestone and packed sand on the pond dams, short grass and forest-track sections
typeSpecific.audience: Riders who want long flat days, birdwatchers, families, and anyone who thinks a fish dinner is a legitimate reason to travel

packingNotes: Tyres of 35–42 mm with some tread. The dams are packed sand and crushed limestone and turn soft after rain.
Mosquito repellent with DEET for the June and July reed margins; the Třeboň bogs are serious about this.
Binoculars, compact. This is one of Central Europe's best inland birding landscapes and the dams put you at eye level with the water.
Sunblock; there is no shade on a pond dam for kilometres at a time.
CZK cash in small notes for pubs, ferry-style pond crossings and information centres.
A spare tube and a patch kit — bike shops exist in Třeboň, Budějovice and Krumlov and essentially nowhere else on the route.
whatCouldGoWrong: **The bike wagon on the Krumlov line is full.** Summer Sunday services genuinely refuse bikes. Fallback: take an Os regional service, or ride the 25 km back to Budějovice on the Vltava path, which is flat and asphalt.

**Heavy rain turns the dam tops to mud.** Packed sand becomes unrideable after 24 hours of rain. Fallback: the Day 3 asphalt route via Chlum u Třeboně and Borovany substitutes for the Rožmberk day without losing distance.

**The carp harvest closes a dam.** During the výlov the working dams are shut to through traffic. Fallback: ride the outer ring of the pond system on asphalt and come back on foot to watch — which is the better experience anyway.

trips.title: The Bodensee-Radweg Full Loop

bestPeriod.note: July and August are ridable but the path through Meersburg and Lindau becomes a slow-moving queue by 11:00.

trips.gatewayAirport: Zürich (ZRH)
trips.summary: The full 260 km circuit of Lake Constance across Germany, Austria and Switzerland, stitched together with car ferries, lake steamers and regional trains.
trips.hook: The Bodensee-Radweg is the most heavily used long-distance cycle route in Germany, and it earns that traffic. Seven days lets you ride the whole 260 km circuit at a pace that leaves time for the Untersee, the Rhine delta and two of the lake's islands. It is flat, waymarked to an almost absurd standard, and crosses three countries in a single week without a single serious climb.

snapshot.Country: Germany, with Austria and Switzerland on the loop
snapshot.Base(s): Konstanz (3 nights), Friedrichshafen (1), Bregenz (1), Arbon (1), Konstanz (1)
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: Approx. 270 km, +1,300 m cumulative. Asphalt and compacted gravel, almost entirely traffic-free or on marked lanes
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Zürich, then SBB via Winterthur and Kreuzlingen to Konstanz, around 1 h 40
snapshot.Who It Suits: First-time tourers, families with teenagers, and anyone who wants distance without gradient

itinerary.title: Reichenau and the Untersee
itinerary.morning: Collect bikes in Konstanz. Kultur-Rädle, opposite the station on Bahnhofplatz, has rented trekking bikes and e-bikes here for decades and will fit panniers. Radweg-Reisen, headquartered in Konstanz, is the local operator to use if you want the whole week booked with luggage moved hotel to hotel.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride west along the Untersee shore to Reichenau, the island of three Carolingian and Ottonian churches and a UNESCO listing since 2000. The causeway is flat and the market gardens either side supply most of the lake's vegetables. Continue to Allensbach and back.
itinerary.evening: Konstanz old town. The Niederburg lanes behind the Münster are quieter than the harbour, and the walk out to the Imperia statue is worth twenty minutes.
itinerary.dayStats: 45 km · +150 m · asphalt, short gravel on the Reichenau causeway approach.

itinerary.title: Ferry to Meersburg, on to Friedrichshafen
itinerary.morning: The Konstanz–Meersburg car ferry runs around the clock at roughly 15 minute intervals in daytime and takes about 15 minutes. A cyclist with a bike pays approximately €5. It leaves from Staad, 4 km north-east of the centre.
itinerary.afternoon: Meersburg climbs steeply from the harbour, so walk the Steigstrasse rather than fighting it. Then the shore route through Hagnau, Immenstaad and Fischbach to Friedrichshafen, past orchards that supply the lake's Most and Apfelsaft.
itinerary.evening: Friedrichshafen. The Zeppelin Museum in the old Hafenbahnhof holds a full-scale reconstruction of a section of the Hindenburg. It closes at 17:00, so ride briskly.
itinerary.dayStats: 40 km · +200 m · asphalt lakeside path.

itinerary.title: Lindau and the Austrian corner
itinerary.morning: East to Langenargen, Kressbronn and Nonnenhorn, the last German villages. This stretch is the quietest asphalt on the north shore.
itinerary.afternoon: Lindau sits on an island connected by a causeway, with the lion and lighthouse at the harbour mouth. Cross into Austria at Bregenz, only 10 km on. The Pfänderbahn cable car carries bikes for a supplement and drops you at 1,064 m for a view down the whole lake.
itinerary.evening: Bregenz. If the Bregenzer Festspiele is running in July or August, the floating stage on the lake is visible from the shore path for free.
itinerary.dayStats: 40 km · +150 m without the Pfänder, asphalt.

itinerary.title: The Rhine delta into Switzerland
itinerary.morning: South out of Bregenz along the Rheindelta, where the Alpenrhein enters the lake. It is a Ramsar wetland and one of central Europe's better bird sites in spring and autumn. Surface here is compacted gravel on dike tops.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross the Swiss border at Sankt Margrethen, then Rorschach and Horn to Arbon. Swiss francs take over; card payment is universal but ATMs dispense CHF only.
itinerary.evening: Arbon. The lakefront lido and the Saurer museum in the old truck works are both small and both quick.
itinerary.dayStats: 42 km · +180 m · asphalt with 8 km of compacted dike gravel.

itinerary.title: Romanshorn, Kreuzlingen, back to Konstanz
itinerary.morning: Arbon to Romanshorn is 8 km. From here the SBB ferry crosses to Friedrichshafen in about 40 minutes if you want to shortcut; otherwise continue west along the Swiss shore.
itinerary.afternoon: Uttwil, Kesswil, Münsterlingen and Kreuzlingen, which runs seamlessly into Konstanz across the border. The frontier is a line on the pavement with a customs post nobody stops at.
itinerary.evening: Back in Konstanz for two nights. Eat in Kreuzlingen if the Swiss franc is kind, in Konstanz if it is not.
itinerary.dayStats: 40 km · +160 m · asphalt.

itinerary.title: Stein am Rhein and the Seerhein
itinerary.morning: West from Konstanz along the Seerhein through Gottlieben, then the Untersee's Swiss shore to Steckborn and Berlingen. Reeds, fishing huts, very little traffic.
itinerary.afternoon: Stein am Rhein has the most completely painted Renaissance façades on the Rathausplatz of any town on the lake. Return by SBB from Stein am Rhein to Kreuzlingen with a Velo-Tageskarte, roughly CHF 14, self-loading into the marked carriage.
itinerary.evening: Konstanz. The Sea Life aquarium and the Bodensee-Naturmuseum share a building if the weather has broken.
itinerary.dayStats: 45 km ridden · +200 m · asphalt, short gravel through the Wollmatinger Ried.

itinerary.title: Mainau and the Bodanrück
itinerary.morning: North from Konstanz along the Überlinger See to Mainau, the island garden run by the Bernadotte family. Bikes park at the bridge; the island is walked, not ridden.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb over the Bodanrück ridge through Dettingen and Wallhausen, the only real gradient of the week at around 180 m, then drop back to Konstanz. Return bikes, or continue by train.
itinerary.evening: SBB to Zürich airport takes just under two hours with a change at Winterthur.
itinerary.dayStats: 45 km · +260 m · asphalt with a short forest gravel descent.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Barbarossa
accommodationStrategy.description: A 15th-century house on Obermarkt in the pedestrian core, five minutes from the station and the ferry buses. It has a locked internal bike room, which is the deciding factor in a town where bike theft at the harbour is a genuine problem. Ask for a courtyard room; the square is loud until midnight.
accommodationStrategy.booking: two months ahead, four for June.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Buchhorner Hof
accommodationStrategy.description: A long-established family house two streets back from the harbour, ADFC Bett+Bike certified, with a lockable garage and a hose for washing the bikes down after the delta gravel. Walking distance to the Zeppelin Museum and the ferry pier.
accommodationStrategy.booking: six weeks ahead.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Weisses Kreuz
accommodationStrategy.description: Central Bregenz, close to the Pfänderbahn valley station and the lakefront path, with secure bike storage. It is the practical overnight for the Austrian night because it removes any transfer at the start of the delta ride.
accommodationStrategy.booking: three months ahead if the Festspiele is on.

logistics.emergency: Emergency number is 112 in all three countries. Swiss mountain and lake rescue is reached on 1414 (Rega). Water rescue on the lake is coordinated by the DLRG and the Wasserschutzpolizei.

other.text: Emergency number is 112 in all three countries. Swiss mountain and lake rescue is reached on 1414 (Rega). Water rescue on the lake is coordinated by the DLRG and the Wasserschutzpolizei.

Bike carriage: on German regional trains you need a Fahrradkarte, roughly €6–€7 for a day in Baden-Württemberg. On IC and EC services a bike reservation is compulsory and costs around €9. Swiss trains need a Velo-Tageskarte at roughly CHF 14, with a compulsory reservation on some IC services. Austrian ÖBB regional bike tickets are a few euros. Buy before boarding; conductors fine.
The Katamaran between Konstanz and Friedrichshafen crosses in 50 minutes but carries only a handful of bikes and they must be booked. The Konstanz–Meersburg car ferry has no such limit.
Look for the ADFC Bett+Bike sign. Certified places guarantee a locked bike store, a drying room and a one-night booking.
Three countries, two currencies. Switzerland uses CHF and Austria and Germany use EUR, but Swiss lakeside businesses generally take euro cash at a poor rate. Cards are better.
German shops close at 20:00 and all day Sunday. Swiss shops close at 18:30 on weekdays. Plan food on Saturday afternoon.
Swimming is permitted almost everywhere on the lake, but the Rheindelta reserve has marked no-entry zones during nesting season from March to July.

proTips: Ride the loop clockwise. The prevailing wind is westerly, so a clockwise circuit puts it behind you on the long north-shore day and keeps the lake on your right for photographs.
The Bodensee Card PLUS covers around 160 attractions and both Mainau and the Pfänderbahn. If you use three of them in the week it pays for itself; if you use two it does not.
Take the 07:00 Konstanz–Meersburg ferry rather than a mid-morning one. The path through Meersburg is empty before 09:00 and unusable by noon.

The Bodensee-Radweg splits into a shore variant and an inland variant on several sections. The inland variant is quieter and often shorter; the shore variant has the views. Ride inland when it is busy.

Sailing on the lake works to a Bft scale posted at every harbour. The orange flashing beacons mean a strong-wind warning and boat services stop; that is also your cue that the exposed dike sections will be brutal.
On Mainau, arrive after 16:00. The coach parties leave, the entry queue disappears, and the light on the Italian rose garden is better.
Buy Swiss provisions in Kreuzlingen only if you must. Crossing back into Konstanz for a supermarket saves roughly a third.

raw.Total Distance / Terrain: Approx. 270 km, +1,300 m cumulative. Asphalt and compacted gravel, almost entirely traffic-free or on marked lanes
raw.Who It Suits: First-time tourers, families with teenagers, and anyone who wants distance without gradient

typeSpecific.surface: Approx. 270 km, +1,300 m cumulative. Asphalt and compacted gravel, almost entirely traffic-free or on marked lanes
typeSpecific.audience: First-time tourers, families with teenagers, and anyone who wants distance without gradient

packingNotes: 35–40 mm tyres. The dike gravel through the Rheindelta and the Wollmatinger Ried is loose in places.
A dry bag. Lake squalls arrive in under twenty minutes and the exposed shore has no cover.
Swimming kit and a quick-dry towel, carried on top. There are public lidos at Konstanz, Arbon, Lindau and Bregenz.
A cable lock plus a second small lock for wheels; bike theft at ferry piers is common.
Coins in both EUR and CHF for lido lockers and toilets.
Sunglasses and lip balm; glare off the water is constant even in October.
Lights, mandatory in Germany and Switzerland and needed in the Lindau causeway underpasses.
Passport or national ID. Border checks are rare but the Swiss and Austrian frontiers do run spot checks.
whatCouldGoWrong: **High water.** Snowmelt in June can flood shore sections near Radolfzell and the Rheindelta. Signed inland diversions exist; follow them rather than pushing through.

**A ferry cancellation.** Strong wind stops the passenger boats and the Katamaran, though the Konstanz–Meersburg car ferry usually keeps running. Fall back on the train around the lake via Radolfzell and Singen.
**Trains full of bikes.** Summer weekends fill the regional bike carriages by 09:00. Ride the first service of the day or accept the next one.
**Crowding.** In July the path between Meersburg and Friedrichshafen is genuinely dangerous at midday. Ride the inland variant or start at dawn.
**Currency surprises.** Swiss restaurants are 30–50 per cent dearer than German ones. Budget the Arbon night accordingly or eat a picnic on the lakefront.

trips.title: Bornholm Round: Granite Coast & Smokehouse Loop

bestPeriod.window: Mid-May to mid-September; peak light and open smokehouses late June–August; quietest late May and first half of September
bestPeriod.raw: Mid-May to mid-September; peak light and open smokehouses late June–August; quietest late May and first half of September

accommodation.note: €90–150 per night, double (guesthouse to design hotel); hostels €35–55 pp

food.note: €45–70 per day (smokehouse buffets €20–28, dinner €35–60)

transport.note: €120–190 total: Copenhagen–Ystad–Rønne ferry combo, plus €90–130 bike hire for the week

activities.note: €60–110 total: Hammershus, Christiansø ferry, brewery and workshop visits

profile.difficultyNote: Easy–moderate. 105–135 km signposted loop split over 5 riding days; 300–450 m gain per day; no sustained climbs

trips.summary: A seven-day cycling trip itinerary in Bornholm, Baltic Sea, Denmark.

itinerary.title: Arrival, Rønne and the west coast warm-up
itinerary.morning: Train from Copenhagen Central to Ystad in Sweden (about 1 h 40 with the through ticket), then the Bornholmslinjen fast ferry Ystad–Rønne, roughly 1 h 20. Collect bikes at a Rønne rental within walking distance of the terminal; ask for 32–38 mm tyres, they make the gravel sections painless.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride the coastal path north to Hasle, an easy flat 12 km on asphalt with the Baltic on your left. Stop at Hasle Røgeri for your first *sol over Gudhjem* — smoked herring, raw egg yolk, radish, chives, rye.
itinerary.evening: Continue to Jons Kapel, a sea-cliff chapel formation reached by wooden stairs, then back to Rønne. Dinner at a harbourside table; early night, the ferry day is longer than it reads.
itinerary.dayStats: 24 km, asphalt

itinerary.title: Rønne to Allinge via Hammershus
itinerary.morning: North on the coast route through Sorthat-Muleby and Hasle, then onto the Ringebakkerne cliff section — this is the most dramatic asphalt on the island, quarried granite falling straight into the sea.
itinerary.afternoon: Hammershus, the largest medieval fortress ruin in Northern Europe, with the low-slung visitor centre built into the hillside opposite. Allow two hours. Push on over Hammerknuden past Hammer Fyr lighthouse and the flooded Opalsøen quarry.
itinerary.evening: Roll down into Sandvig and Allinge. Dinner at Nordlandet's restaurant if you want the design-hotel version of the island, or the harbour grill in Allinge for the honest one.
itinerary.dayStats: 36 km, 420 m gain

itinerary.title: Allinge to Gudhjem, round churches and Christiansø
itinerary.morning: Inland loop to Olsker and Østerlars round churches — Østerlars is the largest and oldest of the four, a whitewashed defensive drum from around 1160.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend to Gudhjem, the steepest little town on Bornholm, and take the Christiansøfarten boat to Christiansø in the Ertholmene group, about an hour each way. No bikes, no cars, 90 residents, a 17th-century naval fortress and the country's easternmost point.
itinerary.evening: Back in Gudhjem, dinner at the harbour, then walk up Bokul rock for sunset over the roofs.
itinerary.dayStats: 28 km

itinerary.title: Gudhjem to Svaneke, the craft corridor
itinerary.morning: Coastal ride via Melsted and Listed. Stop at Bornholms Kunstmuseum on the Helligdomsklipperne cliffs — the building is worth the ticket on its own.
itinerary.afternoon: Svaneke, Denmark's best-preserved small town and the island's maker capital: Svaneke Bryghus for beer, Svaneke Chokoladeri, Pernille Bülow's glassblowing workshop, Bornholms Mosteri for apple must.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Svaneke; if you have booked far ahead, this is the night to drive or taxi to Kadeau Bornholm at Sømarken for the island tasting menu.
itinerary.dayStats: 26 km

itinerary.title: Svaneke to Dueodde and Aakirkeby
itinerary.morning: South through Nexø, then the long white sand of Dueodde — the finest-grained beach in Denmark, used historically for hourglasses. Lighthouse climb for the flat forest view.
itinerary.afternoon: Turn inland on the old railway grade (compacted gravel) toward Aakirkeby, passing Hallegård farm shop for smoked sausage.
itinerary.evening: Stay near Aakirkeby or Sømarken. Quiet interior night; stars are excellent here.
itinerary.dayStats: 34 km, mixed surface

itinerary.title: Almindingen forest and Ekkodalen
itinerary.morning: Into Almindingen, Denmark's third-largest forest. Ride the gravel through Ekkodalen — the echo valley, a rift with 20 m rock walls — and climb Rytterknægten (162 m), the island's high point, with the Kongemindet tower on top.
itinerary.afternoon: Paradisbakkerne on the eastern edge: granite hills, glacial erratics, marked walking trails if you want to leave the bike. Loop back west to Nylars round church, the best preserved of the four.
itinerary.evening: Return to Rønne. Dinner and a last harbour beer.
itinerary.dayStats: 30 km, 450 m gain

itinerary.title: Coastal spin and departure
itinerary.morning: Short flat spin south to Arnager and its long wooden pier, then back. Return bikes.
itinerary.afternoon: Ferry Rønne–Ystad, train to Copenhagen. If you have a late flight, the alternative is the Rønne–Køge overnight route (about 5.5 h) which takes bikes without fuss.

accommodationStrategy.name: Nordlandet
accommodationStrategy.description: Former sanatorium above the north coast, Nordic-modern rooms, sea-facing terrace restaurant. Locked bike storage in the grounds and a laundry, which matters mid-week. Best positioned for the Hammershus and Hammerknuden days.

accommodationStrategy.name: Danchells Anneks
accommodationStrategy.description: Small, family-run, on the slope above the harbour. Two minutes from the Christiansø jetty, so you can ride the morning loop, dump the bike, and walk to the boat. Ask for a ground-floor room — Gudhjem is all stairs.

accommodationStrategy.name: Green Solution House (Hotel GSH)
accommodationStrategy.description: Cradle-to-cradle designed hotel, five minutes from the ferry terminal, with secure indoor cycle parking and tools. Ideal for the first and last nights so an early ferry never becomes a taxi problem.

logistics.connectivity: 4G/5G is reliable island-wide; there are thin patches in Almindingen and along the north cliffs. Download the offline map layer before Day 6.
logistics.emergency: 112. Bornholm Hospital is in Rønne. Pharmacy hours are short outside Rønne — carry chain lube, spare tubes and any prescriptions with you.
logistics.weather: Bornholm is a Baltic island: wind decides your day more than rain. A 12 m/s westerly makes the west coast leg genuinely hard and the east coast easy — ride the loop clockwise on westerly days, anticlockwise on easterlies. Sea fog can close in on the north coast in late May and early June.
logistics.bookingWindows: Kadeau Bornholm: opens reservations by season, book 2–3 months ahead. Nordlandet and Stammershalle Badehotel: 3–4 months for July. Christiansø boat: same-week is fine except in the last two weeks of July. Bike rental: 3 weeks ahead for the summer peak, and specify pannier racks.
logistics.money: Denmark uses DKK, not the euro. Cards work everywhere including farm honesty stalls; carry a €20 equivalent in coins only for a few harbour toilets and air pumps.
logistics.transportRules: Cycling is legal on all signposted *cykelveje*; the numbered island routes are marked with blue signs. Two-abreast riding is allowed only where it does not obstruct. Right-of-way at Danish roundabouts favours traffic already in the circle. Lights are mandatory from dusk and police do enforce it.
logistics.gettingThere: The fast route is Copenhagen → Ystad (Swedish rail, passport/ID needed for the Danish–Swedish border check) → Bornholmslinjen ferry. Buy the combined DSB "Bornholm" through-ticket; bike spaces on the ferry are limited and must be reserved separately in July and August.

proTips: Ride the loop **anticlockwise** and you get the granite north coast on Days 2–3 while your legs are fresh and the smokehouse crowd is still in Rønne.
Smokehouses run buffet lunches; arrive at **11:30, not 13:00**, and you skip the queue and get the herring still warm.
Ferry bikes: book the **07:30 Ystad departure** on arrival day. It puts you on the island before noon with a full riding afternoon, and the return spaces on the last boat are what actually sell out.
Christiansø runs a handful of guest beds in the old fortress buildings. Booking one night there is the single most memorable upgrade on this itinerary, and almost nobody does it.
The island's **Bornholms Valsemølle** and Lehnsgaard rapeseed oil ship internationally, so shop on Day 6, not Day 1 — panniers are finite.
Late-season trick: the second week of September has open smokehouses, warm sea, and half the accommodation price of the first week of August.

trips.title: Saaremaa & Muhu: Juniper Island Loop

bestPeriod.window: Late May to mid-September; June for wildflower meadows and midnight-ish light, September for empty roads and warm sea
bestPeriod.raw: Late May to mid-September; June for wildflower meadows and midnight-ish light, September for empty roads and warm sea

accommodation.note: €55–110 per night, double (guesthouse to spa hotel); manor splurge €220+

food.note: €30–50 per day — Estonia's islands are the best value in this dataset

transport.note: €90–150: Tallinn–Virtsu bus or car, foot-passenger ferry with bike €4–7 per crossing, bike hire €70–110 per week

activities.note: €40–80: Kuressaare Castle, Kaali crater, Angla windmills, spa entry

profile.difficultyNote: Easy. Flattest island cycling in the Baltics; 40–65 km per day, under 150 m gain per day

trips.summary: A seven-day cycling trip itinerary in West Estonian Archipelago, Estonia.

itinerary.title: Virtsu, ferry to Muhu, Koguva village
itinerary.morning: Bus or transfer from Tallinn to Virtsu (about 2 h). Take the TS Laevad ferry Virtsu–Kuivastu, 27 minutes; bikes board with foot passengers.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride west across Muhu to Koguva, an entirely preserved fieldstone-walled fishing village that is now an open-air museum with people still living in it. Stone walls, thatched roofs, juniper everywhere.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Pädaste Manor's Alexander restaurant if you are doing the one splurge night, or the simpler Sea House terrace on the same estate. Sunset over the Muhu strait.
itinerary.dayStats: 28 km

itinerary.title: Muhu to Kuressaare via the Väinatamm causeway
itinerary.morning: East to Liiva and the church with its 13th-century paintings, then across the Väinatamm — a 3.5 km stone causeway built in the 1890s linking Muhu to Saaremaa, dead flat and fully exposed to crosswind.
itinerary.afternoon: Through Orissaare and south on the main road, then peel off onto the coastal gravel via Kõiguste bay. Stop at the Kaali meteorite crater — a 110 m water-filled impact crater about 3,500 years old, small and strange, with eight satellite craters in the woods around it.
itinerary.evening: Arrive Kuressaare. Beer in the town square, dinner at Ku-Kuu in the old town.
itinerary.dayStats: 52 km

itinerary.title: Kuressaare, castle day and a short spin
itinerary.morning: Kuressaare Episcopal Castle — the best-preserved medieval fortress in the Baltics, a square limestone keep with a full moat and bastions. Give it three hours; the Saaremaa Museum inside is thorough.
itinerary.afternoon: Easy flat ride west to Nasva harbour and the Sõrve road's first stretch. Swim at Mändjala's shallow pine-backed beach.
itinerary.evening: Saaremaa's spa culture is real and cheap. Book an evening slot at one of the Kuressaare spa hotels — sauna, seawater pools, and a mud treatment for the price of a city cocktail.
itinerary.dayStats: 25 km

itinerary.title: Sõrve peninsula out-and-back
itinerary.morning: South down the Sõrve peninsula, a 32 km finger of land pointing at Latvia. Ride the west-coast road via Järve and Lõu; almost no traffic.
itinerary.afternoon: Sõrve lighthouse at the tip, 52 m, climbable, with the Gulf of Riga on one side and the open Baltic on the other. The peninsula was the site of brutal 1944 fighting — bunkers and the Sõrve Military Museum are along the return.
itinerary.evening: Return north to Kuressaare on the east-coast road for variety. Long day; eat early and well.
itinerary.dayStats: 66 km, the long day

itinerary.title: Northwest coast: Panga cliff and Mustjala
itinerary.morning: North through Kihelkonna's flatlands, onto compacted limestone gravel through juniper heath — this is the classic Saaremaa surface and it rides beautifully on 35 mm tyres.
itinerary.afternoon: Panga cliff (Panga pank), a 21 m limestone escarpment straight down into the sea, the highest on the island and an old sacrificial site. Continue to Mustjala.
itinerary.evening: Stay in a Mustjala-area farm guesthouse. Smoked fish, home-brewed island beer, and dark skies.
itinerary.dayStats: 58 km, mixed gravel

itinerary.title: Vilsandi National Park and Angla
itinerary.morning: West to Loona and the Vilsandi National Park visitor centre. At low water and with a guide, the Vilsandi crossing to the island is a wading and shallow-boat affair; otherwise ride the Harilaid peninsula to Kiipsaare lighthouse, which leans in the sea like a small Baltic Pisa.
itinerary.afternoon: East to Angla windmill hill — five wooden windmills on a ridge, the classic Saaremaa image — and the Karja church nearby with its unusual carved stone reliefs.
itinerary.evening: Back to Kuressaare or Orissaare depending on your ferry time tomorrow.
itinerary.dayStats: 55 km

itinerary.title: Muhu, ferry, and out
itinerary.morning: Cross the causeway back to Muhu, ride the northern lane past Muhu ostrich farm and the Muhu bread bakery, and reach Kuivastu with an hour spare.
itinerary.afternoon: Ferry to Virtsu, bus to Tallinn (about 2 h), leaving a Tallinn evening if you want it.
itinerary.dayStats: 30 km

accommodationStrategy.name: Pädaste Manor
accommodationStrategy.description: Restored 16th-century estate on the south Muhu shore, spa in the old stables, Alexander restaurant working almost exclusively from island produce. Perfect first or last night: it is 20 minutes from the ferry, so it absorbs travel-day fatigue, and it has covered bike storage.

accommodationStrategy.name: Grand Rose SPA Hotel / Georg Ots Spa Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: Two mid-price spa hotels a few minutes from the castle. The point is the recovery: thermal pools, saunas and a masseur on the premises after the Sõrve day. Both accept bikes in luggage rooms — ask when booking rather than on arrival.

accommodationStrategy.name: Farm guesthouses around Mustjala and Kihelkonna
accommodationStrategy.description: Family-run, €50–70 a double, breakfast included and dinner if you ask by lunchtime. This is where the trip stops being a route and starts being Saaremaa. Book direct by phone or email; many are not on international platforms.

logistics.connectivity: Estonia has excellent, cheap mobile data island-wide including the Sõrve tip. E-services (ferry tickets, bus tickets, parking) are all app-based and work in English.
logistics.emergency: 112. Kuressaare Hospital is the only full facility; the Sõrve peninsula and northwest gravel are 45–60 minutes from it.
logistics.weather: Continental-maritime: warm calm Junes, but gales are possible any month and the causeway is fully exposed. Sea temperature peaks at 18–20 °C in early August.
logistics.bookingWindows: Pädaste Manor: 3+ months for summer weekends. Kuressaare spa hotels: 4–6 weeks. Bike rental: reserve 2–3 weeks out and confirm the rack and pannier situation in writing.

other.label: Ferries
other.text: TS Laevad runs Virtsu–Kuivastu roughly hourly in season. Foot passengers with bikes almost never need a reservation; cars very much do in July. Timetables shift seasonally. `verify: true`

other.label: Ticks
other.text: Saaremaa is a genuine tick-borne encephalitis area. TBE vaccination is recommended for anyone riding gravel and stopping in meadows and long grass. Check daily; use permethrin-treated socks.

other.label: Roads
other.text: Estonian drivers are courteous but rural speed limits are 90 km/h. Daytime running lights are mandatory for cars, and reflective elements are legally required for pedestrians and strongly advised for cyclists after dusk.

proTips: Come in **early June**: the alvar meadows — thin-soil limestone grassland with wild orchids — are at their peak, and Saaremaa has some of Europe's richest orchid populations.
Saaremaa's home-brewed farmhouse beer (*koduõlu*) is a living tradition, not a revival. Ask a guesthouse host; it is rarely sold commercially and almost never exported.
Book the **spa evening**, not the spa morning. Estonian spa hotels are half-empty after 20:00 and the day-guest crowd is gone.
The Kaali crater car park is jammed 11:00–14:00 with coach tours off the Muhu ferry. Ride there at **16:30** instead.
Carry cash of €20–40. Village shops and farm stalls in the west take cards, but a few honesty boxes and the smallest smokehouses do not.
If the wind turns hard westerly, flip Days 4 and 5 — Sõrve into a 12 m/s headwind for 32 km is the one way to make this easy island hard.

trips.title: Girona & the Costa Brava

bestPeriod.window: March–early June & mid-September–early November
bestPeriod.avoid: August — Costa Brava roads clog with beach traffic and inland temperatures hit 35°C; late December–January brings ice on Rocacorba's upper slopes
bestPeriod.raw: March–early June & mid-September–early November

accommodation.note: Girona city hotels €90–€160 pppn; a Costa Brava night costs more

food.note: Menú del día €14–€18; Girona dinner €30–€45 with wine

transport.note: Airport transfer, Rodalies R11 legs, one van shuttle to Sant Feliu

activities.note: Carbon road hire €280–€420/week, Dalí museum €17, café habit

profile.difficultyNote: 4/5 — Rocacorba alone is a 992 m summit at 7% average, and the week routinely runs 100 km days

trips.gatewayAirport: GRO Girona–Costa Brava, 15 min to the city centre; BCN Barcelona El Prat, 1 h 20 min by AVE plus a short ride
trips.summary: Girona is not a scenic backdrop that happens to have cyclists in it; it is a town whose economy has partly reorganised around them. Within 20 km of the Pont de Pedra you can be on the Els Àngels climb, on the hardpack of the Ruta del Carrilet, or in the Gavarres forest on gravel that has never seen a car. This week strings together the four climbs that define the local calendar — Els Àngels, Rocacorba, Sant Hilari and Sant Grau — connects them with the two greenways that make recovery days genuinely restful, and puts one day on the Costa Brava's coast road between Sant Feliu de Guíxols and Tossa. Expect fast group rides, excellent coffee, and roads whose surface quality is consistently better than anything else in this collection.

itinerary.title: Arrival, bike fit, and Els Àngels
itinerary.morning: Collect the bike from Eat Sleep Cycle on Plaça de Catalunya — allow a full hour for fit, pedals and a shakedown spin. Coffee at Espresso Mafia on Carrer de la Cort Reial.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride the classic opener: out through Quart and Sant Medir, up Els Àngels to the sanctuary at 485 m, then the fast descent to Madremanya and back through Celrà. This is the loop every visiting rider does first, for good reason.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at La Fàbrica on Carrer de la Barca, the cyclists' canteen run by former pro Christian Meier, or tapas at Konig on Plaça Independència.
itinerary.dayStats: 52 km / 780 m ascent / 100% paved / Els Àngels 10.4 km at 4.6%

itinerary.title: Rocacorba, the reference climb
itinerary.morning: Ride north via Sarrià de Ter and Sant Julià de Ramis, then along the Banyoles road. Warm up properly; Rocacorba punishes anyone who arrives cold.
itinerary.afternoon: The climb: 13.4 km, 940 m, 7% average, 15% pitches, finishing at the masts at 992 m. Descend carefully — the road is narrow, gravel-strewn in places, and there is no run-off. Coffee and a swim at Estany de Banyoles on the way home.
itinerary.evening: Federal Café on Carrer Nou del Teatre for a slower, Anglophone-friendly evening, or Nu on Carrer Abeuradors for a proper Catalan tasting menu.
itinerary.dayStats: 92 km / 1,510 m ascent / 100% paved / summit 992 m / max gradient 15%

itinerary.title: Gavarres gravel and the Els Metges loop
itinerary.morning: Swap onto a gravel bike and head east into the Gavarres massif through Sant Martí Vell and Madremanya. The pistes here are hardpack forest road with occasional loose granite decomposition.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride the Els Metges loop — the medieval villages of Sant Martí Vell, Púbol with its Dalí-decorated castle for Gala, and Monells with its arcaded square. Return on the Ter river path.
itinerary.evening: Vermut and anchovies at La Vermuteria, then dinner at Le Bistrot on the Pujada de Sant Domènec steps for pizzes de coca.
itinerary.dayStats: 74 km / 890 m ascent / 45% paved, 50% hardpack piste, 5% loose gravel / Púbol castle €10

itinerary.title: Sant Hilari and the Guilleries
itinerary.morning: West through Bescanó and Anglès, then the long, even climb to Sant Hilari Sacalm — 17.2 km at 4.1%, a genuinely rhythmic ascent with tree cover most of the way.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend via Osor and Sant Feliu de Pallerols, then join the Carrilet I greenway at Amer for the flat run home. The greenway's packed sand is fine on 28 mm.
itinerary.evening: Cal Ros on Carrer Cort Reial, an old-school Girona house doing suquet and rice dishes; ask for the day's arròs.
itinerary.dayStats: 118 km / 1,690 m ascent / 78% paved, 22% greenway hardpack / Sant Hilari summit 801 m

itinerary.title: The Carrilet to the sea, and Sant Grau
itinerary.morning: Ride the Ruta del Carrilet II end to end: 41.9 km of packed granite sand from Girona through Llagostera and Castell d'Aro, mostly downhill at half a percent, to Sant Feliu de Guíxols.
itinerary.afternoon: Take Sant Grau up from Sant Feliu — 8.6 km at 4.4% to 468 m — then the GI-682 corniche to Tossa de Mar, which is the single best sea-cliff road in Catalonia. Swim at Cala Pola.
itinerary.evening: Can Segura in Tossa for fideuà, or back in Sant Feliu, Can Dulce on Carrer Sant Joan.
itinerary.dayStats: 88 km / 920 m ascent / 52% greenway hardpack, 48% paved / Carrilet II 41.9 km at 0.5% average
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Sant Pol, Sant Feliu de Guíxols

itinerary.title: Empordà plain, Peratallada and back inland
itinerary.morning: North through Palamós and Palafrugell to Peratallada, a stone village so intact it is essentially a film set, then Pals with its brick tower and rice paddies.
itinerary.afternoon: Turn inland through La Bisbal d'Empordà, the ceramics town, and climb Santa Pellaia — 6.8 km at 5.2% to 465 m — back over the Gavarres to Girona.
itinerary.evening: L'Alqueria on Carrer Ginesta for the best arròs a la cassola in the city; book two days ahead.
itinerary.dayStats: 104 km / 1,180 m ascent / 92% paved, 8% hardpack / Santa Pellaia 6.8 km at 5.2%

itinerary.title: Mare de Déu del Mont, or a soft last spin
itinerary.morning: The optional big finish: north via Banyoles and Besalú's eleventh-century bridge to Mare de Déu del Mont, 18.5 km at 5.3% to a sanctuary at 1,115 m with the Pyrenees laid out north. The soft option is the Ter river path to Sant Julià and back.
itinerary.afternoon: Return the bike to Eat Sleep Cycle, then walk Girona's Passeig de la Muralla along the Carolingian walls and through the Call, the medieval Jewish quarter.
itinerary.evening: Final coffee at La Fàbrica, then the 15-minute transfer to GRO.
itinerary.dayStats: 126 km / 1,980 m ascent (big option) or 38 km / 210 m (soft option) / summit 1,115 m

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Nord 1901
accommodationStrategy.description: Two minutes' walk from Eat Sleep Cycle on Plaça de Catalunya, with a locked garage for bikes and a small pool for post-ride legs. On the Mercadal side of the river, so no cobbles or steps with a bike. Roughly €130–€190 double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Bike Breaks Girona Cycle Centre apartments
accommodationStrategy.description: Purpose-built for riders: workshop access, wash bay, laundry, and a shop downstairs that will fix anything. Less charming than a hotel, considerably more useful across a six-day riding block. Around €90–€140 for a twin apartment.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Sant Pol
accommodationStrategy.description: The right one-night coastal stop at the far end of the Carrilet, with bike storage and a beach 30 m from the door, positioned at the foot of the Sant Grau climb. €110–€170 double, and it lets you split the week rather than commuting back to Girona.

logistics.connectivity: 4G and 5G throughout, including on Rocacorba's summit. Spain is in the EU so roaming applies. Strava heat-mapping is unusually reliable here for finding legal gravel — but check for private-estate signs in the Gavarres.
logistics.emergency: 112. Catalonia's GEM mountain rescue covers the Guilleries and Montseny. Spain honours EHIC/GHIC. Hospital Josep Trueta in Girona is the trauma centre. Helmets are compulsory outside urban areas in Spain and on all roads for under-16s.
logistics.weather: The tramuntana, a dry north wind off the Pyrenees, can gust above 90 km/h in the Empordà plain between Figueres and Pals, and crosswinds there are more dangerous than any climb this week. Spring garbinada sea breezes build from 13:00. Rocacorba holds ice in shaded corners into March.
logistics.bookingWindows: Girona hotels fill for Sea Otter Europe in September and for the Girona Cycling Festival — book three months out. Eat Sleep Cycle carbon bikes need four to six weeks in March–May. La Fàbrica does not take dinner reservations for small groups; L'Alqueria and Nu do and want two to five days.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards accepted essentially everywhere including mountain-top bars. Tipping is not customary beyond rounding; 5–10% for a full dinner is generous. Carry €10 in coins for vending machines at greenway stations.
logistics.transportRules: Rodalies R11 carries bikes free outside weekday peaks. AVE and Avant require a bagged or boxed bike. No vignette in Spain; AP-7 tolls were removed in 2021 so approach roads are free. Rental cars may not cross into Andorra without permission. Cyclists must use a reflective vest at night on interurban roads.
logistics.permits: The Gavarres and Montseny are protected but freely rideable on forest tracks; some pistes close during high fire-risk periods, which the Generalitat declares daily in summer. Drones need AESA registration and are banned over the Dalí sites. Wild camping is prohibited across Catalonia.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable but tastes poor in Girona; refill from fountains at Els Àngels and Sant Grau. Processionary caterpillars in pine forests from February to April are dangerous to skin and lethal to dogs. Summer fire bans can close forest roads without notice. Wild boar are common at dusk on the Gavarres pistes.

proTips: Ride Rocacorba on a weekday morning. Weekend traffic on the single-lane upper section is not cars but other cyclists descending, and there is no room for two abreast.
Eat Sleep Cycle supplies no lock. Buy or borrow one before your first café stop — bike theft in Girona city is real and specifically targets rental carbon.
The Carrilet greenways have no cafés for long stretches around Cassà de la Selva. Load up in Llagostera, which has the only reliable mid-route stop.
Girona's group rides leave from Plaça de la Independència and outside the Eat Sleep Cycle Hub between 09:00 and 10:00 most days. Ask in the shop the evening before rather than turning up cold.
Descend Els Àngels toward Madremanya rather than back to Quart. The surface is better, the corners are open, and it puts you on the best breakfast loop in the region.
In high fire-risk summers the Generalitat closes Gavarres forest tracks at short notice — check the day's level before committing to a gravel route with no paved escape.
Sant Grau and the GI-682 to Tossa should be ridden before 11:00 in shoulder season. After that it becomes a motorcycle road.
Book Rodalies bike travel outside 07:00–09:30 and 17:00–19:30. Outside those windows it is free and unlimited; inside them you will be turned away.

raw.Rocacorba (from Banyoles side, via Pujar: 13.4 km, 940 m ascent, 7.0% average, 15% maximum on the ramps above the reservoir, summit 992 m at the transmitter masts. Dead-end road, single lane in places, almost no traffic. The reference climb — most local riders know their time on it.
raw.Els Àngels (from Girona via Sant Medir/Q: 10.4 km, 470 m ascent, 4.6% average, 9% maximum, summit 485 m at the sanctuary. The everyday climb, ridden before work by half the peloton living in the city.
raw.Sant Hilari Sacalm (from Anglès): 17.2 km, 700 m ascent, 4.1% average with a 10% section at Osor, summit 801 m — the long tempo climb, and the gateway to the Montseny foothills.
raw.Sant Grau (from Sant Feliu de Guíxols): 8.6 km, 380 m ascent, 4.4% average, summit 468 m, the coastal balcony climb linking Sant Feliu to Tossa de Mar.
raw.Greenways: Ruta del Carrilet II (Girona–Sant Feliu de Guíxols) is 41.9 km of packed granite sand on a former narrow-gauge formation, high point 136 m at Cassà de la Selva, average grade 0.5%. Carrilet I (Olot–Girona) adds 54 km on similar surface via Les Planes d'Hostoles and Amer.
raw.Week surface split: approximately 72% paved (excellent chip-seal and asphalt), 24% packed granite sand on the greenways and Gavarres pistes, 4% loose forest gravel on the Els Metges and Madremanya link tracks. A 28–32 mm road setup handles the whole week; 38 mm gravel opens the Gavarres.
raw.Bike hire: Eat Sleep Cycle at Plaça de Catalunya 15, 17004 Girona is the main hub — open Monday to Sunday 09:00–14:00 and 17:00–20:00, with a 2026 fleet spanning Colnago, Wilier, Basso and Cannondale road bikes, Wilier gravel, e-road, e-gravel, e-MTB and Brompton. Each rental includes an inner tube, tyre levers and mini-pump; pedals, saddles and helmets are extras and no lock is supplied. Free overnight bike storage at the Hub, and delivery across Girona, the Costa Brava and the Pyrenees by quote. Bike Breaks Girona Cycle Centre and Terra Bike Tours are the established alternatives, both with bike-box storage. Indicative rates run €40–€60/day for carbon road, €35–€50 gravel, €45–€65 e-road, with weekly rates of roughly €280–€420. One-way drop-off on the Costa Brava is a delivery-quote matter rather than a fixed fee.
raw.Bike-friendly accommodation logistics: Hotel Nord 1901 has a locked garage two minutes from Plaça de Catalunya; Hotel Ultònia offers secure storage and a 07:00 breakfast; Bike Breaks runs cyclist-specific apartments with workshop access and a wash bay. Girona's old town is stairs and cobbles — book on the Mercadal side of the Onyar if you value wheeling a bike straight to the door.
raw.Bike on public transport: Rodalies de Catalunya suburban trains (line R11 Girona–Figueres–Portbou, RG1 to Blanes) carry bikes free outside weekday peaks in designated spaces. Long-distance AVE and Avant services from Barcelona require the bike to be bagged or boxed within specified dimensions, or booked into a limited bike space on some Euromed services. Sarfa/Moventis coaches to the Costa Brava take bikes in the hold at driver's discretion for a small fee.

typeSpecific.surface: approximately 72% paved (excellent chip-seal and asphalt), 24% packed granite sand on the greenways and Gavarres pistes, 4% loose forest gravel on the Els Metges and Madremanya link tracks. A 28–32 mm road setup handles the whole week; 38 mm gravel opens the Gavarres.

sources.verified: Eat Sleep Cycle's Girona address at Plaça de Catalunya 15, opening hours, 2026 fleet composition (Colnago, Wilier, Basso, Cannondale, Brompton, e-bike and gravel options), inclusion of tube, levers and mini-pump, free overnight Hub storage, no lock supplied, and delivery-by-quote across Girona, Costa Brava and Pyrenees; Ruta del Carrilet II length of 41.9 km, packed granite sand surface, 136 m high point at Cassà de la Selva and 0.5% average grade.
sources.confidenceNotes: Eat Sleep Cycle daily and weekly rates are not published on the rental page and are indicative only — re-verify through their booking engine before publishing, along with Bike Breaks and Terra Bike Tours pricing and bike-box policies. Rodalies bike-carriage peak-hour windows and AVE bagging dimensions change with timetable revisions; confirm with Renfe. Climb figures for Rocacorba, Sant Hilari, Sant Grau, Santa Pellaia and Mare de Déu del Mont are drawn from standard published profiles and should be spot-checked. Restaurant and hotel pricing is prior-season. Summer forest-track closures depend on the daily fire-risk declaration and cannot be predicted in advance.

trips.title: The Alsace Vineyard Route by Bike

bestPeriod.note: Late September and early October put you in the vineyards during the vendanges, with tractor traffic on the narrow lanes.

trips.gatewayAirport: EuroAirport Basel-Mulhouse-Freiburg (BSL)
trips.summary: A week on the Véloroute du Vignoble d'Alsace and EuroVelo 15, riding grand cru slopes by day and returning to Colmar by free regional train.
trips.hook: Alsace hands cyclists a rare combination. A continuously signed route runs the length of the vineyard, there is a village worth stopping in roughly every eight kilometres, and a dense regional train network will carry your bike free when your legs are finished. The riding is rolling rather than mountainous, apart from one deliberate day of climbing to a castle on a ridge.

snapshot.Base(s): Colmar (5 nights), Obernai (1), Strasbourg (1)
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: Approx. 335 km, +3,000 m cumulative. Asphalt lanes and canal paths, with short sections of compacted vineyard track
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to EuroAirport Basel-Mulhouse-Freiburg, then TER 200 via Mulhouse to Colmar (approx. 1 h 15 door to door with the airport shuttle)
snapshot.Who It Suits: Riders comfortable with 50–70 km days and 500–900 m of climbing, who want wine and villages more than mileage

itinerary.title: Three castles above Eguisheim
itinerary.morning: Collect bikes in Colmar. Colmarvélo, the municipal hire service, rents city and trekking bikes by the day; for a trekking bike with racks and panniers, or an e-bike with a 500 Wh battery, book ahead through an Accueil Vélo certified shop or have Vélo Voyageur or Abicyclette Voyages deliver machines to your hotel. Check the Accueil Vélo sticker at every stop you plan on this week; it guarantees a pump, a repair kit and secure parking within 5 km of the route.
itinerary.afternoon: A short shakedown loop south. Follow the Véloroute du Vignoble d'Alsace out of Colmar to Wettolsheim and Eguisheim, then climb the vineyard lane to Husseren-les-Châteaux and the three ruined towers above it. That is 240 m of gain in about 5 km. Descend to Turckheim through the Brand grand cru.
itinerary.evening: Back in Colmar for the Marché Couvert on Place de l'Ancienne Douane, then dinner at Wistub Brenner. Order the baeckeoffe rather than the tarte flambée.
itinerary.dayStats: 35 km · +420 m · asphalt, 3 km compacted vineyard track.

itinerary.title: Kaysersberg to Ribeauvillé
itinerary.morning: North on the vineyard route to Ammerschwihr and Kientzheim, then Kaysersberg. Domaine Weinbach sits at the Clos des Capucins below the Schlossberg grand cru; tastings are by appointment only and worth arranging weeks ahead.
itinerary.afternoon: Riquewihr, then the short climb to Hunawihr with its fortified church, then Ribeauvillé. Hugel & Fils and Trimbach both run walk-in tasting rooms with fixed hours; the appointment-only estates do not. Return south via Bergheim and the flat lanes through Ostheim.
itinerary.evening: Eat at Winstub Zum Pfifferhüs in Ribeauvillé before riding back to Colmar in the last of the light.
itinerary.dayStats: 58 km · +560 m · asphalt throughout.

itinerary.title: Haut-Koenigsbourg
itinerary.morning: Take the TER from Colmar to Sélestat with the bike. Bikes travel free and unreserved on TER Grand Est, in the carriages marked with a bicycle pictogram. Ride to Châtenois, then begin the climb through Kintzheim.
itinerary.afternoon: The road to Haut-Koenigsbourg climbs about 550 m in 8 km, with sustained pitches of 7 to 9 per cent. The castle was rebuilt for Kaiser Wilhelm II between 1900 and 1908 and the view runs from the Vosges to the Black Forest. Descend north to Dambach-la-Ville, then follow the route through Itterswiller and Andlau, where Domaine Marc Kreydenweiss farms the schist of the Kastelberg.
itinerary.evening: Barr, then Obernai. Overnight in Obernai; the medieval centre around Place du Marché is small enough to walk in half an hour.
itinerary.dayStats: 52 km · +900 m · asphalt, one steep sustained climb.

itinerary.title: The Bruche canal into Strasbourg
itinerary.morning: Obernai to Rosheim and Molsheim, the northern end of the vineyard proper. This is the gentlest riding of the week.
itinerary.afternoon: At Molsheim join the Canal de la Bruche towpath, a flat, largely traffic-free run of about 25 km into Strasbourg. Surface is a mix of asphalt and compacted gravel. It delivers you at the Petite France quarter.
itinerary.evening: Strasbourg. The cathedral astronomical clock performs at 12:30, so it is a morning target rather than an evening one. Eat in the Krutenau instead of the tourist blocks around Place Kléber.
itinerary.dayStats: 44 km · +250 m · asphalt plus 25 km of canal towpath.

itinerary.title: EuroVelo 15 down the Rhine
itinerary.morning: Leave Strasbourg southbound on EuroVelo 15, the Rhine Route, through the Neuhof forest and the Rhine polders. The surface is flat and fast, mostly asphalt on dike tops.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross to Germany and back on the Rhinau ferry, which is free for cyclists and runs continuously in daylight, then continue past Marckolsheim. Leave the river at Artolsheim for Sélestat and take the TER back to Colmar, a 15 minute hop.
itinerary.evening: Colmar. The Petite Venise canals are quiet after 20:00 once the day-trip coaches have gone.
itinerary.dayStats: 55 km · +150 m · asphalt dike paths, short gravel sections in the forest.

itinerary.title: South to the Rangen de Thann
itinerary.morning: Colmar to Rouffach on the vineyard route, past the Vorbourg slope, then Pfaffenheim and Westhalten.
itinerary.afternoon: Guebwiller sits under the Kitterlé and Kessler grand crus and the road tilts noticeably here. Continue through Soultz to Thann, whose Rangen is the steepest vineyard in Alsace at up to 68 per cent, planted on volcanic rock. Zind-Humbrecht and Schoffit both hold parcels there. Return by TER from Thann to Colmar.
itinerary.evening: A quiet night. Book the two-star kitchen at JY'S in Colmar only if you are willing to lose the following morning.
itinerary.dayStats: 52 km · +450 m · asphalt.

itinerary.title: The Fecht valley to Munster
itinerary.morning: West out of Colmar on the Fecht valley cycle route towards Munster, a steady false flat of about 19 km along the valley floor with the Vosges crest ahead.
itinerary.afternoon: Munster for the cheese, which is AOP and sold at its best from the farms above the town. The climb to the Petit Ballon or the Route des Crêtes is available if you have legs left; it adds 700 m. Otherwise coast back to Colmar or take the TER from Munster.
itinerary.evening: Return the bikes. The TER 200 runs Colmar to Basel in about 50 minutes for the airport.
itinerary.dayStats: 40 km · +300 m (add 700 m for the crest option) · asphalt.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Turenne
accommodationStrategy.description: Ten minutes on foot from Petite Venise and five from the station, which matters because four of the seven days use the train. Ask at booking for the enclosed private parking rather than the street; it is the reason to choose this over the guesthouses inside the pedestrian zone, where you will be carrying a loaded bike over cobbles.
accommodationStrategy.booking: three months ahead for September and October.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Le Colombier
accommodationStrategy.description: A converted merchant house on rue Dietrich with an inner courtyard where bikes can be locked out of the weather. Obernai is the right overnight for the Haut-Koenigsbourg day because it puts the following morning on the flat run to Molsheim.
accommodationStrategy.booking: two months ahead.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Cour du Corbeau
accommodationStrategy.description: A 16th-century galleried inn near the Corbeau bridge, with a courtyard and staff used to cyclists arriving off the Bruche towpath. The location kills the need for any city transport on the one urban night of the week.
accommodationStrategy.booking: three months ahead, longer if the European Parliament is sitting.

logistics.emergency: Emergency number is 112. In France, 15 reaches SAMU medical dispatch and 18 the fire service, who also handle road accidents.

other.text: Emergency number is 112. In France, 15 reaches SAMU medical dispatch and 18 the fire service, who also handle road accidents.

Bikes travel free and without reservation on TER Grand Est regional trains, in the marked areas, subject to space. TGV INOUI requires a €10 bike reservation for an assembled bike and space sells out. Regional buses in Alsace do not take bikes.

Navigation is by the green Alsace à Vélo panels. The Véloroute du Vignoble d'Alsace runs Marlenheim to Thann; EuroVelo 5 crosses the plain via Strasbourg and Mulhouse; EuroVelo 15 follows the Rhine. Download the GPX from alsaceavelo.fr rather than trusting a routing app, which will send you onto the D-roads.

Luggage transfer is not a public service here. Vélo Voyageur and Abicyclette Voyages arrange it as part of a booked itinerary; otherwise a local taxi will move bags between hotels for roughly €40–€60 a leg.
Most estates close between 12:00 and 14:00, and many close all day Sunday and Monday. Village bakeries sell out of kougelhopf by 10:00 on Sunday.
Cards work everywhere, but small growers and the Munster farms often prefer cash.
Alsace has a 0.5 g/l blood alcohol limit that applies to cyclists in practice through the offence of riding while impaired. Spit at tastings or ride an e-bike and go slowly.

proTips: Ride the vineyard route northbound in the morning and the plain southbound in the afternoon. The prevailing wind runs up the Rhine valley from the south-west and turns the flat return legs into work if you get the order wrong.
Book Domaine Weinbach and Trimbach by email at least three weeks out, in French, naming a specific date and a party size. Both refuse walk-ins at busy periods but rarely refuse a written request.
The Haut-Koenigsbourg car park fills by 10:30 in season. Cyclists ride past the queue to the bike racks at the ticket office and buy on the spot.
Sélestat is the smartest rail hub on the route, not Colmar. It has more northbound services and lets you cut any day short from Dambach, Châtenois or Marckolsheim.
The Rhinau ferry is free, runs on demand and gets you 20 minutes of Baden riding, which is the cheapest way to add a second country to the week.
Buy a picnic at the Colmar Marché Couvert before 11:00 on a Saturday. It shuts early and there is nothing comparable in the villages.
