raw.Who It Suits: Riders comfortable with 50–70 km days and 500–900 m of climbing, who want wine and villages more than mileage

typeSpecific.surface: Approx. 335 km, +3,000 m cumulative. Asphalt lanes and canal paths, with short sections of compacted vineyard track
typeSpecific.audience: Riders comfortable with 50–70 km days and 500–900 m of climbing, who want wine and villages more than mileage

packingNotes: 32 mm tyres minimum. The vineyard connectors are compacted stone and 25 mm road tyres are miserable on them.
A proper lock. Bikes are left outside tasting rooms and churches all week.
Two 750 ml bottles. There are fountains in the villages but nothing at all on the Haut-Koenigsbourg climb.
Rain jacket and a spare pair of gloves. Vosges foothill weather turns fast in May and October.
A wine-bottle sleeve or a padded pannier insert if you intend to carry purchases; better still, have estates ship.
Sunscreen. The vineyard is unshaded from 09:00 to 18:00.
Front and rear lights, mandatory after dark.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Vendanges traffic.** From mid-September the vineyard lanes carry tractors and hoppers. Ride the plain routes at harvest peak and save the slopes for early morning.
**A full TER.** Bike spaces on the Colmar–Sélestat and Thann shuttles fill on summer weekends. Fall back to the following service; frequency is every 30 to 60 minutes.
**A closed estate.** Many small domaines shut for two weeks in August and again during harvest. Confirm 48 hours ahead and keep the cooperative cellars, which keep regular hours, as a backup.
**Thunderstorms on the ridge.** The Haut-Koenigsbourg day is exposed. If storms are forecast after 14:00, start at 08:00 or swap the day for the Rhine leg.
**A mechanical.** Village bike shops are rare. Carry two tubes and a chain link; the reliable workshops are in Colmar, Sélestat and Strasbourg.

trips.title: La Loire à Vélo — Orléans to Saumur on EuroVelo 6
trips.subRegion: Loire Valley, Centre-Val de Loire and Anjou

bestPeriod.note: May and June for the gardens at Villandry and Chaumont; September for warm water in the Loire and empty châteaux after the French holidays end.

trips.gatewayAirport: Paris (CDG)
trips.summary: Around 290 flat kilometres of dedicated greenway and levee path from Orléans to Saumur, with a château every day and a train back at the end.
trips.hook: The last wild river in France runs between sandbars and willow islands, and someone had the sense to build 900 km of cycle route along it. This is the central section, the one with the châteaux, and it is almost aggressively easy: dedicated greenway, levee tops, and lanes through vineyards, with a total climb over seven days that a single Alpine col would beat before lunch.

snapshot.Base(s): Orléans → Beaugency → Blois → Amboise → Tours → Chinon → Saumur
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx 290 km, roughly 1,200 m cumulative gain; around 85% asphalt greenway and small roads, the remainder compacted crushed limestone (sable stabilisé) on levee sections
snapshot.Getting There: Paris (CDG) → RER B to Paris-Austerlitz, Intercités to Orléans (approx 1h10, bike reservation required). Return by TER Rémi from Saumur
snapshot.Who It Suits: Families, first tourers, anyone who wants a week of riding where the ride is not the hardest part of the day

itinerary.title: Orléans and the first levee
itinerary.morning: Arrive in Orléans. Détours de Loire has agencies here and in nine other Loire towns, which is what makes this trip work: hire in Orléans, hand back in Saumur. Trekking bikes from approx €18 per day, e-bikes from approx €35, one-way drop-off approx €25–40.
itinerary.afternoon: Roll out west on the south bank, leaving the city on greenway past the Pont George V and the Quai du Châtelet, then up onto the levee — the raised flood dyke that carries much of La Loire à Vélo — through Meung-sur-Loire, where Villon was imprisoned in the château.
itinerary.evening: Beaugency is a small stone town with a Romanesque keep, a twenty-two-arch medieval bridge and considerably fewer visitors than anywhere downstream. The Place du Martroi has the market and the cafés.
itinerary.dayStats: 32 km, +90 m, asphalt with 4 km compacted limestone on the levee.

itinerary.title: Chambord across the forest
itinerary.morning: Cross to the north bank at Beaugency and follow the signed spur into the Domaine national de Chambord. The approach runs through a 5,440-hectare walled hunting park, the largest in Europe, with deer and wild boar at the edges.
itinerary.afternoon: Chambord itself: 440 rooms, the double-helix staircase, and a roofline of chimneys that looks like a small city. Entry approx €16, and the bike racks are at the Porte Royale. Then east along the Cosson and the forest greenway to Blois.
itinerary.evening: Blois climbs its hill in staircases. The Château Royal has four wings in four architectural styles, from Gothic to Classical, all facing one courtyard; the son et lumière runs in summer.
itinerary.dayStats: 50 km, +190 m, asphalt with 7 km of forest track and crushed limestone.

itinerary.title: Chaumont's gardens to Amboise
itinerary.morning: South bank out of Blois through Chailles and Candé, then a stretch of levee with the river wide and braided below. This is prime sandbar country; in low water the islands are big enough to walk on.
itinerary.afternoon: Chaumont-sur-Loire sits above a short steep ramp, the only climb worth naming so far. The Domaine runs the Festival International des Jardins from late April to early November — thirty commissioned garden installations; combined ticket approx €21. Give it two hours.
itinerary.evening: Amboise. Leonardo da Vinci died at Clos Lucé, 400 metres from the royal château where he is buried in the Chapelle Saint-Hubert. Château approx €17.50, Clos Lucé approx €19.
itinerary.dayStats: 42 km, +210 m, asphalt with 5 km crushed limestone.

itinerary.title: Vouvray, the troglodyte bank and Tours
itinerary.morning: North bank from Amboise through Lussault and Vouvray. The coteau is honeycombed with troglodyte cellars cut into the tuffeau, and the Chenin Blanc here runs from bone dry to intensely sweet. Domaine Huet has been the Vouvray reference since 1928; tastings by appointment.
itinerary.afternoon: The last 12 km into Tours run on greenway beside the Loire and then along the Cher. Tours is the largest city on the route and the natural rest point.
itinerary.evening: Place Plumereau and the half-timbered streets of Vieux-Tours. The Rue Colbert has the better kitchens; rillons and rillettes de Tours are the local charcuterie and they are not the same thing.
itinerary.dayStats: 34 km, +240 m including the Vouvray coteau, asphalt.

itinerary.title: Villandry's gardens and the Bréhémont levee
itinerary.morning: West along the Cher to its confluence, then the north bank to Villandry. The Renaissance kitchen garden — nine squares of vegetables planted as a formal parterre, replanted twice a year — is the reason to come; gardens only approx €8, château and gardens approx €13.50.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue on the levee through Bréhémont, one of the most peaceful stretches of the whole route, with the Loire on one side and poplar plantations on the other. Langeais has a fifteenth-century château with an intact drawbridge, approx €12.
itinerary.evening: Sleep in Langeais or push 8 km to Bréhémont, where Loire Vélo Nature rents e-bikes and runs shuttles and where the village is a single street facing the water.
itinerary.dayStats: 45 km, +150 m, roughly 12 km compacted limestone levee.

itinerary.title: Azay-le-Rideau and the Chinon vineyards
itinerary.morning: South from Langeais over the river and up the Indre valley to Azay-le-Rideau, a château built on an island in the Indre and reflected in it; approx €13. The approach through Rigny-Ussé passes the Château d'Ussé, the Sleeping Beauty one.
itinerary.afternoon: West through Rivarennes and Huismes into Chinon. The last 8 km climb gently through Cabernet Franc vineyards — Chinon AOC — before the fortress appears on its ridge above the Vienne.
itinerary.evening: The Forteresse Royale de Chinon, where Joan of Arc identified the Dauphin in 1429, approx €10.50. The old town below has the best restaurant density between Tours and Saumur.
itinerary.dayStats: 48 km, +280 m, asphalt with short gravel sections along the Indre.

itinerary.title: The confluence, Fontevraud and Saumur
itinerary.morning: Down the Vienne to Candes-Saint-Martin, where the Vienne joins the Loire. The viewpoint above the collegiate church is the best panorama on the route and takes ten minutes to walk up.
itinerary.afternoon: Montsoreau's white château stands directly in the water. Two kilometres inland, the Abbaye Royale de Fontevraud — the largest surviving monastic city in Europe — holds the tombs of Eleanor of Aquitaine, Henry II and Richard the Lionheart; approx €13.
itinerary.evening: Into Saumur past the Ackerman and Bouvet-Ladubay cellars cut into the tuffeau, where Saumur Brut is aged. Drop the bike at the Détours de Loire agency; TER Rémi carries bikes free to Tours or Angers.
itinerary.dayStats: 40 km, +230 m, asphalt with 6 km crushed limestone.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel de l'Abeille
accommodationStrategy.description: Run by the same family since 1903, two streets from the station and directly on the route out of town. It carries the Accueil Vélo label, which in practice means a locked bike room, a pump and a basic tool kit at reception — the national standard worth checking for at every stop.
accommodationStrategy.booking: six weeks ahead.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Anne de Bretagne
accommodationStrategy.description: On a quiet square at the foot of the château staircase, with a garage for bikes and a five-minute walk to everything in Blois. It is the practical Day 2 finish: you arrive tired from Chambord and do not want a hill or a taxi.
accommodationStrategy.booking: two months ahead for June–September.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Anne d'Anjou
accommodationStrategy.description: An eighteenth-century mansion directly beneath the château on the Loire quay, with a walled courtyard for bikes and a listed staircase. It is 900 metres from Saumur station, so the last morning is a roll rather than a scramble.
accommodationStrategy.booking: three months ahead; Saumur fills during the Cadre Noir events and the July horse shows.

logistics.emergency: 112 across France; 15 for SAMU medical, 18 for fire. Riverside stretches between villages have coverage but the Sologne forest edge near Chambord can drop out.
logistics.bookingWindows: Chambord and Fontevraud sell timed online tickets that skip the queue. Bikes go in racks outside every site; none allow bikes inside the grounds.
logistics.money: Cards everywhere, including most bakeries. Village shops close 12:30–15:30 and all day Sunday afternoon and Monday. Restaurant kitchens stop at 14:00 and do not reopen before 19:00 — plan lunch, or carry it.

other.label: Accueil Vélo
other.text: The national cycle-tourism label. Accredited hotels, B&Bs and repair shops sit within 5 km of the route, keep secure storage and a repair kit, and display a green-and-blue logo. Filter every booking on it.

other.label: Bikes on trains
other.text: TER Rémi in Centre-Val de Loire carries assembled bikes free, no reservation, in marked spaces — first come, first served, and the Orléans–Tours–Saumur axis fills on summer weekends. Intercités from Paris-Austerlitz and TGV to Tours/Saint-Pierre-des-Corps require a paid bike reservation, approx €10, bookable up to four months ahead and genuinely limited. Book the outbound the day reservations open.

other.label: Rental and one-way
other.text: Détours de Loire operates a network of agencies from Orléans to Saumur and beyond, with one-way returns for approx €25–40. Loire Vélo Nature at Bréhémont is the specialist for e-bikes and shuttles in the Touraine section.

other.label: Luggage transfer
other.text: Randovélo, based in the Loire valley, and Détours de Loire both move bags hotel-to-hotel for roughly €15–22 per bag per stage. Book at least three weeks out for July and August.

other.label: Legal
other.text: Helmets are compulsory for under-12s only. Lights and a rear reflector are required after dark. The Loire itself is dangerous to swim — strong undertows, shifting sandbars and no lifeguards outside designated bases.

proTips: Ride west, as this itinerary does. The greenway sections and the château sequence both work better downstream, and the TER return from Saumur is faster and cheaper than the reverse.
Book the Intercités bike slot from Paris the moment the timetable opens. There are typically only a handful of bike spaces per train and they are gone weeks before the seats.
Arrive at Chambord after 16:30. Most of the coach traffic has left, the light on the west façade is at its best, and the domaine's outer park stays open later than the château.
At Chaumont, buy the combined garden festival ticket and start with the far end of the park, working back. Everyone else starts at the château.
Use the south bank between Blois and Amboise and the north bank between Amboise and Tours. Both are signed; the choices above are the quieter and better-surfaced of each pair.
Fontevraud opens at 09:30 and the abbey church is empty for the first forty minutes. It is a fifteen-minute climb from Montsoreau — do it before the Saumur run, not after.

raw.Who It Suits: Families, first tourers, anyone who wants a week of riding where the ride is not the hardest part of the day

typeSpecific.surface: approx 290 km, roughly 1,200 m cumulative gain; around 85% asphalt greenway and small roads, the remainder compacted crushed limestone (sable stabilisé) on levee sections
typeSpecific.audience: Families, first tourers, anyone who wants a week of riding where the ride is not the hardest part of the day

packingNotes: Tyres of 32–38 mm. The levee sable stabilisé punishes narrow rubber and there is no reason to run it here.
A light rain shell; Loire weather is Atlantic and showers arrive fast and pass in twenty minutes.
Sun protection, including arm covers. The levee tops have no shade for long stretches and reflect off the river sand.
A cable lock. Every château has racks; none has supervision.
Two bottles; village fountains exist but are inconsistent, and July on the levee is hot.
Spare tube, levers, pump — Accueil Vélo repair points are frequent but they close at 12:30.
whatCouldGoWrong: **No bike space on the Paris train.** Intercités and TGV bike slots are hard-capped. Fallback: take an ordinary TGV to Saint-Pierre-des-Corps with the bike boxed, or ride the Paris–Orléans section of EuroVelo 3 over two days.

**Summer heat above 35 °C.** The levee has no shade and the Loire valley gets genuinely hot in July and August. Fallback: start at 07:00, take a four-hour lunch, ride again from 17:00; every stage here is short enough to split.

**Rain turns the levee slow and the bike filthy.** Fallback: the parallel departmental roads are quiet, signed as alternates and fully asphalt; the TER between any two towns on the route takes bikes free.

trips.title: Peloponnese: Arcadia & the Argolid

bestPeriod.window: Late March–early June & mid-September–early November
bestPeriod.avoid: July–August, when Arcadian afternoons pass 36°C and the Argolid coast road fills with weekend traffic from Athens
bestPeriod.raw: Late March–early June & mid-September–early November

accommodation.note: Nafplio boutique €90–€150 pppn; Arcadian stone guesthouses €70–€120

food.note: Taverna mains €9–€15; a Nafplio dinner with wine €25–€35

transport.note: Athens transfer, van shuttles between Nafplio, Dimitsana and Leonidio

activities.note: Bike hire €200–€280/week, Epidaurus €12, Mycenae €12, Palamidi €8

profile.difficultyNote: 4/5 — the Leonidio–Kosmas ascent and the Arcadian gorge roads deliver 1,200–1,900 m days on relentlessly uneven surfaces

trips.gatewayAirport: ATH Athens Eleftherios Venizelos, 2 h to Nafplio by road; KLX Kalamata is 2 h 15 min to Dimitsana
trips.summary: The Peloponnese hides its cycling behind its archaeology. Behind Nafplio's Venetian waterfront and the theatre at Epidaurus sits Arcadia, a highland of stone villages, plane-shaded ravines and roads that switchback for twenty kilometres without a village. This week works three distinct terrains: the Argolid's low, fast, ruin-studded coastal plain; the Lousios gorge country around Dimitsana and Stemnitsa, where monasteries are built into cliff faces; and the eastern seaboard at Leonidio, where 300 m orange limestone walls rise straight out of a village and the road to Kosmas is one of the great climbs of southern Europe. It rewards riders who accept rough chip-seal, long empty stretches and a genuine language barrier once you leave the coast.

itinerary.title: Nafplio, Palamidi and a coastal opener
itinerary.morning: Arrive from Athens, take delivery of the bike, and walk Nafplio's old town — Syntagma Square, the Venetian arsenal, and the Bourtzi fortress on its islet.
itinerary.afternoon: An easy coastal spin south-east to Karathona beach and back via Arvanitia, then the optional 999 steps up to the Palamidi fortress on foot. The view down the Argolic gulf is the geographic orientation for the whole week.
itinerary.evening: Aiolos Tavern on Vasilissis Olgas for kokkinisto and a carafe of Nemea red, or Ta Fanaria under the bougainvillea on Staikopoulou.
itinerary.dayStats: 34 km / 320 m ascent / 95% paved / Palamidi 999 steps, €8 entry
itinerary.sleep: Amfitriti Pension or Hotel Ippoliti, Nafplio

itinerary.title: Epidaurus, Mycenae and the Argolid ring
itinerary.morning: East on the quiet inland road through Ligourio to the Sanctuary of Asklepios at Epidaurus. The fourth-century theatre seats 14,000 and its acoustics still work from the top row — test it before the coaches arrive at 10:00.
itinerary.afternoon: Loop north-west through the citrus plain to Mycenae for the Lion Gate and the beehive Treasury of Atreus, then back to Nafplio past the Bronze Age Tiryns walls.
itinerary.evening: To Kentrikon on Plateia Syntagmatos for mezze, then a nightcap on the Akronafplia waterfront.
itinerary.dayStats: 88 km / 940 m ascent / 100% paved / Epidaurus €12, Mycenae €12

itinerary.title: Artemisio pass into Arcadia
itinerary.morning: West through Argos and up the old Tripoli road to the Artemisio pass — 18.7 km at 3.9% to 720 m, effectively abandoned by traffic since the A7 motorway tunnel opened, which makes it one of the best-surfaced empty climbs in Greece.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend to the Tripoli plain and continue west into the Menalon foothills toward Dimitsana, climbing steadily through fir. The last 12 km gain 500 m.
itinerary.evening: Arrive Dimitsana at 950 m. Eat at a taverna on the main street — the Arcadian standard is goat, hilopites pasta and mountain greens.
itinerary.dayStats: 106 km / 1,880 m ascent / 92% paved, 8% hardpack / Artemisio summit 720 m, Dimitsana 950 m

itinerary.title: Lousios gorge, Prodromou and Stemnitsa
itinerary.morning: Drop into the Lousios gorge and ride to the trailhead for Moni Prodromou, a fourteenth-century monastery built into an overhang above the river. The last approach is on foot; bikes stay at the top.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb the 4.8 km at 8.2% out of the gorge to Stemnitsa at 1,080 m, a stone village of silversmiths, then loop back to Dimitsana via the Open-Air Water Power Museum, which explains how these villages made gunpowder for the 1821 revolution.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Trikolonion Country Hotel in Stemnitsa — Arcadian cooking taken seriously, with a fire in shoulder season.
itinerary.dayStats: 38 km / 1,120 m ascent / 70% paved, 25% hardpack, 5% loose gravel / Stemnitsa 1,080 m

itinerary.title: Across the Parnon flank to Leonidio
itinerary.morning: East and south from Stemnitsa toward Tripoli and the Parnon road, a long transitional day through highland villages with almost no services. Fill bottles at Vourvoura; the next reliable water is 40 km on.
itinerary.afternoon: The descent to Leonidio is the reward — a 25 km drop through the Dafnonas gorge with orange limestone walls closing overhead. Arrive at sea level in a village of tower houses.
itinerary.evening: Taverna Michael & Margaret in Leonidio, the climbers' canteen, for stuffed aubergine and the local tsakoniki melitzana.
itinerary.dayStats: 92 km / 1,340 m ascent / 88% paved, 12% gravel / descent 25 km losing 1,150 m

itinerary.title: Leonidio to Kosmas, the queen stage
itinerary.morning: The main event: 30.4 km and 1,180 m from the sea to Kosmas at 1,150 m, passing the Elonis monastery bolted into the cliff at kilometre 13. Start by 08:00 — the gorge holds heat all afternoon.
itinerary.afternoon: Coffee under the plane trees in Kosmas square, then descend the same road. The surface is good but the corners are blind and goats use them.
itinerary.evening: Back in Leonidio, eat at Panjika and look up at the Mars and Kokkinovrachos walls turning red at dusk — this is one of Europe's major sport-climbing venues and the village fills with climbers in spring.
itinerary.dayStats: 62 km / 1,290 m ascent / 100% paved / Kosmas 1,150 m, 30.4 km at 3.9% average, max 11%

itinerary.title: The Argolic coast road back to Nafplio
itinerary.morning: North along the coast through Tyros, Paralio Astros and the Astros wetlands, a rolling seaside road with constant 3–6% undulations and views across to the Argolid.
itinerary.afternoon: Finish in Nafplio, return the bike to the operator's drop-off, and spend the last hours at the Archaeological Museum on Syntagma Square, which holds the Dendra bronze panoply.
itinerary.evening: Final dinner at Ta Fanaria, then the 2 h transfer to Athens.
itinerary.dayStats: 76 km / 890 m ascent / 100% paved / one-way drop-off charge €50–€90
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Ippoliti, Nafplio, or an Athens airport hotel

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Ippoliti
accommodationStrategy.description: A restored mansion a block from the waterfront with a courtyard that will take bikes and a location that avoids the old town's stone staircases. Walking distance to every taverna on this route and to the Palamidi steps. Roughly €130–€190 double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Trikolonion Country Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: The best base in Arcadia: a lockable ground-floor room for bikes, a serious kitchen, and a position at 1,080 m that puts the Lousios gorge circuit on the doorstep. Cold at night in April and October — it has fireplaces for a reason. €110–€160 double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Panjika
accommodationStrategy.description: Built around the climbing community, which means indoor gear storage, a kitchen that opens early, and staff who know the condition of every road on Parnon. Simple rooms, excellent information, and the social centre of the village. €70–€110 double.

logistics.connectivity: 4G is good on the coast and in Nafplio, patchy through the Lousios gorge and unreliable on the Parnon flank. Greece is in the EU so roaming applies. Offline maps are essential in Arcadia, where village signage is Greek-script-only and many road numbers on maps do not exist on the ground.
logistics.emergency: 112 nationally; the Hellenic Coast Guard is 108 and matters on the Argolic coast. Greece honours EHIC/GHIC. Hospitals are at Nafplio and Tripoli; Leonidio has a health centre only, and serious cases go to Tripoli, ninety minutes away over the mountains.
logistics.weather: The meltemi north wind is a summer Aegean phenomenon and affects the Argolic coast less than the islands, but it still builds afternoon headwinds on the Astros stretch. Arcadia gets sharp afternoon thunderstorms from May, and the Menalon highlands can drop below freezing in April and November. Leonidio's gorge acts as a heat trap.
logistics.bookingWindows: Leonidio fills completely with climbers in March, April and October — book three months ahead for those windows. Trikolonion has few rooms; two months. GR Cycling bikes need four weeks. Epidaurus summer festival performances sell out months in advance and fill Nafplio's hotels on those weekends.
logistics.money: Greece is in the eurozone. Cards are accepted in Nafplio and Leonidio; mountain tavernas in Arcadia and village kafeneia are often cash-only and ATMs are absent between Dimitsana and Leonidio. Tipping is rounding up, or 5–10% for a full meal.
logistics.transportRules: Greek motorway tolls are barrier-paid in cash or card; there is no vignette. The A7 Moreas motorway is prohibited to bicycles. KTEL buses take boxed bikes in the hold at driver's discretion. Hellenic Train's Proastiakos services carry bikes but do not serve any town on this route. Rental cars may not be taken to Albania or North Macedonia without written permission.
logistics.permits: Archaeological sites charge separately: Epidaurus €12, Mycenae €12, Palamidi €8, with reduced winter pricing from November to March. Bicycles cannot be taken inside site boundaries — plan for a lock or a rotation. Monasteries including Prodromou and Elonis enforce dress codes: covered shoulders and knees, no cycling shorts. Drones are banned over all archaeological sites and require Hellenic CAA registration.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable in Nafplio and most Arcadian villages fed by mountain springs, but bottled is the norm on the coast. Livestock guardian dogs on Arcadian roads are the most common cyclist incident here — do not sprint, dismount and put the bike between you and the dog. Sea urchins are widespread on rocky Argolic entries. Snakes are present but rarely an issue on road.

proTips: Ride to Epidaurus for opening at 08:00. The theatre is empty for the first forty minutes and the acoustic demonstration only works without a crowd in it.
The old Artemisio road is the hidden gem of the Argolid — since the A7 tunnel opened it carries almost nothing, and it is far better surfaced than its map status suggests.
In Leonidio, ask at Panjika about road conditions on Parnon before committing. The upper forest roads are frequently damaged by winter runoff and no online map reflects it.
Carry a bike lock. Every archaeological site on this route requires you to leave the bike outside, often unsupervised.
Kosmas square is the only reliable food and water on the queen stage after kilometre 6. Do not descend on empty bottles assuming you will find a village.
Tsakonian aubergine from around Leonidio is a PDO product and appears on menus for a short season from late summer. Ask whether it is the real thing.
Time Arcadia for mid-May, when the Menalon meadows are in flower and Dimitsana is still cool enough to climb comfortably at midday.

If you want the Odontotos rack railway from Diakofto to Kalavryta, treat it as a rest-day excursion by car and leave the bikes behind — it is a 22 km gorge line with limited capacity, not a bike-transport option.
Book van shuttles through your Nafplio hotel rather than online. There is no useful public transport between Nafplio, Dimitsana and Leonidio, and local drivers are cheaper than agency bookings.

raw.Queen climb — Leonidio to Kosmas (via Mo: 30.4 km, 1,180 m ascent, 3.9% average with sustained 7–9% sections through the Dafnonas gorge and a maximum of 11%, summit 1,150 m at Kosmas village square. The Elonis monastery is bolted into the cliff at kilometre 13.
raw.Second climb — Artemisio pass from Argos: 18.7 km, 730 m ascent, 3.9% average, high point 720 m on the old Tripoli road, now near-empty since traffic moved to the A7 motorway tunnel.
raw.Mount Parnon approach — Leonidio to Kary: 24 km with 1,340 m ascent on progressively rougher tarmac to roughly 1,250 m, with the Parnon summit at 1,935 m reachable only by gravel forest road beyond.
raw.Lousios gorge circuit (Dimitsana–Stemnit: 38 km, 1,120 m ascent, on a mixture of narrow tarmac and hardpack track, with a 4.8 km ramp at 8.2% out of the gorge floor back to Stemnitsa at 1,080 m.
raw.Week surface split: approximately 68% paved — Greek chip-seal, often coarse, patched, and gravelly on bends — 22% hardpack and forest track in Arcadia, 8% loose gravel on the Parnon and Prodromou approaches, 2% cobbled village lanes. A 30–35 mm tyre on a road bike, or a proper gravel setup, is the sensible choice; 25 mm is punishment.
raw.Bike hire: GR Cycling operates a dedicated Leonidio programme with road and gravel fleets and self-guided packages, and is the most established rental option for this corner of the Peloponnese; they will deliver bikes to Nafplio and Leonidio. Indicative rates run €30–€45/day for carbon road or gravel, €45–€60/day e-bike, and roughly €200–€320/week. Rental in Arcadia's mountain villages does not exist — arrange delivery. One-way drop-off between Nafplio and Leonidio is feasible with a repositioning charge in the €50–€90 band; bike boxes are typically held at the operator's base rather than at hotels.
raw.Bike-friendly accommodation logistics: Leonidio's guesthouses are geared to sport climbers and are used to storing gear — Panjika in the village centre is the community hub with indoor storage and an early-opening kitchen. Trikolonion Country Hotel in Stemnitsa has a lockable ground-floor room. In Nafplio, ask for a hotel in the Pronia district rather than the old town, where every property is up stone stairs. Hose access is rare — carry a chain-cleaning kit.
raw.Bike on public transport: Hellenic Train's Athens–Kiato and Kiato–Aigio Proastiakos services take bikes in designated spaces, but the network does not reach Nafplio, Leonidio or Arcadia — there is no rail option inside this route. KTEL intercity buses will carry a bike in the hold at the driver's discretion for €5–€10, boxed or bagged, and refuse them when the hold is full. The Odontotos rack railway from Diakofto to Kalavryta, 22 km through the Vouraikos gorge, is a spectacular optional day but is not a practical bike-carriage service — treat it as a bike-free excursion, and confirm bike policy directly with Hellenic Train if you intend otherwise.

typeSpecific.surface: approximately 68% paved — Greek chip-seal, often coarse, patched, and gravelly on bends — 22% hardpack and forest track in Arcadia, 8% loose gravel on the Parnon and Prodromou approaches, 2% cobbled village lanes. A 30–35 mm tyre on a road bike, or a proper gravel setup, is the sensible choice; 25 mm is punishment.

sources.verified: GR Cycling's existence as an operating Greek cycling company with a specific Leonidio Peloponnese programme, including self-guided trips, which supports it as the primary rental and logistics contact for this route.
sources.confidenceNotes: Rental day and weekly rates, the delivery radius to Nafplio and Arcadia, and one-way drop-off pricing are indicative and must be confirmed with GR Cycling before publishing. Bike carriage on KTEL buses is entirely at driver discretion and cannot be relied on as published. The Odontotos rack railway's bicycle policy was not confirmed and should be checked directly with Hellenic Train before any itinerary depends on it. Climb figures for Leonidio–Kosmas, Artemisio and the Lousios gorge ramp are from standard published profiles and should be spot-checked. Archaeological site entry fees change annually and have reduced winter rates — re-verify. Guesthouse names and rates in Leonidio, Dimitsana and Stemnitsa are prior-season and should be confirmed as still trading. Parnon forest-road condition varies year to year with winter damage.

trips.title: Istria: The Parenzana & the Hilltowns

bestPeriod.window: Late April–mid-June & September–end October
bestPeriod.avoid: July–August — coastal roads saturated with Austrian and Italian holiday traffic, and the Mirna valley sits at 34°C with high humidity
bestPeriod.raw: Late April–mid-June & September–end October

accommodation.note: Hilltown boutique €90–€150 pppn; Rovinj coastal night pushes higher

food.note: Konoba mains €14–€22; truffle dishes €28–€45 in season

transport.note: Airport transfers, luggage moves between Buje, Motovun and Rovinj

activities.note: Gravel hire €180–€250/week, Parenzana Museum €4, Učka park access

profile.difficultyNote: 3/5 — the rail-trail itself is graded at railway gradients, but the hilltown spurs and the optional Vojak day are genuinely hard

trips.gatewayAirport: TRS Trieste–Ronchi, 75 min to Buje; PUY Pula, 60 min to Motovun; LJU and VCE both around 2 h 30 min
trips.summary: The Parenzana is an abandoned narrow-gauge railway that ran 123 km from Trieste to Poreč between 1902 and 1935, and its Croatian section is now the best-surfaced long gravel corridor in the northern Adriatic. This week uses it as a spine: hardpack embankments, unlit stone tunnels and viaducts through the Mirna valley, with detours climbing off it to Grožnjan, Motovun, Buje and Oprtalj, each a walled hilltown on its own knoll. Add a truffle lunch in Livade, two days of Malvazija tasting, an optional 1,401 m ascent of Vojak on Učka, and a finish on the Rovinj coast. It is the gentlest week in this collection on paper and the most tempting to overcook, because every hilltown demands a climb.

itinerary.title: Buje, and the first tunnels
itinerary.morning: Transfer from Trieste to Buje and take delivery of the bike. Climb into Buje's old town for the loggia and the view over the Mirna basin — the whole week's terrain visible in one sweep.
itinerary.afternoon: Join the Parenzana north of Buje and ride the restored section toward Kostanjica, through the first stone tunnel and across the viaducts. Turn at Završje, a half-abandoned village with a leaning bell tower.
itinerary.evening: Konoba Morgan in Brtonigla — game, Istrian beef and one of the region's most serious wine lists, heavy on Teran and Malvazija.
itinerary.dayStats: 38 km / 470 m ascent / 70% hardpack, 30% paved / two unlit tunnels

itinerary.title: Grožnjan, the artists' town on the ridge
itinerary.morning: Ride the Parenzana east and take the spur up to Grožnjan — 3.4 km at 6.8%. The town has been an artists' colony since the 1960s and its lanes are mostly galleries and studios; ride in early and it is silent.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend to the trail and continue toward Livade through the longest tunnel section, then loop back on the valley road via Oprtalj's lower slopes.
itinerary.evening: Konoba Bastia in Grožnjan for fuži with truffle and a bottle of Kozlović Malvazija.
itinerary.dayStats: 54 km / 780 m ascent / 60% hardpack, 35% paved, 5% setts / Grožnjan summit 288 m

itinerary.title: Mirna valley, Livade truffles and up to Motovun
itinerary.morning: Follow the Parenzana into the Mirna valley floor and stop at the Parenzana Museum in Livade for the railway's history, rolling stock photographs and old timetables — €4, twenty minutes, worth it.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride the valley flats to the Motovun forest, then the ramp: 1.6 km at 9.1%, setts for the final 400 m. Push if it is wet. Walk the Motovun town walls at golden hour.
itinerary.evening: Konoba Mondo just below the Motovun gate — the region's best-known truffle kitchen, small, book ahead. In autumn ask what the white truffle price is before ordering.
itinerary.dayStats: 47 km / 690 m ascent / 55% hardpack, 40% paved, 5% cobbles / Motovun 277 m, max 12%

itinerary.title: Oprtalj, Zavrsje and the Istrian interior
itinerary.morning: Climb north from Livade to Oprtalj (378 m), a 6.2 km ascent at 5.9% with continuous switchbacks and the finest single panorama in inland Istria.
itinerary.afternoon: A gravel loop through Sovinjak and Buzet's outskirts on farm hardpack, returning down the Mirna. Buzet is the truffle capital and its Subotina festival in September serves a giant truffle omelette in the square.
itinerary.evening: Restaurant Zigante in Livade, the truffle house that made the region's name. Expensive and unapologetic; the tasting menu runs €90–€130.
itinerary.dayStats: 63 km / 1,120 m ascent / 45% hardpack, 55% paved / Oprtalj 6.2 km at 5.9%

itinerary.title: The Vojak day, or the Vižinada alternative
itinerary.morning: For the queen stage, van-transfer to Lovran and climb Učka: 22.6 km, 1,380 m, via Poklon at 922 m to Vojak at 1,401 m, with the Kvarner gulf and the Julian Alps from the summit tower. The Učka tunnel is closed to bikes, so this pass road is the only line.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend the same way to Lovran, or continue to Opatija for the Lungomare. Riders skipping Vojak instead take the Parenzana west from Motovun to Vižinada and Baldaši, the loosest and least restored gravel on the route.
itinerary.evening: Konoba Batelina at Banjole near Pula if you have transport — a fish restaurant that treats offcuts and shark as seriously as sea bass. Otherwise Konoba Mondo again in Motovun.
itinerary.dayStats: 45 km / 1,380 m ascent (Vojak option) or 52 km / 540 m (Vižinada option) / summit 1,401 m

itinerary.title: Parenzana to Poreč, then the coast to Rovinj
itinerary.morning: Complete the Parenzana to Poreč through Vižinada and Nova Vas, finishing at the sea. In Poreč, the Euphrasian Basilica's sixth-century apse mosaics are a UNESCO site and open all day.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride south on the coastal lanes via Funtana and Vrsar, skirting the Limski kanal — a drowned karst canyon rather than a fjord, whatever the signage says — into Rovinj.
itinerary.evening: Monte, just under the church of St Euphemia in Rovinj, holds a Michelin star; book weeks out. The cheaper move is grilled fish on the Rovinj waterfront.
itinerary.dayStats: 71 km / 640 m ascent / 50% hardpack, 50% paved / Parenzana Croatian section complete
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Adriatic or Hotel Angelo d'Oro, Rovinj

itinerary.title: Rovinj, Bale and the ride out
itinerary.morning: A flat loop inland to Bale, a compact stone village with a Venetian palace, then back through the Kamenjak vineyards on white roads.
itinerary.afternoon: Return the bike at the operator's Rovinj or Poreč drop-off, then walk Rovinj's Grisia street up to St Euphemia and climb the 60 m bell tower.
itinerary.evening: Ice cream and a Malvazija on the Rovinj harbour before the Pula or Trieste transfer.
itinerary.dayStats: 42 km / 380 m ascent / 65% paved, 35% white road / drop-off fee €40–€70 outside the Parenzana corridor
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Adriatic, Rovinj, or an airport hotel

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel San Rocco
accommodationStrategy.description: Purpose-built for the Parenzana crowd: lockable garage, wash-down point, early breakfast on request, and a restaurant that will feed you at cyclist hours. Brtonigla sits between Buje and Umag, which puts three trail access points within 6 km. Around €150–€210 double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Kaštel
accommodationStrategy.description: The only real hotel inside Motovun's walls, with a vaulted ground-floor room for bikes and a spa that is unusually good for the price. Being inside the gate means you avoid re-climbing the 9% ramp after dinner. €120–€180 double.

accommodationStrategy.name: La Parenzana
accommodationStrategy.description: Literally on the old railway formation, with a bike shed, a workshop bench and a restaurant doing Istrian home cooking. The budget option at roughly €70–€100 double, and the most convenient base if you intend to ride the corridor end to end rather than detour.

logistics.connectivity: 4G is good in the valleys and towns, weak in the Motovun forest and inside every tunnel. Croatia is in the EU, so roaming is included. Download the Parenzana GPX before travelling — junctions on unrestored sections near Baldaši are poorly signed.
logistics.emergency: 112. HGSS mountain rescue covers Učka. Croatia honours EHIC/GHIC. The main hospitals are in Pula and Rijeka; Motovun and Grožnjan have no out-of-hours medical cover at all.
logistics.weather: The bora funnels down from the Ćićarija in autumn and spring, gusting hard on the Vojak summit road and the exposed Buje ridge. The Mirna valley traps fog until mid-morning in October, which makes the unlit tunnels genuinely dangerous. Summer thunderstorms build over Učka after 15:00.
logistics.bookingWindows: Motovun and Grožnjan beds sell out for the September truffle season three to four months ahead. Zigante and Monte want two to four weeks. Rental gravel bikes need three to four weeks in shoulder season. The Motovun Film Festival in late July fills every bed in the Mirna valley.
logistics.money: Croatia adopted the euro on 1 January 2023, so no kuna and no exchange step. Cards are widely accepted; small konobas in the interior and the Parenzana Museum sometimes take cash only. Round up rather than tipping a percentage.
logistics.transportRules: Croatian motorway tolls are distance-based and paid at barriers or by ENC transponder — there is no vignette. The Učka road tunnel is tolled and prohibited to cyclists. Bikes on regional buses depend on the driver and hold space; they are refused on busy summer services. Cross-border car rental into Slovenia and Italy is usually permitted but must be declared. Bicycle lights and a bell are legally required.
logistics.permits: Učka Nature Park is free to enter on a bicycle but has marked no-cycling footpaths. The Parenzana is a public route with no fee. Truffle hunting requires a licence and cannot be done casually. Drone use near the Euphrasian Basilica and Rovinj's old town is restricted; register with the Croatian CAA.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable everywhere including hilltown fountains. Ticks are present in the Motovun forest and on Učka from spring to autumn; TBE occurs in inland Istria. Nose-horned vipers live on dry karst slopes — a real if low risk when scrambling off-trail. Adriatic jellyfish blooms hit in late summer.

proTips: Carry a 600-lumen front light and a rear light for the tunnels. Several are over 100 m, curved, wet and completely dark; phone torches are not adequate.
Ride the Motovun ramp before 09:00. After that you share 3.5 m of cobbled lane with delivery vans and tour minibuses that cannot reverse.
Truffle prices are seasonal and volatile — white truffle from October to December, black from spring. Ask for the day's price per gram before ordering a shaved dish, not after.
The Vižinada–Baldaši section is the roughest on the corridor and unsuitable for e-bikes with narrow tyres. If your fleet is trekking-spec, skip it and use the parallel asphalt.
Buy Malvazija directly at Kozlović near Momjan or Kabola at Kanedolo. Cellar-door prices are far below Rovinj restaurant markups and both will ship.
Time the trip for the Subotina festival in Buzet on the second weekend of September if you want the giant truffle omelette, but book beds two months out.
Ask your hotel to book the luggage transfer with the same operator supplying the bikes. Splitting them across two companies is how bags end up in the wrong hilltown.
If the bora is forecast above 60 km/h, abandon the Vojak plan outright. The summit road has no barriers and the crosswind on the final 6 km is unmanageable on a bike.

raw.Spine route — Parenzana, Croatian sectio: roughly 78 km with about 900 m of cumulative ascent, held to railway gradients of 1–3% wherever the original formation survives, with sharper modern link ramps into villages.
raw.Motovun ramp: 1.6 km at 9.1% average from the Mirna valley floor to the town gate, the final 400 m on polished limestone setts that are lethal when wet. Summit 277 m.
raw.Grožnjan spur: 3.4 km at 6.8% from the Parenzana embankment, 220 m ascent, summit 288 m. Mixed hardpack and broken asphalt.
raw.Optional queen stage — Vojak, Učka: from Lovran on the Kvarner side, 22.6 km with 1,380 m of ascent, averaging 6.2% via the Poklon saddle at 922 m, then the narrow 6 km summit road to Vojak at 1,401 m, the highest point in Istria. Fully paved but exposed. Note the Učka road tunnel is tolled and closed to bicycles — the pass road is the only cycling option.
raw.Week surface split: approximately 40% compacted limestone hardpack (the Parenzana formation), 45% paved secondary road, 10% loose gravel on unrestored sections between Vižinada and Baldaši, 5% cobbled hilltown setts. Tunnels are unlit — a real front light is mandatory, not optional.
raw.Bike hire: Rental Center in Umag rents Parenzana-specific gravel and trekking bikes plus e-bikes and handles trailhead delivery; CCT Bike Rental serves the Parenzana corridor with road and gravel machines delivered to accommodation; Bike Tours Istria run guided and self-guided Parenzana packages with hire included. Indicative rates: €25–€35/day gravel or trekking, €40–€55/day e-bike, €180–€280/week. One-way drop-off between Buje, Motovun and Poreč is standard within the Parenzana operators and usually free inside the corridor; drop-off in Rovinj or Pula typically costs €40–€70. Bike-box storage is generally free for the rental period.
raw.Bike-friendly accommodation logistics: Hotel San Rocco in Brtonigla has a lockable garage, a wash-down point and will produce a 07:00 breakfast on request; Hotel Kaštel in Motovun stores bikes in a vaulted ground-floor room, which matters because you cannot leave anything in the square overnight; La Parenzana in Volpija sits directly on the trail with a bike shed and a basic workshop bench.
raw.Bike on public transport: Istrian rail is largely irrelevant to this route — the Pula–Divača line does not serve the Parenzana towns usefully and bike space is limited. Regional buses (Autotrans, Arriva) will carry bikes in the hold at driver's discretion for €3–€5, but never on full summer services. Jadrolinija and Venezia Lines coastal catamarans out of Poreč and Rovinj generally refuse full-size bikes; car ferries take them free or for a nominal fee. Plan on van transfers rather than public transport.

typeSpecific.surface: approximately 40% compacted limestone hardpack (the Parenzana formation), 45% paved secondary road, 10% loose gravel on unrestored sections between Vižinada and Baldaši, 5% cobbled hilltown setts. Tunnels are unlit — a real front light is mandatory, not optional.

sources.verified: The Parenzana's route Trieste/Muggia–Poreč and its promotion as a cross-border cycling trail; existence of Rental Center in Umag and CCT Bike Rental serving the Parenzana corridor; Bike Tours Istria running Parenzana packages; Croatia's euro adoption.
sources.confidenceNotes: Rental day and weekly rates, one-way drop-off fees and free bike-box storage are indicative and need checking against 2026 price lists. The Croatian Parenzana section's exact rideable length and the condition of the unrestored Vižinada–Baldaši stretch change with maintenance funding — verify locally before publishing. Učka summit road access, any seasonal vehicle restrictions and the confirmed prohibition of bicycles in the Učka tunnel should be re-checked with Učka Nature Park. Konoba Bastia, Konoba Mondo and Zigante opening seasons vary; Zigante menu pricing is an estimate. Bus bike-carriage rules are discretionary and unreliable as published. Hotel rates are prior-season estimates.

trips.title: The Balaton Ring: Seven Days Around Hungary's Inland Sea

bestPeriod.window: mid-May to mid-June, then the first three weeks of September
bestPeriod.avoid: late July–August (heat, Balaton crowds, and a path that jams solid between Siófok and Zamárdi)

accommodation.note: €330–€560 (€45–€80/night, panzió and vendégház doubles)

food.note: €175–€260 (€25–€37/day, csárda lunches and borozó dinners)

transport.note: €120–€190 (bike rental €90–€140 + MÁV tickets, bike tickets, the Szántód ferry)

activities.note: €70–€120 (Festetics Palace, Tihany Abbey, tastings, Hévíz thermal lake)

profile.difficultyNote: Moderate

trips.gatewayAirport: Budapest Ferenc Liszt (BUD), then MÁV line 26 (Kelenföld → Balatonfüred → Tapolca, 2 h 10) north shore, or line 29 (Székesfehérvár → Siófok → Nagykanizsa) south. Hévíz-Balaton (SOB) has limited seasonal traffic [VERIFY: 2026 SOB routes].

trips.hook: Balaton is shallow, jade-green and 77 km long, and the ring around it is flat enough that all the climbing is voluntary. This week rides the paved Balatoni Bringakör anticlockwise, then leaves it twice — over the Tihany peninsula, and into the basalt buttes and gravel lanes of the Káli basin. Fried fogas, cold Olaszrizling, reed beds full of grebes, and one short ferry that saves you forty kilometres.

snapshot.Best period: Mid-May to mid-June, or the first three weeks of September
snapshot.Start / End: Balatonfüred → Balatonfüred (loop, ~308 km ridden; the ring itself is ~204 km)
snapshot.Getting there: Budapest Ferenc Liszt (BUD), then MÁV line 26 (Kelenföld → Balatonfüred → Tapolca, 2 h 10) north shore, or line 29 (Székesfehérvár → Siófok → Nagykanizsa) south. Hévíz-Balaton (SOB) has limited seasonal traffic [VERIFY: 2026 SOB routes].

itinerary.title: Arrival, Csopak and a shakedown
itinerary.morning: Train in, collect the bike, set it up properly — saddle height, brake reach, rack bolts. Coffee on the **Tagore sétány**, the lime-shaded Balatonfüred promenade where Tagore planted a tree in 1926.
itinerary.afternoon: East on the separated path to **Csopak**, then inland to **Jásdi Pince** or **Figula Pincészet** for Csopaki Olaszrizling — flinty and high-acid off Permian red sandstone [VERIFY: current tasting hours]. On to **Alsóörs** and its red-sandstone Turkish House, then back.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Kisfaludy Ház** on the hillside, terrace looking straight down the peninsula, or cheaper and better at **Baricska Csárda** below it. Mákos guba at **Bergmann Cukrászda**. Early night: tomorrow has the best climb.

itinerary.title: Tihany, the abbey, and the volcanic west
itinerary.morning: Flat path to **Tihany-rév**, then the climb in the small ring. At the top, the twin-towered **Tihanyi Bencés Apátság**, founded 1055, whose charter holds the oldest written Hungarian words. Walk Echo Hill for the **Belső-tó**, the crater lake sitting 25 m above Balaton.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to Aszófő, through Örvényes, Balatonudvari and **Balatonakali**, where the path fails and road 71 begins — take the parallel village streets at Zánka and Balatonszepezd. Fogas lunch at **Révfülöp**, then 12 km under the Badacsony basalt.
itinerary.evening: Base in **Badacsony**. Climb the vineyard road to **Laposa Birtok** for Kéknyelű and Juhfark facing the water, or to **Szent Orbán Borház** higher up for dinner over the whole lake [VERIFY: current hours and tasting reservation policy].

itinerary.title: Káli basin: gravel, basalt organs, stone seas
itinerary.morning: Off the ring. Climb through Káptalantóti to **Kővágóörs**, then gravel into the **Káli-medence** — hayfields, dry-stone walls, volcanic buttes. Stop at the **Szentbékkálla kőtenger**, a field of wind-carved sandstone blocks you can scramble on.
itinerary.afternoon: Farm track to **Salföld Major** and its grey cattle, racka sheep and buffalo, then **Kékkút**, the spring behind every Theodora bottle in Hungary. Finish at the **Hegyestű Geológiai Bemutatóhely** above Monoszló: a quarried cone whose sheared face is a wall of hexagonal basalt columns.
itinerary.evening: Eat at **Káli Art Inn** in Köveskál, or taste at **Villa Sandahl** in Kővágóörs [VERIFY: current opening days]. Descend to Badacsony with Szent György-hegy (415 m) and Csobánc (376 m) black against the sky.

itinerary.title: Szigliget, Kis-Balaton and the Festetics
itinerary.morning: Leave the bikes below **Szigliget** and walk 20 minutes to **Szigligeti Vár**, the 13th-century castle that never fell to the Ottomans and owns the western basin view. Down for the flat run to Balatonederics.
itinerary.afternoon: Packed limestone past **Fenékpuszta**, where the Zala leaves the **Kis-Balaton** marshes — spoonbills, purple herons, hundreds of great white egrets in September. Into **Keszthely** on the lakefront path.
itinerary.evening: The **Festetics-kastély**, 101 rooms and a 90,000-volume Helikon Library, is the best interior on the lake [VERIFY: current hours and ticket price]. Dinner at **Bacchus Étterem**. If legs allow, spin 5 km to **Hévíz** and float on the 33–36 °C thermal lake.

itinerary.title: South shore, sphere lookout, and Kistücsök
itinerary.morning: South to **Balatonberény**, where the path leaves road 71 for good and runs flat behind the reeds. Balatonmáriafürdő, Balatonfenyves and the kisvasút crossings — the fastest 25 km of the week, and a tailwind leg in the usual north-westerly.
itinerary.afternoon: Ramp up to **Fonyód**'s Bélatelep villa terrace for the postcard of Badacsony and Szigliget across the water, then **Balatonboglár** and the 1960s concrete **Gömbkilátó** on Várdomb, before dropping to Balatonlelle and **Konyári Pincészet** for the south shore's most serious red.
itinerary.evening: Sleep in **Balatonszemes** and eat at **Kistücsök**, thirty years the best restaurant on Balaton, built around the lake's own fish and Somogy's growers — book ahead [VERIFY: current opening days and reservation lead time]. Natural wine afterwards at **Bakos Bar**, a few doors along.

itinerary.title: Szántód, the ferry, back to the north
itinerary.morning: Easy path through **Balatonszárszó** — pause at the József Attila memorial, where the poet died in 1937 — then Balatonföldvár and **Zamárdi**, with the Szamárkő boulder above the village for one more climb.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Szántód–Tihany car ferry**, BAHART's crossing of the lake's narrowest point (~1.5 km), takes seven minutes, runs year-round and carries bikes without fuss — 1,000 HUF for the passenger and 400 HUF for the bike, so about €3.50 (1,400 HUF) all in, with under-14s free and a car at 3,100 HUF (BAHART tariff from 1 June 2026). It trades the dull 40 km Siófok arm for the best short boat ride in Hungary.
itinerary.evening: Climb from Tihany-rév to the village once more in evening light, then coast to **Balatonfüred**. Dinner at **Vitorlás Étterem** by the Round Church, then out along the pier as the yacht club boats come in.

itinerary.title: The eastern arm, and out
itinerary.morning: East to **Alsóörs**, then the short inland ramp to **Felsőörs** and its 13th-century Romanesque provost's church — the finest small church on the lake and almost always empty.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to **Balatonalmádi**, up to the **Óvári kilátó** for the last panorama, then the Wesselényi beach for a swim: still around 20 °C in September.
itinerary.evening: Return the bike, then the train from Balatonalmádi or Balatonfüred. With three spare hours, ride the extra 12 km to Balatonkenese and Balatonfűzfő and close the ring by wheel rather than by ferry.

accommodationStrategy.name: Blaha Lujza Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: the actress's own 1860s villa, 200 m from the Tagore sétány and the bike path, with a courtyard where bikes lock up out of the weather. Marina, rental shop and station all walkable.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4–6 weeks ahead for May and September; 8–10 for the late-July Anna Ball week.

accommodationStrategy.name: Borbarátok Panzió
accommodationStrategy.description: a working wine house with rooms, a locked bike store, and a kitchen that will still feed you at 21:00 after the Káli day. It sits at the foot of the vineyard road, so the Laposa and Szent Orbán climb starts at the door.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–5 weeks ahead, direct by email rather than the portals [VERIFY: current room rates].

accommodationStrategy.name: A Balatonszemes vendégház
accommodationStrategy.description: the quiet south-shore stretch between the resort clusters, three minutes from the path and walking distance from Kistücsök — which matters after 56 km.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–4 weeks ahead; two-night minimums are common in July–August, single nights fine in shoulder season.

logistics.connectivity: Full 4G/5G on both shores (Telekom, Yettel, One). Only the Káli-medence between Salföld and Monoszló is patchy. Carry the route offline.
logistics.emergency: 112. Hospitals in Keszthely, Siófok and Veszprém; Balatonfüred has the State Heart Hospital. Water rescue is VMSZ, via 112.
logistics.weather: The shore storm masts are not decorative. One flash per second is a first-degree warning, a fast double flash second-degree — get off the exposed north-shore road at once. Squalls arrive from the north-west in under thirty minutes with 60–80 km/h gusts.
logistics.bookingWindows: Beds 3–6 weeks in shoulder season, 8–12 for July–August. Bikes 2–3 weeks. Kistücsök and the better Badacsony cellars, 1–2 weeks.
logistics.money: Forint, roughly 390–410 HUF to €1. Cards work almost everywhere including village csárdas, but carry 15,000–20,000 HUF for the ferry kiosk, small cellars and lángos stands.
logistics.transportRules: Front and rear lights after dark and a bell are legally required. Helmets are mandatory outside built-up areas where the limit exceeds 50 km/h — which includes road 71. Cyclist alcohol tolerance is effectively zero: tastings are a lunch activity.
logistics.permits: No permit needed, but the Balaton-felvidéki Nemzeti Park confines cycling to marked forest and farm roads — stay off the single-track on Szent György-hegy and Badacsony. Kis-Balaton's inner reserve is closed; the Kányavári-sziget boardwalk is the public part.

proTips: **Ride anticlockwise.** The prevailing north-westerly pushes you along the long, fast south shore and keeps the water on your right all week.
**Roll by 08:00 in September.** Empty path, best light, and you clear road 71 under Badacsony before the wine traffic wakes.
**Treat the train as a get-out.** Every town here has a station within 300 m of the path — a headwind or a broken spoke just costs a 500 HUF kerékpárjegy.
**Take the Szántód ferry.** The Siófok arm is the ring's least interesting 40 km, and the crossing hands you Tihany from the water.
**Taste on the hill, sleep in the village.** Laposa and Szent Orbán are 150 m above Badacsonytomaj: ride up before dinner, walk down after.
**Say it right.** *"Egy pohár Kéknyelűt kérek"* gets the local grape, not the tourist Riesling; *"Van kerékpártároló?"* asks about bike storage.
**Swap Day 7 for Hévíz** if your legs are finished — floating at 33–36 °C over 38 m of peat beats 31 km of shoreline.

raw.Daily distance / gain: D1 Balatonalmádi–Csopak–Balatonfüred 29 km / +190 m. D2 Balatonfüred–Tihany–Badacsony 54 km / +430 m. D3 Káli-medence loop 57 km / +720 m. D4 Badacsony–Szigliget–Keszthely 39 km / +200 m. D5 Keszthely–Fonyód–Balatonszemes 56 km / +160 m. D6 Balatonszemes–Szántód–ferry–Balatonfüred 42 km / +280 m. D7 Balatonfüred–Alsóörs–Balatonalmádi 31 km / +260 m. Total ≈308 km / +2,240 m.
raw.Surface split: North shore ~70% dedicated asphalt path, ~25% shared low-traffic road, ~5% packed limestone at Fenékpuszta. The gaps at Balatonakali, Zánka and Badacsony–Ábrahámhegy put you on the shoulder of **road 71**, narrow and fast — the week's only real hazard. South shore ~95% separated path from Balatonberény to Siófok. The Káli day is ~45% asphalt, ~50% compacted gravel and dolomite farm track, ~5% loose basalt: 35 mm tyres minimum, 40 mm better.
raw.The Tihany climb: Flat to Tihany-rév, then ~90 m in 3.5 km at 4–6% to the Abbey terrace (village ~130 m; lake level 105 m; Csúcs-hegy 232 m, Óvár 219 m). Anticlockwise you take the gentler east flank up and the steeper west flank down to Aszófő.
raw.Rental: Balatonfüred's shops cluster around the **Tagore sétány** marina; Siófok's around **Petőfi sétány** and the Sió canal quay. Trekking bikes €10–€16/day (4,000–6,500 HUF), e-bikes €22–€30/day (9,000–12,000 HUF), weekly rates 25–35% less; panniers rarely included. [VERIFY: 2026 Balatonfüred and Siófok rental trading names, addresses and rates — cross-check the operator list on the official Balatoni Bringakör site.]
raw.Bike-friendly stays: Insist on a locked *zárható kerékpártároló*, a floor pump and breakfast from 07:30; ask for the **Kerékpárosbarát Szálláshely** designation by name.
raw.Trains with a bike (MÁV-START): Bikes ride the marked carriage on almost all Balaton regionals and fast trains on a separate **kerékpárjegy**, 500 HUF (~€1.25) for 24 hours and a single journey, with 15% off in the MÁVPlusz app; on InterCity a bike **kerékpárhelyjegy** is compulsory on top, 100–990 HUF depending on route and season, and the quota is small, so book in the app days ahead for summer weekends (2026 tariff). Lines 26 and 29 add summer bike capacity, which makes bailing out of a leg trivial.

trips.title: Valle d'Itria & Salento by Bike

bestPeriod.window: Late March–mid-June & mid-September–early November
bestPeriod.avoid: July–August — 36°C inland, zero shade on the murgia, and coastal roads jammed with beach traffic
bestPeriod.raw: Late March–mid-June & mid-September–early November

accommodation.note: Trullo and albergo diffuso €80–€130 pppn; a Savelletri masseria doubles it

food.note: Fornello pronto grills €15–€22; Lecce trattorie €25–€35 with wine

transport.note: Airport transfers, one FSE regional train leg, luggage move to Lecce

activities.note: Road or gravel hire €190–€240/week, Egnazia €7, Torre Guaceto guided entry €10

profile.difficultyNote: 3/5 — rolling rather than mountainous, but 700–1,100 m of ascent a day accumulates on rough limestone lanes

trips.gatewayAirport: BRI Bari Karol Wojtyła, 65 min to Locorotondo; BDS Brindisi Salento is 45 min to Ostuni and 40 min to Lecce
trips.summary: The Valle d'Itria is a shallow limestone basin stitched with dry-stone walls, olive trunks the width of a car, and trulli that appear in fields the way boulders do elsewhere. Riding it means constant micro-climbs on white lanes between Locorotondo, Cisternino and Martina Franca, then a fast drop off the Murgia escarpment at Ostuni to a coastline of dune, macchia and Roman ruin. The last two days shift south to the Salento, where the landscape flattens, the light hardens, and the ride from Lecce to Otranto runs through baroque towns and scarred olive groves. It is a cycling week built around food and surface variety rather than climbing, and it rewards a gravel bike over a race bike.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Locorotondo, the valley's first white lanes
itinerary.morning: Land at Bari, transfer to Locorotondo and collect the bike from Puglia On Bike. Walk the circular centro storico — the town is a perfect ring of whitewashed houses with pitched cummerse roofs found nowhere else in Puglia.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride a soft opener anti-clockwise through Contrada Serralta and Contrada Trito on strade bianche, looping past working trulli and vineyards of verdeca and bianco d'Alessano.
itinerary.evening: Quanto Basta on Via Morelli in Locorotondo — craft beer, bruschetta and a terrace over the valley. Follow with a nightcap at U Curdunn.
itinerary.dayStats: 31 km / 380 m ascent / 45% paved, 55% strade bianche

itinerary.title: The Trulli Ring, and Alberobello before the buses
itinerary.morning: Leave by 07:30 for Alberobello so you reach the Rione Monti and Rione Aia Piccola trullo districts before the coach parties. Ride the back lanes via Contrada Sisto rather than the SP113.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to Martina Franca for the baroque Palazzo Ducale and Via Cavour, then Cisternino on the ridge lanes. This is the loop's rough section — expect washboard limestone.
itinerary.evening: Cisternino's fornello pronto ritual: choose your meat at a butcher such as Zio Pietro, they grill it, you eat it upstairs with a jug of local red. Bombette are the obligatory order.
itinerary.dayStats: 68 km / 890 m ascent / 40% paved, 60% strade bianche and farm track

itinerary.title: Murgia plateau, Selva di Fasano and the escarpment view
itinerary.morning: Climb east from Locorotondo through Selva di Fasano to the plateau lip at 431 m, where the land falls 400 m to the Adriatic in a single step. The Montevicoli ramp hits 11%.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend to Ceglie Messapica for the Messapian walls and a long lunch, then return by the Contrada Vitti white roads. Ceglie is the valley's serious food town and worth the detour on its own.
itinerary.evening: Back in Locorotondo, dinner at La Taverna del Duca on Via Papatotero — orecchiette with cime di rapa, and a bottle of Locorotondo DOC white.
itinerary.dayStats: 62 km / 1,050 m ascent / 60% paved, 40% white road / high point 431 m / max gradient 11%

itinerary.title: Off the escarpment to Ostuni and the coast
itinerary.morning: Ride the descent to Ostuni via Contrada Lamacoppa, then climb the last kilometre through Porta San Demetrio into the white city. Coffee in Piazza della Libertà, then the cathedral's rose window.
itinerary.afternoon: Drop to the coast through the ancient olive groves of the Piana degli Olivi Secolari — trees dated at over a thousand years, several fenced as monumental. Reach the Torre Guaceto marine reserve and ride its sand-and-hardpack coast track.
itinerary.evening: Osteria del Tempo Perso in Ostuni, cut into the rock behind the cathedral. Order the lamb and a Susumaniello.
itinerary.dayStats: 74 km / 780 m ascent / 65% paved, 32% hardpack, 3% dune sand / Ostuni climb 8.1 km at 3.2%, max 9%

itinerary.title: Egnazia, Savelletri and the transfer to Lecce
itinerary.morning: North along the coast road past Torre Canne to the Parco Archeologico di Egnazia, a Messapian and Roman port town with a preserved Via Traiana paving slab and a small but excellent museum.
itinerary.afternoon: Lunch at Savelletri on the harbour, then either ride inland to Fasano and take the regional train, or transfer by van to Lecce with the bikes. Arrive in time to walk Piazza del Duomo at dusk.
itinerary.evening: Alle Due Corti on Corte dei Giugni in Lecce for uncompromising Salentine cooking — ciceri e tria, and pezzetti di cavallo if you are curious.
itinerary.dayStats: 58 km ridden / 520 m ascent / 85% paved / Egnazia entry €7 / transfer to Lecce 1 h 15 min

itinerary.title: Lecce to Otranto and the Adriatic edge
itinerary.morning: Out of Lecce on the SP1 toward Vernole and Acaya, a fortified Renaissance village with intact walls, then the Le Cesine WWF reserve where the road runs between lagoon and dune.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue via San Foca and Roca Vecchia to Otranto. The Grotta della Poesia sinkhole at Roca is the swim stop. In Otranto, the cathedral's twelfth-century mosaic floor and the martyrs' chapel are 20 minutes well spent.
itinerary.evening: Peccato di Vino on Via Rondachi in Otranto — raw seafood and Negroamaro on a lane behind the castle.
itinerary.dayStats: 79 km / 610 m ascent / 90% paved, 10% dune track / total climbing below 200 m altitude throughout
itinerary.sleep: Palazzo Rollo, Lecce (train back from Otranto, or van shuttle)

itinerary.title: Salento loop through Galatina and out
itinerary.morning: A final flat loop south-west from Lecce to Galatina for the Basilica di Santa Caterina d'Alessandria, whose frescoed interior is the best painted surface in Puglia and almost always empty.
itinerary.afternoon: Return via Copertino's Angevin castle and the vineyards around Leverano. Hand the bike to the operator's Lecce drop-off point, agreed at booking.
itinerary.evening: Pasticciotto and caffè leccese at Avio in Lecce before the transfer to Brindisi.
itinerary.dayStats: 66 km / 340 m ascent / 95% paved / one-way drop-off fee €50–€80
itinerary.sleep: Palazzo Rollo, Lecce, or a Brindisi airport hotel

accommodationStrategy.name: Sotto le Cummerse
accommodationStrategy.description: Restored houses scattered through the historic centre, all with kitchens, and a ground-floor annexe used for bike storage. You wake up inside the walled town and are on white roads within 400 m. Roughly €95–€135 double, and the reception will handle Puglia On Bike deliveries.

accommodationStrategy.name: Masseria Il Frantoio
accommodationStrategy.description: A seventeenth-century masseria with a subterranean olive mill that doubles as bike storage. Positioned on the SS16 side of Ostuni, so you exit straight onto the coastal lanes. Eight-course estate dinners on request; €180–€260 double, and worth exactly one night.

accommodationStrategy.name: Palazzo Rollo
accommodationStrategy.description: A seventeenth-century palazzo on Corte dei Rollo, inside the pedestrian core but with an internal courtyard for bikes and a rooftop loggia. Two minutes from Piazza Sant'Oronzo and about €90–€140 double, which is the sweet spot for two nights of Salento riding.

logistics.connectivity: 4G and 5G are strong throughout, including on the white roads. Italy is in the EU so roaming is included. Offline mapping still matters: many strade bianche are unnamed and Google routing will occasionally send you into a private masseria drive.
logistics.emergency: 112 across Italy; 118 still reaches ambulance dispatch directly. The main trauma centres are Ospedale Perrino in Brindisi and Vito Fazzi in Lecce. Italy requires cyclists to carry a reflective gilet and use lights in tunnels and after dusk on extra-urban roads.
logistics.weather: Spring brings the scirocco, a hot southerly carrying Saharan dust that drops visibility and coats bikes in red grit. Autumn produces short, violent coastal thunderstorms. Wind, not gradient, is the limiting factor on the Salento coast — 25–35 km/h afternoon sea breezes are routine.
logistics.bookingWindows: Masserie around Savelletri and Ostuni sell out for May and September six months ahead. Rental bikes need four to six weeks. Alle Due Corti and Osteria del Tempo Perso take same-week bookings outside August. Torre Guaceto's guided reserve entries should be reserved a few days out.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are near-universal, but the butcher-grills of Cisternino and rural masseria farm shops often prefer cash. A coperto of €2–€3 per person is standard and is not a tip; tipping beyond rounding up is not expected.
logistics.transportRules: No vignette in Italy; motorway tolls apply on the A14 north of Bari only. Trenitalia regional bike tickets are €3.50 for 24 hours. FSE regional trains take bikes with a supplement but have very limited space, no reservation, and none on replacement buses. Rental cars crossing to Albania by ferry from Brindisi need written permission.
logistics.permits: Torre Guaceto is a protected marine and terrestrial reserve — stay on marked tracks, no off-piste riding on dunes, and swimming is zoned. Egnazia archaeological park charges €7. Drone flying is banned over archaeological sites and requires ENAC-compliant registration. Monumental olive trees are legally protected; do not lean bikes against them.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable but heavily chlorinated and tastes of it; most riders buy still water. Xylella fastidiosa has killed vast tracts of Salento olives — the dead groves are not fire-safe, and cigarette discipline matters. Jellyfish blooms of Pelagia noctiluca hit the Adriatic coast in late summer. Loose dogs on farm lanes are a genuine hazard; do not sprint.

proTips: Reach Alberobello's Rione Monti before 08:30 or after 18:30. Between those hours it is the single most crowded square kilometre in southern Italy.
Ride the white roads clockwise out of Locorotondo — the dry-stone walls throw shade on the eastern side of the lanes until about 11:00, which is worth several degrees in May.
In Cisternino, order at the butcher counter and pay there, not at the table. Tell them how many bombette per person; four is a normal serving, six is a cyclist's.
Ask your masseria for a 07:00 breakfast the night before. Puglian hotels default to 08:30, which is an hour of lost cool riding.
Torre Guaceto's inner tracks are sand over hardpack. Drop 10 psi at the gate and re-inflate at the exit; the reserve office has no pump.
Buy Locorotondo DOC and Valle d'Itria whites at the source rather than in Ostuni — the same bottle is routinely 40% cheaper in the producing village.
FSE track works regularly suspend the Martina Franca line at short notice. Confirm the day before, and always have a van fallback for the Lecce transfer.
The Grotta della Poesia at Roca Vecchia is free and unstaffed early; by noon in shoulder season it has a queue for the single entry ladder.

raw.Signature loop — the Trulli Ring (Locoro: 68 km, 890 m ascent, run entirely on strade bianche and single-track asphalt lanes between dry-stone walls, with no climb over 3 km.
raw.Escarpment climb — Ostuni from Villanova: 8.1 km, 260 m ascent, 3.2% average with a 9% pinch through the Porta San Demetrio approach, summit 218 m. Short, but it is the only sustained gradient on the coast side.
raw.Martina Franca–Ceglie Messapica murgia c: 4.6 km at 4.8%, maximum 11% on the Contrada Montevicoli ramp, high point 431 m near Selva di Fasano — the top of the plateau and the day's only real view.
raw.Week surface split: roughly 55% paved (much of it patched, chip-sealed provincial lane), 30% strade bianche and compacted limestone farm track, 12% cracked concrete masseria access roads, 3% sandy dune track inside Torre Guaceto. Puglian asphalt is often worse than the gravel — run 35–40 mm.
raw.Bike hire: Puglia On Bike, based in Locorotondo, is the region's most established rental and guiding outfit, with road, gravel and e-bike fleets and delivery across the Valle d'Itria. Velo Service and Veloce Rental both operate road and gravel hire out of Alberobello, and CCT Bike Rental covers Locorotondo, Alberobello and Cisternino with delivery-to-accommodation. Indicative rates: €25–€35/day for an aluminium road or gravel bike, €45–€60/day carbon, €35–€45/day e-bike; weekly €190–€260. One-way drop-off in Lecce is possible with most operators for a €50–€80 repositioning fee — agree it in writing at booking. Bike boxes are stored free by Puglia On Bike for the rental duration.
raw.Bike-friendly accommodation logistics: Sotto le Cummerse in Locorotondo distributes guests across restored houses and locks bikes in a ground-floor annexe; Masseria Salamina at Pezze di Greco has a stone outbuilding, a hose and a compressor line; Masseria Il Frantoio near Ostuni will store bikes in the old olive mill. Ask specifically for a room at ground level — Valle d'Itria stairs are stone, narrow and unforgiving with a bike on your shoulder.
raw.Bike on public transport: Trenitalia regional services take bikes on a €3.50 ticket valid 24 hours, in marked carriages. The Ferrovie del Sud Est network — Bari–Putignano–Martina Franca–Taranto and the Lecce branches — carries bikes on regional trains with a supplement but has limited space and no reservation, and replacement buses will not take them. Check FSE engineering works before relying on the Martina Franca line.

typeSpecific.surface: roughly 55% paved (much of it patched, chip-sealed provincial lane), 30% strade bianche and compacted limestone farm track, 12% cracked concrete masseria access roads, 3% sandy dune track inside Torre Guaceto. Puglian asphalt is often worse than the gravel — run 35–40 mm.

sources.verified: Existence and Locorotondo base of Puglia On Bike as a rental and tour operator; Veloce Rental and CCT Bike Rental offering road and gravel hire in Alberobello, Locorotondo and Cisternino; Trenitalia regional bike-ticket structure.

Egnazia and Torre Guaceto entry prices and Torre Guaceto's guided-access requirements change season to season.
