trips.title: Luxembourg on the PC Network

bestPeriod.note: Mid-September puts you on the Moselle during the grape harvest and the Riesling festivals in Grevenmacher and Wormeldange.

trips.gatewayAirport: Luxembourg (LUX)
trips.summary: A week on Luxembourg's national PC cycle routes, linking the Moselle vineyards to the Mullerthal sandstone and the Our valley, with free public transport throughout.
trips.hook: Luxembourg is small enough to cross in a day and varied enough that you will not want to. The national pistes cyclables, signed PC1 through PC23, are mostly former railway alignments and river towpaths, which means gradients built for steam locomotives rather than for cyclists. Public transport is free, trains carry bikes free, and the whole country sits inside a 60 km square.

snapshot.Base(s): Remich (3 nights), Echternach (3), Vianden (1)
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: Approx. 285 km, +2,600 m cumulative. Asphalt river paths and rail-trails, with compacted gravel forest tracks in the Mullerthal
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Luxembourg-Findel, then a free bus to the city and a free CFL train onward. Bikes travel free on CFL trains
snapshot.Who It Suits: Riders who want three landscapes in one small country and dislike paying for transport

itinerary.title: Out of the city to the Moselle
itinerary.morning: Collect bikes. Rentabike Miselerland, the regional hire network run by the Moselle tourist office, has stations at Remich, Grevenmacher and Schengen with trekking bikes and e-bikes, and lets you drop at a different station from the one you collected at. In the capital, vel'OH is the shared-bike system but not suitable for a touring week.
itinerary.afternoon: Leave Luxembourg City south-east on EuroVelo 5, which runs through the country on its way from London to Brindisi, then pick up the Syre valley towards Munsbach and Roodt-sur-Syre before dropping to the river. The descent to the Moselle at Grevenmacher or Remich is long and easy.
itinerary.evening: Remich. The promenade along the river is the town's whole social life. Caves St Martin, cut into the rock north of town, run cellar tours and Crémant tastings.
itinerary.dayStats: 45 km · +350 m · asphalt, mostly separated cycle path.

itinerary.title: PC3 south to Schengen and the tri-border
itinerary.morning: Follow PC3, the Moselle cycle route, south from Remich through Bech-Kleinmacher and Wellenstein. The path runs on the flood dike, dead flat, with vineyards climbing the slope on your right.
itinerary.afternoon: Schengen, where the 1985 agreement was signed on a boat moored in the river. The European Museum is small and free to enter. From here you can touch Germany and France within a kilometre: cross the bridge to Perl, ride down to the Roman villa at Nennig with its gladiator mosaic, then return along the German bank.
itinerary.evening: Back in Remich. Domaines Vinsmoselle, the growers' cooperative, has its Caves de Wellenstein nearby; the Auxerrois and Pinot Gris are the local benchmarks rather than the Riesling.
itinerary.dayStats: 42 km · +120 m · asphalt dike path.

itinerary.title: PC3 north to Grevenmacher and Trier
itinerary.morning: North on PC3 through Ehnen, with its wine museum in a vigneron's house, and Wormeldange, where Domaine Alice Hartmann farms the Koeppchen slope. Grevenmacher is 20 km from Remich.
itinerary.afternoon: Caves Bernard-Massard at Grevenmacher runs guided visits with a Crémant tasting and has done since 1921. Then continue to Wasserbillig, where the Sûre joins the Moselle, and on into Germany to Trier along the Mosel-Radweg, another 15 km. The Porta Nigra and the imperial baths are inside the ring road.
itinerary.evening: Return by train from Trier to Wasserbillig and Luxembourg. Bikes travel free on CFL; on the German side you need a Fahrradkarte for the short hop, roughly €3.
itinerary.dayStats: 52 km · +200 m · asphalt.

itinerary.title: The Sûre valley to Echternach
itinerary.morning: From Wasserbillig, PC2, the Trois Rivières route, follows the Sûre upstream. The river marks the German border the whole way, so you ride with Rhineland-Palatinate on the far bank. Rosport has the Tudor museum, dedicated to the local inventor of the lead-acid battery.
itinerary.afternoon: Echternach at 22 km, the oldest town in the country, built around the abbey founded by Willibrord in 698. The basilica crypt holds his sarcophagus. Switch bikes here to Rentabike Mëllerdall if you want a mountain bike for the next two days.
itinerary.evening: Ride the flat 3.5 km loop around the Echternach lake at dusk. Dinner on the Place du Marché under the Gothic Denzelt.
itinerary.dayStats: 45 km · +400 m · asphalt with short gravel sections above Rosport.

itinerary.title: Mullerthal sandstone
itinerary.morning: The Mullerthal Trail itself is a walking route and bikes are not permitted on it. Instead use the Mountainbike Park Mëllerdall, a signed network of graded loops out of Echternach, or ride the road circuit to Berdorf and Consdorf. The plateau is cut by narrow sandstone gorges and the climbs out of them are short and steep.
itinerary.afternoon: Beaufort for the castle, which pairs a medieval ruin with a Renaissance house, then Larochette in its rock amphitheatre. The descent into the Ernz Noire valley is a genuine reward.
itinerary.evening: Back to Echternach via Waldbillig and Grundhof. Refuel with a Bouneschlupp or a Judd mat Gaardebounen if the kitchen is traditional.
itinerary.dayStats: 52 km · +700 m · asphalt with 12 km of compacted forest gravel.

itinerary.title: Up the Our to Vianden
itinerary.morning: North from Echternach on PC2 through Bollendorf-Pont and Dillingen, then Wallendorf-Pont, where the Our joins the Sûre. This is the quietest riding of the week.
itinerary.afternoon: The Our valley to Vianden climbs steadily for about 20 km. Vianden's castle is the largest fortified residence west of the Rhine from the 11th to the 14th century, restored from ruin after 1977. The chairlift above the town runs to a viewpoint over the whole valley and takes bikes.
itinerary.evening: Victor Hugo's house on the Vianden bridge is a museum; he stayed here four times in exile.
itinerary.dayStats: 45 km · +550 m · asphalt.

itinerary.title: Sûre valley to Ettelbruck
itinerary.morning: Down the Our to Bettel, then west along the Sûre to Diekirch, home of the national brewery and the National Museum of Military History, which covers the Battle of the Bulge in unusual depth.
itinerary.afternoon: Ettelbruck is 5 km further and is the rail hub for the north. If you have time, extend up the Sûre towards Erpeldange and Bourscheid, where the castle sits on a spur 150 m above the river.
itinerary.evening: CFL from Ettelbruck to Luxembourg City takes 25 minutes, bikes free. Airport bus from the station is free.
itinerary.dayStats: 38 km · +280 m · asphalt with a short rail-trail section.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Saint-Nicolas
accommodationStrategy.description: On the Moselle promenade, family-run, with a garage for bikes and a spa that is genuinely useful after two consecutive days on the dike path. Remich is the right Moselle base because PC3 runs both directions from the door and the Schengen and Grevenmacher days need no transfer.
accommodationStrategy.booking: two months ahead, three for the September wine weekends.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Bel Air
accommodationStrategy.description: Set in its own grounds above the town, with secure bike storage, a workshop corner and a drying room. It is used to riders coming back muddy off the Mullerthal gravel, which most town hotels are not.
accommodationStrategy.booking: six weeks ahead. Echternach's Youth Hostel by the lake is the budget alternative and also has a locked bike store.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Heintz
accommodationStrategy.description: A former abbey building on the Grand-Rue, run by the same family for generations, with a rear courtyard for bikes. It sits below the castle and above the Our, which is exactly where you want to be for a single night.
accommodationStrategy.booking: two months ahead; Vianden has few beds.

logistics.emergency: Emergency number is 112; police are on 113. Mobile coverage is good even in the Mullerthal gorges.

other.text: Emergency number is 112; police are on 113. Mobile coverage is good even in the Mullerthal gorges.

All public transport in Luxembourg has been free in second class since March 2020. Bicycles travel free of charge on CFL trains, in the carriages marked with a bike pictogram, without reservation. Space is limited, so avoid the 07:00–09:00 commuter peak into the capital.
Cross-border services are not free. A ticket is needed the moment you continue past Wasserbillig into Germany or past Rodange into Belgium, and German regional trains require a separate bike ticket.

The PC routes are signed with white bike symbols on a blue background carrying the route number. PC3 is the Moselle, PC2 the Trois Rivières route through Echternach and Vianden. The Mobilitéit app and the visitluxembourg GPX downloads are both reliable.

Rentabike Mëllerdall and Rentabike Miselerland allow one-way drops within their own networks and both hire e-bikes. Neither is a repair shop; workshops are in Echternach, Grevenmacher and the capital.
Luggage transfer is not a public service. Ask your hotel; several will move bags between Remich, Echternach and Vianden for €30–€50, or use a local taxi.
Fuel is cheap here; restaurant prices are not. Expect Belgian rather than German levels.
Wild camping is prohibited without landowner permission. Campsites line the Sûre and the Our.

proTips: Ride the Moselle northbound in the morning. The valley wind builds from the south-west after midday and pushes you home to Remich in the afternoon.
Book Caves Bernard-Massard and Caves St Martin the day before by phone. Both take walk-ins, but the guided cellar visit runs on fixed times and the last one is usually at 16:00 or 17:00.
The chairlift at Vianden takes bikes and the descent on the plateau road is far more pleasant than climbing it. Buy a single up, ride the top loop, freewheel back.
Echternach is a better Mullerthal base than Beaufort or Larochette because it has the bike hire, the workshop, the train-replacement bus links and the only reliable evening kitchens.
Cross into Germany for dinner from Remich or Echternach. Prices at Nennig, Bollendorf and Echternacherbrück are noticeably lower and the bridges take two minutes.
The Mullerthal gravel loops are graded like ski runs. The blue loops are ridable on a trekking bike with 40 mm tyres; the red and black ones are not.

raw.Total Distance / Terrain: Approx. 285 km, +2,600 m cumulative. Asphalt river paths and rail-trails, with compacted gravel forest tracks in the Mullerthal
raw.Who It Suits: Riders who want three landscapes in one small country and dislike paying for transport

typeSpecific.surface: Approx. 285 km, +2,600 m cumulative. Asphalt river paths and rail-trails, with compacted gravel forest tracks in the Mullerthal
typeSpecific.audience: Riders who want three landscapes in one small country and dislike paying for transport

packingNotes: 38–42 mm tyres. The Mullerthal forest tracks are rooty sandstone and the Sûre path has gravel sections.
A rear light with a steady mode for the Rosport and Bollendorf tunnels on the old rail alignments.
A jacket that packs small; the Öslinger plateau catches Atlantic weather the Moselle never sees.
Cash in small notes for village bakeries and cellar tastings.
A passport or ID card; you cross into Germany twice and France once.
A 1 litre bottle; the Our valley has long stretches with no shop.
whatCouldGoWrong: **The commuter peak.** Bike spaces on CFL trains into Luxembourg City between 07:00 and 09:00 disappear. Ride out of the capital rather than into it, or travel after 09:30.
**Rain in the Mullerthal.** Wet sandstone is genuinely slick and the gravel loops become unrideable. Swap to the Consdorf and Berdorf road circuit, which drains within the hour.
**A closed cellar.** Small Moselle growers open by appointment only outside July and August, and most shut entirely during harvest. Vinsmoselle's cooperative cellars keep regular hours as a fallback.
**Vianden's bed shortage.** The town has a few hundred beds and sells out for the medieval festival in early August. Diekirch and Bettel are 12 km away and always have space.
**An e-bike battery on the Our climb.** The 20 km rise to Vianden will drain a tired battery. Charge overnight, ride the first half in eco mode, and note that Rentabike stations have chargers.

trips.title: Gravel in the Codru: Seven Days Through Moldova's Wine Hills
trips.subRegion: Codru hills — Strășeni, Nisporeni, Călărași, Orhei

bestPeriod.window: the first three weeks of September — harvest, hard dry clay, and 25 °C instead of 35 °C
bestPeriod.avoid: March–April and November (clay tracks unrideable), and July–August (35 °C with no shade on the ridges)

accommodation.note: €190–€330 (€27–€47/night, village guesthouses with half board)

transport.note: €110–€230 (bike rental €90–€180 or your own bike's flight surcharge, plus rutieră bail-outs)

activities.note: €70–€130 (monastery donations, reserve visit, cellar tours, Orheiul Vechi)

profile.difficultyNote: Moderate

trips.gatewayAirport: Chișinău International (KIV), 13 km from town. Bring your own bike boxed if you can — rental stock in Moldova is thin and mostly hardtail MTB rather than gravel.
trips.summary: The Codru is not flat and Moldova is not a road-bike country. This is 370 km of ridge-and-valley on a 35–40 mm tyre: resurfaced asphalt for an hour, then a slab of cracked Soviet concrete, then eight kilometres of…
trips.hook: The Codru is not flat and Moldova is not a road-bike country. This is 370 km of ridge-and-valley on a 35–40 mm tyre: resurfaced asphalt for an hour, then a slab of cracked Soviet concrete, then eight kilometres of packed clay farm track between vineyards with a monastery at the end of it. Climbs come in twenty-minute bites and add up to nearly 5,000 metres. Village wells, dogs, plum orchards, and almost no other cyclists.

snapshot.Start / End: Chișinău → Chișinău (loop, ~370 km, ~4,800 m ascent)
snapshot.Getting there: Chișinău International (KIV), 13 km from town. Bring your own bike boxed if you can — rental stock in Moldova is thin and mostly hardtail MTB rather than gravel.

itinerary.title: Out of the capital, under it, and up
itinerary.morning: Leave Chișinău early on the northern exit towards Cricova; the first 8 km are urban and unpleasant, and after 07:30 they get worse. **Cricova** at 15 km — the 120 km cellar city, toured **by vehicle**, reservation-only, Matinal tour 250 MDL.
itinerary.afternoon: North-west on the R20 and then farm tracks through vineyards to **Strășeni**, the gateway town to the Codru. First real climb: the ridge out of the Ichel valley, 120 m in 2 km.
itinerary.evening: Strășeni is a working town, not a pretty one. Eat, buy tomorrow's water and food, and get the bike into a locked yard.

itinerary.title: Căpriana and the forest
itinerary.morning: Climb west into the **Codru forest** — hornbeam, oak and lime, closed canopy, and forest track that is fast when dry and greasy under leaf litter when not.
itinerary.afternoon: **Căpriana Monastery**, first documented in **1429** and the oldest in Moldova, restored in the 2000s: three churches, a walled compound, a spring, and a lot of Sunday visitors from the capital. Shoulders covered, and there is a shop selling monastery wine.
itinerary.evening: Down to **Lozova** at the reserve's edge. Village guesthouse, home cooking, and an early night — tomorrow is the biggest climbing day so far [VERIFY: current Căpriana monastery guesthouse and refectory arrangements].

itinerary.title: Reserve and the Hâncu ridge
itinerary.morning: The **Codru Nature Reserve** at Lozova: Moldova's oldest scientific reserve, with a natural history museum open daily 08:00–17:00. **Guided visits must be booked ahead** (tel 0237 47 386 / 0698 82 478) — it is not a walk-up, and the trails are not open access [VERIFY: current Codru reserve visit fee].
itinerary.afternoon: South-west on ridge track to **Hâncu Monastery** (Mănăstirea Hâncu, founded 1678) in its wooded fold — the descent to it is a 150 m drop on loose clay, so check your brakes at the top rather than halfway down.
itinerary.evening: North-west to **Nisporeni**, a district town with a hotel, a market and an ATM. Refill everything [VERIFY: current Nisporeni hotel rates and whether bike storage is indoors].

itinerary.title: The roof of Moldova
itinerary.morning: East to **Vărzărești**, whose monastery has a claim as one of the country's earliest foundations, then a long ridge line on farm track with the Prut plain visible to the west on a clear morning.
itinerary.afternoon: **Bălănești Hill (Dealul Bălănești)**, **430 m — the highest point in Moldova**, above Bălănești village. The final approach is a rutted field track; the summit is a mast and a marker, and the view over the Codru is genuinely worth the disappointment of the summit itself.
itinerary.evening: North-east down to **Călărași**, wine town and rail junction. This is the best-supplied stop after Chișinău — a proper supermarket, a bike-washable yard, and *rachiu* if you want it.

itinerary.title: Across to the Răut side
itinerary.morning: East on the R25 through orchard country. The concrete-slab sections start around here; ride the smoother wheel track and expect your hands to complain by lunch.
itinerary.afternoon: **Bahmut** and the long rolling transition out of the Codru proper — the hills lower, the tree cover thins, and the wind starts to matter more than the gradient.
itinerary.evening: **Ivancea**, and the **Balioz manor**, a restored 19th-century estate house holding a museum of Moldovan folk crafts, with a park you can lie down in [VERIFY: current Ivancea manor museum hours and entry].

itinerary.title: The Răut meander
itinerary.morning: Track north-east to the **Orheiul Vechi** reserve. The approach along the Răut, on clay above the river, is the single best hour of riding on this loop.
itinerary.afternoon: **Orheiul Vechi**: the cave monastery in the limestone spur above **Butuceni**, entry **20 MDL** adult / 10 MDL reduced, guide 200 MDL in Romanian or 300 MDL in English for up to ten people. Leave the bike at the guesthouse and walk the promontory.
itinerary.evening: Butuceni or **Trebujeni** guesthouse. Half board, house wine, and a sky with no light pollution in it.

itinerary.title: Home the fast way
itinerary.morning: Out along the river, then the climb onto the plateau at Furceni — 130 m, the last real effort of the week.
itinerary.afternoon: South-west on a mix of R-road asphalt and track through Bulăiești and Peresecina, joining the main road for the final approach to the city.
itinerary.evening: Into Chișinău on the northern boulevards. Clean the bike, then **Carpe Diem** or **Invino** for the Fetească Neagră you have been riding past all week.

accommodationStrategy.name: Lozova village guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: at the Codru reserve gate, so the guided reserve visit is a morning walk rather than a drive, with a locked yard for the bikes, an outside tap for the clay and a kitchen that will feed you at whatever hour you arrive.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 2–3 weeks ahead by phone; ask the host to confirm the reserve booking for you in Romanian.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel in Călărași
accommodationStrategy.description: the mid-trip reset — the only place between Chișinău and Orhei with a supermarket, an ATM, a pharmacy and enough hot water for two bikes and two riders. Secure ground-floor storage, and the rail line here if you truly need to abandon.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 1–2 weeks ahead; midweek availability is never a problem.

accommodationStrategy.name: Butuceni village guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: inside the Orheiul Vechi reserve, five minutes from the cave monastery path, with a yard, half board and the Belvedere platform for sunrise before the day-trip coaches arrive from the capital.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–4 weeks ahead — the village has a few dozen beds and Chișinău takes them at weekends.

logistics.connectivity: Moldova is **not** in EU roaming — buy an Orange or Moldcell SIM at KIV. Coverage on the ridges is good; it drops in the Codru forest valleys. Load offline maps and a GPX before you leave, because signposting on farm track is nil.
logistics.emergency: **112**, English usually available. Give a village name and direction, not a GPS string. There is no cycling-specific rescue; ambulances will not reach you on a field track, so ride out to a road before calling if you can.
logistics.weather: Rain is the trip's only real hazard. A summer thunderstorm turns 40% of a day's route into unrideable gumbo within twenty minutes and it stays that way for a day or more. Watch the forecast every evening and be willing to swap a track day for the parallel asphalt R-road.
logistics.bookingWindows: Codru reserve, Cricova and any winery visit need a phone call days ahead. Guesthouses 2–4 weeks in season. A rented gravel bike, several weeks.
logistics.money: Moldovan leu. Cards work in Chișinău, Călărași and Nisporeni; village guesthouses, wells, monastery shops and roadside sellers are **cash only**. Carry 2,000–3,000 MDL and keep small notes for the rutieră.
logistics.transportRules: Ride on the right, lights front and rear, and use a **hi-vis vest** — it is expected of cyclists on rural roads at dusk and drivers here overtake close. Village dogs and free-roaming livestock are on every unfenced road.
logistics.permits: No permit for ordinary roads or forest tracks. **The Codru scientific reserve is by prior arrangement only** — do not simply ride into it. Orheiul Vechi charges 20 MDL. Wild camping is legally grey and socially odd; every village has a bed.

proTips: **The dog technique, learned properly.** Village dogs chase wheels, not people. **Stop pedalling and dismount** — most break off immediately. Put the bike between you and the dog, keep walking at the same pace, do not run, do not shout high, and say ***"Marș!"*** low and flat, which is the word every Moldovan dog has heard. Cross to the far side of the road and keep going. A frame pump held loosely is a deterrent you rarely need to use.

**Village wells (*fântână*) — use them, with judgement.** Almost every crossroads has one, usually with a bucket and often a shared cup, and locals drink from them daily. But shallow wells in this farmland carry **nitrate from fertiliser and livestock**, which no filter or purification tablet removes and which boiling concentrates. Prefer a deep well in the village centre that people are actively using, ask *"Se poate bea?"*, and carry bottled water for the second half of a hot day.

**The rutieră is your bail-out — with conditions.** Minibuses run every district road to Chișinău. Bikes are **at the driver's discretion**, usually accepted for a small extra fare if the bus is not full, and your odds improve enormously if you **take the front wheel off before he looks at it**. Sprinter-type vans have no luggage bay, so a full bus is a straight no. Flag it down at a village stop and ask *"Se poate cu bicicleta?"* [VERIFY: current rutieră bicycle surcharge].
**Ride the track days early.** Clay holds dew until nine and heat-cracks by noon; the ridges are 8 °C hotter at 14:00 with no shade whatever. Leave at 06:30 and be finished by two.
**Lube the chain every single evening.** Loess dust is abrasive and strips lubricant in a day; a dry chain on a 900 m climbing day is how drivetrains die 60 km from the nearest replacement.

**Buy from the gate.** Small producers along the Codru sell at a third of restaurant prices, and a guesthouse will happily open a bottle you turn up with. Send anything serious home rather than carrying it over Bălănești Hill.

**Book one rest afternoon at Orheiul Vechi.** It is the only place on the loop worth a half-day off the bike, and arriving in the morning of Day 6 rather than the evening buys you the promontory in good light.

raw.Daily distance, ascent and surface split: **Day 1** Chișinău → Cricova → Strășeni, **40 km / +450 m** — 70% asphalt, 20% concrete slab, 10% clay track. **Day 2** Strășeni → Căpriana → Lozova, **45 km / +700 m** — 40% asphalt, 15% slab, 45% forest and farm track. **Day 3** Lozova → Codru reserve → Hâncu → Nisporeni, **55 km / +850 m** — 50% asphalt, 10% slab, 40% track. **Day 4** Nisporeni → Vărzărești → Bălănești Hill → Călărași, **60 km / +900 m** — 45% asphalt, 15% slab, 40% track. **Day 5** Călărași → Bahmut → Ivancea, **65 km / +750 m** — 60% asphalt, 20% slab, 20% track. **Day 6** Ivancea → Orheiul Vechi loop, **45 km / +550 m** — 40% asphalt, 10% slab, 50% track. **Day 7** Orheiul Vechi → Chișinău, **60 km / +600 m** — 65% asphalt, 15% slab, 20% track.
raw.This is a gravel trip, and only a gravel: **35–40 mm tyres minimum**, tubeless or with two spare tubes, and a frame with mud clearance. Moldovan farm track is fine-grained loess and clay: it is fast, hard and lovely when dry, and after rain it becomes ***gumbo*** — a sticky paste that packs solid between tyre and fork until the wheel stops turning and you carry the bike. A 28 mm road bike will get you between towns on asphalt and nowhere else. The **Codru is genuine ridge-and-valley terrain**, 200–430 m, and the climbing arrives as repeated 60–120 m ramps at 8–12% on loose surface — riders consistently underestimate it.
raw.Bike rental and logistics: Chișinău has a handful of bike shops and small tour operators renting mostly cross-country hardtails; a true gravel bike is hard to source and should be reserved weeks ahead by email. Assume you will need to bring your own pedals, saddle and shoes regardless [VERIFY: current Chișinău gravel-bike rental operators and daily rates].
raw.No bike shops outside Chișinău — plan fo: Once you leave the capital there is no spares network. Village hardware shops sell inner tubes for Soviet-era 28-inch wheels and nothing else. Carry: two tubes, tubeless plugs, a spare **derailleur hanger**, quick links, spare spokes, brake pads, a folding tyre, chain lube (the clay strips it), and a mini pump plus CO2. A broken hanger 60 km from Chișinău otherwise ends the trip.
raw.Bike-friendly accommodation features: Village *pensiuni* almost all have a locked yard, a shed or a *beci* (cellar) you can wheel a bike into, an outside tap for washing off clay, and a line to dry kit. Ask for *"un loc pentru bicicletă"* when booking; nobody will refuse.
raw.Trains and buses with a bike: Moldova's passenger rail network is minimal and not useful for this loop. The practical bail-out is the ***rutieră*** minibus — see below.

typeSpecific.surface: **Day 1** Chișinău → Cricova → Strășeni, **40 km / +450 m** — 70% asphalt, 20% concrete slab, 10% clay track. **Day 2** Strășeni → Căpriana → Lozova, **45 km / +700 m** — 40% asphalt, 15% slab, 45% forest and farm track. **Day 3** Lozova → Codru reserve → Hâncu → Nisporeni, **55 km / +850 m** — 50% asphalt, 10% slab, 40% track. **Day 4** Nisporeni → Vărzărești → Bălănești Hill → Călărași, **60 km / +900 m** — 45% asphalt, 15% slab, 40% track. **Day 5** Călărași → Bahmut → Ivancea, **65 km / +750 m** — 60% asphalt, 20% slab, 20% track. **Day 6** Ivancea → Orheiul Vechi loop, **45 km / +550 m** — 40% asphalt, 10% slab, 50% track. **Day 7** Orheiul Vechi → Chișinău, **60 km / +600 m** — 65% asphalt, 15% slab, 20% track.

trips.title: Kotor Serpentine & Lovćen: 25 Hairpins Above the Boka
trips.subRegion: Bay of Kotor, Lovćen NP & the Old Royal Capital

bestPeriod.window: Late April–mid-June & mid-September–late October
bestPeriod.avoid: July–August — 35 °C at sea level, cruise-ship coach convoys on the bay road, and the serpentine's daytime one-way restrictions at their tightest; December–February brings snow and ice above 1,000 m on Lovćen.
bestPeriod.raw: Late April–mid-June & mid-September–late October

accommodation.note: Kotor/Dobrota guesthouse €55–€95 pppn; one night in Njeguši or Cetinje €40–€60

food.note: Konoba mains €9–€16; Njeguši pršut-and-cheese board €12; coastal fish is double

transport.note: Airport transfer, Kamenari–Lepetane ferry, one cable-car lift, van recovery

activities.note: Road bike hire €180–€240/week, Lovćen NP entry, Mausoleum, Cetinje museums

profile.difficultyNote: 4/5 — five riding days between 800 m and 1,900 m of ascent, with one climb that gains nearly a kilometre of altitude in a single unbroken hour

trips.gatewayAirport: TIV Tivat — 25 min drive / 22 km ride to Kotor; PDG Podgorica 1 h 30 min; DBV Dubrovnik 2 h with a land border that can add 90 min in summer
trips.summary: This is a week built around one road. The old Austro-Hungarian carriage road from Kotor to Njeguši — the P1, the Kotor Serpentine, the Ladder of Cattaro's tarmac successor — stacks twenty-five numbered hairpins into a limestone wall and lifts you from the quay to a saddle at nearly 950 m without a single flat metre. Everything else in the week is arranged around that climb: a bay warm-up on the Perast–Risan shore, the high plateau of Lovćen NP and Njegoš's mausoleum, the imperial small-town calm of Cetinje, a gravel day into the Krivošije backcountry, a Vrmac ridge traverse, and a coastal spin down the Budva riviera. It suits climbers who are comfortable descending on narrow roads with hip-height stone parapets and, sometimes, none.

itinerary.title: Land at Tivat, ride the bay to Kotor
itinerary.morning: Collect the bike in Tivat or ride the 22 km shore road from the airport around the bay through Prčanj and Muo, with the walls of Kotor opening ahead. Traffic is heavy but slow.
itinerary.afternoon: Settle in Dobrota, then a flat spin north along the waterfront promenade to Ljuta and back — 16 km with almost no ascent, purely to check cleats, brakes and gearing before anything serious.
itinerary.evening: Konoba Ćatovića Mlini at Morinj, a restored watermill on the bay north of Kotor, for grilled fish and the house bread. Book a day ahead.
itinerary.dayStats: 38 km / 210 m ascent / 100% paved / airport-to-Kotor 22 km

itinerary.title: Perast, Risan and the Roman mosaics
itinerary.morning: North on the bay road to **Perast**, park the bike at the quay and take the shuttle boat to **Our Lady of the Rocks** — the artificial islet built on centuries of dropped stones. Climb the bell tower of St Nicholas for the strait view.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to **Risan** for the 2nd-century Roman villa mosaics, including the sleeping Hypnos, then loop back with the short climb to **Kostanjica**. Save the legs.
itinerary.evening: Back in Kotor, eat at Konoba Portun in the Old Town — black risotto and buzara. Walk the Sea Gate and the Square of Arms afterwards.
itinerary.dayStats: 46 km / 480 m ascent / 96% paved / Our Lady of the Rocks boat ≈€5 return

itinerary.title: The Serpentine: twenty-five hairpins to Njeguši
itinerary.morning: Leave Dobrota by 07:00. The climb starts at the Škaljari roundabout; hairpin 1 is signed within two kilometres. The gradient sits at 5–7% and never relents — pace it as an hour of steady tempo, not an effort. Fort Gorazda and the Ladder of Cattaro mule path cross the road twice.
itinerary.afternoon: Over the **Krstac saddle at 940 m** and down the far side into **Njeguši**, the Petrović dynasty's home village, for pršut air-dried in the mountain draught and Njeguški sir. Descend the serpentine mid-afternoon.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Galion, on the water below the walls, watching the light leave the cliff you climbed.
itinerary.dayStats: 44 km / 1,150 m ascent / 100% paved / P1 climb 16 km at 5.8%, max 11%, 25 hairpins

itinerary.title: Lovćen, the Mausoleum and down to Cetinje
itinerary.morning: The serpentine again, but this time through Njeguši and on into **Lovćen National Park**, climbing gently across karst pasture and black-pine forest to **Ivanova Korita (1,270 m)**.
itinerary.afternoon: The spur to the **Njegoš Mausoleum** car park at ≈1,570 m, then 461 steps on foot through the rock tunnel to Jezerski vrh (1,657 m) — Meštrović's granite Njegoš under a gold mosaic vault, and a view that on a clear day reaches the Albanian Alps. Long descent to **Cetinje (671 m)**.
itinerary.evening: Cetinje is a former royal capital of embassy villas and closed shutters. Eat at Kole for cicvara and priganice; the town is quiet by 22:00 and that is the point.
itinerary.dayStats: 62 km / 1,900 m ascent / 100% paved / high point 1,570 m ridden, 1,657 m walked / 461 steps

itinerary.title: Vrmac ridge and the Kamenari ferry
itinerary.morning: Roll the fast 30 km descent from Cetinje to Budva, then the coast to Tivat. Alternatively shuttle back to Kotor and start fresh.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb from Škaljari to **Trojica** and onto the **Vrmac military road** — graded limestone gravel along the whole ridge to **Fort Vrmac (785 m)**, an intact Austro-Hungarian work with the bay on one side and Tivat on the other. Descend to Gornja Lastva and Tivat, ride to Lepetane, take the **ferry to Kamenari**, and return along the north shore.
itinerary.evening: Konoba Feral in Herceg Novi if you extend, or back in Dobrota for grilled squid.
itinerary.dayStats: 58 km / 1,050 m ascent / 70% paved, 30% gravel / Vrmac climb 9.5 km at 7.9% / ferry €1 with a bike, 10 min

itinerary.title: Krivošije backcountry gravel
itinerary.morning: North to **Risan**, then up the Grahovo road's own serpentines into the **Krivošije** — a limestone plateau of sinkholes, abandoned Austro-Hungarian blockhouses and villages of four people. Traffic effectively stops after the first ten hairpins.
itinerary.afternoon: Gravel spurs around **Dragalj** and the Han Dragalj junction, then the open road to **Grahovo** if legs allow. Carry all your food and 2 litres of water — there is no shop between Risan and Grahovo you can rely on.
itinerary.evening: Return by the same descent, which is the finest unphotographed descent in Montenegro. Dinner at Konoba Akustik, Dobrota.
itinerary.dayStats: 74 km / 1,450 m ascent / 65% paved, 35% gravel / Risan climb 19 km at 4.6% / high point ≈900 m

itinerary.title: Budva riviera and out
itinerary.morning: Over the low Trojica pass to Budva and along the riviera to Sveti Stefan, Pržno and Rijeka Reževići — rolling, 4–8% pitches, sea on your left the whole way.
itinerary.afternoon: Turn at Petrovac, ride back to Tivat, wash and return the bike. Swim at Jaz if the water is warm enough.
itinerary.evening: Late flight from TIV, or a last dinner in Kotor's Old Town at Bastion.
itinerary.dayStats: 68 km / 900 m ascent / 100% paved / Kotor–Budva 22 km, Budva–Petrovac 18 km
itinerary.sleep: Airport-side Tivat room, or out on the evening flight

accommodationStrategy.name: Dobrota waterfront guesthouse
accommodationStrategy.description: The functional base for the whole week: ground-floor or courtyard bike storage, a tap and hose for salt and limestone dust, parking if you also have a car, and a flat 2 km promenade into the Old Town so you never carry a bike up steps. Roughly €55–€95 per room per night in shoulder season.

accommodationStrategy.name: A Njeguši village house
accommodationStrategy.description: Sleeping at the top of the serpentine flips the week: you descend to breakfast and climb home. Rooms are simple, heating matters even in May, and dinner is whatever the household is smoking. Around €40–€60 per room, cash. Worth one night to ride Lovćen on fresh legs.

accommodationStrategy.name: Small guesthouse, central Cetinje
accommodationStrategy.description: The right overnight for the Lovćen point-to-point, saving a 900 m re-climb at the end of the hardest day. Bikes go in a hallway or shed; ask explicitly. Cetinje is 40 minutes' descent from the coast and 10 °C cooler in June.

logistics.connectivity: 4G is strong through the bay, along the coast and in Cetinje; it thins on the Lovćen plateau and is genuinely absent in parts of the Krivošije around Dragalj. **Montenegro is outside EU roaming**, though EU-operator rates to the Western Balkans have been reduced by agreement — check your tariff or buy a local prepaid SIM (Telekom, One, m:tel) at Tivat airport for a few euro. Download offline maps for the whole Boka.
logistics.emergency: 112 works nationally; ambulance 124, police 122. Mountain rescue is coordinated through 112 and is thin on Lovćen — response to the plateau can take well over an hour. The nearest full hospital is Kotor General; serious trauma goes to Podgorica. **Montenegro is not in the EU and EHIC/GHIC do not apply** — carry travel insurance that names road cycling and repatriation.
logistics.weather: The bay is one of the wettest places in Europe — Crkvice, above Risan, records some of the continent's highest annual rainfall. Expect violent, short autumn downpours that make the serpentine's polished tarmac treacherous. The **bura** funnels down the mountain wall in winter and shoulder season and can gust hard at Krstac. Temperature drops 8–12 °C between Kotor quay and the Mausoleum: always carry a packable jacket and long fingers.
logistics.bookingWindows: Bay accommodation for June and September should be booked 6–10 weeks ahead; July–August, four months. Bikes at Bajković or 3E: 3–4 weeks in shoulder season. Ćatovića Mlini: a day or two. Nothing on Lovćen needs booking except a Njeguši room, which needs a phone call.
logistics.money: Montenegro uses the **euro unilaterally** without being in the eurozone or the EU. Cards are accepted in Kotor, Budva and Tivat; Njeguši households, mountain konobas, the Krivošije and small ferries are cash. Carry €50–€80 in small notes. Tipping is rounding up, 10% for a proper dinner.
logistics.transportRules: No road vignette in Montenegro; the Sozina tunnel toll (≈€3.50 for cars) is irrelevant here. **Bicycles are banned from Sozina and are a bad idea in the Vrmac road tunnel** — take the ridge or the ferry instead. Rental cars crossing to Croatia, Bosnia or Albania need a green card and written permission from the rental firm; expect a €30–€60 cross-border fee. The Kamenari–Lepetane ferry needs no booking.
logistics.permits: **Lovćen National Park** charges a modest per-person entry (a few euro) at the Ivanova Korita gate; the **Njegoš Mausoleum** is a separate ticket of roughly €5. Cyclists are frequently waved through the park gate but should carry cash. Drones require Civil Aviation Agency approval and are prohibited over the Mausoleum and the Kotor fortifications, which are UNESCO-listed. Wild camping in the national park is not permitted.
logistics.health: Tap water in Kotor, Cetinje and Njeguši is potable; assume nothing in the Krivošije. Ticks are present in Lovćen's pasture and forest edge April–October. The single biggest hazard is **descending traffic on the serpentine** — tour vans, hire cars on the wrong line, and drivers stopped mid-hairpin for photographs. Descend on the outside of your lane, cover the brakes, and use a loud rear light in the tunnels.

proTips: **Ride the serpentine uphill before 08:00 and downhill before 10:00.** In the summer season the P1 operates directional restrictions — descending traffic is barred through the middle of the day and ascending traffic in the late afternoon — precisely to stop the road gridlocking. Cyclists are not the target, but you do not want to be in the queue that results. Check the signs at the Škaljari roundabout on arrival.

**Count the hairpins.** They are numbered on small posts; if you lose count you have miscounted, because there are exactly 25 on the Kotor side. It is a genuinely useful pacing tool — a third of the climb is done by number 9.

**Use the Kotor Cable Car as a one-way lift** if you want the Lovćen plateau without the climb, or to salvage a day of bad legs. Bikes go in the gondolas for a supplement; it shuts in strong wind, so it is not a plan you can rely on.

**Buy pršut in Njeguši at a house, not a restaurant.** The village smokehouses sell whole and sliced; the mountain draught and the sea air are the entire point of the product and it is half the coastal price.
**Do the Krivošije day with 35 mm+ tyres and full food.** Between Risan and Grahovo you will pass more abandoned blockhouses than open shops. There is no water tap you can count on after Risan.

**Skip the Vrmac road tunnel on a bike.** It is unlit, has no walkway and carries fast traffic. The ridge gravel is the whole reason to be on Vrmac anyway, and the Lepetane ferry gets you home for a euro.
**Base in Dobrota, not inside the walls.** Kotor's Old Town is stairs, alleys and cruise-ship crowds from 09:00, and getting a bike in or out of it is a daily argument.
**Take a rear light for the serpentine even in daylight.** The short rock galleries near the top are unlit and drivers coming down out of the sun genuinely will not see you.
**Ride Lovćen on a Tuesday or Wednesday.** Cetinje and the Mausoleum absorb the coastal coach tours at weekends, and the plateau road is single-lane in places.

raw.Loop 1 — The Serpentine and Njeguši (Day: Kotor → P1 serpentine → Krstac saddle → Njeguši → back down. **44 km / 1,150 m ascent.** The out-and-back is the classic; the descent is the reason people come.
raw.Loop 2 — Lovćen crown (Day 4): Kotor → serpentine → Njeguši → Ivanova Korita → Njegoš Mausoleum car park → Cetinje. **62 km / 1,900 m ascent**, point-to-point, ending in Cetinje.
raw.Loop 3 — Vrmac ridge (Day 5): Kotor → Škaljari → Trojica → Vrmac military road → Fort Vrmac → Gornja Lastva → Tivat → Lepetane ferry → Kamenari → Kotor. **58 km / 1,050 m ascent.**
raw.Loop 4 — Krivošije gravel (Day 6): Risan → Krivošije serpentines → Dragalj → Grahovo → return. **74 km / 1,450 m ascent.**
raw.Kotor Serpentine (P1), Kotor → Krstac sa: ≈16 km, 930 m gained, **5.8% average**, ramps to **11%** on hairpins 18–24, summit **940 m**. Twenty-five numbered switchbacks, all paved, carriageway 3.5–5 m with passing bays. Roughly 300 m of unlit short tunnels/rock galleries near the top — carry a rear light.
raw.Krstac → Njeguši → Ivanova Korita: a further 18 km at **3–6%**, topping 1,270 m at Ivanova Korita, then the spur to the **Mausoleum car park at ≈1,570 m** — the last 4 km hold **7–9%**.
raw.Krivošije from Risan (toward Grahovo): ≈19 km, 880 m, **4.6% average**, max 9%, its own set of Austro-Hungarian hairpins and about a third the traffic of the Kotor side.
raw.Vrmac from Škaljari to Fort Vrmac: 9.5 km, 760 m, **7.9% average**, max 14% on the concrete ramps above Trojica; summit fort **785 m**.
raw.Week surface split: ≈78% paved (narrow, chip-sealed, no shoulder), 16% graded limestone gravel on the Vrmac military road and Krivošije spurs, 4% rough double-track around Dragalj, 2% cobbled village lane in Njeguši. A 28–32 mm tyre covers the road days; take 35–40 mm if you want the Krivošije and Vrmac days properly.
raw.Bike hire: **Bajković Bike** (bajkovicbike.com) rents from Kotor and Dobrota — city, trekking, MTB and e-bikes, roughly **€15–€25/day** for a hybrid and **€35–€45/day** e-bike, with weekly rates around €90–€180. **3E Travel** (3etravel.me) rents in both Kotor and Podgorica, which makes a Kotor-pick-up/Podgorica-drop feasible for a one-way finish — expect a **€30–€60 relocation charge**. **Montenegro Plus** (montenegroplus.me) supplies e-MTB and trekking fleets for bay tours. Genuine carbon road bikes with compact gearing are scarce: if you want 34×34 or lower for the Mausoleum spur, bring your own bike or reserve months ahead.
raw.Bike-friendly accommodation logistics: Nowhere in Kotor's walled Old Town has step-free bike access — it is all stairs and alleys, and the town gates close to vehicles. Sleep in **Dobrota**, along the waterfront north of the walls, where guesthouses have ground-floor rooms, gated courtyards and a hose. Confirm a locked indoor space in writing; cycle theft in the bay is real. Njeguši and Cetinje properties are simple houses with a shed or a hallway.
raw.Bikes on ferries and buses: The **Kamenari–Lepetane ferry** across the Verige strait runs 24 hours, every 15–20 minutes by day, crossing in about 10 minutes. A car is roughly **€5**; foot passengers cross free and **a bicycle is €1 or waved through**. No booking, no timetable to plan around — just ride on. Intercity buses (Blue Line, Autoboka) take a bike in the luggage bay for **€1–€2 at the driver's discretion**, wheel out, and refuse point-blank when the bay is full. There is no train in the Boka. The **Kotor Cable Car** (Dub, above Kotor, to Kuk at ≈1,350 m on the Lovćen plateau) carries bikes in the gondolas for a supplement and turns the serpentine into a descent-only day — around **€25 return, €17 one-way**, closed in high wind.

typeSpecific.surface: ≈78% paved (narrow, chip-sealed, no shoulder), 16% graded limestone gravel on the Vrmac military road and Krivošije spurs, 4% rough double-track around Dragalj, 2% cobbled village lane in Njeguši. A 28–32 mm tyre covers the road days; take 35–40 mm if you want the Krivošije and Vrmac days properly.
