trips.title: Paris by the Block — Seven Arrondissements, Seven Days

bestPeriod.note: Late September and early October give warm terraces and reopened kitchens after the August closures; May is beautiful and busy.

trips.gatewayAirport: Paris Charles de Gaulle (CDG)
trips.summary: Paris taken one walkable arrondissement at a time, with four days spent entirely off the museum spine and a market anchoring each district.
trips.hook: The mistake in Paris is treating it as a list of monuments joined by métro rides. Done properly it is a set of villages with numbers, and each one holds a morning market, a church, a park and a street of shops within about a kilometre. Three days here go to the great collections. The other four never leave the eastern and northern arrondissements, and they are the days where you eat best.

snapshot.Base(s): Paris, single base (11e Oberkampf or 3e Haut-Marais)
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 80–95 km on foot; flat except the Belleville, Ménilmontant and Butte-aux-Cailles slopes; 9 arrondissements
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to CDG, RER B to Gare du Nord in 30 min; or Eurostar and TGV into Gare du Nord, Gare de l'Est and Gare de Lyon
snapshot.Who It Suits: Second-and-beyond visitors, walkers, market shoppers; anyone who wants to stop queueing

itinerary.title: Le Marais: Place des Vosges to the Enfants Rouges
itinerary.morning: One block, all day. Start at Place des Vosges (completed 1612, the oldest planned square in Paris) under the arcades, then the Musée Carnavalet on rue de Sévigné — the city's own history museum in two hôtels particuliers, reopened in 2021 after five years of work. The permanent collection is free; only the temporary shows are ticketed.
itinerary.afternoon: The Musée Picasso in the Hôtel Salé (Jean Boullier de Bourges, 1659), timed entry, book two or three days ahead for weekends. Then walk rue des Rosiers, the Pletzl's old Jewish street, and the courtyards of the Hôtel de Soubise on rue des Francs-Bourgeois.
itinerary.evening: The Marché des Enfants Rouges on rue de Bretagne, opened in 1615 and the oldest covered market in Paris — a dozen food counters under one roof, open Tuesday to Sunday, closed Monday, and best at lunch rather than dinner. Eat there or on rue de Bretagne, then drink in the Haut-Marais around rue de Turenne.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km walked. Arrondissements: 3e, 4e. Ticket spend approx. €16–€24.

itinerary.title: Île de la Cité and the Latin Quarter
itinerary.morning: Sainte-Chapelle (consecrated 1248) first thing. The 09:00 and 09:15 slots are the ones worth having — the fifteen windows only work with morning light, and by midday the upper chapel is shoulder to shoulder. Slots release online roughly two months ahead and summer mornings go early; the combined Sainte-Chapelle plus Conciergerie ticket saves a few euros and lets you walk straight into the second site.
itinerary.afternoon: Notre-Dame, reopened in December 2024, is free but managed by timed reservation through its official app; a tranche of slots is released a couple of days in advance and a further tranche on the day, so check both. Then cross to the Left Bank: Shakespeare and Company, the Panthéon (Jacques-Germain Soufflot, completed 1790) with its Foucault pendulum and the roof colonnade, and the Arènes de Lutèce, a Roman amphitheatre hidden behind rue Monge.
itinerary.evening: Rue Mouffetard for the market street — stalls Tuesday to Sunday morning, restaurants at night. Dinner around the Contrescarpe end.
itinerary.dayStats: 10 km walked. Arrondissements: 1er, 4e, 5e. Ticket spend approx. €35–€45.

itinerary.title: Belleville and Ménilmontant, off the spine
itinerary.morning: Métro to Belleville and straight into the Marché de Belleville on the boulevard — Tuesday and Friday mornings, roughly 07:00 to 14:30, the cheapest and most crowded market in the city, North African and Chinese and Vietnamese all at once. Climb rue de Belleville, then Parc de Belleville for the view down the whole axis to the Eiffel Tower from the top terrace at 108 metres.
itinerary.afternoon: Père-Lachaise (Alexandre-Théodore Brongniart, 1804), the first garden cemetery in Europe: 44 hectares, cobbled avenues, and a free map at the conservation office by the Porte des Amandiers gate. Enter from the top at Gambetta and walk downhill. Then rue de Ménilmontant and the street art on rue Dénoyez.
itinerary.evening: Parc des Buttes-Chaumont (Jean-Charles Alphand, 1867), built on a former gypsum quarry with a suspension bridge by Gustave Eiffel's workshop and a temple on a rock island. Then dinner around rue Sainte-Marthe or the Belleville Chinese restaurants on rue de Belleville itself.
itinerary.dayStats: 11 km walked, 120 m of climbing. Arrondissements: 19e, 20e, 11e. Ticket spend approx. €0–€5.

itinerary.title: Saint-Germain, Orsay and the 7e
itinerary.morning: The Musée d'Orsay in Victor Laloux's 1900 railway station, converted by Gae Aulenti in 1986. Timed entry, and the honest advice is to book the last slots rather than the first: Thursday evening opening runs until 21:45 and the Impressionist floor at 20:00 is a different museum. Free on the first Sunday of the month, which is exactly when not to go.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk to the Musée Rodin on rue de Varenne, whose garden ticket alone is cheap and holds *The Thinker*, *The Gates of Hell* and a rose garden with chairs. Then across into Saint-Germain: Église Saint-Sulpice, the Cour du Commerce Saint-André, rue de Buci.
itinerary.evening: The Marché Raspail on boulevard Raspail is Tuesday, Friday and Sunday mornings only — the Sunday edition is entirely organic and famous — so if your day falls otherwise, eat instead on rue de Seine or rue des Canettes.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km walked. Arrondissements: 6e, 7e. Ticket spend approx. €30–€40.

itinerary.title: Canal Saint-Martin and the 10e, off the spine
itinerary.morning: Start at the Hôpital Saint-Louis (Claude Vellefaux, 1607), whose brick-and-stone courtyard is one of the oldest intact ensembles in Paris and is open to walk through. Then the Marché Couvert Saint-Quentin (1866), a cast-iron and glass hall on boulevard de Magenta, open Tuesday to Sunday.
itinerary.afternoon: The Canal Saint-Martin itself, cut 1802–1825: nine locks, two swing bridges, and iron footbridges over the whole run from the Bassin de la Villette down to the Bastille tunnel. Walk the towpath south, stopping on rue de Marseille, rue Beaurepaire and rue de Lancry for the shops. On Sundays the quays close to cars entirely.
itinerary.evening: Rue Oberkampf and rue Saint-Maur in the 11e for dinner and bars — this is where Paris in its thirties actually drinks. Passage Brady, the covered Indian arcade off rue du Faubourg-Saint-Denis, is the cheap alternative.
itinerary.dayStats: 10 km walked. Arrondissements: 10e, 11e. Ticket spend approx. €0–€8.

itinerary.title: Butte-aux-Cailles and the 13e, off the spine
itinerary.morning: Métro to Corvisart and climb into the Butte-aux-Cailles — a village of two-storey houses, cobbled lanes and an artesian well on place Paul-Verlaine that still runs 28°C water from 582 metres down. The Cité Florale and the rue Dieulafoy garden-city streets are five minutes south.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to the Manufacture des Gobelins on avenue des Gobelins, the state tapestry works operating on the site since the 17th century, with guided workshop visits on set days. Then the 13e's other face: the Olympiades slab towers of the 1970s and Paris's real Chinatown along avenue de Choisy and avenue d'Ivry, and the Bibliothèque nationale de France François-Mitterrand (Dominique Perrault, 1995), four glass towers around a sunken pine forest.
itinerary.evening: Eat Vietnamese or Chaozhou on avenue de Choisy, then walk a section of the Petite Ceinture — the abandoned 1860s belt railway, opened to the public in stretches, including a long green corridor in the 15e and shorter ones here.
itinerary.dayStats: 11 km walked, 60 m of climbing. Arrondissements: 13e. Ticket spend approx. €0–€15.

itinerary.title: Batignolles and the back of Montmartre, off the spine
itinerary.morning: The Marché Biologique des Batignolles on boulevard des Batignolles runs Saturday mornings, roughly 09:00 to 14:00, and is the northern counterpart to Raspail. Then Square des Batignolles, the Cité des Fleurs — a private lane of 1840s villas off rue de la Jonquière — and the shops on rue Legendre and rue des Dames.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk east into the 18e and take Montmartre backwards: up rue Lepic past the Moulin de la Galette, the Musée de Montmartre on rue Cortot with Renoir's garden and the studio Suzanne Valadon and Utrillo worked in, the Clos Montmartre vineyard, and rue Saint-Vincent. You will reach Sacré-Cœur from behind with no funicular queue and no staircase crowd.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in the 9e around rue des Martyrs — a food street of butchers, cheesemongers and bakeries by day and restaurants by night — then last drinks in South Pigalle.
itinerary.dayStats: 10 km walked, 130 m of climbing to the Butte. Arrondissements: 17e, 18e, 9e. Ticket spend approx. €12–€18.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Jules & Jim
accommodationStrategy.description: Three buildings around a courtyard in the Haut-Marais with a fire pit and a late bar. It puts Day 1 on your doorstep and is within walking distance of the canal and the République interchange, which feeds five métro lines. Rooms are small in the Parisian way; the courtyard is the point.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 10–12 weeks ahead.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Fabric
accommodationStrategy.description: A converted textile workshop off rue Oberkampf, which is the best-value dinner neighbourhood in central Paris and the natural base for the eastern half of this itinerary. Métro Saint-Ambroise and Parmentier are both two minutes away; Père-Lachaise and the canal are walkable.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 10 weeks ahead.

accommodationStrategy.name: An apartment in the 11e or 10e
accommodationStrategy.description: Seven days makes a kitchen worth having when the markets are half the itinerary. A registered short-let with a proper number displayed avoids the enforcement problems Paris has with unlicensed rentals. Ask which floor and whether there is a lift — Haussmann buildings routinely have six.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 10–12 weeks ahead.

logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European. French specifics: SAMU medical 15, police 17, fire 18, and 114 by SMS for the deaf and hard of hearing. Pharmacies with a green cross show the rotating night duty on the door.
logistics.bookingWindows: Sainte-Chapelle: slots open roughly 60 days out, morning slots go first, and the security queue on boulevard du Palais adds 20 minutes regardless. Notre-Dame: free reservation via the official app, a batch released about two days ahead just after midnight and more on the day. The Catacombes: timed, and typically sold out a week ahead. Musée d'Orsay and Musée Picasso: two to four days is usually enough except Saturdays.
logistics.money: Cards work everywhere including buses via contactless; markets often want cash, so carry €40–€60. Service is included by law — leaving a couple of euros is generous, not required. Say *bonjour* on entering any shop; skipping it is the single most common visitor error.

other.label: The pass decision
other.text: Since the 2025 fare reform Paris has one flat métro/RER fare across all zones — a single Métro-Train ticket at approx. €2.50, bus and tram at approx. €2.00, and a book of ten loaded onto a **Navigo Easy** card (card fee approx. €2) at roughly €19–€21. For a week of heavy use the **Navigo Découverte** weekly pass at approx. €32 plus a €5 card fee covers zones 1–5, which includes both airports, Versailles and Disneyland.

other.label: The Navigo trap
other.text: The weekly pass runs Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59 no matter which day you buy it. Arrive on a Thursday and you pay a full week for four days. You also need a passport-format photo glued to the card — bring one or use a station photo booth. Buy it Monday to Wednesday for the current week, Thursday onward for the next.

other.label: The Paris Visite trap
other.text: Sold hard at airport counters at roughly €17 for one day to €55 for five days in zones 1–3, with "discounts" that are typically a euro or two off things you were not going to do. It is worse value than a carnet on Navigo Easy in almost every scenario, and its zone 1–3 version excludes CDG.

other.label: Airport transfers
other.text: RER B to and from CDG costs approx. €13 as a single, or nothing extra if your Navigo Découverte covers the week. Orly is reachable by métro 14 for a similar flat fare. Never take an unbooked "taxi" tout at arrivals; the official taxi rank has a fixed flat fare to central Paris posted on a sign.

other.label: Opening-hour traps
other.text: The Louvre closes Tuesday; Orsay and Picasso close Monday; the Marché des Enfants Rouges closes Monday. Most street markets are morning only and finish by 14:30. Many independent restaurants close Sunday and Monday, and a substantial number shut for two or three weeks in August.

proTips: Book the last Orsay slot on a Thursday. The museum runs to 21:45 and the fifth-floor Impressionist rooms after 20:00 are as close to empty as they ever get.
Enter Père-Lachaise at Porte Gambetta, the top gate, and walk downhill to the Père-Lachaise métro. Everyone else does it the other way and climbs.
Buy at the market at the *end*, not the beginning. Belleville, Raspail and Batignolles all discount in the final half hour as stalls break down.
Rue des Martyrs in the 9e is a better food street than anything in the Marais and requires no ticket at all. Do it on the way to or from Montmartre.
The Musée Rodin sells a garden-only ticket for a few euros. On a warm afternoon it is the best-value seat in central Paris.
Climb the Panthéon's colonnade rather than the Eiffel Tower for the view: same rooftop panorama, a fraction of the queue, and open April to October.
Use the Vélib' bike share for the canal and Belleville days. A short-term pass costs a few euros and the towpath route from La Villette to Bastille is nearly all separated cycle track.

Approach Montmartre from the north-west via rue Lepic and rue Saint-Vincent. The staircase and funicular crowds all arrive from the south, and you get the vineyard and the Musée de Montmartre garden on the way.

typeSpecific.surface: approx. 80–95 km on foot; flat except the Belleville, Ménilmontant and Butte-aux-Cailles slopes; 9 arrondissements
typeSpecific.audience: Second-and-beyond visitors, walkers, market shoppers; anyone who wants to stop queueing

packingNotes: Shoes that will take 12 km a day on stone — this itinerary walks more than most Paris weeks.
One outfit that will not look out of place at dinner in the 6e; Paris is not formal but it is not casual either.
A folding market bag and a small cool bag if you are self-catering.
A passport-format photo for the Navigo Découverte card, or the coins for a station photo booth.
A compact umbrella; Paris rain is frequent, light and unpredictable in every month.
Layers for museum interiors and evening terraces, which diverge by ten degrees in spring and autumn.
A refillable bottle — the green Wallace fountains run drinking water from March to November, and there are Eau de Paris sparkling fountains in several parks.
A daypack small enough to keep on your front in the métro at rush hour; pickpocketing on lines 1, 4 and the RER B is organised and constant.
whatCouldGoWrong: **You buy the Navigo Découverte on a Friday.** It expires Sunday night. Fallback: buy a book of ten on a Navigo Easy card instead, which never expires and can be topped up, and switch to the weekly pass on Monday if you are still in town.

**Sainte-Chapelle morning slots are gone.** Fallback: take an afternoon slot but visit on the brightest day of your week, or go to the Conciergerie first and use the combined ticket; alternatively Saint-Séverin and Saint-Eustache have serious stained glass with no ticket at all.

**A transport strike.** Regular and usually announced days ahead. Fallback: Paris is walkable end to end in about two hours, Vélib' keeps running, and this itinerary is built on district blocks precisely so that a strike day costs you nothing — just do the nearest arrondissement.

**August closures.** Many of the best restaurants and some markets shut for weeks. Fallback: the covered markets — Enfants Rouges, Saint-Quentin — and the Chinatown restaurants of the 13e stay open through August almost without exception.

**Pickpocketed on the métro or at a museum entrance.** Fallback: carry nothing in a back pocket, keep the bag in front on lines 1 and 4, and if it happens, report at any commissariat for the insurance paperwork and cancel cards through your bank app immediately.

trips.title: Athens Beyond the Rock: Neighbourhoods, Marble and the Saronic Light

bestPeriod.window: Late March–mid May & late September–early November
bestPeriod.avoid: July–August — 38°C on unshaded marble, the Acropolis closes midday in heatwaves, and half of Exarchia and Pangrati shuts for August.
bestPeriod.raw: Late March–mid May & late September–early November

accommodation.note: Boutique double, per-person share, Koukaki or Plaka fringe

food.note: Mezedopoleio dinner €18–28, souvlaki €4–5, one €50 tasting dinner

transport.note: Airport metro both ways, 5-day urban ticket, Sounion coach or Aegina ferry

activities.note: Acropolis €30, Acropolis Museum, NAM, Benaki, Kerameikos

profile.difficultyNote: 2 — 8–11 km a day; Acropolis, Filopappou and Lycabettus supply about 300 m of ascent between them, all on polished, slippery rock.

trips.gatewayAirport: ATH — Eleftherios Venizelos; Metro Line 3 to Syntagma/Monastiraki 40 min (€9), X95 express bus to Syntagma 60–90 min (€5.50)
trips.summary: Most people give Athens 36 hours and see one hill. A week lets the city separate into its actual parts: the archaeological core, the 19th-century neoclassical spine from Syntagma to Omonia, and the living neighbourhoods — Koukaki, Pangrati, Exarchia, Kypseli — where Athenians actually eat, argue and drink. This itinerary front-loads the Acropolis at first slot, then spends real time on the things people skip: the National Archaeological Museum's bronzes, Byzantine Athens, the SNFCC's Renzo Piano park, and the Saronic light at Sounion. Walking is short-distance but relentlessly uphill and downhill on marble that has been polished by two thousand years of feet.

itinerary.title: Arrival, Plaka and the first hill
itinerary.morning: Metro Line 3 in from ATH (€9), drop bags in Koukaki, then coffee at **Little Tree Book Café**, Kavalloti 2, under the museum.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk **Anafiotika** — the Cycladic quarter built by 19th-century Naxian and Anafiot masons under the north cliff — then down through Plaka to the **Roman Agora** (€8) and the octagonal **Tower of the Winds** (Andronicus of Cyrrhus, 1st century BC).
itinerary.evening: Sunset from **Filopappou Hill** (free, 20 min up) for the profile view of the Acropolis, then dinner at **Karamanlidika tou Fani**, Sokratous 1, for cured meats and cheese; €22–30pp.
itinerary.dayStats: 6.3 km, 110 m ascent; Metro Line 3 €9; Roman Agora 08:00–17:00; Filopappou open dawn to dusk.

itinerary.title: Acropolis at 08:00, then the museum
itinerary.morning: **Acropolis, first slot at 08:00** (€30, hourly slots, 15 minutes' grace either side). Go up the west ramp, do the Propylaia and Parthenon before the 09:00 cohort arrives, then the Erechtheion and the Belvedere. Descend by the south slope past the **Theatre of Dionysus** and the **Odeon of Herodes Atticus** (both on the Acropolis ticket).
itinerary.afternoon: **Acropolis Museum** (€15 summer / €10 winter, Dionysiou Areopagitou 15) — the top-floor Parthenon gallery is oriented to the actual building, and the glass floor over the excavated Roman neighbourhood is the best part of the ground level.
itinerary.evening: **Mani Mani**, Falirou 10 (Peloponnesian Mani cooking, book 3–5 days, €30–40pp), then a rooftop drink at **Couleur Locale**, Normanou 3.
itinerary.dayStats: 7.1 km, 180 m ascent; Acropolis 08:00–20:00 summer, to 17:00 winter; Acropolis €30, museum €15.

itinerary.title: The Agora, Kerameikos and Psyrri
itinerary.morning: **Ancient Agora** (€10) — the reconstructed Stoa of Attalos museum and the Temple of Hephaestus, the best-preserved Doric temple anywhere, standing complete because it served as a church until 1834.
itinerary.afternoon: **Kerameikos** (€8) for the cemetery road and the Dipylon Gate, then walk Ermou east and into **Psyrri**'s workshop lanes and street art around Sarri and Agiou Dimitriou.
itinerary.evening: **Ta Karamanlidika** or, better, **Nolan**, Voulis 31–33 (Greek-Japanese, book 5–10 days, €40–55pp). Late drinks in **Monastiraki** at Six d.o.g.s, Avramiotou 6–8.
itinerary.dayStats: 8.4 km, 70 m ascent; Metro Line 1/3 Monastiraki; Agora 08:00–20:00 summer; Kerameikos 08:30–15:30 winter.

itinerary.title: Cape Sounion day trip
itinerary.morning: KTEL orange coach from **Mavromateon terminal** (Pedion tou Areos) down the Athens Riviera through Glyfada and Lagonisi, about 1h45, ~€7. Sit on the right for the Saronic coast.
itinerary.afternoon: **Temple of Poseidon at Sounion** (€10, 09:30 to sunset) — Doric, 444 BC, 15 columns standing on the headland; find Byron's carved signature on the north-east pillar. Lunch at **Syrtaki** below the site.
itinerary.evening: Stay for sunset over the Saronic — the reason the coach schedule exists — then the last bus back around 19:00–20:00. Late dinner in **Pangrati** at **Kalamaki Kolonaki** or **Colibri**, Empedokleous 9.
itinerary.dayStats: 3.5 km walked; coach 1h45 each way, ~€14 return; temple €10; sunset 19:00–20:30 in shoulder season.

itinerary.title: National Archaeological Museum, Exarchia, Kypseli
itinerary.morning: **National Archaeological Museum**, Patission 44 (€12 summer / €6 winter) — three hours minimum. The Mycenaean gold, the Antikythera Mechanism, the Artemision Bronze and the Cycladic figurines are the spine of the collection.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk into **Exarchia** for the bookshops around Themistokleous and Plateia Exarcheion, then up **Strefi Hill** for the city's least touristed view. Continue north to **Kypseli** and the restored **Dimotiki Agora Kypselis** market hall on Fokionos Negri.
itinerary.evening: **Oikonomou**, Troon 41 in Ano Petralona, a genuine old-school taverna with the day's pots on display; €18–25pp, cash preferred, no bookings.
itinerary.dayStats: 9.2 km, 90 m ascent; Metro Line 1 Victoria; NAM 13:00–20:00 Tue, 08:30–15:30 Wed–Mon in winter.

itinerary.title: Byzantine Athens, Benaki and the SNFCC
itinerary.morning: **Byzantine and Christian Museum**, Vasilissis Sofias 22 (€8) and the **Benaki Museum of Greek Culture**, Koumpari 1 (€12) — the Benaki's Ottoman-era interiors and the folk-costume floor are the underrated part.
itinerary.afternoon: Tram or the free SNFCC shuttle from Syntagma to the **Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center** at Kallithea (free) — Renzo Piano's canopy, the National Library reading room, the Great Lawn, and the lighthouse deck for the Saronic view.
itinerary.evening: Eat in Pangrati: **Seychelles** (Keramikou 49, Metaxourgeio) or **Mavro Provato**, Arrianou 31–33 in Pangrati, for mezedes; €25–35pp, book 3–5 days.
itinerary.dayStats: 7.6 km; tram line 6 or free shuttle; SNFCC grounds 06:00–00:00; Benaki closed Tuesdays.

itinerary.title: Market morning and departure
itinerary.morning: **Varvakios Agora** on Athinas — the meat and fish halls at 08:00, the spice and olive stalls opposite, and a bowl of *patsas* at **Papandreou** inside the hall if you have the nerve.
itinerary.afternoon: Souvlaki at **Kostas**, Pentelis 5 (one shop, one recipe, closes when the meat runs out), then Metro Line 3 from Syntagma to ATH.
itinerary.evening: Flight out.
itinerary.dayStats: 4.1 km; Varvakios 07:00–15:00, closed Sundays; airport metro 40 min, €9; allow 2 h at ATH.

accommodationStrategy.name: Coco-Mat Athens BC
accommodationStrategy.description: Two minutes from the Acropolis Museum on the quiet south side, so the 08:00 Acropolis slot is a ten-minute walk uphill. Rooftop with a direct Parthenon view, and Koukaki's café strip on Drakou is a better breakfast option than anything in Plaka. €150–210 double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Perianth Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: A restored 1930s modernist block with commissioned Greek art, a bakery downstairs and immediate access to Psyrri and the Agora. Right for a trip weighted toward evenings out. €180–250.

accommodationStrategy.name: Athens Was
accommodationStrategy.description: On the pedestrianised archaeological promenade, mid-century Greek design, rooms with sightlines to the south slope. Pricier per night but eliminates all transit on the two Acropolis days. €190–270.

logistics.connectivity: Full EU roaming and excellent 5G. The Metro has coverage throughout. Offline maps are worth having for Anafiotika, where the lanes defeat routing.
logistics.emergency: 112 unified; 166 ambulance, 100 police, 199 fire. Tourist police on 1571. Evangelismos is the central hospital with English-speaking staff. EU/EHIC applies.
logistics.weather: The **meltemi**, a dry northerly, blows July–September and can cancel Aegina hydrofoils at force 6+ while leaving the city merely windy. Heatwaves now routinely trigger **midday Acropolis closures (typically 12:00–17:00)** announced same-morning by the culture ministry. Winter brings brief but heavy rain and the marble becomes dangerously slick.
logistics.bookingWindows: Acropolis 1–3 weeks on hhticket.gr, choosing the 08:00 slot; Nolan and Seychelles 5–10 days; Mani Mani and Mavro Provato 3–5 days; Sounion coaches are walk-on; Aegina ferries book same-day except summer weekends.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are near-universal since the tax reforms, but neighbourhood tavernas, the Varvakios stalls and Kostas are cash-friendlier. Tip 5–10%. Bread and cover charges of €0.50–1.50 per head are standard and legal.
logistics.transportRules: Validate the Ath.ena ticket at the gate and again on buses; inspectors work Line 3 and the X95. **Urban tickets do not cover the airport** — you need the €9 airport product or the €20 three-day tourist ticket. Metro Line 3 to the airport runs only every 30 minutes, so check the departure board rather than assuming turn-up-and-go.
logistics.permits: Greece's **climate-resilience levy** replaced the old hotel tax: roughly €1.50–€10 per room per night depending on category and season, charged at the property. Archaeological sites ban tripods, drones and large bags; the Acropolis prohibits food and refuses entry with selfie sticks. Free-admission days at state sites fall on 6 March, 18 April, 18 May, the last weekend of September, 28 October, and the first Sunday of each month from November to March.
logistics.health: Tap water in central Athens is potable. Real hazards are heatstroke on unshaded sites, polished marble underfoot at the Acropolis and Filopappou, and pickpocketing on the Line 3 airport trains and around Omonia. Wear grip soles, not sandals, on the Rock.

proTips: Book the **08:00 Acropolis slot** and go straight to the Parthenon's east end. By 09:30 the cruise cohorts land and the Propylaia becomes a bottleneck for the rest of the day.

The old €30 five-day multi-site state ticket **was discontinued in April 2025** — do not buy a "combined ticket" from a reseller assuming it is the government one. Verify what a package actually includes before paying a premium.
In summer, check the culture ministry's morning announcement for **midday Acropolis heat closures** before setting out; the site now regularly shuts 12:00–17:00 on red-warning days.
State museums and sites are **free on the first Sunday of each month from November to March** — the National Archaeological Museum on such a day is the single best free thing in Europe.
Take the **X95 bus back to the airport**, not the metro, if your flight is before 07:00 or after 23:30 — it runs 24 hours and costs €5.50 against a €40 taxi.
Sit on the **right-hand side of the Sounion coach** going out for the coastal views, and buy the return leg ticket on arrival at Sounion so you are not standing in the sunset queue.
Eat in **Pangrati and Ano Petralona**, not Plaka: same money buys a different quality of meal, and the walk to Plateia Varnava from the Acropolis is twenty minutes downhill.
The **SNFCC runs a free shuttle bus** from Syntagma every half hour — it saves the tram and drops you at the canopy entrance.

raw.Walkable blocks: Plaka/Anafiotika (Adrianou → Mnisikleous → the Cycladic whitewashed lanes under the north cliff, 1.2 km, 60 m ascent); Monastiraki/Psyrri (Ermou → Agiou Dimitriou → Sarri, 1.3 km); Koukaki (Dimitrakopoulou → Drakou → Veikou, 1.1 km flat, the best café density in the city); Exarchia (Themistokleous → Plateia Exarcheion → Strefi Hill, 1.4 km with a 50 m climb); Pangrati (Plateia Varnava → Arhimidous → the First Cemetery, 1.5 km); Kypseli (Fokionos Negri's 900 m linear park).
raw.Transit pass: the **Ath.ena Ticket** paper card or Ath.ena Card holds a **90-minute ticket at €1.20**, a **24-hour at €4.10**, a **5-day at €8.20** (none of which cover the airport), and a **3-day tourist ticket at €20.00** which does include one airport return. Contactless bank cards now work at gates for full-fare products.
raw.Airport transfer: **Metro Line 3** (blue) ATH → Syntagma, ~40 min, **€9 single / €16 return valid 30 days**; trains every 30 min from 06:30 to 23:30. **X95 express bus** to Syntagma runs 24 hours at **€5.50** and takes 60–90 min depending on traffic. Taxi is a fixed €40 daytime / €55 night to the centre.
raw.Booking timeline: the **Acropolis operates hourly timed slots** with a per-slot visitor cap — book on the official **hhticket.gr** portal 1–3 weeks ahead in spring and autumn, and take the **08:00 first slot**. The old €30 five-day combined state ticket was **discontinued in April 2025**; the €30 now buys the Acropolis alone, and other sites are ticketed separately or through private multi-site passes. **Acropolis Museum** and the **National Archaeological Museum** are same-day. Restaurants: Nolan and Seychelles want 5–10 days.
raw.Architectural focal points: Iktinos and Kallikrates's Parthenon (447–432 BC) and its entasis and inward-leaning columns; Mnesikles's Propylaia; the Erechtheion's Caryatid porch (originals in the museum, casts in situ); Hadrian's Library and the Tower of the Winds in the Roman Agora; the 11th-century cloisonné brickwork of Kapnikarea and the Little Metropolis; the Athenian Trilogy on Panepistimiou by Theophil and Christian Hansen (1859–85); Bernard Tschumi's 2009 Acropolis Museum with its glass-floored excavation; Renzo Piano's 2016 SNFCC under its sliding canopy.
raw.Eating structure: mezedopoleia and *koutoukia* for dinner across Psyrri, Pangrati and Exarchia; souvlaki and *koulouri* by day; one modern kitchen mid-week; a market morning at Varvakios. Old-school tavernas take walk-ins; the modern set requires booking.
raw.Day trip: **Cape Sounion** by **KTEL Attikis orange coach** from Pedion tou Areos / Mavromateon terminal, about 1h45 along the coastal road, roughly €7 each way — or **Aegina** by Hellenic Seaways ferry from Piraeus, 40 min by Flying Dolphin (~€18) or 70 min conventional (~€10–14).

The old €30 five-day combined state ticket was **discontinued in April 2025**; the €30 now buys the Acropolis alone, and other sites are ticketed separately or through private multi-site passes. **Acropolis Museum** and the **National Archaeological Museum** are same-day. Restaurants: Nolan and Seychelles want 5–10 days.

sources.verified: Acropolis adult admission confirmed at **€30 year-round with hourly timed slots** and a 15-minute grace window either side; the official state reservation portal is **hhticket.gr**; the government's €30 five-day combined multi-site ticket was **discontinued in April 2025** and remaining "combo" products are private packages. OASA fares confirmed from the operator's own price list: 90-minute €1.20, 24-hour €4.10, 5-day €8.20, 3-day tourist ticket €20.00 including airport transfer, airport metro €9 one-way / €16 return valid 30 days, X95 express bus €5.50.
sources.confidenceNotes: Acropolis Museum (€15/€10) and National Archaeological Museum (€12/€6) seasonal pricing, and the individual site fees for the Ancient Agora, Kerameikos and Sounion, are 2025–26 figures revised each spring — re-verify. The Greek climate-resilience levy bands change by season and were last restructured in 2024; confirm current rates. KTEL Sounion coach fare and timetable, and Aegina ferry pricing, are approximate and seasonal. Summer midday Acropolis closures are weather-dependent and announced same-day. Restaurant booking lead times and Kostas's opening hours should be re-checked.

trips.title: Districts and Domes: Seven Days in Budapest, Pest Side First
trips.subRegion: Budapest — Pest districts V–IX, Buda I–II, XIII and Óbuda

bestPeriod.window: late April to early June, and the second half of September
bestPeriod.avoid: mid-July to mid-August (35 °C in the stone streets, Sziget week, half the good kitchens on holiday)

accommodation.note: €420–€700 (€60–€100/night, central district V–VII)

food.note: €210–€350 (€30–€50/day, one tasting menu included)

transport.note: €25–€45 (BKK 7-day travelcard plus a funicular and a boat)

activities.note: €130–€230 (Parliament, Opera, two baths, synagogue complex, Hospital in the Rock)

profile.difficultyNote: Easy

trips.gatewayAirport: Budapest Ferenc Liszt (BUD), 16 km out. Bus **100E** direct to Deák Ferenc tér, or **200E** to Kőbánya-Kispest and M3. Rail: Keleti and Nyugati stations, both on the metro.
trips.summary: Budapest rewards a week because it is really several cities stacked on one river — a Habsburg parade ground in District V, a French boulevard in VI, a bombed-and-reoccupied Jewish quarter in VII, an interwar Bauhaus…
trips.hook: Budapest rewards a week because it is really several cities stacked on one river — a Habsburg parade ground in District V, a French boulevard in VI, a bombed-and-reoccupied Jewish quarter in VII, an interwar Bauhaus grid in XIII, and a Roman town at the end of the tram line. Seven days lets you walk one district a day, book the baths at the right hour, and still eat properly. Flat, cheap by Western European standards, and best in shoulder season.

snapshot.Best period: Late April–early June, second half of September
snapshot.Start / End: Budapest → Budapest (single base, no relocation)
snapshot.Getting there: Budapest Ferenc Liszt (BUD), 16 km out. Bus **100E** direct to Deák Ferenc tér, or **200E** to Kőbánya-Kispest and M3. Rail: Keleti and Nyugati stations, both on the metro.

itinerary.title: District V, the parade ground
itinerary.morning: Start at **Szabadság tér**: the Hungarian National Bank, the former Stock Exchange, the Soviet war memorial and the contested 2014 occupation monument all facing each other across one square.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Parliament** on your booked slot — the Grand Staircase, the dome hall and the Holy Crown, 45 minutes, passport in hand. Then the riverbank and the **Shoes on the Danube Bank** memorial.
itinerary.evening: Coffee under the frescoes at **Café Gerbeaud** on Vörösmarty tér (since 1858), then dinner at **Hungarikum Bisztró** on Steindl Imre utca — small, permanently booked, and the best straightforward Hungarian cooking near the Parliament [VERIFY: current Hungarikum Bisztró reservation policy].

itinerary.title: Andrássy út and District VI
itinerary.morning: Walk Andrássy from Deák to Oktogon, then ride one stop on **M1** purely for the 1896 station tiling. Book a **State Opera House** tour or the evening performance.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to **Hősök tere** and the Városliget. Then **Széchenyi Baths** (1913) — the outdoor pools in the neo-baroque courtyard, best from 16:00 when the day crowds thin.
itinerary.evening: Eat at **Kispiac Bisztró** on Hold utca, a ten-table room doing duck, pickles and *főzelék* properly, then walk two minutes to see Lechner's **Postal Savings Bank** floodlit.

itinerary.title: District VII, the Jewish quarter
itinerary.morning: The **Dohány Street Synagogue** (Ludwig Förster, 1859), the largest in Europe, with the Jewish Museum and the Wallenberg memorial garden. Then the **Rumbach Sebestyén utca synagogue** (Otto Wagner, 1872, restored and reopened 2021).
itinerary.afternoon: The **Kazinczy utca Orthodox synagogue** (Löffler brothers, 1913), then the quarter's courtyards — Gozsdu udvar, the fire walls, the plaques.
itinerary.evening: **Gettó Gulyás** on Wesselényi utca for a proper goulash and *pörkölt* comparison, then **Szimpla Kert** on Kazinczy — arrive before 21:00 if you want to see the building rather than the crowd.

itinerary.title: Buda: Castle Hill and Rózsadomb
itinerary.morning: The **Budavári Sikló** funicular up from Clark Ádám tér, then **Matthias Church**, the **Fisherman's Bastion** at opening for the empty terraces, and the Hungarian National Gallery in the Castle.
itinerary.afternoon: **Hospital in the Rock** on Lovas út — the wartime and Cold War hospital and nuclear bunker cut into the Castle Hill karst, on a booked guided tour [VERIFY: current Sziklakórház tour price and languages].
itinerary.evening: Down to **II. Rózsadomb** for **Gül Baba türbéje**, the restored Ottoman dervish tomb on Mecset utca, then dinner at **Stand25 Bisztró** in the Hold utcai Vásárcsarnok back across the river [VERIFY: current Stand25 location and opening days].

itinerary.title: Districts VIII and IX
itinerary.morning: The **Palotanegyed**: Mikszáth Kálmán tér, Krúdy utca, the Wenckheim Palace that is now the Szabó Ervin Library — walk into the reading rooms on the upper floors, they are open to visitors.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Hungarian National Museum** on Múzeum körút, then south into **Ferencváros**: Ráday utca, and the **Great Market Hall** (Pecz Samu, 1897) at Fővám tér for paprika, *kolbász* and a first-floor *lángos*.
itinerary.evening: The **Bálna** on the embankment for the river view, then **Rosenstein** on Mosonyi utca near Keleti — Hungarian-Jewish home cooking, three decades in one family, and the single most reliable dinner in Budapest [VERIFY: current Rosenstein booking lead time].

itinerary.title: Óbuda and Aquincum
itinerary.morning: HÉV from Batthyány tér to **Óbuda**: the cobbled **Fő tér**, the Zichy Palace courtyard, the **Vasarely Museum** and the **Kiscelli Museum** in its ruined baroque church.
itinerary.afternoon: On to **Aquincum**, the civilian town of the Roman provincial capital of Pannonia Inferior — a full excavated street grid, mosaics and the reconstructed water organ, plus the military amphitheatre on the way back [VERIFY: current Aquincum Museum hours and winter closure].
itinerary.evening: Return south on the **D11/D12** boat if the timetable allows, and eat in **XIII. Újlipótváros** on Pozsonyi út, under the Bauhaus façades and among people who live here.

itinerary.title: Gellért, the market and the last walk
itinerary.morning: The **Gellért Baths** (1918) — Art Nouveau glass, Zsolnay tiling and the finest interior of any bath in the city. Go at opening; the thermal pools are quiet before 10:00.
itinerary.afternoon: Up the **Gellért-hegy** to the Citadella and the Liberty Statue for the whole-city panorama, then down over the **Szabadság híd** and one last circuit of the Great Market Hall.
itinerary.evening: **Bors GasztroBár** on Kazinczy utca for a soup and a baguette standing up — €5, twenty minutes, and better than half the sit-down restaurants — then Tram 2 north along the river with the Parliament lit up.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotels around Szabadság tér and Október 6. utca
accommodationStrategy.description: the quietest central address in the city. You are 10 minutes' walk from the Parliament, the Basilica and the Chain Bridge, on the M3 and the 2 tram, and out of the ruin-bar noise cone entirely.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4–8 weeks ahead; longer over Easter, the 20 August national holiday and New Year.

accommodationStrategy.name: Apartments off Pozsonyi út
accommodationStrategy.description: the best value-per-square-metre in Budapest, in a real residential district with 1930s modernist blocks, the 4/6 tram at the end of the street and a genuine neighbourhood food scene. Fifteen minutes to the Parliament on foot.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–6 weeks ahead direct or through the usual platforms; weekly rates are common [VERIFY: typical Újlipótváros weekly apartment rate].

accommodationStrategy.name: Small hotels on Mikszáth Kálmán tér
accommodationStrategy.description: cheapest of the three, walkable to the National Museum, Ráday utca and the Jewish quarter, and surrounded by student cafés rather than stag parties. Good if you want the VII district by night without sleeping in it.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 2–4 weeks ahead; the quarter is not yet a fixed point on the tourist map.

logistics.connectivity: Full 4G/5G everywhere including the whole metro network. Free wifi in the baths' lobbies, most cafés and BKK boats.
logistics.emergency: **112**. Pharmacies marked *gyógyszertár*; there are 24-hour ones near Nyugati and on Alkotás utca. Tap water is safe and good.
logistics.weather: Continental. April swings from 6 °C to 24 °C in a week; July and August routinely hold 33–36 °C with no breeze in the Pest grid, which is why the baths and the museums are the afternoon plan in summer. Winter is grey and damp rather than snowy.
logistics.bookingWindows: Parliament tours and Opera performances first, then the Hospital in the Rock, then baths and the synagogue complex. Restaurants: Rosenstein and Hungarikum Bisztró a week or two ahead, Kispiac and Stand25 a few days.
logistics.money: Hungary uses the **forint**, not the euro; roughly 395–400 HUF to €1 [VERIFY: current HUF/EUR rate]. Cards are accepted almost everywhere, including markets. **Never change money on the street**, and avoid the airport bureaux. ATMs: use bank-branded machines and always decline "dynamic currency conversion" — the machine's own rate is 8–12% worse. Tipping is 10%, and check whether *szervízdíj* is already on the bill.
logistics.transportRules: Buy the 7-day BKK travelcard at any metro window or the BudapestGO app. It does **not** cover the funicular, the Castle bus, or airport taxis. The HÉV suburban rail needs a supplement beyond the city boundary. Ride-hailing is Bolt; ordinary street taxis must be ordered by app or phone, not hailed.
logistics.permits: No permits needed. Alcohol is not permitted on public transport. The Dohány complex is closed Saturdays and on Jewish holidays. Photography is restricted inside the Parliament's Holy Crown hall, and drones are banned over the whole city centre.

proTips: **Book the Parliament tour the moment you fix your dates.** It is the one hard constraint in the week: timed, capped, ID-checked, and gone days in advance in May and September.

**Baths at opening or after 16:00.** Gellért at 09:00 is a cathedral with six people in it; Széchenyi at 13:00 is a swimming pool with six hundred. Pay the extra for a **cabin** rather than a locker — it is a private changing room and worth the difference.
**Ride M1 end to end for the price of one journey.** Vörösmarty tér to Mexikói út is five minutes and the best-preserved 1896 interior in Europe.

**Do the ruin bars at 19:00, not midnight.** Szimpla Kert is a genuinely extraordinary building and you cannot see any of it after 22:00. The Sunday morning **farmers' market inside Szimpla** is the other half of the trick — same courtyard, jam and cheese instead of beer.
**Cross the river by boat, not bridge, at least once.** BKK's D11/D12 are included in the travelcard and give you the Parliament from the water for nothing.
**Say *"Kérek egy…"* and *"Egészségedre!"*** Hungarian is not guessable from any other language you know, and two phrases correctly used change how you are treated in a *kifőzde*.

**Keep District VIII in reserve for a wet afternoon.** The Szabó Ervin Library's palace reading rooms are free to enter, warm, almost empty, and the finest interior in the city that nobody queues for.

Validate paper tickets; inspectors work the metro escalators relentlessly.

The **Budavári Sikló funicular** (1870) from Clark Ádám tér to the Castle, about 4,000 HUF (€10) return and not covered by the travelcard [VERIFY: current funicular fare]. BKK Danube boats **D11 and D12** run a weekday commuter service up and down the river and are included in the travelcard — a free river cruise if you time it [VERIFY: current D11/D12 season and timetable].

And the 1930s **Bauhaus** blocks of Újlipótváros around Pozsonyi út — flat façades, corner windows, a different century two tram stops from the Parliament.

trips.title: Naples Vertical: Spaccanapoli, Sanità and the Bay

bestPeriod.window: Late March–early June & late September–early November
bestPeriod.avoid: August — the city empties, half the good kitchens shut for *ferie*, and Pompeii is a furnace; mid-winter brings closed catacomb tours on wet days.
bestPeriod.raw: Late March–early June & late September–early November

accommodation.note: B&B or small hotel double, per-person share, Centro Storico or Chiaia

food.note: Pizza €6–9, trattoria lunch €15–22, one €45 seafood dinner

transport.note: Weekly TIC, Circumvesuviana returns, Alibus, funiculars

activities.note: MANN, Sansevero, catacombs, San Martino, Pompeii

profile.difficultyNote: 3 — 8–11 km a day with real vertical: the Pedamentina's 414 steps, Sanità's staircases, Vomero funicular alternatives.

trips.gatewayAirport: NAP — Naples Capodichino; Alibus to Piazza Garibaldi 15 min / Molo Beverello 25 min (€3 in advance, €4 on board), taxi flat fare ~€23–27
trips.summary: Naples is stacked — Greek grid under Roman market under Baroque church under a modern city that never stopped using any of it. This week works the vertical: the decumani of the Centro Storico and Spaccanapoli, the Rione Sanità's staircases and catacombs, Vomero above on the funicular, Chiaia along the water, and the Quartieri Spagnoli's grid climbing the hill behind Via Toledo. It is loud, dense, and rewards early starts and precise ticketing — Cappella Sansevero now admits nobody without a pre-booked slot. Pompeii or Herculaneum takes a day out on the Circumvesuviana. Come hungry and with proper shoes.

itinerary.title: Arrival and the decumani
itinerary.morning: Alibus in, drop bags, then straight onto **Via dei Tribunali**. Coffee at **Caffè Mexico**, Piazza Dante — order it *amaro* unless you want it sweet by default.
itinerary.afternoon: **Duomo di Napoli** and the Cappella del Tesoro di San Gennaro, then the Gothic **Santa Chiara** and its majolica cloister (€6). Walk Spaccanapoli west past **Gesù Nuovo**'s pyramid-faceted façade to Piazza del Gesù.
itinerary.evening: Pizza at **Pizzeria Gino e Toto Sorbillo**, Via dei Tribunali 32 — take a number from the man at the door, expect 30–60 min, €6–9. Digestivo on Piazza Bellini.
itinerary.dayStats: 5.4 km, 60 m ascent; Alibus €3; Santa Chiara cloister 09:30–17:30; pizza €6–9.
itinerary.sleep: Atelier Inès Suite Art, Vico dei Panettieri, Centro Storico.

itinerary.title: Cappella Sansevero and MANN
itinerary.morning: Pre-booked slot at **Cappella Sansevero**, Via Francesco de Sanctis 19 (€12, 09:00–19:00, closed Tuesdays, last entry 18:30). Twenty minutes is enough for the room; the *Cristo Velato* and the anatomical machines in the crypt are the two things to actually look at.
itinerary.afternoon: **MANN — Museo Archeologico Nazionale** (€22 including special exhibitions; closed Tuesdays). Prioritise the Farnese Bull and Hercules, the Pompeian mosaics including the Alexander Mosaic, and the Gabinetto Segreto.
itinerary.evening: **Trattoria da Nennella** in the Quartieri Spagnoli (Vico Lungo Teatro Nuovo 105) for the theatre and a €15 set menu, cash only, no bookings. Or **Tandem** on Via Paladino for ragù.
itinerary.dayStats: 7.0 km, 90 m ascent; Metro Line 1 to Museo; Sansevero €12, MANN €22; both closed Tue.

itinerary.title: Rione Sanità and the catacombs
itinerary.morning: Up through Porta San Gennaro into **Sanità**. **Palazzo dello Spagnolo** and **Palazzo Sanfelice** courtyards (free, look up at the open staircases), then the **Cimitero delle Fontanelle** ossuary (free, Via Fontanelle 80).
itinerary.afternoon: Guided tour of the **Catacombe di San Gennaro** (€14 combined with San Gaudioso, tours hourly 10:00–17:00, run by the Cooperativa La Paranza) — 4th-century frescoed loculi under the Basilica dell'Incoronata del Buon Consiglio.
itinerary.evening: **Concettina ai Tre Santi**, Via Arena della Sanità 7 — the neighbourhood's own pizzeria, book online or wait; €10–16. Sfogliatella from **Pasticceria Poppella** afterwards.
itinerary.dayStats: 8.3 km, 150 m ascent; catacombs €14, guided only; Fontanelle 10:00–17:00, closed Wed.

itinerary.title: Pompeii by Circumvesuviana
itinerary.morning: Porta Nolana 08:00 Circumvesuviana toward Sorrento, off at **Pompei Scavi–Villa dei Misteri**, ~36 min, ~€3.20. Enter at Porta Marina with a pre-booked ticket (€22 full site). Head first to the Villa dei Misteri at the far end while everyone else does the Forum.
itinerary.afternoon: Work back through the Casa del Fauno, the Lupanar, the Terme Stabiane and the Amphitheatre. Four hours minimum; there is no shade on the Via dell'Abbondanza.
itinerary.evening: Back by 18:00. Dinner at **Antica Osteria Pisano**, Piazzetta Crocelle ai Mannesi 1, for *pasta e patate con provola*; €20–28pp.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km walked at Pompeii; train 36 min each way, ~€6.40 return; site 09:00–19:00 April–October, last entry 17:30.

itinerary.title: Vomero, San Martino and the funiculars
itinerary.morning: **Funicolare Centrale** from Via Toledo to Piazza Fuga (covered by the TIC), then the **Certosa di San Martino** (€6) — Fanzago's marble church, the Presepe Cuciniello nativity, and the best single view of the bay from the Belvedere.
itinerary.afternoon: **Castel Sant'Elmo** (€5) above it, then descend the **Pedamentina di San Martino**, 414 steps down to Corso Vittorio Emanuele — 25 minutes and the finest walk in the city.
itinerary.evening: **Chiaia**: aperitivo on Piazza dei Martiri, then dinner at **Trattoria dell'Oca**, Via Santa Teresa a Chiaia 11 (book 3–5 days, €30–40pp).
itinerary.dayStats: 6.8 km plus 414 steps descent, 200 m net drop; funicular on TIC; Certosa 08:30–19:30, closed Wed.

itinerary.title: Royal Naples, the waterfront and Caravaggio
itinerary.morning: **Palazzo Reale** (€10), the Galleria Umberto I, and **Teatro di San Carlo** on a 30-minute guided visit (€9, hourly). Then **Castel Nuovo**'s Renaissance triumphal arch from Piazza Municipio.
itinerary.afternoon: Bus or walk the Lungomare Caracciolo to **Castel dell'Ovo** (free) and Borgo Marinari. Then **Pio Monte della Misericordia**, Via dei Tribunali 253 (€10), for Caravaggio's *Sette opere di Misericordia* still hanging in the chapel it was painted for.
itinerary.evening: Seafood at **Ristorante Zi' Teresa** on Borgo Marinari, or fried classics standing at **Friggitoria Vomero**. €25–45pp.
itinerary.dayStats: 9.1 km, flat; Palazzo Reale 09:00–20:00, closed Wed; Pio Monte 09:00–18:00.

itinerary.title: Underground and departure
itinerary.morning: **Napoli Sotterranea**, Piazza San Gaetano 68 (€12, guided, hourly) — Greek cisterns, Roman theatre remains under an apartment, and WWII shelters, 90 minutes.
itinerary.afternoon: Last pizza at **L'Antica Pizzeria da Michele**, Via Cesare Sersale 1 (two toppings only, €5–6, take a ticket), then Alibus from Piazza Garibaldi to NAP.
itinerary.evening: Flight out.
itinerary.dayStats: 4.2 km; Sotterranea tours on the hour; Alibus 15 min from Garibaldi; allow 2 h at NAP.

accommodationStrategy.name: Atelier Inès Suite Art
accommodationStrategy.description: Four rooms inside the decumani grid, thirty seconds from Spaccanapoli, so the 09:00 Sansevero slot is a walk not a metro ride. Soundproofed windows matter here more than anywhere: ask for a courtyard-facing room. €110–160 double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Casa D'Anna
accommodationStrategy.description: A frescoed apartment above Sanità with a library, a terrace and hosts who know the catacomb schedule. Fifteen minutes' downhill walk to the Duomo, and it puts you inside the neighbourhood rather than visiting it. €120–170.

accommodationStrategy.name: Grand Hotel Parker's
accommodationStrategy.description: The 1870 grande dame with a rooftop restaurant over the bay, on the funicular line and away from the Centro Storico's night noise. Worth it if you want quiet and a car-accessible entrance. €200–300.

logistics.connectivity: Full EU roaming, good 4G/5G; signal drops entirely in the catacombs, Fontanelle and Napoli Sotterranea. Download offline maps for Sanità, where the alley network defeats GPS.
logistics.emergency: 112 unified emergency number; 118 direct for ambulance. Ospedale Cardarelli and Pellegrini are the central ERs. EU/EHIC applies.
logistics.weather: Autumn *acqua alta* rain events flood the lower Centro Storico streets in minutes and can close Pompeii's outer insulae. Summer humidity off the gulf makes 33°C feel like 40°C on the Via dell'Abbondanza.
logistics.bookingWindows: Cappella Sansevero is booking-only, released 60 days ahead with a second drop two days before. Catacombe di San Gennaro 3–7 days. Pompeii 2–5 days on pompeiisites.org. Teatro di San Carlo tours 2–3 days. Restaurants: 50 Kalò and dell'Oca 3–5 days; Michele, Sorbillo and Nennella take no bookings at all.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are now widely accepted but Nennella, Fontanelle offerings, and many *friggitorie* remain cash. Coperto of €1.50–3 is normal; service is not usually added, round up.
logistics.transportRules: Validate the TIC in the machine at every entry, including funiculars — inspectors are frequent on Line 1. Circumvesuviana tickets are separate from the city TIC unless you hold a regional UnicoCampania fare. The Campania ArteCard 3-day (about €32) bundles regional transport with two free museum entries and is worth it if you do Pompeii plus MANN plus the Certosa.
logistics.permits: Naples tourist tax runs roughly €1.50–€5 per person per night by accommodation category, paid on site. Pompeii bans backpacks over 30x30x15 cm — use the free Porta Marina deposit. Drones are banned over all archaeological parks.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable and comes from the Serino aqueduct. Traffic is the real risk — scooters treat pedestrian crossings as advisory; cross with locals. Watch phones on Via Toledo and the Circumvesuviana, which is genuinely the least secure transport in the region.

proTips: Book **Cappella Sansevero for 09:00 on the day it opens after a Tuesday closure** — the room holds few people and the first slot is the only quiet one.
At Pompeii, walk **west to the Villa dei Misteri first** and reverse the standard flow; you will have the frescoes to yourself for twenty minutes while the crowd fills the Forum.
Take the **Circumvesuviana from Porta Nolana, not Garibaldi** — it is the line's origin station, so you board an empty train and get a seat for the 36 minutes.
The **Pedamentina di San Martino** should be walked downhill only: 414 steps with the whole bay in front of you, and it deposits you at Corso Vittorio Emanuele for the walk into Chiaia.
For pizza without the two-hour Sorbillo wait, go to **Da Attilio** in the Pignasecca or **Concettina ai Tre Santi** in Sanità at 12:30 — same quality, local queue.
The **Cooperativa La Paranza** ticket bundles San Gennaro and San Gaudioso catacombs; the guides are Sanità residents and the money funds the neighbourhood, which is the whole point of the project.
Buy the **Alibus ticket at a tabaccheria before boarding** — €3 instead of €4, and the driver often has no change.

Naples closes on a rota: Sansevero and MANN on **Tuesday**, Certosa and Palazzo Reale on **Wednesday**, Fontanelle on **Wednesday**. Plan Tuesday for Sanità and Wednesday for the Centro Storico churches.

raw.Walkable blocks: Centro Storico (Via dei Tribunali → Via San Gregorio Armeno → Spaccanapoli/Via Benedetto Croce, a 1.6 km cross of Greek decumani); Sanità (Piazza Cavour → Via Sanità → Palazzo dello Spagnolo → Catacombe di San Gennaro, 1.5 km with 70 m ascent); Quartieri Spagnoli (Via Toledo → Vico Lungo del Gelso, 900 m of grid on a 12% slope); Chiaia (Piazza dei Martiri → Via Chiaia → Lungomare Caracciolo, 2.1 km flat); Vomero (Piazza Vanvitelli → Via Scarlatti → Certosa di San Martino, 1.2 km).
raw.Transit pass: the **TIC** integrated ticket covers ANM metro, buses, funiculars and EAV lines inside the city — around €1.50 for 90 minutes, €4.50 daily, €15.80 weekly. Cheaper ANM-only singles exist from about €1.00 but do not cover regional trains.
raw.Airport transfer: **Alibus** (ANM) Capodichino → Piazza Garibaldi → Piazza Municipio/Molo Beverello, every 20–25 min, €3 bought in advance at a tabaccheria or €4 from the driver, valid 90 minutes. The taxi flat fare to the centre is posted at the rank.
raw.Booking timeline: **Cappella Sansevero** — mandatory advance booking on ticket.museosansevero.it; slots open 60 days out with a second release two days before, and the Veiled Christ hours sell out weeks ahead in spring. **Catacombe di San Gennaro** — guided-only, book 3–7 days on catacombedinapoli.it. **Pompeii** — book 2–5 days on ticketing.colosseo-style official portal (pompeiisites.org). **MANN** and **Certosa** accept same-day.
raw.Architectural focal points: the Greek-Roman street grid still legible in the decumani; Sanmartino's *Cristo Velato* (1753) and Queirolo's *Disinganno* net in Cappella Sansevero; Ferdinando Sanfelice's double-flight *scala aperta* at Palazzo dello Spagnolo (1738), the Neapolitan Baroque staircase perfected; Cosimo Fanzago's inlaid marble in the Certosa di San Martino; Gae Aulenti's Museo metro station and the Toledo station by Óscar Tusquets Blanca.
raw.Eating structure: pizzerie for lunch (€6–9 and a queue), trattorie for dinner in Sanità and Chiaia, *friggitorie* between. Reservation reality: Michele and Da Attilio take numbers not bookings; 50 Kalò and Sud take reservations.
raw.Day trip: **Pompeii** on the **Circumvesuviana Naples–Sorrento line** from Napoli Porta Nolana/Garibaldi to Pompei Scavi–Villa dei Misteri, ~36 min, roughly €3.20 each way; Herculaneum (Ercolano Scavi) is ~20 min and about €2.50.
