trips.title: Two Ends of a Long Country: Bratislava and Košice in a Split Week
trips.subRegion: Bratislava (Staré Mesto, Petržalka, Devín) and Košice (Hlavná, Spiš)

bestPeriod.window: mid-May to late June, and September — terrace weather, no August closures, Košice before the student term crush
bestPeriod.avoid: late December (Bratislava's markets are lovely and the hotel rates are not) and January–February fog on the Danube

accommodation.note: €350–€630 (€50–€90/night; Košice is materially cheaper than Bratislava)

food.note: €175–€280 (€25–€40/day — Slovak restaurant prices remain low outside the Bratislava tourist core)

transport.note: €90–€150 (Vienna airport bus, the Bratislava–Košice IC train, two city transport passes)

activities.note: €90–€170 (castles, museums, Spiš, the Gold Treasure)

profile.difficultyNote: Easy

trips.gatewayAirport: **Fly to Vienna (VIE), not Bratislava.** The airport bus to Bratislava takes about an hour and runs many times a day, and Vienna's route network is incomparably better than BTS's. Košice (KSC) has flights to Vienna, Prague, Warsaw, London and Bratislava.
languages: Hungarian (widely in the east and the south)
trips.summary: Slovakia is 430 km wide and its two cities have almost nothing in common. Bratislava is a Habsburg river town wedged against two borders, with a coronation cathedral, a Secession church the colour of a swimming pool,…
trips.hook: Slovakia is 430 km wide and its two cities have almost nothing in common. Bratislava is a Habsburg river town wedged against two borders, with a coronation cathedral, a Secession church the colour of a swimming pool, and Europe's densest concrete suburb across the Danube. Košice is a Gothic east-Slovak capital built along one enormous elongated square, with the easternmost Gothic cathedral in Europe at the top of it. Between them: a five-and-a-half-hour train and an entirely different country.

snapshot.Start / End: Bratislava (3 nights) → Košice (3 nights), fly out of Košice or return by train
snapshot.Getting there: **Fly to Vienna (VIE), not Bratislava.** The airport bus to Bratislava takes about an hour and runs many times a day, and Vienna's route network is incomparably better than BTS's. Košice (KSC) has flights to Vienna, Prague, Warsaw, London and Bratislava.

itinerary.title: Arrival and the Staré Mesto
itinerary.morning: Land at Vienna, take the airport coach to Bratislava — about an hour, several operators, arrivals at Most SNP or the main bus station [VERIFY: current Vienna airport–Bratislava coach fare and frequency]. Drop bags, buy an IDS BK multi-day pass.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk in through **Michael's Gate** and down Michalská to **Hlavné námestie** — the Roland Fountain, the Old Town Hall, and the French soldier leaning on the bench. Then the **Primate's Palace**, for the Hall of Mirrors and the six English **Mortlake tapestries** telling the story of Hero and Leander, found walled up in 1903 [VERIFY: current Primate's Palace hours and ticket].
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Modrá Hviezda** on Beblavého, on the climb to the castle — game, venison, dark beer, and the best traditional table in the old town.

itinerary.title: The Blue Church, the castle, the bridge
itinerary.morning: The **Blue Church** on Bezručova — Lechner's Church of St Elizabeth, 1913, blue from the plaster to the roof tiles to the pews. Opening is tied to the Mass schedule, so check the parish board and go early [VERIFY: current visiting hours outside services].
itinerary.afternoon: Up to **Bratislava Castle**, rebuilt after its 1811 fire and 20th-century ruin, housing the **Slovak National Museum**'s history exhibition and a terrace over the Danube, Austria and Hungary at once.
itinerary.evening: Across the **Most SNP** to the **UFO** observation deck on its single pylon, 95 m up, for the sunset over Petržalka and the river. Then back for beer at **Bratislavský meštiansky pivovar** on Drevená [VERIFY: current UFO deck admission].

itinerary.title: Petržalka, Slavín and Devín
itinerary.morning: **Petržalka**, seriously and not as a joke: built 1973–85, around 100,000 people in prefabricated *paneláky*, and by population density **the densest housing district in Central Europe**. Walk the Chorvátske rameno waterway, look at the colour repainting and the mature trees, and note that it works — full services, a tram-line extension, and low crime. It is the most instructive hour in the city.
itinerary.afternoon: Back over the river to **Slavín**, the Soviet war memorial and cemetery on the hill above the embassy quarter — 6,845 Red Army dead from the 1945 battle for the city, and the best panorama in Bratislava.
itinerary.evening: Bus 29 to **Devín**, the castle on the cliff at the **Morava–Danube confluence**, a Great Moravian stronghold and later a hard Iron Curtain frontier. Dinner back in town at the **Slovak Pub** on Obchodná — *bryndzové halušky*, *pirohy*, long wooden tables.

itinerary.title: East, by train
itinerary.morning: The **IC to Košice** from Bratislava hlavná stanica. Watch the country change: Danubian lowland, then the Váh valley, then the Tatras on the northern horizon around Poprad, then the eastern hills.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive Košice and walk straight out onto **Hlavná ulica**. Get your bearings around the **singing fountain** and its adjacent musical clock, in the park in front of the cathedral.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Med Malina** on Hlavná — Slovak and Polish country cooking in a cellar, and the most reliably good meal in the city.

itinerary.title: The Gothic day
itinerary.morning: The **Cathedral of St Elisabeth**, begun around 1378: **the largest church in Slovakia** and **the easternmost Gothic cathedral in Europe**, with Rákóczi's crypt below and a north tower you can climb. Next door, St Michael's Chapel and the Urban Tower.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Lower Gate (Dolná brána)** — an archaeological undercroft beneath Hlavná preserving the medieval city gate, bastion and waterway, entered from the street. Then **Miklušova väznica**, the Miklós Prison, a pair of 15th-century houses converted into a jail and now a museum with the cells and torture chamber intact [VERIFY: current Lower Gate and Miklušova väznica hours and tickets].
itinerary.evening: **Rosto** for grilled meat and a good wine list. Slovak wine from the Tokaj slopes on the Hungarian border is the local pour and worth ordering.

itinerary.title: Spiš Castle and Levoča
itinerary.morning: East Slovak Museum first, if you have not yet: the **Košice Gold Treasure** — 2,920 gold coins, three gold medals and a Renaissance chain, walled up in the 17th century and found by chance in 1935, the largest hoard of its kind in Europe [VERIFY: current East Slovak Museum hours and Gold Treasure display].
itinerary.afternoon: Then west by train or car to **Spiš Castle (Spišský hrad)** — UNESCO-listed, and **one of the largest castle complexes in Central Europe** at over four hectares, standing on a travertine hill with nothing around it. Pair it with **Levoča**, the walled Spiš town whose Church of St James holds the world's tallest late-Gothic wooden altarpiece, carved by Master Pavol around 1517. *(Alternative: the **Slovak Karst** caves — Domica, Gombasek, Ochtinská Aragonite — also UNESCO, and closer.)*
itinerary.evening: Back to Košice. A late dinner at **Villa Cassa**, the city's most serious kitchen, in a restored townhouse.
itinerary.dayStats: day trip, ~2 h each way

itinerary.title: The last of Košice
itinerary.morning: The **Kunsthalle / Hala umenia** in the converted 1960s swimming hall on Rumanova — Slovakia's first purpose-built contemporary art institution outside Bratislava, and a good corrective to a week of Gothic.
itinerary.afternoon: Hlavná's courtyards, the Executioner's Bastion, the State Theatre, and the shops on Mlynská. Buy Slovak Tokaj and *bryndza* to take home.
itinerary.evening: Fly out of Košice (KSC), or take the night or evening IC back west. Košice airport is 6 km from the centre and the taxi is ten minutes.

accommodationStrategy.name: A hotel on Panská or Ventúrska
accommodationStrategy.description: puts you inside the pedestrian core, so all three Bratislava days start on foot and the airport coach drop at Most SNP is a five-minute walk. The trade-off is Friday and Saturday night noise — ask for a courtyard room.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4–6 weeks ahead; Bratislava rates spike for Vienna-overflow weekends [VERIFY: current nightly rates].

accommodationStrategy.name: A guesthouse or apartment near Šafárikovo námestie
accommodationStrategy.description: the cheaper, quieter alternative ten minutes from Hlavné námestie, with a tram stop, the Blue Church five minutes away and the Danube embankment at the end of the street. Better value than the old-town core by a third.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–4 weeks ahead on any platform.

accommodationStrategy.name: A hotel on or just off Hlavná
accommodationStrategy.description: everything in Košice is on this one square, so anywhere on it removes transport from the equation entirely; the station is a ten-minute walk east for the Spiš day trip. Košice room rates run well below Bratislava's for the same standard.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 2–3 weeks ahead, except during the Košice Peace Marathon weekend in early October, when the city fills.

logistics.connectivity: Excellent 4G/5G in both cities and on the IC train. Free wi-fi in most cafés and on many DPB and DPMK vehicles.
logistics.emergency: **112**. Pharmacies are *lekáreň*; each city has a rotating night duty pharmacy posted on the door.
logistics.weather: Bratislava is Pannonian — hot summers, humid, with real thunderstorms; Košice sits lower and further east and gets colder winters and drier summers. Winter fog on the Danube can close the UFO deck's views for days.
logistics.bookingWindows: Hotels 2–6 weeks. The Bratislava–Košice IC seat 1–2 weeks. Slovak Philharmonic and Slovak National Theatre 2–4 weeks. Everything else takes walk-ins.
logistics.money: **Slovakia uses the euro**, and card acceptance is near-universal in both cities, including on ticket machines and in most restaurants. Carry €40–€60 in cash for market stalls, church donation boxes and the smaller Spiš-area sites.
logistics.transportRules: IDS BK and DPMK tickets must be **validated on boarding** — inspectors are frequent and the fine is immediate and cash-or-card on the spot. Luggage over a certain size needs its own ticket on Bratislava transport. The **Vienna airport coach** is the better arrival than BTS; it is also the better departure, running through the night.
logistics.permits: No permits needed. Photography is restricted inside the Blue Church during services and in parts of the East Slovak Museum's treasury. Drones are prohibited over both city centres and over Spiš Castle.

proTips: **Fly to Vienna.** The coach to Bratislava takes an hour and costs less than most airport transfers, and Vienna offers ten times the route choice. Book the return leg with enough slack for a border-queue delay.
Visit the **Blue Church at 08:00 on a weekday**, before the tour groups and while the low light is coming through the east windows. It is a parish church first and a monument second.
Give **Petržalka** two hours and cross on foot over the Most SNP or the Starý most. Understanding it is the difference between having seen Bratislava and having seen its postcard.
Take the **IC east on a weekday morning** and buy the seat reservation online; the Friday-afternoon service is full of students going home and there is no standing room worth having for five hours.
Eat off Hlavná in Košice, not on it. Terraces on the square carry a premium; the same kitchens' side-street rooms are 20–30% cheaper.
Do **Spiš Castle before 10:00 or after 16:00** in high summer — it is fully exposed, there is no shade on the upper ward, and the mid-afternoon heat on that travertine hill is punishing.
Learn *"Prosím si..."* (I'd like...) and *"Zaplatím, prosím"* (the bill, please). Slovak service warms noticeably to the attempt, and in Košice a *"köszönöm"* also lands well.

raw.Walkable blocks — Bratislava: The **Staré Mesto** is small enough to cross in fifteen minutes: **Michalská and Ventúrska** (the axis through Michael's Gate, the only surviving city gate), **Hlavné námestie** and **Františkánske námestie**, **Panská** and **Laurinská** for shops, **Kapitulská** — the quietest and oldest street, running to the cathedral — and **Židovská** and **Beblavého** climbing the castle hill. Across the river, **Petržalka** is a different exercise entirely, best walked along the Chorvátske rameno and the Sad Janka Kráľa park.
raw.Walkable blocks — Košice: Essentially one: **Hlavná ulica**, a 1.2 km spindle-shaped square that widens around the cathedral and narrows at each end, with **Mlynská**, **Alžbetina** and **Hlavná's** courtyards branching off. Everything in this itinerary except the East Slovak Museum's annexes is on or within 200 m of it.
raw.Transit passes and fares — Bratislava: The city network is **DPB** (buses, trolleybuses, trams), integrated into the regional **IDS BK** zone system. Bratislava city is **zones 100 + 101**; a ticket priced for those two zones covers everything you will use, including the bus to Devín. Fares are time-based rather than per-journey — short (about 15 minutes), standard (about 30), and longer bands, plus **24-hour, 72-hour and 7-day** passes, with the multi-day passes clearly the better buy from day one. Buy at machines, at kiosks, or in the IDS BK app; **validate paper tickets on boarding** [VERIFY: current IDS BK zone 100+101 single and multi-day fares].
raw.Transit passes and fares — Košice: **DPMK** runs trams, trolleybuses and buses; the tram loop around the centre and the lines out to the East Slovak Museum's Rodošto and the suburbs are the useful ones. Tickets are time-banded (roughly 30 and 60 minutes) with day passes available, and are cheaper than Bratislava's. Košice is compact enough that most visitors buy two or three singles across the whole stay [VERIFY: current DPMK fares and day-pass price].
raw.The train — and how long this country is: The **Bratislava–Košice IC** is the country's flagship service and it takes **about 5 h 20 to 6 h**, roughly 445 km via Trnava, Žilina, Poprad-Tatry and Prešov. There is no faster option; the alternative is a 1-hour flight. Book the IC seat in advance — it is reservation-based — and take a window on the right heading east for the High Tatras between Ružomberok and Poprad [VERIFY: current ZSSK IC fare and reservation rules].
raw.Cultural booking timelines: Very little in Slovakia genuinely sells out. The exceptions: the **Blue Church**, which is a working parish and open to visitors only in narrow windows around services; **Spiš Castle** in July–August, where the car park rather than the ticket office is the constraint; and any **Slovak Philharmonic** or **Slovak National Theatre** performance in Bratislava, which needs 2–4 weeks. Museums here take walk-ins.
raw.Architectural focal points and periods: **Gothic**: St Elisabeth's in Košice (14th–15th c.), St Martin's Cathedral in Bratislava, Levoča's St James with the Master Pavol altar. **Baroque**: the **Primate's Palace** (1778–81, Melchior Hefele) and the Pálffy and Esterházy town palaces that give the Staré Mesto its street walls. **Hungarian Secession**: **Ödön Lechner's Church of St Elizabeth — the Blue Church** (1909–13), the purest thing he built, with its blue-glazed Zsolnay ceramics and rolled parapet. **Czechoslovak functionalism**: the **Manderla** tower on Námestie SNP (1935), Bratislava's first high-rise and the emblem of the interwar republic. **Socialist modernism**: the **UFO** on the Most SNP (1972) and Petržalka itself.

trips.title: Pristina & Prizren: Kosovo's Two Cities in Seven Days
trips.subRegion: Kosovo — Pristina, Prizren & the Rugova highlands

bestPeriod.window: Mid-May–late June & September–mid October
bestPeriod.avoid: December–February (Pristina's winter inversion traps lignite smog and air quality collapses); August is hot and dusty with monasteries at their busiest.
bestPeriod.raw: Mid-May–late June & September–mid October

accommodation.note: Good central doubles at €50–80; Kosovo is the cheapest capital in Europe

food.note: Mains €4–8, macchiato €1–1.50, a serious dinner rarely exceeds €25

transport.note: Intercity buses, two airport transfers, one hired car or driver for Rugova

activities.note: Most museums €1–3; the cost is guides and the Rugova day

profile.difficultyNote: 2 — 6–9 km a day in the cities, plus one 8–12 km hiking option in Rugova with 350–500 m of ascent.

trips.gatewayAirport: PRN — Pristina International "Adem Jashari"; airport shuttle or taxi to central Pristina 20 min (€15–20 fixed); no train link
trips.summary: Kosovo gives you two entirely different cities four days apart on the same €5 bus. Pristina is young, loud and architecturally strange — Yugoslav brutalism, a spiky National Library, an unfinished Orthodox cathedral, and the Newborn monument that gets repainted each February. Prizren is Ottoman: a river through the middle, a hillside fortress, a 17th-century mosque on the square, and a Serbian Orthodox cathedral rebuilt after 2004. Between and around them are the Gračanica and Visoki Dečani monasteries, still under protection, and the Rugova gorge. It is the cheapest week in this collection, and the least infrastructure-heavy: expect minibuses, cash, and conversations.

itinerary.title: Pristina: the boulevard and the library
itinerary.morning: Taxi in from PRN, drop bags, then walk **Bulevardi Nënë Tereza** from Skanderbeg's statue north. Macchiato at **Dit' e Nat'**, Fazli Grajçevci 5, a bookshop-café that functions as the city's living room.
itinerary.afternoon: **National Library of Kosovo** (free, enter and look up at the domes from inside — it is the whole argument), the unfinished **Christ the Saviour cathedral** beside it, and the **University** campus. Then **Newborn** on Bill Clinton Boulevard, repainted every 17 February, and the **Heroinat** memorial of 20,000 pins.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Liburnia**, Rr. Perandori Justinian 9 — Kosovar home cooking done seriously, €12–20pp. Then rakia at Soma Book Station.
itinerary.dayStats: 6.4 km, flat; taxi PRN €15–20; library open Mon–Fri 08:00–20:00; mains €5–8.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Gracanica or Swiss Diamond Prishtina, central Pristina.

itinerary.title: Ottoman Pristina, Gračanica monastery
itinerary.morning: The old quarter — **Xhamia e Madhe** (Great Mosque, 1461), the **Great Hammam**, the **Clock Tower**, and the **Ethnological Museum Emin Gjiku** (€2), an 18th–19th-century Ottoman family compound with the *oda* reception room intact and excellent guides.
itinerary.afternoon: Gjilan-bound bus from the main station to **Gračanica** — 20 minutes, €1. The 1321 monastery church, five domes stacked in a pyramid, holds some of the finest surviving Serbian medieval frescoes. Cover shoulders and knees; no photography inside.
itinerary.evening: Back in Pristina, **Te Zoti** or **Renaissance 2** (Rr. Sylejman Vokshi, no menu, no prices, a set procession of dishes and wine, ~€20pp, ring the bell).
itinerary.dayStats: 5.8 km; bus €1 each way, 20 min; Emin Gjiku 10:00–17:00, closed Mondays; Gračanica daylight hours, closed midday.

itinerary.title: Kosovo Museum, Grand Hotel context, bus to Prizren
itinerary.morning: **Kosovo Museum**, Rr. Ali Pashë Tepelena (€2), for the Neolithic *Goddess on the Throne* from Tjerrtorja, and the **Kosovo Art Gallery** nearby. Walk past the **Grand Hotel Prishtina** — worth ten minutes for the lobby and the story of a five-star state hotel that lost its stars one at a time.
itinerary.afternoon: Bus from Pristina station to **Prizren**, ~1h45, €5, departures every 20–30 min. Check into the old town and walk **Shadervan** square at golden hour.
itinerary.evening: **Te Syla**, off Shadervan, for *qebapa* and *suxhuk*; €8–14pp. Then the riverside terraces along the Lumbardhi.
itinerary.dayStats: 5.1 km; bus 1h45 / €5; Kosovo Museum 10:00–17:00, closed Mondays.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Prizreni or Centrum Hotel, Prizren old town.

itinerary.title: Prizren: mosques, the League, and Kalaja
itinerary.morning: **Sinan Pasha Mosque** (1615) on Shadervan — the single-dome hall and painted mihrab — then the **Gazi Mehmed Pasha Hammam** and the **Stone Bridge** over the Lumbardhi.
itinerary.afternoon: **League of Prizren complex** (€1), the reconstructed 1878 house where the Albanian national movement was founded; then the **Church of Our Lady of Ljeviš** (14th century, UNESCO, burnt in 2004, restored — access by arrangement) and the Catholic **Cathedral of Our Lady of Perpetual Succour**.
itinerary.evening: Climb to **Kalaja fortress** (free, 30 min, 130 m) for sunset over the roofs and the Šar mountains behind. Dinner at **Ambient**, Rr. Sharri, €10–18pp.
itinerary.dayStats: 6.7 km incl. 130 m fortress climb; League complex 09:00–17:00; Kalaja open, unlit — carry a torch for the descent.

itinerary.title: Visoki Dečani and Gjakova
itinerary.morning: Pre-arranged visit to **Visoki Dečani Monastery** near Deçan — driver from Prizren (~€40–60 return, 1h) or bus to Deçan then taxi. At the gate you pass a KFOR checkpoint, surrender bags and register with passports; the 1327–35 church holds around a thousand frescoes and the largest surviving medieval Byzantine-rite fresco programme anywhere.
itinerary.afternoon: On to **Gjakova** for the reconstructed **Çarshia e Madhe** bazaar, the longest in Kosovo, and the Hadum Mosque.
itinerary.evening: Back to Prizren. **Marashi** on the riverbank for trout, €12–18pp.
itinerary.dayStats: ~120 km driven; Dečani open roughly 09:00–13:00 and 15:00–17:00; passport mandatory; no photography inside the church.

itinerary.title: Rugova Gorge and Peja
itinerary.morning: Bus or driver Prizren → **Peja** (1h15–1h30). The **Patriarchate of Peć** (small entry fee, passport required, KFOR-adjacent) at the gorge mouth — four churches under one roof, 13th–14th century.
itinerary.afternoon: Into the **Rugova Gorge**: the Via Ferrata Ari, the zipline, or the walk toward the Drelaj villages. A hired car or driver is the only practical way; €25–40 for the half day.
itinerary.evening: Peja's bazaar and a beer at the **Birra Peja** brewery town it is named for, or return to Pristina by the 18:00–19:00 bus (€5, 1h30).
itinerary.dayStats: 8–12 km hiking option, 350–500 m ascent; Peja bus €5 / 1h30; driver into Rugova €25–40.
itinerary.sleep: Swiss Diamond Prishtina (back in Pristina) or Hotel Dukagjini, Peja.

itinerary.title: Pristina coffee, Bear Sanctuary, departure
itinerary.morning: If time allows, the **Bear Sanctuary Prishtina** at Mramor (€2–3, 20 min by taxi), where bears rescued from restaurant cages live out their lives — a very Kosovar postscript. Otherwise, a last slow macchiato on Rr. Rexhep Luci.
itinerary.afternoon: Souvenir *filigran* silver from the old quarter workshops, then taxi to PRN.
itinerary.evening: Flight out.
itinerary.dayStats: 4.0 km; taxi PRN €15–20; allow 2 h at PRN for non-Schengen departure; macchiato €1–1.50.

accommodationStrategy.name: Swiss Diamond Prishtina
accommodationStrategy.description: On the pedestrian boulevard itself, so the Library, Newborn and the bus station are all a walk. Reliable heating and filtration, which matters given Pristina's winter air quality, and a functioning gym after bus days. €90–130 double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Prizreni
accommodationStrategy.description: Fifty metres off Shadervan and directly under the Kalaja path, so the sunset climb is a fifteen-minute round trip. Rooms are simple and the terrace breakfast looks at the Sinan Pasha dome. €50–75.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Dukagjini
accommodationStrategy.description: The obvious Rugova base if you extend the gorge into two days, on Peja's main square with parking, and the drivers who work the canyon wait outside. €60–90.

logistics.connectivity: **Non-EU roaming.** Kosovo is not in the EU roaming zone, though it participates in the Western Balkans roaming agreement and some EU operators now apply a capped Balkans rate — check before you land. Local Vala or IPKO prepaid SIMs cost €5–10 with generous data and are sold at the airport. Note that some Serbian networks bleed across in the north and can trigger unexpected charges.
logistics.emergency: 112 works; 192 police, 194 ambulance. Kosovo has no formal mountain-rescue service in Rugova — the local guiding outfits are the de facto rescue, so hike with one. **Kosovo is outside the EU and EHIC does not apply**; carry full medical insurance and confirm your policy covers Kosovo specifically, since some exclude it by name.
logistics.weather: Pristina's winter **thermal inversion** traps lignite-power-station smoke in the basin, and PM2.5 readings regularly go off scale between December and February. Rugova gets snow into May and the gorge road can close after storms; the Šar range above Prizren holds snow into June.
logistics.bookingWindows: Visoki Dečani 48–72 hours ahead with passport details, by email or phone to the monastery. DokuFest accommodation in Prizren three months ahead for early August. Rugova drivers and via ferrata guides 2–3 days. Buses are turn-up-and-go.
logistics.money: **Kosovo uses the euro** unilaterally, without being in the eurozone or the EU. Cash dominates — most restaurants, all buses, all taxis, museums and monastery donations are cash-only. ATMs are plentiful in Pristina and Prizren and thin elsewhere. Tipping is rounding up. Serbian dinars circulate in the northern municipalities and in Serb-majority villages like Gračanica.
logistics.transportRules: No rail worth using. Intercity buses are frequent, cheap and pay-on-board; the Pristina station is on Bill Clinton Boulevard, well signed. **A Kosovo entry stamp does not bar you from Serbia, but entering Serbia from Kosovo at a Kosovo-Serbia crossing can be refused if you did not enter Kosovo via Serbia** — plan any Belgrade combination to go Serbia → Kosovo → third country, or fly. Rental cars from Kosovo often cannot be driven into Serbia; check the contract.
logistics.permits: No tourist tax. Visoki Dečani and the Patriarchate of Peć require passports at the gate, ban photography inside the churches, and enforce dress codes (covered shoulders and knees, no shorts, headscarf offered for women). Drones are prohibited near all KFOR-protected sites.
logistics.health: Tap water is treated and generally potable in Pristina and Prizren but many locals drink bottled; if in doubt, buy it. Kosovo is safe for visitors, with very low violent crime. **Unexploded ordnance remains a residual risk in remote uncleared areas** — stay on marked paths in the Rugova and Šar backcountry.

proTips: Email **Visoki Dečani at least 72 hours before** with the full name and passport number of every visitor. Turning up unannounced at the KFOR checkpoint usually means being turned away.
Check your operator's **Western Balkans roaming cap** before landing, or buy a €5 Vala or IPKO SIM at PRN. Default non-EU data rates in Kosovo are brutal.
Visit **Newborn on or just after 17 February** if the dates fall right — the monument is repainted every Independence Day and the design is a national conversation.
In Pristina, the **National Library must be entered**, not photographed from outside. The domes, the light wells and the reading rooms are the building; the fishnet exterior is only half the joke.
Take the **Gjilan bus for Gračanica** rather than a taxi — €1, twenty minutes, and it drops you at the monastery wall.
Prizren's **Kalaja fortress has no lighting**. Climb for sunset, but carry a phone torch for the descent, which is loose gravel in the dark.

Order **flija** where you see it advertised on a village menu — a layered pancake cooked in rings under a hot lid, made to order and needing an hour, so ask when you arrive rather than when you're hungry.
Time an August visit around **DokuFest** in Prizren, or deliberately avoid it: the festival takes over the fortress, the river and every bed in town.

raw.Walkable blocks: Pristina centre (**Bulevardi Nënë Tereza** pedestrian spine → Skanderbeg statue → Newborn → Bill Clinton Boulevard, 1.8 km, flat); Pristina old quarter (Xhamia e Madhe → Ethnological Museum Emin Gjiku → Great Hammam, 900 m); Prizren old town (**Shadervan** square → Stone Bridge → Sinan Pasha Mosque → riverfront Marash, 1.1 km flat, then a 30-minute 130 m climb to **Kalaja**).
raw.Transit: there is no urban pass worth bu: Pristina city buses cost €0.40–0.50 paid in cash to the driver, and everything central is walkable. **Intercity buses** run from Pristina's main station on Bill Clinton Boulevard: Prizren roughly €5 and 1h45 (departures every 20–30 min), Peja €5 and 1h30 (every 20 min), Gjakova €5, Gračanica €1 on the Gjilan bus (20 min, every 30 min).
raw.Airport transfer: PRN is 18 km from the centre with **no train and no reliable public bus**. Take the fixed-price taxi (€15–20) or a hotel transfer. Book a return pickup the night before — the airport rank thins out after the evening bank of departures.
raw.Booking timeline: **Visoki Dečani** requires advance permission — email or phone the monastery at least **48–72 hours ahead** with full passport details for every visitor; you hand over your passport and bags at the KFOR checkpoint on arrival. **Gračanica** takes walk-ins during daylight but closes at midday for services. Prizren's Documentary and Short Film Festival (**DokuFest**, early August) fills every bed in the city three months out. Restaurants almost never need booking outside DokuFest.
raw.Architectural focal points: Andrija Mutnjaković's 1982 **National Library of Kosovo** — 99 domes and a full aluminium fishnet skin, the most argued-about building in the Balkans; the unfinished **Christ the Saviour** cathedral beside it; the 1961 **Grand Hotel Prishtina**, once the state's showpiece and now a half-empty monument to a different era; the 1615 **Sinan Pasha Mosque** in Prizren, built with stone reportedly taken from Visoki Dečani; the 14th-century Raška-Byzantine **Gračanica** (c. 1321, King Milutin's endowment, UNESCO-listed); **Visoki Dečani** (1327–35), Romanesque-Byzantine hybrid in banded marble with roughly a thousand surviving frescoes.
raw.Eating structure: Pristina for modern Balkan and specialty coffee (Soma Book Station, Dit' e Nat'), Prizren for grills and river terraces (Te Syla, Marashi), plus *flija* and *tavë* wherever it is offered. Cash-first everywhere.
raw.Day trip: **Rugova Gorge** from Peja — bus Pristina → Peja €5 / 1h30, then taxi or hired driver into the canyon (€25–40 for a half day), with the Via Ferrata Ari and the Rugova zipline as options and Patriarchate of Peć at the gorge mouth.

Prizren's Documentary and Short Film Festival (**DokuFest**, early August) fills every bed in the city three months out. Restaurants almost never need booking outside DokuFest.
