trips.hook: Slovakia keeps five UNESCO towns and villages within a comfortable day's drive of each other and almost nobody visits them in sequence. This is a week of three beds and long afternoons: a silver town inside a collapsed volcano, the tallest Gothic altar on earth, a burgher square with its medieval plot lines intact, and a log village where the smoke still smells of spruce. Deliberately unhurried, unfashionable, and very cheap.

snapshot.Start / End: Bratislava → Košice (point-to-point, ~520 km by road)
snapshot.Getting there: Fly Bratislava (BTS) or Vienna (VIE, 70 km); return from Košice (KSC). Rail alternative: Bratislava–Hronská Dúbrava–Banská Štiavnica, then IC to Poprad and Spišská Nová Ves.

itinerary.title: Into the caldera
itinerary.morning: Collect the car in Bratislava and take the R1 east to Žiar nad Hronom, then the switchbacks up to Banská Štiavnica — about two and a half hours. The town sits inside a collapsed volcanic caldera, which is why the streets run at impossible angles.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk Trojičné námestie, the plague column and the **Old Castle** — a 13th-century church fortified against the Ottomans. Then up to the **New Castle**, a white watchtower with the best single view of the roofs.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at a guesthouse table. Order *kapustnica*, the sauerkraut and sausage soup, and ask about the *tajchy* — your hosts will each name a different favourite.
itinerary.dayStats: Bratislava → Banská Štiavnica, 190 km

itinerary.title: Adits and reservoirs (Banská Štiavnica)
itinerary.morning: The **Slovak Mining Museum's Bartolomej adit** (Štôlňa Bartolomej) at the open-air museum: helmet, lamp, boots and an underground hour in a real 18th-century working [VERIFY: current adit tour times and price]. Book the first slot; groups fill the later ones.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the **Calvary** — 23 stations climbing a volcanic cone to a twin-towered upper church, restored from near-ruin over twenty years. It takes an hour up and is the single best thing in the town.
itinerary.evening: Swim in a *tajch*. **Klinger** is nearest, **Počúvadlo** the biggest and warmest. These are 18th-century mining water reservoirs built by Hell and Mikovíny to power pumps — engineering, not leisure, and now the town's swimming lakes.

itinerary.title: Across to Spiš
itinerary.morning: Drive east via Zvolen and Banská Bystrica, then the R2/D1 to Poprad — around three hours. Break at **Vlkolínec** above Ružomberok, a UNESCO log-house village of 45 dwellings, still inhabited, still without a souvenir strip [VERIFY: current Vlkolínec entry fee].
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive in Levoča and simply walk the square before the light goes. The town walls are largely complete and you can circle most of them.
itinerary.evening: Eat *pirohy* and *halušky* in a cellar restaurant off Námestie Majstra Pavla, then look at the Cage of Shame, a 16th-century iron cage on the square where scolds and drunks were displayed.
itinerary.dayStats: Banská Štiavnica → Levoča, 200 km

itinerary.title: The tallest altar in the world (Levoča)
itinerary.morning: The **Basilica of St James**. **Master Pavol of Levoča** carved its high altar between 1507 and 1517 — **18.6 m of limewood**, the tallest Gothic altarpiece anywhere, with the Last Supper predella and life-size apostles. Entry is by timed guided visit from the ticket office opposite; go at opening [VERIFY: current basilica ticket price and tour times].
itinerary.afternoon: The Renaissance **town hall** and the Master Pavol House museum. Then climb to the Mariánska hora pilgrimage basilica above the town for the Spiš basin panorama.
itinerary.evening: Guesthouse dinner. Ask for *bryndzové halušky* made with real sheep bryndza rather than cow-curd substitute — say *"z ovčej bryndze, prosím"*.

itinerary.title: Castle and chapter
itinerary.morning: Drive fifteen minutes to **Spišské Podhradie** and up to **Spiš Castle (Spišský hrad)**, one of the largest castle complexes in central Europe, spread over a travertine hill. Wear real shoes; the upper ward is exposed and there is no shade [VERIFY: current Spišský hrad entry fee and season].
itinerary.afternoon: Cross the valley to **Spišská Kapitula**, the walled ecclesiastical town — one street, two gates, the Romanesque St Martin's Cathedral and the canons' houses. It is silent, and takes an hour.
itinerary.evening: Back in Levoča for a wine on the square. The Spiš towns were German-settled from the 13th century, and the burgher plot widths on the square still show it.
itinerary.dayStats: Levoča base, 30 km round trip

itinerary.title: North to Šariš
itinerary.morning: Detour to **Kežmarok** for the **wooden articular church** — built 1717 without a single nail, of yew and red spruce, seating 1,500, put up under Habsburg rules that forbade stone, towers and a town-centre site for Protestants. UNESCO-listed [VERIFY: current articular church opening hours].
itinerary.afternoon: Drive to **Bardejov** via Prešov, about two hours. Walk **Radničné námestie**, ringed by gabled burgher houses, with the 1509 town hall standing free in the middle.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in a house on the square. Bardejov closes early; eat at 18:00 like the locals.
itinerary.dayStats: Levoča → Bardejov, 100 km, via Kežmarok

itinerary.title: Wafers and the suburbium (Bardejov)
itinerary.morning: **St Egidius (Bazilika sv. Egídia)**, an 11-altar Gothic church whose winged altarpieces survive largely in place. Climb the tower if it is open [VERIFY: current tower access].
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the **Jewish suburbium** north-west of the walls — the 1836 Old Synagogue, the ritual bath and the assembly house, one of the most complete surviving Jewish town quarters in Slovakia. Then take the bus or drive 5 km to **Bardejovské Kúpele** for the spa colonnade and a bag of *oplátky* eaten warm.
itinerary.evening: Drive or take the train to Košice, 75 km, for the flight out — or stay a last night and eat *šúľance s makom* somewhere with a tiled stove.

accommodationStrategy.name: Penzión Cosmopolitan II
accommodationStrategy.description: on the historic core within three minutes of Trojičné námestie, so you can park once and not touch the car for two days — which matters in a town where every street is a gradient. Breakfast, and staff who will tell you which tajch is warm this week.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct or Booking.com, 4–6 weeks ahead; longer for the September weekends [VERIFY: current nightly rate].

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel U Leva
accommodationStrategy.style: historic house on the main square
accommodationStrategy.description: directly on Námestie Majstra Pavla, so the basilica is a 90-second walk and you can be first through the door at opening, before the coaches from Poprad. Restaurant on site for the nights you cannot face going out.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct, 3–4 weeks ahead; it fills for the July Marian pilgrimage weekend.

accommodationStrategy.name: Penzión Semafor
accommodationStrategy.description: a short walk below the square with parking, a family kitchen doing genuine Šariš cooking, and hosts who will book you into the synagogue visit — which is not a walk-in.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct by phone or email, 2–3 weeks ahead.

logistics.connectivity: 4G/5G is good in all four towns; Vlkolínec and the upper Calvary are patchier. Free Wi-Fi in most guesthouses and on Levoča's square.
logistics.emergency: 112 nationwide. Hospitals in Banská Štiavnica (small), Poprad and Bardejov. Nothing here is remote enough to need mountain rescue, but if you walk the Štiavnické vrchy ridges, HZS is **18 300** and Slovak mountain rescue is chargeable without insurance.
logistics.weather: Continental. Spring and autumn swing 15 °C in a day; the caldera holds fog until mid-morning in September. Pack a warm layer even in June — Levoča sits at 570 m and Bardejov at 277 m, and the evenings feel it.
logistics.bookingWindows: Guesthouses 3–6 weeks. The exceptions are the first weekend of September in Banská Štiavnica (**Salamander** mining festival, when the whole town is booked out months ahead) and the Levoča pilgrimage weekend in early July [VERIFY: 2027 Salamander dates].
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are accepted in towns; carry €60–€80 cash for adit tours, church entries, village entry fees and market stalls. ATMs on every main square.
logistics.transportRules: A car makes this week; without one, use IC trains to Poprad and Prešov plus regional buses (cp.sk for timetables). If driving motorways, buy the **e-vignette** at eznamka.sk — it is plate-registered and there is no windscreen sticker. Blood-alcohol limit is **0.0‰**, absolutely.
logistics.permits: No permits. Almost every museum in Slovakia closes **Monday**; plan Monday as a driving or walking day. Vlkolínec charges a small village entry fee and is a living settlement — do not photograph through windows.

proTips: Do the Levoča basilica at opening, not after lunch. The Master Pavol altar is visited in timed groups and the mid-morning slots go to school and coach parties; the first tour of the day is often six people.

Swim at **Počúvadlo** rather than Klinger in high summer, and at Klinger in September when Počúvadlo has cooled. Locals treat the tajchy as a temperature ladder and will tell you which one is currently right.
Buy bryndza and *žinčica* at a roadside *salaš* on the Ružomberok–Poprad stretch, not in a shop. The whey is only good the day it is made, and it will not exist by afternoon.
Ask your guesthouse at breakfast whether they will cook dinner. Most will, for €10–€14 a head, and it is invariably better than the restaurant on the square.
Skip the Spiš Castle car park queue by arriving before 09:30 or after 15:30; the site is huge and thins out fast in the last two hours.
Learn *"Prosím si účet"* (the bill, please) and *"Máte domácu polievku?"* (do you have homemade soup?). Soup is the point of a Slovak lunch and is usually not on the printed menu.
If Monday falls mid-trip, use it for Vlkolínec and the Calvary — both outdoor, both open, both better empty.

raw.Village and town squares by name: **Trojičné námestie** in Banská Štiavnica — a sloping triangle of merchant houses around the 1759 plague column, with the Old Castle above and the New Castle on its own knoll. **Námestie Majstra Pavla** in Levoča, a vast rectangle holding the Basilica of St James, the Renaissance town hall with its arcades, the Evangelical church and the **Cage of Shame**. **Radničné námestie** in Bardejov, the most intact Gothic-burgher square in Slovakia, closed at the top by St Egidius. **Vlkolínec** has no square at all — it has one lane, 45 log houses, a wooden belfry and a two-storey log bell tower.
raw.Market days and where to buy: Levoča's produce market runs on the lower square most mornings, busiest Friday and Saturday [VERIFY: current Levoča market days]. Banská Štiavnica has a Saturday farmers' market on Trojičné námestie in season [VERIFY: current market schedule]. Bardejov's market sits below the square by the bus station. Buy *bryndza* — the salted sheep's cheese with PGI protection — direct from a *salaš* rather than a supermarket, and drink the *žinčica* whey alongside it while it is fresh.
raw.Named crafts: **Modra majolica** (blue-and-white tin-glazed earthenware, still hand-painted at the Modra workshop). **Čičmany patterning** — the white lime geometry painted onto dark log walls in the Žilina region, now Slovakia's most-reproduced folk motif. **Bardejov's oplátky**, the wafer-thin spa wafers sold at Bardejovské Kúpele. Woodcarving and gilding around Levoča, a direct inheritance of Master Pavol's workshop.
raw.Boutique and small stays: Everything here is a *penzión* or a converted burgher house; there is no international chain outside Košice. Expect €35–€60 a night for a double with breakfast, and dinner cooked to order if you ask in the morning.
raw.Pacing rule: Three bases in seven nights: Banská Štiavnica (nights 1–2), Levoča (nights 3–5), Bardejov (nights 6–7). Never more than one relocation every two days, and two of the three relocations are under two hours.

sources.confidenceNotes: - Verified: Banská Štiavnica, Levoča with the Spiš Castle group, Bardejov, Vlkolínec and the Kežmarok wooden articular church are all UNESCO World Heritage; Master Pavol's high altar in the Basilica of St James is 18.6 m and the tallest Gothic altarpiece in the world; the *tajchy* are 18th-century mining water reservoirs; Slovakia uses the euro; emergency 112, HZS 18 300, and Slovak mountain rescue is chargeable without cover; Slovak drink-driving limit is 0.0‰; the motorway vignette is electronic and plate-registered. - `[VERIFY]` items in this file: 10 (see inline markers above) - Last reviewed: 2026-09-02

trips.title: San Marino & the Montefeltro: Towers, Truffles and Block-Printed Linen
trips.subRegion: San Marino & the Emilia-Romagna / Marche border

bestPeriod.window: Late April–June & September–early November (October for the truffle fair)
bestPeriod.avoid: Mid July–August, when Rimini's coastal traffic clogs every approach road and Monte Titano bakes; also February, when Montefeltro fog sits all day and hill restaurants close
bestPeriod.raw: Late April–June & September–early November (October for the truffle fair)

accommodation.note: Two bases; €75–€125 pp/night in small historic hotels

food.note: €12–€20 Romagnolo mains; truffle dishes €25–€40 in October

transport.note: Small rental car 5 days, or Bonelli buses and regional trains

activities.note: Three Towers ticket, San Leo fortress, printing workshop, museums

profile.difficultyNote: 2 — the Titano ridge path between the towers and San Leo's approach are steep but short; nothing longer than 4 km

trips.gatewayAirport: RMI — Rimini Federico Fellini, 30 min to San Marino; BLQ Bologna is the bigger hub, 1 h 40 by car or 1 h by train to Rimini plus a 50 min bus
trips.summary: Two nights on a limestone crag that has been an independent republic since the fourth century, then four in the Malatesta hill country that surrounds it. San Marino is best understood as a strange, steep, self-governing village rather than a curiosity, and it is transformed the moment the last day-tripper takes the cable car down. Below it, the Montefeltro gives you San Leo's cliff fortress, Pennabilli's poet's gardens, Verucchio's Iron Age museum and Santarcangelo's tufa caves and printing workshop — all within a 40 km radius. One move, two open afternoons, and, if you time it for October, four Sundays of white truffle in Sant'Agata Feltria. It suits people who like small, dense places and don't need a coastline.

itinerary.title: Up Monte Titano
itinerary.morning: Land at Rimini and take the Bonelli bus or a car up to San Marino — the road climbs 700 m in 20 km and the republic appears as a wall of rock with buildings on top of it. Leave the car in the multi-storey car parks below the walls.
itinerary.afternoon: Check in inside the walls, then walk the ridge: Guaita first, then the Passo delle Streghe to Cesta, where the museum of ancient weapons sits at the republic's high point.
itinerary.evening: The town after 18:00 is a different place. Aperitivo on Piazza della Libertà, then dinner at Ristorante Righi or a smaller osteria off Contrada Omerelli — try the nidi di rondine, Romagna's baked rolled pasta.
itinerary.dayStats: RMI–San Marino 27 km / 35 min; Bonelli bus roughly 50 min, about €5 each way, 10–12 daily. Cesta at 755 m. Two-tower ticket roughly €7–€10.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Titano, Città di San Marino

itinerary.title: Market morning below the crag
itinerary.morning: Take the cable car down to Borgo Maggiore — 90 seconds, and the best two euros in the republic — for the Thursday market on Piazza Grande from 06:00. Cheese, cured meat, plants, cheap clothes and locals doing their weekly shop.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk back up the old path rather than riding, then the State Museum and the Basilica del Santo Marino. Late in the day, the terrace outside Cesta faces the Adriatic and, on clear days, shows the Croatian coast.
itinerary.evening: Second night on the crag, and the only night it makes sense to eat late in the upper town. Piadina and Sangiovese if you want the honest version.
itinerary.dayStats: Cable car 1.5 min, roughly €2.80 single / €4.50 return, every 15 min. Market 06:00–14:00 Thursday. Uphill path 1.8 km / 200 m.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Titano, Città di San Marino

itinerary.title: San Leo's cliff, then down to Santarcangelo
itinerary.morning: Drive south-west to San Leo, where a fortress sits on a sheer sandstone block above a village of 300 people. Cagliostro died in a cell here in 1795 with no door — food was lowered through the ceiling. The Romanesque Pieve and Duomo below are the best of their kind in the region.
itinerary.afternoon: North to Santarcangelo di Romagna, on the flat, and check in. Walk the tufa grotte beneath the hill — a network of tunnels of contested purpose — and then Piazza Ganganelli.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Osteria La Sangiovesa in the Palazzo Nadiani, a Romagnolo institution of piadina, tagliatelle and a great deal of Sangiovese.
itinerary.dayStats: San Marino–San Leo 25 km / 40 min; San Leo–Santarcangelo 35 km / 45 min. San Leo at 601 m, fortress entry roughly €10. Grotte tour about 45 min, €4–€6.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Della Porta, Santarcangelo di Romagna

itinerary.title: Printing linen, then nothing at all
itinerary.morning: Stamperia Marchi for the block-printing session: choose a pear-wood block, ink it in rust dye, press it onto linen, and watch the mangano — a stone-weighted wooden press from the 1700s — finish the cloth.
itinerary.afternoon: Blank. Santarcangelo is a town made for sitting: the arcades of Via Cesare Battisti, a bar table, a book. If you must move, the Rocca Malatestiana is a ten-minute walk up.
itinerary.evening: Piazza Ganganelli fills from 18:30. Eat where the queue is, and order the cappelletti in brodo if it's autumn.
itinerary.dayStats: Workshop 60–90 min, roughly €25–€45 depending on the cloth. Santarcangelo at 42 m — the only flat night of the week. Rocca walk 700 m / 45 m.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Della Porta, Santarcangelo di Romagna

itinerary.title: Verucchio and the Marecchia valley
itinerary.morning: Verucchio, 15 km up the valley, for the Museo Civico Archeologico — the Villanovan princely burials found here are among the richest Iron Age finds in Italy, with 8th-century BC textiles and a wooden throne. Then the Rocca Malatestiana on the ridge.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue up the Marecchia to Pennabilli for Tonino Guerra's gardens: the Orto dei Frutti Dimenticati with its forgotten fruit varieties and hand-painted ceramics, and the Giardino Pietrificato's mosaics.
itinerary.evening: Back down the valley. Dinner in Santarcangelo again — the advantage of a four-night base.
itinerary.dayStats: Santarcangelo–Verucchio 15 km / 20 min; Verucchio–Pennabilli 35 km / 50 min. Verucchio at 333 m, Pennabilli at 629 m. Museum entry roughly €6–€8; Guerra's gardens free.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Della Porta, Santarcangelo di Romagna

itinerary.title: Sant'Agata Feltria, truffles and an idle afternoon
itinerary.morning: Sant'Agata Feltria for the Sunday truffle fair if you are here in October — the whole village turns into a market, with the Rocca Fregoso above and the 1605 Teatro Angelo Mariani open. Out of season, come anyway for the theatre and a quiet lunch.
itinerary.afternoon: Nothing scheduled. Drive back over the ridge slowly, stop where the view is good, and be back in Santarcangelo by mid-afternoon.
itinerary.evening: Last dinner. If it's truffle season, this is the night to spend money on a plate of tagliolini al tartufo bianco.
itinerary.dayStats: Santarcangelo–Sant'Agata Feltria 45 km / 1 h. Sant'Agata at 607 m. Fair Sundays: 4, 11, 18, 25 October and 1 November 2026. White truffle at fair prices roughly €200–€400 per 100 g depending on the season.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Della Porta, Santarcangelo di Romagna

itinerary.title: Rimini, and out
itinerary.morning: Drive or train down to Rimini. The Tempio Malatestiano, Alberti's unfinished 15th-century masterpiece, and the Roman Ponte di Tiberio are both a short walk from the station.
itinerary.afternoon: Return the car at Rimini airport, or take the Adriatic line north to Bologna in about an hour for a wider choice of flights.
itinerary.evening: Flight home.
itinerary.dayStats: Santarcangelo–RMI 15 km / 20 min. Santarcangelo–Rimini by regional train 8 min, 1–2 hourly. Rimini–Bologna 1 h by Frecciarossa, 1 h 20 by Regionale.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Titano
accommodationStrategy.description: Open since 1894 on Contrada del Collegio, inside the walls and a minute from Piazza della Libertà, with a terrace restaurant looking down the whole Adriatic plain. Staying inside the walls is the entire argument for two nights here — the town belongs to residents and hotel guests after 18:00. Roughly €95–€150 per double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Della Porta
accommodationStrategy.description: A converted house on Via Andrea Costa in the old town, with a small courtyard, an underground spa in the tufa, and parking — the practical point when you are driving out to a different hill town each day. Two minutes from Piazza Ganganelli. Roughly €110–€160 per double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Locanda San Leone or a Montefeltro agriturismo
accommodationStrategy.description: If you would rather sleep among the hills than in a town, take a small relais in the Marecchia valley between San Leo and Verucchio. It costs less, it is quieter, and it removes the evening square from your week — decide which you want before booking.

logistics.connectivity: **San Marino uses the euro but is not an EU member and is outside the EU roaming area.** Many operators bundle it anyway, but some bill it as rest-of-world; check before you arrive, and be aware that phones on the crag frequently hop between San Marinese and Italian networks. Coverage in the Marecchia valley is good, patchy above Pennabilli.
logistics.emergency: 112 works in both San Marino and Italy. San Marino has its own Gendarmeria and Civil Protection, reachable via 112 or 113 locally. Italian EHIC/GHIC cover does **not** extend to San Marino — check your travel insurance explicitly names it.
logistics.weather: Monte Titano makes its own weather — the republic can be in cloud while Rimini is in sun 700 m below, and the ridge path between the towers is genuinely windy. Montefeltro fog sits in the valleys on autumn mornings and burns off by 11:00. October evenings at Sant'Agata drop to 5–8°C.
logistics.bookingWindows: Beds within 30 km of Sant'Agata Feltria on the October fair Sundays need 3–4 months. Stamperia Marchi sessions want a week's notice. San Marino's hotels are easy midweek, tight on summer weekends.
logistics.money: Euro on both sides of the border — San Marino uses it under a monetary agreement with the EU and mints its own collectable coins, which are legal tender but which nobody will want to spend. Cards are near-universal; carry €50 for the Borgo Maggiore market and the truffle fair. San Marino has no VAT but a similar import levy, so the "duty-free" reputation is largely marketing. Tipping is Italian: round up.
logistics.transportRules: There is no border control between Italy and San Marino, but it is a separate customs territory. Italian rental cars may be driven in freely; check your policy names it. San Marino's historic centre is closed to non-resident traffic — park in the terraced car parks and walk or take the lift shafts. Bonelli Bus runs Rimini station to San Marino roughly 10–12 times daily. Rimini is the rail gateway, on the Milan–Ancona–Bari Adriatic line.
logistics.permits: The Three Towers use a combined ticket; Montale's interior is permanently closed. Drones are prohibited over San Marino's historic centre and require authorisation in Italian airspace. Truffle hunting requires a licence in Italy — buy at the fair.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable throughout. The Passo delle Streghe ridge has low parapets and long drops; it is not a place for unsupervised small children in wind. Santarcangelo's grotte are cool and damp year-round — bring a layer.

proTips: Sleep inside San Marino's walls for at least one night. Between 18:30 and 09:30 the republic reverts to a quiet hill village of 4,000 people, and this is a completely different experience from the daytime souvenir gauntlet.
Take the cable car down to Borgo Maggiore and walk back up. The Thursday market is where the country actually shops, and the return path gives you the crag from below.
For the truffle fair, arrive in Sant'Agata before 09:30. Parking is on the approach roads and fills by mid-morning; the serious truffle buying is also done early.
Buy truffle by weight from a licensed *tartufaio* at the fair rather than jarred paste in a shop. Ask when it was dug — anything over four days old has lost most of its aroma.
At Stamperia Marchi, ask to see the mangano operated rather than only the printing. The stone-weighted press is the rarer thing and the family will run it if the shop is not busy.
San Leo and San Marino look similar on a map and are not remotely similar in feel. Do San Leo on a weekday morning — it holds perhaps a fifth of San Marino's visitors and has the better fortress.
Skip the Rimini coast entirely unless you want it. This week's landscape is the hills behind it, and the beach strip in season will cost you two hours of traffic for very little.

raw.Piazza della Libertà, Città di San Marin: is the republic's stage: the Palazzo Pubblico, the Statue of Liberty, and — in the summer season — the changing of the guard on the hour. It empties dramatically after 18:00 when the coaches leave, and the corso then runs along Contrada del Collegio and Via Basilicius.
raw.Piazza Grande, Borgo Maggiore — Thursday: The republic's real weekly market, in the town below the crag, where San Marinese actually shop. An **antiques market runs the third Sunday of the month, March to December**, in the same square.
raw.Piazza Ganganelli, Santarcangelo di Roma: is the flat-town counterweight — arcaded, café-lined, busy from 18:30, with the tufa grotte tunnelled beneath the hill above it.
raw.Fiera Nazionale del Tartufo Bianco Pregi: The whole village becomes a market: truffle stalls, cheese, chestnuts, and the 1605 Teatro Angelo Mariani, one of Italy's oldest surviving wooden theatres, open alongside it.
raw.Stamperia Marchi, Santarcangelo: has hand-block-printed linen since 1633, using pear-wood blocks and a rust-based dye, finished under an 18th-century wooden *mangano* press turned by a stone counterweight — the last of its kind still in working use.
raw.Pennabilli: carries Tonino Guerra's *Luoghi dell'Anima*: the Orto dei Frutti Dimenticati, an orchard of abandoned fruit varieties, and the Giardino Pietrificato, both free and both odd in the best way.
raw.The Three Towers: run along the Titano ridge: Guaita (the oldest, 11th century), Cesta at 755 m on the summit, and Montale, closed to visitors. The Passo delle Streghe — the Witches' Pass — is the exposed ridge path linking the first two.
raw.Hands-on experience: a block-printing session at **Stamperia Marchi**, inking a pear-wood block and pressing your own tablecloth or runner in the Romagna motifs.
raw.Pacing: one move (San Marino → Santarcangelo on Day 3), blank afternoons on Days 4 and 6, and the short walks that exist: Guaita to Cesta along the ridge (600 m), Borgo Maggiore to Città on the old Costa dell'Arnella path (1.8 km, 200 m of climb), San Leo's Pieve to the fortress (1.1 km).

sources.verified: Borgo Maggiore market confirmed as Thursday, 06:00–14:00, Piazza Grande, with a monthly antiques market on the third Sunday, March–December. Sant'Agata Feltria's Fiera Nazionale del Tartufo Bianco Pregiato 2026 confirmed for Sundays 4, 11, 18 and 25 October plus 1 November 2026. San Marino's use of the euro outside EU membership confirmed.
sources.confidenceNotes: San Marino's roaming treatment varies by operator and is the single most likely thing to catch users out — keep the warning prominent. Cable car and Three Towers ticket prices change annually and were not re-confirmed this run. Bonelli Bus frequency (10–12 daily) is typical but seasonal; direct users to the current timetable. Stamperia Marchi's workshop format and pricing should be confirmed directly, as should Hotel Titano's and Hotel Della Porta's room counts. Truffle price ranges are highly volatile year to year and should be presented as indicative only.

provenance.sourceFormat: md with '## Metadata' bullet block (one file per trip)

trips.title: Albanian Alps to the Riviera
trips.subRegion: Shkodër, Theth, Vlorë & the Albanian Riviera

bestPeriod.window: Late May–late June & mid-September–early October
bestPeriod.avoid: November–April (SH21 to Theth is snowbound and guesthouses shut); late July–August brings 38°C heat and bumper-to-bumper Riviera traffic
bestPeriod.raw: Late May–late June & mid-September–early October

accommodation.note: Guesthouse half-board in Theth; mid-range sea-view rooms in Sarandë

food.note: Byrek and grilled fish are cheap; Ksamil beach clubs are not

transport.note: Rental incl. CDW, fuel, Llogara tunnel toll, Koman ferry, parking

activities.note: Butrint, Rozafa, Theth NP, Blue Eye, Porto Palermo

profile.difficultyNote: 2 — driving-led, with optional 2–4 h valley walks in Theth and a flat 2 km loop at Butrint

trips.gatewayAirport: TIA — Tirana International "Nënë Tereza"; 95 km / 1 h 40 to Shkodër on SH1
trips.summary: This is the drive that shows you two Albanias in one week: the limestone Accursed Mountains where the tarmac ran out until recently, and the Ionian coast where it now runs beautifully. You begin on the flat SH1 to Shkodër, spend a day on the fjord-like Lake Koman ferry, then climb the reengineered SH21 through the Thore tunnel into Theth, a stone village under 2,500 m walls. A long transfer day drops you to the Adriatic at Vlorë, after which the Riviera unrolls — the Llogara Pass at 1,027 m, the Ottoman gunpowder bay at Porto Palermo, Butrint's Roman theatre in the marshes. It suits confident drivers who accept single-track sections, unlit tunnels and the occasional cow, and who want landscape density that Western Europe cannot match at this price.

itinerary.title: Tirana tarmac to the Rozafa ramparts
itinerary.morning: Collect the car airside at TIA and get out of the terminal loop before the Tirana rush thickens. The SH1 north is dual carriageway most of the way to Lezhë, then narrows; expect unsignalled U-turn lanes and mopeds using the hard shoulder as a lane.
itinerary.afternoon: Reach Shkodër by early afternoon and drive straight up to Rozafa Castle before the light hardens — the ramparts sit above the confluence of the Drin, Buna and Kir, and the free car park inside the lower gate saves a hot walk. Then park the car for the night and walk Rruga Kolë Idromeno, the pedestrianised Ottoman-Italianate spine.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Tradita Geg & Tosk, in a restored 18th-century house with a stone courtyard — order the smoked trout from the Drin and the fërgesë.
itinerary.dayStats: 95 km / 1 h 40 driving; Rozafa entry 400 ALL (~€4); zero tolls; sea level throughout.
itinerary.sleep: Rooms Tradita, Shkodër — walled parking inside the property.

itinerary.title: The Koman fjord, on foot
itinerary.morning: Leave Shkodër by 07:15. The SH25 runs via Vau i Dejës and Koman; the final 20 km is a shelf road with rockfall debris and that unlit tunnel. Leave the car in the paid lot at the dam (300–500 ALL) and board the 09:00 Berisha ferry as a foot passenger — three hours of near-vertical schist walls with cable ferries dropping villagers on shingle beaches.
itinerary.afternoon: The boat reaches Fierza around 11:45. Eat at the quayside café, then take the 13:00 return, which gives you the same gorge with the light on the opposite wall. Back at Koman by ~15:45.
itinerary.evening: Drive back to Shkodër (1 h 30) and take an aperitivo on Sheshi Nënë Tereza. Dinner at Restaurant Vila Bekaj for grilled carp.
itinerary.dayStats: 130 km round trip / 3 h driving; 6 h afloat; ferry €9 pp online; parking ~€4; no fuel between Vau i Dejës and Koman.
itinerary.sleep: Rooms Tradita, Shkodër (second night — leave heavy luggage in the room).

itinerary.title: SH21 and the Thore tunnel into Theth
itinerary.morning: Head north on SH1 then fork onto SH21 at Koplik. The climb through Dedaj and Boga is the good part: smooth new asphalt, long sightlines, karst towers. Stop at the Boga plateau layby for coffee.
itinerary.afternoon: Through the Thore tunnel and into the Theth basin on a descent of tight, walled bends. Once in the village, park at your guesthouse and walk to the Church of Theth and the 17th-century Kulla e Ngujimit (lock-in tower) — a working monument to the Kanun blood-feud code.
itinerary.evening: Half-board at your guesthouse is standard and genuinely good: cornbread, fresh cheese, honey, mountain tea. There is one small bar by the church; the valley goes dark early.
itinerary.dayStats: 68 km / 2 h 15; highest point of SH21 ~1,630 m at the tunnel approach; last fuel at Koplik; village lanes are gravel.
itinerary.sleep: Bujtina Polia, Theth — stone guesthouse with off-road parking on grass.

itinerary.title: Blue Eye of Theth, then a long run to the sea
itinerary.morning: Walk or 4x4-shuttle to the Blue Eye of Theth (Syri i Kaltër i Thethit) — 6 km each way from Ndërlysaj on a rough track; the last 25 minutes is a scramble. Do not attempt the track in a low 2WD; the village shuttles charge ~1,500 ALL (~€15) return.
itinerary.afternoon: This is the transfer. Retrace SH21 to Koplik, SH1 south past Lezhë, then the A1/SH2 corridor via Durrës and the SH4 to Vlorë. The Durrës ring is the one genuinely stressful stretch: aggressive undertaking, poor lane discipline.
itinerary.evening: Arrive Vlorë for sunset on the Lungomare. Dinner at Restaurant Nertili on the waterfront — whole sea bass by weight, priced per kilo.
itinerary.dayStats: 315 km / 6 h 15 including the Blue Eye detour; no tolls; fill up at Lezhë; Vlorë hotel parking often €5/night.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Regina City, Vlorë — secure underground garage, five minutes from the promenade.

itinerary.title: Llogara Pass and the Riviera
itinerary.morning: Drive south via Orikum, where the road lifts away from the Karaburun lagoon. Take the SH8 up to the Llogara Pass rather than the tunnel. The Caesar's Pass viewpoint by Hotel Alpin, and the paragliding launch above it, give the best of the Karaburun panorama — go before 10:00 while the haze is thin and the sun is still behind you.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend to Dhërmi and Vuno, then Himarë. Turn off for Porto Palermo, where Ali Pasha's triangular fortress sits on a causeway in a near-perfect bay. Entry is a few hundred lek; the naval base next door means no drones.
itinerary.evening: Continue to Sarandë (SH8 hugging the cliffs above Borsh and Lukovë). Dinner at Taverna Laberia, above the port, for lamb tavë kosi and a Kallmet red.
itinerary.dayStats: 120 km / 3 h 30 with stops; Llogara summit 1,027 m; ~20 hairpins on the north side; tunnel alternative 250 ALL; steep 8–10% gradients on the Palasë descent — use engine braking.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Butrinti & Spa, Sarandë — one of the few central hotels with its own gated car park.

itinerary.title: Butrint, the Blue Eye and Ksamil
itinerary.morning: Be at Butrint National Park for opening. The drive down the Ksamil road takes 25 minutes; park at the site lot. The Greek theatre, the baptistery mosaics (usually under protective sand) and the Venetian tower reward two hours.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross on the Vivari Channel cable ferry (a genuine chain ferry, ~500 ALL for a car) to the Ali Pasha castle, then drive inland to the Blue Eye of Muzinë on the SH99 — a 50 m-deep karst spring. The final 2 km is a rough unsealed track; there is a paid lot at the entrance.
itinerary.evening: Back to Sarandë; sundowners at Mare Nostrum on the promenade, then dinner at Haxhi seafood.
itinerary.dayStats: 90 km / 2 h driving; Butrint 1,200 ALL (~€12); Blue Eye 200 ALL plus 200 ALL parking; ferry 500 ALL.

itinerary.title: Gjirokastër stone city and the run to Tirana
itinerary.morning: Climb inland on the SH99 through the Muzinë pass to Gjirokastër. Park below the bazaar — the upper old town lanes are cobbled at 15% gradient and will punish a rental clutch. The castle, the Skenduli House and the Zekate House are the three worth your time.
itinerary.afternoon: North on SH4 through the Drino valley, joining the A2 Levan–Vlorë motorway and then the SH4 to Tirana. Traffic thickens hard from Fier onward.
itinerary.evening: Drop the car at TIA with a full tank (there is a station 3 km before the terminal on the airport spur; airport refuelling charges are punitive).
itinerary.dayStats: 285 km / 4 h 45; Gjirokastër castle 400 ALL; Muzinë pass ~570 m; no tolls on this routing.
itinerary.sleep: Departure, or Hotel Mondial, Tirana if you fly out on Day 8.

accommodationStrategy.name: Rooms Tradita
accommodationStrategy.description: Two nights here bookends the northern half of the trip without repacking, and the enclosed courtyard parking matters in a city where street parking is contested and opportunistic. Breakfast starts at 07:00, early enough for the Koman ferry run. Roughly €55–€75 a double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Bujtina Polia
accommodationStrategy.description: Half-board is the point: there is effectively no restaurant economy in Theth, and dinner at 19:30 with the family is the experience. Flat grass parking beside the house avoids the deeply rutted lanes further up the valley. About €50–€70 per person with dinner and breakfast.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Butrinti & Spa
accommodationStrategy.description: Chosen almost entirely for the gated car park, which removes the single biggest headache of a Riviera summer. It is a five-minute walk from the promenade, has a sea-facing pool for the dead hours of the afternoon, and sits on the correct side of town for the Butrint road. €90–€150 a double in shoulder season.

logistics.connectivity: Albania is **not** in the EU roaming zone, though Vodafone, One and some EU operators now include it in "Western Balkans" bundles — check before you land or buy a Vodafone AL tourist SIM (~€10 for 20 GB). There is no signal for most of the Koman gorge and patchy coverage in Theth. Download offline maps for the whole north.
logistics.emergency: 112 works nationally; 127 is the ambulance line and 129 the police. Mountain rescue in the Accursed Mountains is informal — guesthouses and the Theth NP ranger post coordinate. Confirm your travel insurance explicitly covers Albania and non-EU medical repatriation; many EU-only policies do not.
logistics.weather: Afternoon thunderstorms build over the Accursed Mountains from roughly 14:00 in June and September, and they close the Theth road with mud and rockfall for hours at a time. On the Riviera, a strong northwesterly can make the Llogara descent gusty enough to move a high-sided car.
logistics.bookingWindows: Theth guesthouses fill 4–6 weeks ahead for June and September weekends. Book the Koman ferry online 3–5 days ahead if taking a car (bookferryberisha.com); as a foot passenger you can usually walk on. Butrint needs no advance ticket.
logistics.money: Currency is the lek (ALL), ~100 ALL ≈ €1. Cards work in Tirana, Shkodër and Sarandë hotels; assume cash-only in Theth, at the ferry, at rural fuel stations and for all parking. Withdraw from Credins or Raiffeisen ATMs and decline dynamic currency conversion. Tipping is rounding up, or 5–10% for a real meal.
logistics.transportRules: No vignette. Headlights are mandatory day and night. The alcohol limit is 0.01% — effectively zero. Speed cameras are concentrated on the SH1 and the Fier bypass, and rental companies pass fines on with a €25–€40 admin charge. Cross-border into Montenegro or Greece requires a Green Card and the agency's written permission letter; get both in writing at pickup.
logistics.permits: Theth is a national park — camping requires permission and open fires are banned. Drones are prohibited over Porto Palermo, Butrint and all military installations, and Albania requires registration for drones above 250 g. Butrint is a UNESCO site with no drone use at all.
logistics.health: Tap water is chlorinated and generally safe in cities but tastes poor; most travellers buy bottled. Spring water in Theth is drinkable. Ticks are present in the northern beech forests May–July. There is no altitude concern on this route. Sea urchins are common on the rocky Riviera entries — bring reef shoes.

proTips: Do the Koman ferry as a **foot passenger round trip** rather than shipping the car. You see the same gorge twice in different light, save €35–€40, and avoid the fact that the Fierza side commits you to a 230 km return via Kukës.

Drive the Llogara Pass **northbound to southbound in the morning**. The Karaburun reveal happens on the descent, and before 10:00 the sun is behind you rather than burning straight into the windscreen.
In Theth, arrange the Blue Eye 4x4 shuttle the night before through your guesthouse. Walk-up prices at Ndërlysaj are roughly 40% higher and the vehicles fill by 09:00.
Fuel discipline: treat Koplik, Lezhë, Orikum and Delvinë as your mandatory fill points. Rural pumps are often attended-only, cash-only, and closed by 20:00.

Sarandë's promenade parking is aggressively ticketed by informal attendants. Pay the €2–€3, take the paper slip, and never leave anything visible — smash-and-grab is the one real property crime on this coast.
Ksamil is a car trap in July and August; the beach clubs' access lanes gridlock by 11:00. Go at 08:00 or skip it for Pulëbardha beach, 3 km north, which has a proper lot.

Buy your Vodafone AL SIM at the airport arrivals kiosk, not in town — the tourist bundle is only sold at certain outlets and it is the difference between having and not having navigation in the north.
Photograph Porto Palermo in the late afternoon, when the sun rakes across the fortress walls from the west and the bay turns navy. Mornings there are flat and backlit.

raw.Total distance: ~1,050 km over 7 days; 5 driving days, 2 largely static. Longest leg is Day 4, Theth–Vlorë, 315 km in a genuine 6 h 15 including stops.
raw.SH21 (Shkodër–Theth), 68 km: fully asphalted since the Thore tunnel opened, but it is a 2-lane-becomes-1.5-lane mountain road with unguarded drops above Boga and roughly 30 tight bends on the descent into Theth. Allow 2 h 15, not the 1 h 20 your phone claims. A normal hatchback manages it in dry weather; a compact SUV with real ground clearance is worth the €10–15/day for the unpaved village spurs inside Theth itself.
raw.Llogara Pass, SH8, 1,027 m: the classic climb from Dukat with ~20 broad hairpins and a sudden reveal of the Karaburun peninsula. The 5.9 km Llogara Tunnel now bypasses it (250 ALL / ~€2.50 for a car, electronic gates, 24/7). Take the tunnel only if weather has closed the pass — the pass is the reason you came, and it costs nothing.
raw.Lake Koman ferry: Berisha operates daily 15 April–5 November; Koman→Fierza departs 09:00, Fierza→Koman 13:00. Foot passengers €9 online / €10 cash; cars are priced by footprint at €7/m² online (a typical compact ≈ €33–€40). The access road SH25 from Vau i Dejës to the Koman dam ends in a 300 m unlit rock tunnel with no lighting and no markings — headlights on, hold the crown of the road.
raw.Cross-border rental rules: Albania is outside the EU and outside the Green Card free-circulation zone for many policies. Most Tirana agencies (Enterprise, Sixt, and the reliable local Ada Rent) permit Montenegro, Kosovo, North Macedonia and Greece for a cross-border fee of €30–€60 plus a Green Card issued at the desk; Serbia and Bosnia are frequently excluded. One-way drops back to TIA are usually free; drops in Sarandë carry €60–€120.
raw.Fuel gaps: there is no reliable fuel between Shkodër and Theth (68 km), none between Koman dam and Vau i Dejës, and the stretch from Llogara down to Himarë has only small independent stations that sometimes run dry in August. Kastrati and Bolv-Oil stations are the dependable brands. Fill at every opportunity above half a tank in the north.
raw.Tolls & vignettes: Albania has no vignette. Tolls exist only on the Llogara Tunnel and the Rrëshen–Kalimash (Kalimash tunnel) motorway toward Kosovo, which this route avoids. Currency is the lek (ALL); ~100 ALL ≈ €1.

sources.verified: Llogara Tunnel status, 2026 toll (250 ALL / ~€2.50) and the fact that the free 1,027 m pass road remains open; Lake Koman Berisha ferry 2026 season (15 April–5 November), 09:00 Koman and 13:00 Fierza departures, and 2026 passenger/vehicle pricing; SH21 Theth road asphalt status and its mid-November to late-March/April seasonal closure; Albania's absence of a national vignette.
sources.confidenceNotes: Koman ferry timings shift with water level and operator, and a second operator sometimes runs a competing schedule — re-verify departure times within a week of travel. Albanian entry fees (Butrint, Rozafa, Blue Eye) are raised without notice and should be re-checked annually. Cross-border rental permissions and Green Card fees vary by agency and change frequently; the €30–€60 band is indicative, not quoted. The Llogara Pass has no fixed closure dates but can shut for 1–7 days after December–February snowfall. Fuel-station brands and locations in the far north change; treat the named fill points as minimums, not guarantees.

provenance.sourceFormat: md with '## Metadata' bullet block (one file per trip)

trips.title: Grossglockner, Timmelsjoch and the Tyrolean Toll Roads
trips.subRegion: Hohe Tauern, Zillertal, Ötztal and the Silvretta

bestPeriod.note: The high toll roads open between late May and mid-June and shut with the first serious snowfall, usually late October.

trips.gatewayAirport: Innsbruck (INN)
trips.summary: A week of Austria's paying mountain highways — Zillertal, Grossglockner, Timmelsjoch and the Silvretta — driven in the right direction at the right hour.
trips.hook: Austria charges money for its finest roads, and they are worth the money. This week links five private mountain highways and half a dozen free passes across Tyrol, Salzburg and Carinthia. Distances are short and times are long: 40 km of hairpins eats ninety minutes, and that is the point.

snapshot.Base(s): Mayrhofen (2 nights), Bruck an der Grossglocknerstrasse (1), Heiligenblut (1), Sölden (2)
snapshot.Best Period: July–September; mid-June and October are viable but pass-dependent
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 1,350 km; sustained alpine hairpins, gradients to 14%, max altitude 2,829 m
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Innsbruck (INN); Munich (MUC) is 2h15 away and usually cheaper
snapshot.Who It Suits: Drivers who enjoy the driving, plus passengers who like glaciers and cake

itinerary.title: Inn valley out, Ziller valley up
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at Innsbruck airport. Before leaving the bay, confirm the digital Vignette is registered to the plate and that the agreement permits Italy. Head east on the A12 Inntalautobahn.
itinerary.afternoon: Leave at Wiesing for the B169 Zillertalstrasse, a flat busy valley road; stop at Zell am Ziller, then on to Mayrhofen at 630 m, where the valley splits into four. Mayrhofen's centre is short-stay metered, so use the hotel garage.
itinerary.evening: Walk the Hauptstrasse and plan tomorrow around the forecast rather than the itinerary.
itinerary.dayStats: 85 km · 1h20 driving · no passes · max altitude 630 m.

itinerary.title: Zillertaler Höhenstrasse and the Schlegeis dam
itinerary.morning: Drive down-valley to Ried im Zillertal and turn up the **Zillertaler Höhenstrasse**, a 48 km private panorama road running along the western flank to Hippach. Toll approx. €11 per car, ticket sold at the barrier. It is single-lane in places with passing bays, gradients to 13%, and it tops out near the Melchboden at about 2,020 m. Caravans and vehicles over 3.5 t are barred. Drive it north to south so the Tux valley and the glacier sit ahead of you.
itinerary.afternoon: Back in Mayrhofen, take the **Schlegeis Alpenstrasse**: 13 km, toll approx. €13, gates open roughly 05:30–22:00 and shut overnight. Two unlit tunnels, gradients around 10–14%, and a finish at the Schlegeisspeicher at 1,782 m under the Hochfeiler. The dam-crest car park fills from 10:30 in August; the lower Zamsergrund lot is the overflow and adds a 15-minute walk.
itinerary.evening: Return to Mayrhofen. The light on the Schlegeis is better at 17:00 anyway.
itinerary.dayStats: 120 km · 3h10 driving · 2 toll roads, 0 through-passes · max altitude 2,020 m.

itinerary.title: Gerlos Alpenstrasse to the Pinzgau
itinerary.morning: Head up the Gerlos valley on the B165 and pay the **Gerlos Alpenstrasse** toll (approx. €12 per car) for the panorama section between Gerlospass, 1,507 m, and Krimml. This is the one you drive for the descent: the road swings out onto the Krimmler Achental with the falls in the windscreen. Use the signed Wasserfall-Blick layby rather than stopping on the carriageway.
itinerary.afternoon: Park at Krimml and walk the lower cascades of the Krimmler Wasserfälle (entry approx. €8; 45 minutes to the first platform). Then run the flat Salzach valley east through Mittersill.
itinerary.evening: Sleep at Bruck or Fusch, ten minutes from the Ferleiten toll gate. Fill the tank tonight; there is no fuel above the gate.
itinerary.dayStats: 130 km · 2h30 driving · 1 pass (Gerlospass) · max altitude 1,507 m.

itinerary.title: Grossglockner Hochalpenstrasse
itinerary.morning: Be at the **Ferleiten** gate by 07:00. The **Grossglockner Hochalpenstrasse** is 48 km from Bruck to Heiligenblut, 36 hairpins, gradients up to 12%, and a day ticket of approx. €46.50 per car (motorcycles around €31). Gates open 05:30 in high summer and close to uphill traffic in the evening — roughly 21:00 in July, earlier from September; the road is shut overnight. Climb through Piffkar and Hochmais to **Fuscher Törl** at 2,428 m.
itinerary.afternoon: Take the 1.7 km cobbled spur to **Edelweissspitze**, 2,571 m — the highest point you can drive to on the road. It is narrow, one-and-a-bit lanes, with a small circular car park that holds perhaps forty cars and no turning room for anything long; if there is a queue at the bottom, come back after 16:00. Then Hochtor tunnel at 2,504 m and the branch road to **Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe**, 2,369 m, facing the Pasterze glacier. Its multi-storey Parkdeck genuinely fills between 10:30 and 15:00 in August, after which traffic is turned back at Guttal; arriving before 09:30 or after 16:00 solves it.
itinerary.evening: Drop to Heiligenblut, 1,301 m, and look back at the Glockner from the churchyard of St. Vinzenz.
itinerary.dayStats: 75 km · 3h30 driving · 2 passes (Hochtor, Fuscher Törl) · max altitude 2,571 m.

itinerary.title: Second crossing, then north to the Ötztal
itinerary.morning: Keep yesterday's ticket: the road sells a discounted second run within a set window, so cross northbound early while the Fuscher Lacke is still glassy.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to Bruck, then Zell am See, over **Pass Thurn** at 1,274 m to Kitzbühel, and along the B170 to Wörgl. Rejoin the A12 west past Innsbruck and turn up the B186 Ötztalstrasse at Ötztal-Bahnhof.
itinerary.evening: Arrive Sölden, 1,368 m, for two nights. Hotel garages are standard; street parking is scarce.
itinerary.dayStats: 295 km · 4h45 driving · 3 passes (Hochtor, Fuscher Törl, Pass Thurn) · max altitude 2,571 m.

itinerary.title: Timmelsjoch and the Jaufen loop
itinerary.morning: Drive south past Zwieselstein to the **Timmelsjoch Hochalpenstrasse**. The Austrian toll is approx. €22 per car; the road opens roughly early June to mid-October, runs 07:00–20:00 only, and is closed to vehicles over 3.5 t and to caravans in either direction. The Austrian ramp is smooth and wide; the summit at 2,509 m carries the Passmuseum, and the Italian descent to Moos in Passeier is the tight one — narrow, unlit tunnels and pitches to 13%.
itinerary.afternoon: Coffee in St. Leonhard in Passeier, then the **Jaufenpass**, 2,094 m, a free, well-graded South Tyrolean pass with 44 bends, into Sterzing/Vipiteno. Return north over the **Brennerpass**, 1,370 m. Take the free SS12/B182 over the top rather than the A22–A13 if you would rather look at Gossensass than pay the Brenner motorway's separate special toll on the Austrian side.
itinerary.evening: Back down the Wipptal to Sölden. This is the longest sustained mountain day of the week.
itinerary.dayStats: 215 km · 5h00 driving · 3 passes (Timmelsjoch, Jaufenpass, Brenner) · max altitude 2,509 m.

itinerary.title: Silvretta Hochalpenstrasse and out
itinerary.morning: Option A, and the better one if the day is clear: drive to the top of the **Ötztaler Gletscherstrasse** above Sölden — toll approx. €22, gates 07:00–17:00 — which reaches the Rettenbachferner car park at 2,829 m, the highest paved point in Austria. Then descend and run the Inn valley west to Landeck.
itinerary.afternoon: South from Landeck up the Paznaun to Galtür, then onto the **Silvretta Hochalpenstrasse**: 34 hairpins and gradients to 12% toward the Bielerhöhe. The lower Partenen ramp on the Vorarlberg side has been shut for rockfall barrier works since 2024 and stays closed until summer 2030, so in 2026 the road is driven as a toll-free there-and-back from Galtür (reopens for the season on 4 June) as far as the Vermuntsee. The Bielerhöhe at 2,032 m sits above the turquoise Silvretta-Stausee, with the Piz Buin behind it.
itinerary.evening: Retrace the Paznaun through Ischgl to Landeck, then back to Innsbruck.
itinerary.dayStats: 280 km · 4h45 driving · 2 passes (Bielerhöhe, plus the Gletscherstrasse spur) · max altitude 2,829 m.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Kramerwirt
accommodationStrategy.description: A centuries-old carved-timber Gasthof in the middle of Mayrhofen with its own garage, which matters because village surface parking is short-stay and enforced.
accommodationStrategy.booking: March for July and August.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Senger
accommodationStrategy.description: An old shingled Kärntner farmhouse minutes below the Glockner road's southern gate, with parking on site and breakfast early enough to make the 07:00 barrier.
accommodationStrategy.booking: four months ahead; Heiligenblut has few beds.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: €150–€230 per night for two, usually half board

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Regina
accommodationStrategy.description: Central Sölden, with an underground garage and both the Timmelsjoch and Gletscherstrasse gates ten minutes away. Summer rates here are a fraction of winter ones.
accommodationStrategy.booking: six weeks ahead in summer.

logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European. Austrian alpine rescue is **140**. Mountain-road breakdowns are recovered by ÖAMTC on 120.
logistics.weather: Afternoon storms build over the Hohe Tauern from about 14:00 in July and August. Check GeoSphere before the Glockner day and drive the high sections in the morning.

other.label: Vignette
other.text: A digital Vignette is compulsory on all Austrian Autobahnen and Schnellstrassen: roughly €13 for 10 days, €32 for two months, €107 for the year in 2026. Buy it from the ASFINAG shop or app, where it activates immediately; third-party resellers can impose a statutory withdrawal delay before validity begins. Rental cars from Austrian branches normally carry one — confirm at the desk.

other.label: Special tolls are separate
other.text: The Vignette buys nothing on the A13 Brenner, the A10 Tauern and Katschberg tunnels, the S16 Arlberg tunnel or the Felbertauerntunnel; each charges its own barrier fee. The five private mountain roads are separate again.

other.label: Cross-border and rentals
other.text: Austrian rentals allow Germany, Italy, Switzerland and Liechtenstein; several restrict travel further east, and cross-border fees of €25–€70 are normal. One-way drops abroad — Innsbruck to Munich — start around €100. Declare the Italy leg.

other.label: Emergencies
other.text: 112 pan-European. Austrian alpine rescue is **140**. Mountain-road breakdowns are recovered by ÖAMTC on 120.

other.label: Opening-hour traps
other.text: Grossglockner, Silvretta, Timmelsjoch, Schlegeis and the Gletscherstrasse all close their gates overnight; above a gate at closing you may descend but not re-enter. Village supermarkets shut at 18:00 and all Sunday.

other.label: Drone rule
other.text: Hohe Tauern National Park and the Grossglockner road prohibit drone launches; fines are real and the road company enforces them at Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe.

proTips: Buy the Grossglockner day ticket and use it twice. The road's discounted second-run ticket, taken the following morning, gives you the whole thing in reverse light for a fraction of the price.
The Edelweissspitze spur is the first thing to jam. Do it on the way *down* on your second Glockner crossing, not on the way up on your first.
Timmelsjoch's toll booth is on the Austrian side only. If you approach from Italy on a return leg you pay nothing, so plan the loop clockwise.
Fuel is cheapest in the valley towns — Zell am Ziller, Mittersill, Landeck. There is no fuel on any of the five toll roads, and Sölden's stations close early.

raw.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 1,350 km; sustained alpine hairpins, gradients to 14%, max altitude 2,829 m
raw.Who It Suits: Drivers who enjoy the driving, plus passengers who like glaciers and cake

typeSpecific.surface: approx. 1,350 km; sustained alpine hairpins, gradients to 14%, max altitude 2,829 m
typeSpecific.audience: Drivers who enjoy the driving, plus passengers who like glaciers and cake

packingNotes: Polarising filter or sunglasses that kill glacier glare; the Pasterze at midday is brutal.
A fleece and a windproof — Edelweissspitze at 2,571 m can be 12°C colder than Mayrhofen.
Coins and small notes for barrier machines and Alm lunches.
Comfortable shoes for the Krimml falls and the Gamsgrubenweg; both involve wet rock.
Motion-sickness remedy for back-seat passengers. Thirty-six hairpins is not a metaphor.
whatCouldGoWrong: **A toll road opens late — or stays shut.** Snow can keep the Timmelsjoch shut into mid-June, and the Silvretta's Vorarlberg (Partenen) ramp is closed for construction until 2030, so 2026 access is Galtür-side only. Fallback: substitute the Kaunertaler Gletscherstrasse, which opens earlier and reaches 2,750 m, or run the Achensee and Kühtai loops instead.
**Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe car park is full.** Traffic is turned around at Guttal. Fallback: continue over Hochtor to Heiligenblut, drop the bags, and come back up in the evening on the same ticket.

**Rental refuses Italy.** Some Austrian franchises exclude it or charge on the spot. Fallback: skip Jaufen and Brenner, drive Timmelsjoch to the summit and back down, and add the Kühtaisattel on the return.
**Overnight gate closure catches you out.** Fallback: Heiligenblut, Galtür and Sölden all sit *below* their respective barriers — plan every night's bed on the valley side of a gate, never above one.

trips.title: Orpheus Country: A Rhodope and Rila Driving Loop from Plovdiv to Sofia

bestPeriod.window: late May to late June for green meadows and full waterfalls, then mid-September to mid-October for colour and empty roads
bestPeriod.avoid: August (Pamporovo and Velingrad full, Trigrad gorge coach traffic) and December–March, when Prevala and the Rila Lakes chairlift road are snowbound

accommodation.note: €230–€420 (€35–€60/night, guesthouses and small hotels)

transport.note: €250–€370 (compact rental €30–€48/day + ~60 L fuel + e-vignette)

activities.note: €60–€110 (caves, Snezhanka tower, Eagle's Eye shuttle, chairlift)

profile.difficultyNote: Moderate

trips.gatewayAirport: Fly into Sofia (SOF), 1 h 45 by A1 to Plovdiv, or Plovdiv (PDV) direct. Rail Sofia–Plovdiv 2 h. Drop the car in Sofia.
trips.currency: Euro (EUR) — sole legal tender since 1 February 2026; mandatory dual BGN display ended 8 August 2026
trips.summary: The Rhodopes are not dramatic in the alpine sense — long, dark, spruce-covered whalebacks with villages in the folds and a road that never stops turning. Then the mountain opens a hole in itself and a river…
trips.hook: The Rhodopes are not dramatic in the alpine sense — long, dark, spruce-covered whalebacks with villages in the folds and a road that never stops turning. Then the mountain opens a hole in itself and a river disappears into it. A week of caves, gorges, monasteries and mehana tables, driven at 45 km/h because that is the honest average, and finished on a chairlift above seven glacial lakes.

snapshot.Start / End: Plovdiv → Sofia (open loop, ~640 km)
snapshot.Getting there: Fly into Sofia (SOF), 1 h 45 by A1 to Plovdiv, or Plovdiv (PDV) direct. Rail Sofia–Plovdiv 2 h. Drop the car in Sofia.

itinerary.title: Plovdiv, and the oldest street in Europe
itinerary.morning: Collect the car, then leave it. Walk the Old Town's cobbled ramps — Balabanov House, Hindliyan House, the Roman Theatre of Philippopolis still used for opera.
itinerary.afternoon: The Roman Stadium under Dzhumaya Square, then Kapana, the craft quarter, for coffee. Climb **Bunardzhika** — the Hill of the Liberators — for the Alyosha monument and the whole Thracian plain at your feet.
itinerary.evening: Dinner of *shopska*, *kavarma* and Mavrud from the Asenovgrad slopes at **Gostilnitsa Chuchura** in the Old Town [VERIFY: current hours]. Confirm the BGTOLL vignette is live on your plate before bed.
itinerary.dayStats: 0 km

itinerary.title: Bachkovo, then the Vacha road
itinerary.morning: **Bachkovo Monastery**, founded 1083 by the Georgian brothers Bakuriani — Bulgaria's second largest, with a 12th-century ossuary and the Virgin Eleusa icon. Buy monastery honey and *katmi* pancakes at the stalls outside.
itinerary.afternoon: North to Krichim, then the reservoir road up the Vacha: 40 km of bends between the Vacha and Devin dams, tunnels, no signal. Arrive **Devin**, a spa town on hot mineral water.
itinerary.evening: Soak in a Devin hotel pool fed by the town springs, then dinner of *cheverme* lamb and *patatnik*, the Rhodopean grated-potato cake that is the region's real signature dish.

itinerary.title: The Devil's Throat and the underworld
itinerary.morning: Drive the gorge into **Trigrad** at 20 km/h. **Dyavolsko Garlo — the Devil's Throat Cave** — swallows the Trigrad river whole: Bulgaria's tallest underground waterfall, about 42 m, in a cathedral-sized hall, with 301 steps cut in rock as the way out. Tradition puts **Orpheus's descent to the underworld** here, and debris thrown in never reappears at the resurgence.
itinerary.afternoon: Back to Teshel, then the **Buynovo gorge** to **Yagodina Cave** — five levels, about 10 km surveyed, a 1,100 m show route at a constant 6°C. Bring a fleece [VERIFY: current hours and ticket price].
itinerary.evening: Take the 4x4 shuttle from Yagodina up the rough forest track to the **Eagle's Eye** platform for sunset over the gorge, then a village guesthouse dinner.
itinerary.dayStats: 65 km / 2 h

itinerary.title: Shiroka Laka and the bagpipe
itinerary.morning: **Shiroka Laka**: white Rhodopean houses with black timber, the Church of the Assumption of 1834 built in 38 days, and the **National School of Folk Arts**, where teenagers learn the **kaba gaida** — the deep-toned Rhodopean bagpipe, longer-droned and a fourth lower than the thin Thracian gaida.
itinerary.afternoon: Over to **Smolyan** for the **Smolyan Lakes** on the town's northern edge — around eight of an original twenty survive — and the Regional Historical Museum's Thracian and folk-costume rooms.
itinerary.evening: Up to **Momchilovtsi**, a ridge village at 1,200 m famous for yoghurt exported to China, for dinner and the best village views in the Rhodopes.

itinerary.title: Snezhanka, then west to Batak
itinerary.morning: Over the **Prevala** saddle to **Pamporovo** and the walk to the **Snezhanka** tower at 1,926 m — 153 steps to the platform, and on a clear morning the Aegean ridge lines of Greek Thrace [VERIFY: current tower hours].
itinerary.afternoon: Long drive via Devin and Dospat across the **Yavorovets** watershed to **Batak**. Visit the Church of St Nedelya, the memorial to the 1876 Batak massacre — a hard, necessary hour that explains Bulgarian nineteenth-century politics better than any museum.
itinerary.evening: Batak reservoir or on to **Velingrad**. Eat trout from the Batak dam, grilled plain with lemon.

itinerary.title: Velingrad springs to the Rila valley
itinerary.morning: **Velingrad**, the self-styled spa capital of the Balkans: the **Kleptuza** karst spring in the town park pushes out cold water beside eighty-odd hot mineral springs. Ninety minutes in a mineral pool before a long drive.
itinerary.afternoon: The Yundola plateau road to Razlog, the **Predel pass** (1,140 m) with the Pirin wall on your left, then Simitli, Kocherinovo and 22 km up the Rilska river to **Rila Monastery**, UNESCO-listed since 1983.
itinerary.evening: Sleep in a monastery cell or the guesthouses in Pastra below. After the coaches leave at 18:00, the striped arcades and **Hrelyo's Tower** of 1335 are yours [VERIFY: current monastery cell rates and check-in cut-off].

itinerary.title: Seven Lakes, then Sofia
itinerary.morning: Early liturgy in the Nativity church, then drive to Sapareva Banya and up to **Panichishte**. The chairlift from **Pionerska hut** lifts you to about 2,100 m by the Rilski Ezera hut.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the cirque: Dolnoto, Ribnoto, Trilistnika, Bliznaka, Babreka, **Okoto** — the deepest cirque lake in Bulgaria at roughly 37.5 m — and **Salzata** at 2,535 m. Three to four hours round trip on rough path; the lakes freeze into June some years.
itinerary.evening: Down the E79 to Sofia, return the car, and finish with *shkembe* or grilled Rhodopean sausage in the Kapana-style bars around Ulitsa Shishman.

accommodationStrategy.name: Rhodopean guesthouse
accommodationStrategy.description: stone-and-timber houses on the Shirokolashka river, wood stoves, *mekitsi* and sheep's yoghurt for breakfast, and hosts who will arrange a bagpipe evening. Parking is on the road — take the compact.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct by phone or Booking.com, 2–3 weeks ahead; the March *Pesponedelnik* kukeri festival fills the village a year out.

accommodationStrategy.name: Rila Monastery cells / Pastra guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: the only way to see the courtyard empty. Cells are spartan — no heating in shoulder season, curfew, cash on arrival.
accommodationStrategy.booking: monastery cells by phone only, 3–4 weeks ahead; keep a Pastra guesthouse as backup.

accommodationStrategy.name: Spa Hotel Persenk
accommodationStrategy.description: enclosed parking, thermal mineral pools fed by Devin's own springs and a restaurant that stays open late — the kind of reset night this drive needs, and Devin sits exactly where the Trigrad and Dospat legs meet. Consistently the highest-rated hotel in the town.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct or via the usual portals, 2 weeks ahead.

logistics.connectivity: A1 and Yettel cover towns and the main roads; expect nothing in the Trigrad and Buynovo gorges or on the Vacha reservoir road. Download offline maps.
logistics.emergency: 112. Mountain rescue is the Bulgarian Red Cross Mountain Rescue Service (PSS); on the Rila lakes carry the hut's number and tell someone your route.
logistics.weather: Rhodope fog forms fast in the gorges and afternoon storms build over Rila from mid-June. The Seven Lakes cirque holds snow patches into July.
logistics.bookingWindows: Guesthouses 2–3 weeks; Rila cells 3–4 weeks; the car 4–6 weeks (manual transmission is the default and much cheaper).
logistics.money: Bulgaria has adopted the euro at the fixed rate of 1 EUR = 1.95583 BGN. Mandatory dual EUR/BGN display **ended on 8 August 2026**, so prices are now quoted in euro alone unless a shop chooses to keep the lev figure for reference; the lev itself ceased to be legal tender on 31 January 2026. Cards are widely taken in towns, but cave tickets, village guesthouses and monastery cells are often cash — carry €60–€80 in small notes.
logistics.transportRules: 50 km/h in towns, 90 outside, 140 on motorway. Dipped headlights compulsory year-round, day and night. Alcohol limit 0.5‰. Winter tyres or chains required 15 November–1 March.
logistics.permits: BGTOLL e-vignette on all national roads. Caves are guided-entry only, on fixed departures, with no photography inside some sections; Rila Monastery bans shorts and bare shoulders in the church.

proTips: Do the Devil's Throat on the **first tour of the day**. The hall's acoustics and the waterfall roar are ruined once three groups overlap, and the 301 steps are a bottleneck.
Sleep in Trigrad or Yagodina, not Devin, if you want the caves without the coach window. The villages are half the price of Pamporovo.
Ask your Shiroka Laka host for *"kaba gaida na zhivo"* — live bagpipe. Students and village players do informal evenings; it costs a round of rakia, not a ticket.
Drive the Trigrad gorge before 09:00 or after 17:00. Coach transfers run mid-morning and mid-afternoon, and that is when the single-track reversing happens.
At the Seven Lakes, walk **anti-clockwise to Salzata first**, then descend past Okoto. Everyone else goes the other way and you will meet the crowd head-on rather than travel inside it.
Rila Monastery is a two-hour day trip from Sofia for the coaches. Staying the night costs about the same as a Sofia hotel and buys you dawn in an empty courtyard.
Buy the vignette yourself on bgtoll.bg if you have any doubt. It takes three minutes, costs less than one fine, and the receipt is your evidence.

raw.Driving legs (km + realistic time): Plovdiv→Bachkovo 30 km/40 min (Asenovgrad, road 86); Bachkovo→Devin 105 km/2 h 30 via Krichim and the Vacha reservoir road; Devin→Trigrad 30 km/55 min; Trigrad→Yagodina 35 km/1 h (back to the Teshel junction, then the Buynovo gorge); Yagodina→Shiroka Laka 45 km/1 h 10; Shiroka Laka→Smolyan 25 km/35 min; Smolyan→Momchilovtsi 18 km/30 min; Smolyan→Pamporovo 16 km/25 min over the Prevala saddle; Pamporovo→Batak 120 km/2 h 40 via Devin and Dospat; Batak→Velingrad 35 km/45 min; Velingrad→Rila Monastery 150 km/2 h 45 via Yundola, Razlog, the Predel pass and Kocherinovo; Rila Monastery→Panichishte 70 km/1 h 40; Panichishte→Sofia 80 km/1 h 15.
raw.Passes and hairpins: The **Prevala** saddle between Smolyan and Pamporovo, around 1,600 m, is the loop's high road point and the first to ice [VERIFY: exact Prevala altitude]. The **Yavorovets** pass carries the Devin–Dospat road over the watershed [VERIFY: Yavorovets altitude and surface]. The Shiroka Laka–Pamporovo climb stacks roughly twenty-five hairpins in 12 km; the Vacha reservoir road runs 40 km of continuous bends with no straight over 300 m. **Predel** (1,140 m) is the only fast pass on the trip.
raw.Honest width warning: The road into **Trigrad** narrows to effectively single-track between the gorge walls — around 3.5 m at the tightest point, with short unlit rock-cut tunnels, no barrier on the river side and passing places every few hundred metres. Fine in a hatchback at 20 km/h; genuinely unpleasant in a large SUV or campervan, and when a coach comes the other way somebody reverses. The Buynovo gorge road to Yagodina is comparable.
raw.Car rental and vignette: Bulgaria's vignette is fully electronic — bought by number plate through **BGTOLL** (bgtoll.bg, the app, or any petrol-station terminal). No sticker; ANPR cameras enforce it. One-day, weekend, weekly, monthly, quarterly and annual products exist; from **1 August 2026** the car (≤3.5 t) tariff is **one day €5.30, weekend €6.60, week €10.00, month €19.90, quarter €35.90, year €64.50** — a 30% rise on the previous rates, so budget the week's vignette at ten euros rather than the older seven. Rentals normally come vignetted — confirm the plate is registered. Cross-border: most Bulgarian rentals allow Greece and Romania with a Green Card and a fee (€30–€60); **North Macedonia, Serbia and Türkiye are usually excluded or need written authorisation**, with extra insurance bought at the Turkish border.
raw.Fuel: Real gaps up here. Fill in **Devin**, **Smolyan** or **Dospat** and never drop below a quarter tank: no fuel in Trigrad, Yagodina, Shiroka Laka or Momchilovtsi, and Devin–Dospat is 60 km of empty forest road.
raw.Viewpoints: The **Eagle's Eye (Orlovo Oko)** glass platform at about 1,563 m above the Buynovo gorge; the **Snezhanka** TV tower at 1,926 m above Pamporovo; the Rozhen meadows above Momchilovtsi; the Hrelyo's Tower courtyard at Rila; the chairlift top station above the Seven Lakes cirque.
