trips.title: Route des Grandes Alpes — Lake Geneva to the Mediterranean

bestPeriod.note: Iseran and Galibier normally open between late May and mid-June and close with the first heavy snow in late October; the full route is only continuous in that window.

basecamps: Thonon-les-Bains to Menton, one night per stage
trips.gatewayAirport: Genève (GVA), out from Nice (NCE)
trips.summary: The classic 720 km traverse from Lake Geneva to Menton across sixteen cols, driven north to south in seven stages with the light behind you.
trips.hook: Sixteen cols, two national parks and a finish where the last hairpin drops into lemon trees. The Route des Grandes Alpes is a signposted itinerary, not a motorway, and it rewards short days: 100 km of Savoyard hairpins takes longer than 300 km of autoroute and leaves you far more tired.

snapshot.Base(s): La Clusaz, Bourg-Saint-Maurice, Valloire, Guillestre, Isola, Sospel
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 775 km; sixteen cols, sustained 7–10% gradients, max altitude 2,764 m
snapshot.Getting There: Fly into Genève (GVA), pick up on the French sector, drop at Nice (NCE)
snapshot.Who It Suits: Confident drivers; not for nervous passengers or anyone towing

itinerary.title: Léman to the Aravis
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at Geneva airport's **French sector**. This matters: the French side has its own arrivals hall and car-hire desks, and hiring there keeps you out of Switzerland entirely, so no Swiss motorway vignette and no cross-border clause. Drive to Thonon-les-Bains on the lake shore, the official kilometre zero.
itinerary.afternoon: Up the Dranse valley on the D902 to Morzine and over the **Col des Gets** (1,163 m), an easy wooded opener with gentle gradients. Down to Taninges and Cluses, then the **Col de la Colombière** (1,618 m), where the last 2 km hit 10% under the Aiguille de Pointe Percée.
itinerary.evening: Sleep at Le Grand-Bornand or La Clusaz. Both have free village parking outside July and August.
itinerary.dayStats: 135 km · 3h00 driving · 2 cols · max altitude 1,618 m.

itinerary.title: Aravis, Saisies and the Cormet
itinerary.morning: The **Col des Aravis** (1,486 m) opens with the Mont Blanc massif framed dead ahead from the chapel at the summit — the best free viewpoint of the first half. Down to Flumet.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Col des Saisies** (1,650 m) is broad, grassy and undramatic; the payoff is the **Cormet de Roselend** (1,968 m) beyond Beaufort. Stop at the Barrage de Roselend layby above the turquoise reservoir, then again at the Plan de la Laie. The descent to Bourg-Saint-Maurice is 20 km of tight, unguarded hairpins — take it slowly and use engine braking.
itinerary.evening: Bourg-Saint-Maurice, 840 m. Buy Beaufort AOP cheese from the cooperative in Beaufort on the way through; it will not survive to Menton, which is the point.
itinerary.dayStats: 95 km · 2h40 driving · 3 cols · max altitude 1,968 m.

itinerary.title: Col de l'Iseran
itinerary.morning: Up the Tarentaise on the D902 through Sainte-Foy and Val-d'Isère to the **Col de l'Iseran**, 2,764 m — the highest paved pass in France. Opening is typically late May to mid-June and closure is late October; the Savoie département publishes daily status, and a June opening does not mean a June without snow banks. Gradients are steady at 6–7% but the air at the top is thin and the wind is constant.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend to **Bonneval-sur-Arc**, a stone-and-lauze village in the Vanoise with cars banned from the core — park at the entrance lot. Then down the Maurienne through Lanslebourg and Modane.
itinerary.evening: Turn up to **Valloire** via Saint-Michel-de-Maurienne and the **Col du Télégraphe** (1,566 m), a 12 km wooded climb averaging 7%. Fill the tank in Modane: there is no fuel between here and Briançon on the pass route.
itinerary.dayStats: 130 km · 3h30 driving · 2 cols · max altitude 2,764 m.

itinerary.title: Galibier and Izoard
itinerary.morning: The **Col du Galibier**, 2,642 m, from Valloire: 18 km at an average of about 7%, with the final kilometre above the tunnel at 10–12%. The summit road over the top is the scenic option; the 1891 tunnel beneath it is narrow, single-file by lights and closed in poor weather. Galibier normally opens in early June. Summit parking is a handful of bays either side — it is a stop-and-go place, not a picnic spot.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to the **Col du Lautaret** (2,058 m), which stays open most of the winter and carries the Jardin Alpin botanical garden. Then Briançon, and up the **Col d'Izoard** (2,360 m). The southern descent through the **Casse Déserte** — a lunar scree bowl with the Coppi and Bobet memorial — is the single most photographed stretch of the route. Park in the marked bays, not on the shoulder.
itinerary.evening: Down the Guil to Château-Ville-Vieille and Guillestre.
itinerary.dayStats: 105 km · 3h20 driving · 3 cols · max altitude 2,642 m.

itinerary.title: Vars and the Bonette
itinerary.morning: The **Col de Vars** (2,109 m) climbs out of Guillestre in wide, well-surfaced curves past the Refuge Napoléon, one of the chain of shelters ordered along these cols in 1854. Descend to Barcelonnette in the Ubaye, an alpine town with Mexican villas built by returning emigrants.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Col de la Bonette**, 2,715 m, with the loop road around the **Cime de la Bonette** at 2,802 m — the highest asphalt in France, though the pass itself is lower than the Iseran. The loop is narrow, unguarded and single-track in places, with no barrier on the drop side. Open roughly June to October.
itinerary.evening: Down the Tinée to Isola. The valley road runs through rockfall galleries and is dark by 19:00 in September.
itinerary.dayStats: 140 km · 3h50 driving · 2 cols plus the Cime loop · max altitude 2,802 m.

itinerary.title: Saint-Martin, Turini and the Mercantour edge
itinerary.morning: Down the Tinée to Saint-Sauveur, then up the **Col Saint-Martin** (1,500 m) into the Valdeblore. Larch forest, hairpins, almost no traffic — the quietest driving of the week.
itinerary.afternoon: Drop into the Vésubie at Saint-Martin-Vésubie, then climb the D70 to the **Col de Turini** (1,607 m) through 34 numbered bends of beech forest. This is the Monte-Carlo Rally's night stage; drive it as if it is not. Descend to Moulinet and Sospel.
itinerary.evening: Sospel, 350 m, on the Bévéra with its tolled medieval bridge. Mediterranean air arrives suddenly here — olives, cicadas, a 20°C swing from this morning.
itinerary.dayStats: 120 km · 3h30 driving · 2 cols · max altitude 1,607 m.

itinerary.title: Castillon and the sea
itinerary.morning: The **Col de Castillon** (706 m) is the last one, a short green climb through the Alpes-Maritimes hinterland. Then the descent to **Menton**, where the route officially ends at the seafront. Swim, then buy citrons de Menton at the covered Marché des Halles.
itinerary.afternoon: The 30 km along the coast to Nice can be done on the Basse Corniche for the views or the A8 for speed. The A8 is tolled — roughly €4–€5 for this stretch — and Nice sits inside a low-emission zone requiring a Crit'Air sticker.
itinerary.evening: Drop the car at Nice airport. Refuel before the terminal: airport-adjacent stations charge a heavy premium.
itinerary.dayStats: 70 km · 1h40 driving · 1 col · max altitude 706 m.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel A la Pastourelle
accommodationStrategy.description: Inside a protected Vanoise village where cars stay at the edge, which means silence after the day-trippers leave and a 30-minute head start on the Iseran in the morning. Simple rooms, a kitchen that feeds walkers, and parking in the village lot ten minutes' walk away.
accommodationStrategy.booking: three months for July and August; the village has very few beds.

accommodationStrategy.name: Refuge Napoléon
accommodationStrategy.description: One of the 1850s shelters built along the imperial road, now run as a mountain inn at 2,109 m with a bar, dormitories and rooms. Sleeping on a col rather than in the valley gives you the pass at dawn and at dusk with no traffic on it.
accommodationStrategy.booking: two months; it closes outside the summer window.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: €80–€130 per night for two, half board typical

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel des Étrangers
accommodationStrategy.description: A long-established hotel in the last valley town before the coast, with its own parking and a pool — which after six days of hairpins is not a frivolity. Ten minutes from the Col de Castillon and forty from Nice airport.
accommodationStrategy.booking: six weeks.

logistics.emergency: 112 everywhere. Mountain rescue is the PGHM, reached through 112. Give a GPS position; valley names repeat across départements.

other.label: Tolls
other.text: France charges **péage** on autoroutes only; every col here is free. You meet péage on the A8 near Nice and, if used, the A40/A41 approach — take a ticket, pay on exit by card. Mont-Blanc and Fréjus tunnels are separate and expensive; neither is needed.

other.label: Crit'Air
other.text: France's air-quality sticker is compulsory in the low-emission zones of Nice, Grenoble, Lyon and Aix-Marseille, and during pollution episodes elsewhere. It costs about €4 from certificat-air.gouv.fr and takes days to arrive by post — order before you fly, or confirm the rental already carries one.

other.label: Rental and drop fees
other.text: Picking up in Geneva's French sector avoids the Swiss annual motorway vignette (CHF 40, no short-term option) and Swiss cross-border clauses. A Geneva-to-Nice one-way drop typically runs €150–€400; a same-country drop from Annecy or Lyon is cheaper. Italy is 15 km from Menton — check the contract if you plan to cross.

other.label: Pass status
other.text: Départements publish live col openings: Savoie for Iseran and Galibier, Hautes-Alpes for Izoard and Vars, Alpes-Maritimes for Bonette and Turini. Check the morning of, not the week before.

other.label: Emergencies
other.text: 112 everywhere. Mountain rescue is the PGHM, reached through 112. Give a GPS position; valley names repeat across départements.

other.label: Fuel
other.text: The route has real gaps. Fill in Cluses, Bourg-Saint-Maurice, Modane, Briançon, Barcelonnette and Saint-Étienne-de-Tinée. Nothing on Iseran, Galibier, Izoard or Bonette, and mountain stations close at 19:00 and on Sunday afternoons.

other.label: Opening-hour traps
other.text: Village restaurants stop lunch at 13:30 and dinner at 21:00, and many close Sunday evening and Monday. Buy bread by 12:00.

proTips: Drive north to south. The sun sits behind you on the southern descents, the gradients suit the loaded car better, and you finish at sea level in warm weather rather than climbing into cold.
Be on the Iseran and the Galibier before 09:30. Cyclists, camper vans and coaches all bunch between 10:00 and 16:00, and the summit car parks hold very few vehicles.
The Galibier tunnel is the bad-weather bypass, not the shortcut. If it is shut and the summit road is open you have lost nothing; if the summit is shut the tunnel usually is too.
At the Casse Déserte on Izoard, stop at the *second* layby heading south. The first is the busy one; the second frames the Coppi–Bobet memorial with the pinnacles behind.
If Bonette is shut, the **Col de la Cayolle** (2,326 m) is the parallel option from Barcelonnette to Guillaumes and rejoins the route near Beuil.

raw.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 775 km; sixteen cols, sustained 7–10% gradients, max altitude 2,764 m
raw.Who It Suits: Confident drivers; not for nervous passengers or anyone towing

typeSpecific.surface: approx. 775 km; sixteen cols, sustained 7–10% gradients, max altitude 2,764 m
typeSpecific.audience: Confident drivers; not for nervous passengers or anyone towing

packingNotes: A jacket that works at 2,800 m in wind: the Cime de la Bonette can be 5°C in July while Menton is 30°C.
Swimwear packed at the top of the bag for day 7 — and for the Lac de Roselend if you are brave.
Sunglasses with real UV protection; high-col glare through a windscreen is punishing.
Motion-sickness tablets for passengers. The Turini descent alone has 34 numbered bends.
Paper map of the Alpes du Sud; signal fails in the Ubaye and upper Tinée.
Comfortable shoes for Bonneval-sur-Arc and the Jardin Alpin at Lautaret.
whatCouldGoWrong: **A col is closed by late snow or rockfall.** Fallback: the Maurienne and Durance valleys run parallel to almost the whole route; you can bypass Iseran via Modane and Galibier via the Lautaret with no backtracking.

**Overheating brakes on a long descent.** Fallback: use second gear from the summit, not the pedal, and pull into a layby if you smell them. The Cormet de Roselend and the Bonette are the two that punish riding the brakes.

**Rain and cloud on the big passes.** Fallback: swap the day — spend it in Briançon's Vauban upper town or Barcelonnette, and take the col the following morning. The route is short enough to absorb one lost day.

**The one-way drop fee comes as a surprise at Nice.** Fallback: confirm the fee in writing at pickup, and compare with returning to Geneva via the A51/A43, which is 6h30 of autoroute but sometimes cheaper than the drop.

activities.note: Mycenae, Epidaurus, Mystras, Olympia, Ancient Messene

profile.difficultyNote: 2 — driving-led, with steep stepped climbs at Monemvasia and Mystras and a hot 1 h at Mycenae

trips.gatewayAirport: ATH — Athens Eleftherios Venizelos; 120 km / 1 h 30 to Nafplio via the A6, A8 and A7
trips.summary: The Peloponnese is the best driving peninsula in Greece precisely because it is not an island: you can build a genuine loop with no ferries, and the terrain changes every ninety minutes. This week runs Venetian Nafplio, the Argolid's Bronze Age citadels, then over the Parnon range on the Kosmas road — a genuinely great mountain drive that almost nobody does — to Monemvasia's rock. The Mani follows: tower villages, Vathia's abandoned skyline, and the road's end at Cape Tenaro where the ancients placed an entrance to the underworld. You finish through Mystras's Byzantine ruins, the Messenian coast castles and Olympia. It suits people who like ancient sites but want the driving to be the connective tissue rather than a chore.

itinerary.title: Corinth Canal and Venetian Nafplio
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at ATH and take the A6/A8 west. Stop at the **Corinth Canal bridge** at Isthmia — park in the layby on the old national road, not the motorway, and walk out over the 90 m-deep cut.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue on the A7 to Nafplio. Park in the free lot by the port at the foot of Akronafplia — the old town's marble lanes are a de facto no-car zone. Walk up to the Palamidi fortress, or drive the road round the back if the 999 steps are too much in the heat.
itinerary.evening: Aperitivo on Syntagma Square, then dinner at Ta Fanaria under the bougainvillea on Staikopoulou — order the rooster in wine and the Nemea red.
itinerary.dayStats: 145 km / 1 h 50; tolls Elefsina €2.50, Isthmos €2.10, Spathovouni €2.95; Palamidi €8; free port parking.
itinerary.sleep: Amfitriti Pension, Nafplio — up on Akronafplia with parking and a full-town view.

itinerary.title: Mycenae, Epidaurus and the Argolid
itinerary.morning: Drive 25 km north to Mycenae. Be at the Lion Gate by 08:30; the site is unshaded and by 11:00 the coaches from the Athens day-trip circuit arrive. The Treasury of Atreus, 500 m down the road, is included.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross the Argolid to the Theatre of Epidaurus — 55 km on the EO70. The acoustics demonstration is real: have someone drop a coin on the orchestra floor while you sit in the top row. The Asklepieion sanctuary beyond it is usually empty.
itinerary.evening: Return to Nafplio via Ligourio. Dinner at Aiolos Tavern in the old town, or drive 12 km to Karathona beach for a swim first.
itinerary.dayStats: 130 km / 2 h 30 round trip; Mycenae €12, Epidaurus €12, combined Argolid ticket €20; no tolls on the EO70; parking free at both sites.

itinerary.title: The Kosmas road and the rock of Monemvasia
itinerary.morning: South on the coast road through Astros to Leonidio, a red-cliffed village at the mouth of the Dafnona gorge. Coffee in the plateia, then start the climb.
itinerary.afternoon: The Leonidio–Kosmas road is the day. Stop at **Elonis Monastery**, glued to a vertical red cliff 15 km up — there is a small car park and a short walk in. Continue to Kosmas at 1,150 m, a plane-tree village on the Parnon watershed, then descend through Geraki to the Laconian plain and Monemvasia.
itinerary.evening: Cross the causeway and walk into the lower town — cars are banned inside the walls and parking is on the mainland side or at the gate lot. Dinner at Matoula, the oldest taverna on the rock, on a terrace over the sea.
itinerary.dayStats: 200 km / 4 h 30; Kosmas 1,150 m; ~30 km of continuous mountain bends; no tolls; last reliable fuel at Leonidio and Molaoi.
itinerary.sleep: Kinsterna Hotel (a restored Byzantine mansion 8 km out, with parking) or Moni Emvasis inside the walls.

itinerary.title: Gytheio, Areopoli and into the deep Mani
itinerary.morning: Explore Monemvasia's upper town at first light — the ruined Agia Sofia on the summit plateau, reached by a stepped path, is empty before 09:00 and blazing after 11:00.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive west via Molaoi and Gytheio (lunch on the harbour at Saga) to Areopoli, capital of the Mani. **Fill the tank here.** Then continue south into the Deep Mani, a treeless limestone landscape of stone war towers.
itinerary.evening: Check into a tower guesthouse. Dinner in Areopoli at Barba Petros for goat and syglino (smoked pork).
itinerary.dayStats: 145 km / 2 h 45; Areopoli is the last dependable fuel southbound; road narrows to 1.5 lanes south of Areopoli.
itinerary.sleep: Antares Hotel or Tainaron Blue Retreat, Areopoli/Vathia — restored stone towers with off-street parking.

itinerary.title: Vathia, Cape Tenaro and the Diros caves
itinerary.morning: Drive the Diros Caves (Vlychada) — a 25-minute punt through a flooded cave system, one of the few genuinely unusual things in the Peloponnese. Book on arrival; it opens at 08:30 and queues by 11:00.
itinerary.afternoon: South to **Vathia**, a skyline of abandoned tower houses on a ridge — park on the road below, the village lanes are impassable. Then to **Cape Tenaro**: the road ends at a car park by the Agioi Asomatoi chapel, and a rocky 35-minute footpath leads past a Roman mosaic to the lighthouse at mainland Greece's southernmost point.
itinerary.evening: Return north to Areopoli or push to Kardamyli. Sunset from the Tenaro path looking west is the single best hour of the trip. Dinner at Elies, on the beach at Ritsa near Kardamyli.
itinerary.dayStats: 90 km / 2 h driving; Cape Tenaro walk 3 km return / 1 h 15; Diros Caves €20; no fuel south of Areopoli.
itinerary.sleep: Kalamitsi Hotel, Kardamyli — olive-grove grounds above its own cove, ample parking.

itinerary.title: Kardamyli, Mystras and Kalamata
itinerary.morning: Walk the Vyros gorge path from Old Kardamyli, or simply swim at Delfinia. Then drive the mountain crossing to Sparta over the **Taygetos**: the EO82 climbs to the Langada Pass at 1,524 m through a gorge of pine and rock — 60 km of continuous curves, one of the great Greek roads.
itinerary.afternoon: Mystras, the Byzantine city on the Taygetos foothills. Enter at the **upper gate**, walk down through the Pantanassa and Perivleptos churches to the lower gate, and take a taxi back up — the reverse costs you 250 m of ascent in the sun.
itinerary.evening: Back over Langada to Kalamata, or stay in the Sparta plain. Dinner at Kardamo in Kalamata for modern Messenian cooking.
itinerary.dayStats: 180 km / 3 h 45; Langada Pass 1,524 m; Mystras €12; Taygetos crossing has no fuel over 60 km.
itinerary.sleep: Elite City Resort, Kalamata — beachfront with underground parking; or Pharae Palace on the seafront.

itinerary.title: Ancient Messene, Methoni and Olympia
itinerary.morning: **Ancient Messene** at Mavrommati is the most underrated site in Greece — a fully excavated 4th-century BC city with an intact stadium and 9 km of walls, and often near-empty. Two hours.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to the coast for **Methoni**'s Venetian sea fortress and its octagonal Bourtzi tower on a causeway, then north up the Messenian coast. If time allows, Koroni's castle is 30 km east.
itinerary.evening: North to Olympia on the E55/EO9 for the Sanctuary of Zeus and the stadium — or, if you are flying out of ATH, take the A7 east from Kalamata and pay the €16.35 run back to Athens. Dinner in Olympia at Aegean.
itinerary.dayStats: 230 km / 4 h; Ancient Messene €10; Methoni castle €4; Olympia €12; Kalamata–Athens tolls €16.35 if returning.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Europa, Olympia (hilltop, pool, parking) — or departure from ATH.

accommodationStrategy.name: Amfitriti Pension
accommodationStrategy.description: Perched on Akronafplia above the old town with its own parking terrace, which solves Nafplio's real problem: the old town is marble-paved and effectively car-free, and the port lots fill by 19:00. Two nights here cover the entire Argolid without repacking. €90–€130 a double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Tainaron Blue Retreat
accommodationStrategy.description: A genuine 19th-century Maniot war tower converted with restraint, at the empty southern end of the peninsula, with parking on the lane below. Being based this far south turns the Cape Tenaro walk into a sunrise or sunset outing rather than a two-hour drive. €160–€240.

accommodationStrategy.name: Kalamitsi Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: Set in olive terraces above a private cove 2 km outside the village, with a large free car park — significant because Kardamyli's single main street has almost no parking and gets solid in September. Breakfast from 07:30 for an early Taygetos crossing. €120–€190.

logistics.connectivity: Greece is in the EU roaming zone. Coverage is good on the coast and on the A7, patchy in the Parnon interior and in parts of the Deep Mani. Download offline maps — several Mani coastal roads are mis-routed by nav apps onto tracks.
logistics.emergency: 112 across Greece. 166 for ambulance, 100 for police, 108 for the coastguard. Mountain rescue on Taygetos and Parnon is coordinated by the Hellenic Rescue Team via 112. Road assistance: ELPA 10400.
logistics.weather: The **meltemi** north wind blows hardest July–August and mainly affects the Aegean side; in the Mani it produces choppy seas and dust. Autumn brings sudden violent thunderstorms over Taygetos, and the Kosmas road is prone to rockfall after heavy rain. Summer inland temperatures at Mycenae and Olympia routinely exceed 38°C with no shade.
logistics.bookingWindows: Nothing here needs long lead times outside August, but Monemvasia's in-the-walls rooms (there are very few) sell out 2–3 months ahead for weekends. Epidaurus theatre performances in the July–August Athens & Epidaurus Festival require tickets months in advance. The Diros Caves cannot be pre-booked.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are accepted at hotels, motorway tolls and most tavernas, but rural Mani tavernas and small fuel stations are frequently cash-only. Keep €100 in cash south of Areopoli. Tipping is 5–10%, left in cash on the table.
logistics.transportRules: No vignette in Greece — tolls are open-barrier and paid per station. Seatbelts front and rear, headlights not required by day. Alcohol limit 0.05% (0.02% for new drivers). Speed cameras are rare but police speed traps on the A7 and the Kalamata approach are common; fines are payable within 10 days at a discount. Rental companies pass fines through with a €30–€50 admin fee.
logistics.permits: Archaeological sites are Ministry of Culture-run: standard hours 08:00–20:00 in summer, 08:30–15:30 in winter, with reduced-price and free-entry days. **Drones are banned over all archaeological sites** and require registration above 250 g. Free camping is illegal and enforced on Mani beaches. Do not remove stones or pottery from any site.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable in Nafplio, Kalamata and Sparta but brackish in the Mani — buy bottled south of Gytheio. Sea urchins are abundant on Mani rock entries; bring reef shoes. Vipers exist on Taygetos and Parnon but bites are very rare. Heat is the actual danger: carry 3 litres of water per person on site days and start every archaeological visit at opening.

proTips: Drive the **Kosmas road west to east** — Leonidio up, Geraki down. Climbing the gorge gives you the Elonis Monastery reveal head-on and puts the morning sun behind you rather than in the windscreen.
Do Mystras top-down. Enter at the upper (castle) gate, walk downhill through the churches to the lower gate, and take the €10 taxi back to your car. Almost everyone does it the exhausting way round.
Buy the **combined Argolid ticket (€20)** covering Mycenae, Epidaurus, Tiryns and the Nafplio museums. It is valid three days and saves roughly €20 per person over separate entries.
Fill the tank at Areopoli before going south, and again at Kalamata before the Taygetos crossing. These two fills eliminate the only genuine fuel anxiety on the loop.

Cape Tenaro's lighthouse path is uneven limestone and takes 35 minutes each way. Go for the last two hours of daylight: cooler, better light, and you get the sunset over the Ionian from the southernmost point of mainland Europe's eastern arm.
Monemvasia's upper town closes earlier than the lower town and is unshaded. Climb it at 08:00 with the gate keeper; by noon the stepped path is a furnace.

Skip the Rio–Antirrio bridge unless you genuinely need to leave the Peloponnese northwards — at €15.90 a car it is one of Europe's most expensive short crossings, and the parallel ferry costs about half.

Ancient Messene has no coach parking to speak of and no cruise-ship pipeline, which is why it is empty. Give it two hours, not the forty minutes most itineraries allow, and walk down into the stadium.
Greek tavernas in the Mani open for dinner at 20:00 and not before. Plan drives to finish by 19:00 and use the gap for a swim rather than circling a closed village square.

raw.Total distance: ~950 km over 7 days. Longest leg is Day 3, Nafplio–Monemvasia via Leonidio and Kosmas, at 200 km in a real 4 h 30 — the mountain section averages 40 km/h.
raw.Moreas motorway (A7), Corinth–Tripoli–Ka: open barrier tolls at Spathovouni €2.95, Nestani €2.80, Manari Bridge €2.30, Veligosti €1.45 and Kalamata €2.25. Athens–Kalamata end to end is **€16.35** for a car across 287 km, of which the A7 portion is €11.75. Payment by card or cash at the booth; the **e-Pass** transponder gives dedicated lanes and small discounts but is rarely worth it for a week.
raw.Rio–Antirrio bridge (Charilaos Trikoupis: **€15.90** for a car as of 1 January 2026 — expensive, and only relevant if you exit the Peloponnese northwards. The Rio–Antirrio ferry is a cheaper alternative at around €8.
raw.The Leonidio–Kosmas road (EO Leonidiou–G: the highlight drive. From sea level at Leonidio it climbs through the Dafnona gorge past the cliff-hung Elonis Monastery to the village of Kosmas at 1,150 m — roughly 30 km of sinuous, well-surfaced two-lane road with sheer drops, tunnels cut into red rock, and virtually no traffic. Occasional rockfall; do not drive it after heavy rain.
raw.The Mani's roads: the west-coast route from Kalamata through Kardamyli to Areopoli is a cliff corniche with tight blind bends and no barrier in places. South of Areopoli toward Vathia and Cape Tenaro the road narrows to 1.5 lanes with rough edges, occasional gravel and free-ranging goats. The final 1.5 km to the Tenaro lighthouse is a footpath, not a road.
raw.Fuel in the Mani: the genuine gap. There is fuel at Areopoli and Gytheio, and effectively nothing between Areopoli and Cape Tenaro (a 45 km round trip) or on the east Mani coast between Kotronas and Gytheio. Many rural stations close 14:00–17:00 and all day Sunday. Fill at Kalamata and again at Areopoli.
raw.Car rental & cross-border: irrelevant here — Greek rentals do not permit Albania, North Macedonia or Turkey without specific arrangement and a Green Card, and nothing on this route needs a border. One-way ATH-to-Kalamata drops run €80–€150. Take the smallest car you are comfortable with: Nafplio, Monemvasia and the Mani villages were built for donkeys.
raw.Driving culture: Greeks drive on the hard shoulder to let faster traffic pass — do the same, it is expected. Overtaking on solid lines is normal. Watch for unlit farm vehicles at dusk, goats on every mountain road, and the fact that rural crossroads frequently have no markings at all.

sources.verified: Moreas (A7) 2026 toll stations and prices — Spathovouni €2.95, Nestani €2.80, Manari €2.30, Veligosti €1.45, Kalamata €2.25, with Athens–Kalamata totalling €16.35 across 287 km and the Corinth–Tripoli–Kalamata A7 portion at €11.75 after the 1 January 2026 indexation; Rio–Antirrio bridge car toll of €15.90 from 1 January 2026; the absence of any Greek vignette system.
sources.confidenceNotes: Greek tolls are index-linked and were raised on 1 January 2026 — re-verify against mydiodia.gr before publishing, and note that further adjustments are announced each December. Archaeological site entry fees change with the Ministry of Culture's annual schedule and differ between summer and winter tariffs; the combined Argolid ticket's scope has changed before. The Leonidio–Kosmas road has no formal closure season but is subject to rockfall and occasional short closures after storms — no live status feed exists, so local enquiry is the only check. Fuel station opening hours in the Mani are informal and seasonal. Diros Caves opening hours and pricing should be re-confirmed; the site closes in rough sea conditions.

trips.title: The Western Arc: Seven Days from the Danube Bend to the Őrség
trips.subRegion: Transdanubia — Danube Bend, Bakony, Balaton Uplands, Őrség, Fertő

bestPeriod.window: the second half of May and the first three weeks of September — Balaton traffic gone, Őrség green, Badacsony cellars open
bestPeriod.avoid: mid-July to late August (Balaton gridlock on roads 71 and 76, and the Káli-medence villages full)

accommodation.note: €350–€600 (€50–€85/night, doubles in guesthouses and small hotels)

transport.note: €250–€380 (car hire €180–€280 + fuel ~€90 for ~870 km + e-matrica)

activities.note: €90–€150 (palaces, abbey, thermal lake, castles)

profile.difficultyNote: Easy

trips.gatewayAirport: Budapest Ferenc Liszt (BUD). Collect the car at the airport, not downtown — you avoid the city entirely on day 1 via the M0 and M2.
trips.summary: A loop of roughly 870 km through the half of Hungary nobody flies in for: basalt buttes standing over Balaton like broken teeth, a stone sea in a valley of six villages, a Benedictine archabbey on a hill that has…
trips.hook: A loop of roughly 870 km through the half of Hungary nobody flies in for: basalt buttes standing over Balaton like broken teeth, a stone sea in a valley of six villages, a Benedictine archabbey on a hill that has been occupied since 996, and a corner of the far west where wooden bell towers still stand over hamlets of ten houses. Mostly two-lane roads, short legs, long lunches. Easy driving, dense payoff.

snapshot.Start / End: Budapest → Budapest (loop, ~870 km)
snapshot.Getting there: Budapest Ferenc Liszt (BUD). Collect the car at the airport, not downtown — you avoid the city entirely on day 1 via the M0 and M2.

itinerary.title: The Danube turns
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at BUD, buy the 10-day e-matrica before you leave the forecourt, and take the M0/M2 north, dropping onto **road 11** at Szentendre. Follow the water through Leányfalu and Dömös — the river is on your right the whole way.
itinerary.afternoon: **Visegrád**: the Royal Palace of the Angevin kings in the town, then the hairpin up to the **fellegvár** citadel for the Danube Bend's defining view. The **Nagyvillám** lookout tower is two minutes further up the ridge road.
itinerary.evening: On to **Esztergom** and its basilica, the largest church in Hungary, on the hill above the Mária Valéria bridge to Slovakia. Climb the cupola before closing, then eat on Széchenyi tér.
itinerary.dayStats: 67 km / 1 h 30 driving

itinerary.title: Into the Bakony
itinerary.morning: South-west across the Transdanubian hills to **Zirc**, the Cistercian abbey town. The **Reguly Antal Műemlékkönyvtár**, the abbey's 1858 library hall, is the stop; the arboretum behind it is free to walk.
itinerary.afternoon: Detour to the **Cuha-völgy**, where the Győr–Veszprém railway threads a limestone gorge on viaducts and through tunnels. Park at Porva-Csesznek station and walk the marked riverside path an hour downstream — it is the prettiest hour of the Bakony.
itinerary.evening: **Bakonybél**, a village of 1,300 under Kőris-hegy with its own Benedictine monastery. Quiet to the point of silence; eat at the village *csárda* and sleep with the windows open [VERIFY: current opening hours of the Zirc abbey library].

itinerary.title: Tihany and the stone sea
itinerary.morning: Down to the lake and out onto the **Tihany peninsula**. The **Benedictine abbey** of 1055 holds the oldest surviving document containing Hungarian words; below it the Belső-tó crater lake sits 25 m above Balaton.
itinerary.afternoon: North into the **Káli-medence**, the basin of six villages. **Köveskál** and **Szentbékkálla** are the two to walk. Above Szentbékkálla lies the ***kőtenger*** — the "stone sea", a field of wind-sculpted Pannonian sandstone blocks scattered across open pasture, twenty minutes on foot from the village.
itinerary.evening: Stay in the basin. Dinner at **Kővirág** in Köveskál, one of the restaurants that made this valley's reputation — book ahead, it is small [VERIFY: current Kővirág opening days].

itinerary.title: Basalt, castle, thermal water
itinerary.morning: **Szent György-hegy** above Hegymagas: an hour up through vineyards to the basalt colonnade, organ pipes of columnar rock, with the whole western basin below.
itinerary.afternoon: **Badacsony**: the **Panoráma út** along the ridge, the **Kisfaludy** lookout, and a cellar for the *szürkebarát* and *kéknyelű* that only really grow here. Then **Szigliget**, castle on its cone, twenty minutes up from the village car park.
itinerary.evening: **Hévíz** — the largest biologically active thermal lake in the world, 38 m deep, water turning over roughly every 3 days, 33–35 °C in summer and swimmable in February. Float, don't swim; stay in no more than 90 minutes [VERIFY: current Hévíz day-ticket price].

itinerary.title: Festetics, then the far west
itinerary.morning: **Keszthely** and the **Festetics Palace**, 101 rooms of Baroque with the Helikon Library's carved oak interiors intact — one of the few Hungarian aristocratic houses whose contents survived 1945.
itinerary.afternoon: West on roads 71 and 76, then across Zala into **Vas** county. The landscape changes: hills close in, oak and chestnut replace vine, and villages fragment into ***szer*** — scattered clusters of farmsteads rather than a street.
itinerary.evening: **Szalafő** in the **Őrség**, seven hamlets strung across ridges. Base here. Dinner is local: buckwheat, *dödölle* potato dumplings, and pumpkin-seed oil poured on everything [VERIFY: current Festetics Palace ticket price].

itinerary.title: Bell towers and a walled town
itinerary.morning: **Pankasz**: the 1755 shingled wooden **bell tower**, a *kettős haranglába* on a bank above the road, the emblem of the Őrség. Then **Velemér**, whose 13th-century Romanesque church holds Johannes Aquila's 1378 frescoes — the light through the south windows is timed to the solstices.
itinerary.afternoon: North to **Kőszeg**, tight against the Austrian border under the Írottkő. Jurisics tér is a complete Renaissance square; the castle held Suleiman's army for 25 days in 1532 and the town bells still ring at 11:00 to mark it.
itinerary.evening: On to **Sopron**, the town that voted to stay Hungarian in 1921. Walk the Belváros horseshoe, climb the **Tűztorony** fire tower, and drink *kékfrankos* from the Sopron hills.

itinerary.title: Fertő, the archabbey, and home
itinerary.morning: East to **Fertő/Neusiedlersee**, a UNESCO cultural landscape shared with Austria — reed beds, a steppe lake barely 1.5 m deep. **Fertőd's Esterházy Palace** at Eszterháza, where Haydn worked for thirty years, is 27 km from Sopron.
itinerary.afternoon: **Pannonhalma Archabbey**, UNESCO-listed and founded in 996 — a working Benedictine community for over a thousand years, with a basilica, a 360,000-volume library and a herb garden. Entry is by **timed guided tour only**; book online [VERIFY: current Pannonhalma tour price and timings].
itinerary.evening: Drop to **Győr** for the Baroque Káptalandomb and an early dinner, then the M1 back to Budapest, 125 km and 1 h 20 with the vignette already on the plate.

accommodationStrategy.name: Kővirág
accommodationStrategy.description: eight rooms in a restored village house in the middle of the Káli-medence, walking distance to the Szentbékkálla trailhead, with the region's best-known kitchen downstairs so you do not drive after dinner — which matters at 0.0‰.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct or by email, 2–3 months ahead for May, June and September weekends.

accommodationStrategy.name: Bakonybél village guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: the only sensible base between the Danube Bend and Balaton, with free street parking, monastery bells instead of traffic, and trailheads for Kőris-hegy and the Gerence valley from the village edge.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–4 weeks ahead; several houses take bookings only by phone, so use a booking platform if your Hungarian is thin.

accommodationStrategy.name: Őrségi vendégház, Szalafő-Pityerszer
accommodationStrategy.description: you sleep inside the settlement pattern the whole region is famous for — a *szer* of a handful of houses on a ridge, with dark skies, and Pankasz and Velemér both within 20 minutes' drive.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4–6 weeks ahead; the Őrség has few beds and September fills first.

logistics.connectivity: 4G/5G is solid on the whole route including the Őrség; Hungary is inside EU roaming. Download offline maps anyway for the Bakony forest roads, where signal drops in the Cuha gorge.
logistics.emergency: **112** for everything. Motorway breakdown: use the orange SOS pillars rather than a mobile — they fix your location automatically. Carry the rental's assistance card.
logistics.weather: Balaton produces fast, violent squalls; the lake's storm-warning system flashes from shore towers (one rate of flashing = come closer to shore, faster = get off the water). On the road, expect standing water on the 71 and vineyard mud washed onto the Panoráma út.
logistics.bookingWindows: Pannonhalma tours and Káli-medence restaurants are the two hard constraints — both 4–8 weeks out for a weekend. Accommodation 3–6 weeks is generally enough outside July–August.
logistics.money: Forint. Cards work almost everywhere including village petrol stations, but carry 20,000–30,000 HUF (~€50–€75) in cash for cellar tastings, castle car parks and small *csárda*. Reject dynamic currency conversion at terminals; pay in HUF.
logistics.transportRules: **0.0‰ alcohol.** **Dipped headlights outside built-up areas at all times.** Vignette by plate before your first motorway metre. Winter tyres are not legally mandatory but are sensible before April. Parking in Balaton resort towns and Sopron's centre is paid by app or machine, typically 09:00–18:00 in season.
logistics.permits: No permits needed anywhere on this route. Drones are restricted over Pannonhalma, Fertőd and the national parks — check before flying. The Fertő-Hanság and Balaton-felvidéki national parks ask you to keep to marked paths off-season during breeding.

proTips: Buy the **national 10-day e-matrica**, never county vignettes. Two counties already exceed it and this route touches six.
Do the **Káli-medence on foot, not by car**. Park in Szentbékkálla, walk to the *kőtenger* and on to Köveskál, and you see the basin the way it is meant to be seen — the villages are 3–4 km apart.
Climb **Szent György-hegy before 09:00**. The basalt colonnade faces south-east and the light on it is gone by mid-morning, along with the parking at Hegymagas.

**Hévíz for 90 minutes, not a day.** The water is medicinal-strength; the recommended maximum immersion is about 30 minutes at a time, three times daily. Go at 08:00 when the surface steams and the coach parties have not arrived.
At Badacsony cellars, ask for ***kéknyelű*** by name. It is grown almost nowhere else on earth, it is not on export lists, and asking for it marks you as someone who did the reading.
Ask the Őrség guesthouse for ***tökmagolaj*** from a named local press rather than a supermarket bottle — the difference between cold-pressed pumpkin-seed oil and the industrial version is total.
Do **Pannonhalma on the way home, not as a day trip**. Book the last tour of the afternoon, then drive the flat M1 in the evening — the hardest 125 km of the loop become the easiest.

raw.Driving legs, km and time: Budapest → **Visegrád** 43 km / 1 h (road 11 along the water, not the M2). Visegrád → **Esztergom** 24 km / 30 min. Esztergom → **Zirc** 105 km / 1 h 40. Zirc → **Bakonybél** 20 km / 30 min. Bakonybél → **Tihany** 70 km / 1 h 15. Tihany → **Köveskál** 25 km / 35 min. Köveskál → **Badacsony** 20 km / 30 min. Badacsony → **Szigliget** 10 km / 15 min. Szigliget → **Hévíz** 30 km / 40 min. Hévíz → **Keszthely** 7 km / 12 min. Keszthely → **Szalafő** 115 km / 2 h. Szalafő → **Kőszeg** 85 km / 1 h 30. Kőszeg → **Sopron** 55 km / 1 h. Sopron → **Fertőd** 27 km / 30 min. Sopron → **Pannonhalma** 90 km / 1 h 20. Pannonhalma → **Győr** 21 km / 25 min. Győr → Budapest 125 km / 1 h 20 (M1).
raw.Vignette (e-matrica), 2026 category D1: 1-day **5,550 HUF** (~€14); 10-day **6,900 HUF** (~€17.50); monthly **11,170 HUF** (~€28); annual **61,760 HUF**. A county (*vármegyei*) annual vignette is **7,190 HUF** each — note that **two county vignettes already cost more than a national 10-day pass**, and this route crosses Pest, Komárom-Esztergom, Veszprém, Zala, Vas and Győr-Moson-Sopron. Buy the **10-day national** and stop thinking about it. Purchase at nemzetiutdij.hu, in the app, or at any large filling station; it is registered to the plate, there is no sticker, and enforcement is by camera.
raw.No passes, but real gradients: There is no alpine pass on this route. The climbs that matter are the **Panoráma út** ridge road above Badacsonytomaj, the switchbacks up to **Tihany** village, and the forest road over the Bakony between Zirc and Bakonybél. None close seasonally; all can be greasy after rain because of vineyard mud and beech leaf.
raw.Named viewpoints and laybys: **Visegrádi fellegvár** and the **Nagyvillám** tower over the Danube's turn; the **Badacsony kilátó** (Kisfaludy lookout) above the basalt columns; **Szent György-hegy** with its organ-pipe basalt colonnade, walk-up from Hegymagas; the **Panoráma út** laybys between Badacsonytomaj and Ábrahámhegy; **Szigliget castle** for the full sweep of the western basin; **Tihany's** Echo Hill and Belső-tó overlook; the **Pankasz** bell tower meadow in the Őrség.
raw.Cross-border rental rules: Hungarian rental fleets normally permit **Austria, Slovakia, Slovenia, Czechia, Croatia and Romania** as standard; each country needs **its own vignette** (Austria's Digitale Vignette, Slovenia's e-vinjeta, Slovakia's eZnámka) and a Hungarian one does not travel. **Serbia and Ukraine are usually excluded** outright, or need a written cross-border authorisation and a **Green Card** at a surcharge. Declare intent at pickup: crossing without authorisation voids the CDW [VERIFY: current cross-border fee at the major Budapest desks].
raw.The rules that catch foreigners: **Zero tolerance on alcohol: the limit is 0.0‰** — not 0.2, not a small beer with lunch, zero. **Dipped headlights are compulsory day and night outside built-up areas.** A hi-vis vest must be worn by the driver if you leave the car on a motorway or main road. Speed limits: 50 in villages, 90 on rural roads, 110 on dual carriageways, 130 on motorways, with fixed and mobile cameras common on road 71 along Balaton.

trips.title: Wild Atlantic Way: Dingle, Iveragh & the Burren
trips.subRegion: County Kerry & County Clare, Wild Atlantic Way

bestPeriod.window: May–June and September for long light, open attractions and manageable traffic; July–August is peak and the coach volume on Slea Head and the Ring of Kerry is significant
bestPeriod.raw: May–June and September for long light, open attractions and manageable traffic; July–August is peak and the coach volume on Slea Head and the Ring of Kerry is significant

accommodation.note: €120–220 per night, double; country-house hotels €250–400

food.note: €55–90 per day; a seafood dinner in Dingle €40–60

transport.note: €350–500: car hire €50–80 per day plus the Irish insurance excess, fuel, one Shannon ferry

activities.note: €90–200: Skellig or Blasket boats, Cliffs of Moher, Muckross House, distillery tours

languages: Irish — the Dingle peninsula west of Dingle town is a Gaeltacht where Irish is the daily language
trips.summary: A seven-day road trips & scenic drive itinerary in County Kerry & County Clare, Wild Atlantic Way, Ireland.

itinerary.title: Shannon or Kerry to Dingle
itinerary.morning: Land at Shannon or Kerry. Collect the car, and read the insurance excess paperwork properly before you sign — Irish CDW terms are their own genre. `verify: true`
itinerary.afternoon: Drive west to Dingle (An Daingean) via Tralee. Arrive with enough light to walk the harbour and Green Street.
itinerary.evening: Dingle is a town of about 2,000 people with an implausible density of good restaurants and pubs. Seafood dinner, then a session — traditional music happens nightly and starts around 21:30.
itinerary.dayStats: 150 km

itinerary.title: Slea Head Drive and the Blaskets
itinerary.morning: The Slea Head Drive loop west of Dingle: beehive huts (clocháns) from the early medieval period, the Gallarus Oratory — a dry-stone corbelled chapel still watertight after twelve centuries — and Dunquin pier's zigzag ramp down the cliff.
itinerary.afternoon: In settled weather, the Blasket Islands ferry from Dunquin to Great Blasket, evacuated in 1953 and the source of an extraordinary body of Irish-language literature. Otherwise the Blasket Centre on the mainland covers it superbly.
itinerary.evening: Back to Dingle. **Driving rule:** the loop is effectively one-way by convention — go clockwise, the way the coaches go, and you will never meet one head-on in a passing place.
itinerary.dayStats: 60 km, all day

itinerary.title: Conor Pass and south to Portmagee
itinerary.morning: The Conor Pass — 456 m, single track in places, cut into the cliff with a lake below and a waterfall you can climb to at the top. Not for camper vans, and genuinely alarming in fog.
itinerary.afternoon: South via Inch Strand — a 5 km sand spit into Dingle Bay — then over to the Iveragh peninsula and out along the Skellig Ring to Portmagee.
itinerary.evening: Portmagee, a single row of painted houses on the harbour. The pub here is the meeting point for the Skellig boatmen; dinner and a pint is also your weather briefing.
itinerary.dayStats: 140 km

itinerary.title: Skellig Michael or the Skellig Ring
itinerary.morning: If you have a landing permit and the sea is calm, the boat to **Skellig Michael** — a 6th-century monastery of stone beehive cells on a pyramid of rock 12 km offshore, 618 steps up, a UNESCO site with a strictly limited number of landing passes per day sold months in advance. It cancels often.
itinerary.afternoon: If not: the Skellig Ring by road — Kerry Cliffs (higher than the Cliffs of Moher and a fraction as busy), Valentia Island via the Portmagee bridge, the Geokaun mountain viewpoint, the tetrapod trackway with 385-million-year-old footprints, and the slate quarry grotto.
itinerary.evening: Portmagee or Cahersiveen. Valentia's Bray Head walk at sunset if the light holds.
itinerary.dayStats: 80 km

itinerary.title: Ring of Kerry to Killarney
itinerary.morning: The Ring of Kerry proper: Waterville, Derrynane with its beach and O'Connell's house, and the Coomakista Pass with the whole bay beneath it.
itinerary.afternoon: Over Moll's Gap and down through Ladies View into Killarney National Park — Ireland's first, with native oakwood, red deer and the three lakes. Muckross House and the Torc Waterfall.
itinerary.evening: Killarney. Busy and unashamedly touristic, but the park at dusk is another matter entirely.
itinerary.dayStats: 120 km

itinerary.title: Shannon ferry, Loop Head and the Cliffs of Moher
itinerary.morning: North to Tarbert and the Shannon car ferry to Killimer (20 minutes), which saves about two hours of driving around the estuary and is a pleasure in itself.
itinerary.afternoon: The Loop Head peninsula — a lighthouse, a sea arch, and almost no visitors, which is the point. Then north to the Cliffs of Moher: 14 km of cliff up to 214 m, with O'Brien's Tower and, in season, puffins on the sea stack.
itinerary.evening: Doolin. Three pubs, all with nightly traditional music, and the best trad scene per capita in Ireland.
itinerary.dayStats: 180 km

itinerary.title: The Burren and out
itinerary.morning: The Burren: 250 km² of limestone pavement, grey and lunar, with Arctic, Alpine and Mediterranean plants growing side by side in the grikes. Poulnabrone dolmen — a portal tomb from around 3800 BC — stands alone on the rock.
itinerary.afternoon: Corkscrew Hill to Ballyvaughan, then along Galway Bay. Shannon airport is 90 minutes from Ballyvaughan; Galway city is 50 minutes north if you are continuing.
itinerary.dayStats: 140 km

accommodationStrategy.name: Castlewood House or Pax House
accommodationStrategy.description: Two long-running guesthouses above Dingle harbour, both with sea views, serious breakfasts and hosts who will book your Blasket ferry and your dinner table. Ten minutes' walk into town, which means you can go to a session without driving.

accommodationStrategy.name: The Moorings
accommodationStrategy.description: On the harbour, above the pub, with the Skellig boat operators at the bar downstairs. If Skellig Michael is your priority, staying here is a material advantage: decisions get made at 07:30 and you will hear them first.

accommodationStrategy.name: Gregans Castle Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: A Georgian house under Corkscrew Hill looking over the Burren to Galway Bay, with one of Ireland's best restaurants and no televisions in the rooms. The right final night, and a complete change of register from the road.

logistics.emergency: 112 or 999. Coast Guard for sea and cliff incidents. Mountain rescue in Kerry via 112. University Hospital Kerry (Tralee) and University Hospital Limerick are the main facilities.
logistics.weather: Atlantic, changeable, four seasons daily. Cliff edges are unfenced in most places and grass on limestone is slippery when wet. Wind at the Cliffs of Moher regularly exceeds safe standing.
logistics.bookingWindows: June–August accommodation in Dingle, Doolin and Portmagee: 3–4 months. Gregans Castle: 3+ months. Restaurants in Dingle in summer: a week ahead, minimum.

other.label: The road is the risk
other.text: Irish regional roads (R-numbers) are posted at 80 km/h and are frequently single-track with stone walls, blind bends and no shoulder. Drive to the road, not the sign. Wing-mirror damage is the most common rental claim in Kerry and Clare.

other.label: Coach convention
other.text: Both the Ring of Kerry and Slea Head Drive are driven by tour coaches in a set direction. Follow it. Meeting a 14 m coach on a cliff-edge passing place is the trip's most avoidable stress.

other.label: Insurance
other.text: Irish car rental excess is high and third-party credit-card cover is often not accepted by Irish firms. Budget for the rental company's own super-CDW or verify your policy in writing beforehand. `verify: true`

other.label: Boats
other.text: Skellig Michael landing permits are limited by the OPW to a small daily number, sold by a handful of licensed operators, released months ahead and cancelled in swell. Book early and hold a plan B. Blasket ferries are less constrained but equally weather-dependent. `verify: true`

other.label: Fuel and cash
other.text: Fuel is available in every town; some rural pumps close at 20:00. Cards are near-universal but a few small ferries and honesty car parks want coins.

proTips: Drive the **Cliffs of Moher at 08:00 or after 18:00**. The visitor centre car park is the bottleneck; the site is open outside centre hours at reduced rates and the light is far better at both ends. `verify: true`
**Kerry Cliffs** are taller than Moher, cost a few euro to a farmer at a gate, and have perhaps a tenth of the people.
Take the **Tarbert–Killimer ferry** even if the timing is neutral. It replaces 90 minutes of estuary driving with a 20-minute crossing and a coffee.
Music sessions are not scheduled entertainment. They start when the musicians arrive, usually 21:30–22:00, and the good ones are in the pub without a sign advertising music.
The Burren is a **spring destination**: May is when the gentians, orchids and mountain avens flower on the limestone, and it is the strangest botanical sight in Europe.

If Skellig Michael cancels — and it cancels roughly one day in three — the eco-tour that circles the rock without landing still gets you the gannet colony on Little Skellig, 70,000 pairs of them, and it sails in conditions when landings cannot.

raw.driving_character: Narrow regional roads with stone walls and no shoulder; coach traffic on the two famous loops; average speeds far below posted limits
raw.mountain_passes: Conor Pass (456 m, Ireland's highest surfaced pass, unsuitable for large vehicles), Moll's Gap, Corkscrew Hill in the Burren
raw.cross_border_rules: Crossing into Northern Ireland (UK) is permitted by most Irish rental firms but requires declared cross-border cover — check before you drive north
