trips.title: Sicily Grand Circuit: Palermo, Etna & the Val di Noto
trips.subRegion: Sicily — Palermo, Etna, the Ionian coast and the Val di Noto

bestPeriod.window: Late April–early June & mid-September–October
bestPeriod.avoid: July–August (40°C inland, Taormina gridlock, hotel rates doubled); January–February for Etna road closures
bestPeriod.raw: Late April–early June & mid-September–October

accommodation.note: Palermo palazzo B&B, Ortigia boutique, one agriturismo

food.note: Street food in Palermo is €5; Ortigia seafood is €45

transport.note: Rental, fuel (~€1.85/l), A19/A20 tolls, ZTL-safe parking

activities.note: Valle dei Templi, Etna cable car, Segesta, Villa Romana

profile.difficultyNote: 2 — driving-led, with a 2 h optional crater walk on Etna and steep cobbled old towns

trips.gatewayAirport: PMO — Palermo Falcone Borsellino; 35 km / 40 min to central Palermo on the A29. Return from CTA Catania is 30 min from Taormina
trips.summary: Sicily is an island the size of Wales with the road inventory of a small country and the driving culture of a contact sport. This circuit runs anticlockwise from Palermo along the Tyrrhenian to Cefalù, climbs Etna's southern flank on the SP92, drops to Taormina and Siracusa, then works west through the Baroque hill towns of the Val di Noto to Agrigento's Greek temples before closing the loop at Segesta and Erice. The distances are modest — around 1,100 km — but almost none of it is fast: the autostrade are patchy and viaduct-limited, the provincial roads are beautiful and slow, and every historic centre is a Limited Traffic Zone with a camera on it. Suited to drivers who want density of sights over speed, and who will do the homework on ZTLs.

itinerary.title: Palermo without the car
itinerary.morning: Land at PMO and take the A29 into the city. Go directly to your hotel's arranged garage — do not attempt to find street parking inside the ring. Then leave the car alone for 24 hours.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the Quattro Canti, the Cattedrale, and the Cappella Palatina in the Palazzo dei Normanni — the finest Arab-Norman mosaic room in Europe. Then the Ballarò or Capo market for panelle and sfincione.
itinerary.evening: Aperitivo on Piazza Sant'Anna, then dinner at Trattoria Ai Cascinari on Via d'Ossuna — order the sarde a beccafico and whatever pasta is on the blackboard.
itinerary.dayStats: 35 km / 40 min from PMO; A29 toll-free; garage €18–€25/night; ZTL active Mon–Fri 08:00–20:00.
itinerary.sleep: Palazzo Sitano or B&B Al Quattro Canti, Palermo — both arrange garage transfers.

itinerary.title: Monreale, the A20 and Cefalù
itinerary.morning: Drive 12 km up to Monreale for the cathedral's 6,000 m² of gold mosaic. Park in the Piazza Vittorio Emanuele paid lot; the approach is steep and narrow and coach-clogged after 10:00.
itinerary.afternoon: Back down and east on the A20 to Cefalù. Park at the Lungomare paid lots (blue lines, €1–€1.50/h) outside the centre — the old town is a seasonal ZTL. Climb the Rocca for the view over the tiled roofs, or settle for the cathedral's Christ Pantocrator.
itinerary.evening: Sunset from the old harbour beach with the cathedral behind you — the best light of the whole north coast. Dinner at Ristorante Kentia.
itinerary.dayStats: 95 km / 1 h 40; A20 toll ~€3.60 Palermo–Cefalù; Monreale parking €2/h; Rocca entry €5, 45 min climb.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Kalura, Cefalù — outside the ZTL with its own free car park.

itinerary.title: Across the island to Etna's southern flank
itinerary.morning: Take the A19 south-east (toll-free) across the wheat interior, an underrated landscape of empty rolling gold. Detour to the Villa Romana del Casale at Piazza Armerina if you want the Roman mosaics — it adds 90 minutes.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb to Nicolosi, then the SP92 to Rifugio Sapienza at 1,910 m. The road threads black 2001 lava. From Sapienza, the cable car plus 4x4 bus reaches ~2,900 m; the cable car alone reaches 2,500 m and you walk the Silvestri craters for free at the car park.
itinerary.evening: Descend to Zafferana Etnea or Linguaglossa on the SP92/SP59 and eat at Ristorante Sabir in Zafferana — pasta alla Norma and Etna Rosso from Nerello Mascalese.
itinerary.dayStats: 210 km / 3 h 30 driving; SP92 climbs 1,200 m in 18 km, ~20 hairpins; Sapienza parking €4–€6; cable car + jeep €70–€95 pp; A19 toll-free.
itinerary.sleep: Shalai Resort, Linguaglossa — vineyard-side, secure parking, on the Etna Nord road.

itinerary.title: Taormina, where the car becomes a liability
itinerary.morning: Drive the SS120 and SS114 down to Taormina — 45 minutes. **Do not drive into Taormina.** Park at Parcheggio Lumbi or Porta Catania (€15–€25/day) and take the free shuttle up. The Corso and the whole upper town are closed to cars.
itinerary.afternoon: The Teatro Antico with Etna framed in the proscenium is the shot; go late afternoon when the coach tours have gone and the light is warm. Then the Villa Comunale gardens and a granita at Bam Bar.
itinerary.evening: Descend to Siracusa on the A18 (toll-free). Park in the Talete multi-storey at the top of Ortigia — the island is a ZTL and Talete is the legal entry. Dinner at Ristorante Regina Lucia on Piazza Duomo.
itinerary.dayStats: 145 km / 2 h 30; Taormina parking €15–€25 + free shuttle; Teatro Antico €14; Talete garage €1.50/h, ~€20/day; A18 toll-free.
itinerary.sleep: Algilà Ortigia Charme Hotel, Siracusa — arranges Talete parking and a ZTL permit for the drop-off.

itinerary.title: Ortigia dawn, then the Baroque hills
itinerary.morning: Walk Ortigia early: the Duomo built into a Greek temple, the Fonte Aretusa, and the Mercato di Ortigia which winds down by 13:00. Collect the car from Talete by 11:00.
itinerary.afternoon: Inland on the SS115 and SP to Noto, then Modica and Ragusa Ibla — three UNESCO Baroque towns in one afternoon. Park below Ragusa Ibla at the Piazza della Repubblica lots; Ibla itself is a ZTL of near-vertical alleys where a car is genuinely stuck. Modica's chocolate at Antica Dolceria Bonajuto is worth the queue.
itinerary.evening: Push west to Agrigento on the SS115 — a slow, truck-heavy road. Dinner at Ristorante Kalòs near the Valle dei Templi.
itinerary.dayStats: 240 km / 5 h with three town stops; SS115 averages 55 km/h; all ZTL — park outside every centre; fuel at Modica before the SS115 run.
itinerary.sleep: Villa Athena, Agrigento — the only hotel with the Temple of Concordia in its window; or Hotel Kaos for a third of the price.

itinerary.title: Valle dei Templi and the Scala dei Turchi question
itinerary.morning: Valle dei Templi at opening (08:30). Start at the Temple of Juno and walk down to Concordia — the best-preserved Doric temple outside Paestum. Two hours before the heat.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive 15 km to Realmonte for the Scala dei Turchi. **Access to the white marl staircase has been restricted since 2019** and sections remain closed on safety and erosion grounds; there is no free parking — use the private lots on the SP68. The reliable move is the viewpoint from Lido Rossello, 1 km east, which gives the whole cliff in profile without any access question.
itinerary.evening: North on the SS189/SS121 to Segesta country. Dinner and a bed at a Trapanese agriturismo; the Baglio Fontanasalsa area near Trapani does proper couscous alla trapanese.
itinerary.dayStats: 165 km / 3 h; Valle dei Templi €12, parking €5; Scala dei Turchi private parking €3–€5; SS115 and SS189 both single carriageway.
itinerary.sleep: Baglio Fontanasalsa, Trapani — restored olive estate, ample courtyard parking.

itinerary.title: Segesta, Erice and the drop-off
itinerary.morning: Segesta at opening: an unfinished 5th-century BC Doric temple standing alone in a field of fennel, and a theatre on the hill above reached by shuttle bus. This is the most atmospheric site on the island and the least crowded before 10:00.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive to Trapani and take the **funivia cable car** up to Erice rather than the SP31 hairpin road — the medieval town at 750 m is a ZTL, parking is scarce, and the cable car is €9.50 return and takes 10 minutes. Genovesi pastries at Maria Grammatico.
itinerary.evening: A29 back to PMO (45 min) and drop the car. If flying from CTA instead, allow 3 h 15 on the A19.
itinerary.dayStats: 105 km / 2 h to PMO; Segesta €6; Erice funivia €9.50 return; A29 toll-free; refuel before the airport spur.

accommodationStrategy.name: Palazzo Sitano
accommodationStrategy.description: Inside the historic centre but with a partnered garage on Via Roma and a driver who takes the car in for you, which removes the ZTL problem on arrival day entirely. Walking distance to Ballarò, the Cattedrale and the Vucciria. €110–€160 a double with breakfast on the terrace.

accommodationStrategy.name: Algilà Ortigia Charme Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: The practical Ortigia choice: it issues a temporary ZTL permit for the drop-off and holds a discounted rate at the Talete garage, which is otherwise the difference between €20 a day and a €100 fine. Arab-Norman-styled rooms on a quiet lane a block from the Duomo. €150–€230.

accommodationStrategy.name: Shalai Resort
accommodationStrategy.description: On Etna's north flank, with private off-street parking and a Michelin-starred restaurant that saves you a post-volcano drive. Positioned for both the SP92 south approach and the Etna Nord road, and 45 minutes from Taormina without the coastal traffic. €160–€240.

logistics.connectivity: Italy is in the EU roaming zone. Coverage is good on the coast and thin in the Madonie and Iblei interiors. Download offline maps for the SP road network — many minor SP roads are mis-mapped or have been closed by landslip for years without the apps knowing.
logistics.emergency: 112 nationwide. 118 for medical, 115 for fire, 1530 for coastguard. Etna is monitored by INGV Osservatorio Etneo; the Guardia Forestale closes the summit access on activity. EHIC/GHIC covers state healthcare for eligible visitors.
logistics.weather: The **scirocco** brings Saharan dust and 40°C+ days to the south coast between May and September, sometimes coating the car in red silt. Etna generates its own weather — 30°C in Catania can be 8°C and blowing at Rifugio Sapienza. Ash fall closes CTA airport several times a year.
logistics.bookingWindows: Valle dei Templi and the Cappella Palatina benefit from online timed tickets in high season. The Etna cable car cannot be pre-booked and queues from 09:30. Taormina hotels sell out for the Taormina Film Fest in June. Aeolian ferries from Milazzo need 1–2 weeks' notice for vehicles, but see the rental note below.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are near-universal now, including parking meters via app (EasyPark works island-wide). Keep €30 in coins for blue-line street parking. Coperto of €2–€3 per person is standard and is not a tip; tipping beyond rounding is not expected.
logistics.transportRules: No vignette in Italy. A20 is barrier-tolled — take a ticket, pay at the exit (cards accepted, avoid the yellow Telepass lanes). ZTL enforcement is camera-based and unforgiving; register your plate with your hotel where possible. Headlights are mandatory outside built-up areas. Alcohol limit 0.05%, and zero for drivers licensed under three years. **Taking a rental car on a ferry to the Aeolian Islands or the mainland requires written permission** — most companies refuse the Aeolians outright, so visit Salina or Lipari as a foot passenger from Milazzo and leave the car in the port lot.
logistics.permits: Etna's summit zone above 2,900 m may only be visited with an authorised alpine guide. Drones are banned over all archaeological sites and within 5 km of Catania and Palermo airports. Removing rock from Scala dei Turchi or lava from Etna carries substantial fines.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable but heavily chlorinated in Palermo and Agrigento; most locals drink bottled. Jellyfish (Pelagia noctiluca) blooms hit the Ionian coast in late summer. Etna's summit involves 3,000 m altitude — go slowly and bring a windproof layer regardless of the coastal temperature. Sun exposure at the archaeological sites is severe with no shade.

proTips: Treat every historic centre as undriveable and budget €15–€25 a day for garages. It is cheaper than one ZTL fine, and the fines arrive months later when you can no longer contest the signage.
In Taormina, park at **Lumbi**, not Porta Catania — Lumbi's free shuttle runs more often and drops you at Porta Messina, the correct end of the Corso for the Teatro Antico.
Photograph Segesta's temple in the first hour after opening, when the low sun rakes the columns and the fennel field is still in dew. By 11:00 it is flat, hot and full of coaches.

On Etna, skip the €90 jeep-to-summit package unless the weather is genuinely clear. The free Silvestri craters walk from the Rifugio Sapienza car park delivers 70% of the volcanic experience for nothing.
Refuel at "fai da te" (self-service) pumps and always before 19:30 inland. Attended service adds €0.20–€0.25 per litre, and rural stations close early and all day Sunday.

Buy the Valle dei Templi ticket that includes the Museo Archeologico Pietro Griffo — most people skip the museum, and it holds the giant Telamon that once stood in the Temple of Zeus you are looking at the ruins of.
Cefalù, Noto and Ragusa Ibla all look best in the hour before sunset when the local limestone goes gold. Structure the day around arriving in one of them at 18:00 rather than at lunchtime.

For Scala dei Turchi, go at sunrise or shoot it from Lido Rossello. Midday turns the white marl into a glare pit and the access situation is unpredictable enough that a guaranteed viewpoint beats a gamble.

Photograph the rental car's roof, wheels and underbody sills at pickup. Sicilian counters dispute roof and alloy damage more than anywhere else in Italy, and dashcam-quality photos with a timestamp are what wins the argument.

raw.Total distance: ~1,100 km over 7 days. Longest leg is Day 5, Siracusa–Agrigento via Modica and Ragusa, at 240 km but a genuine 5 h with the hill-town stops.
raw.SP92 Etna Sud (Nicolosi–Rifugio Sapienza: 18 km of climbing from ~700 m to 1,910 m, roughly 20 wide hairpins, excellent asphalt because it is rebuilt after every major eruption. It runs through 1983 and 2001 lava fields; the surface is grippy but the crosswinds above 1,500 m are real. Free to drive; the Rifugio Sapienza car park is €4–€6/day. Closes without notice during eruptive activity or snow — the Etna road can be shut into April.
raw.Autostrada tolls: the **A20 Messina–Palermo is tolled** (Messina–Palermo ~€11 for a car, collected at Villafranca, Barcellona, Tindari, Sant'Agata and Castelbuono barriers); the **A19 Palermo–Catania is toll-free**, as are the A18 Catania–Siracusa and the A29. Expect long viaduct sections of the A20 to be reduced to a single lane by permanent works.
raw.ZTL discipline — the single biggest cost: Palermo's ZTL covers the historic centre Mon–Fri roughly 08:00–20:00 with camera enforcement; Taormina's Corso Umberto is fully pedestrian with the whole upper town restricted; Siracusa's **Ortigia island is a ZTL with a resident-only core**; Cefalù, Ragusa Ibla, Modica and Noto all run seasonal ZTLs. Fines are €80–€120 per pass, arrive 6–12 months later via the rental company with a €40 admin fee, and each camera pass is a separate fine.
raw.Autovelox and tutor systems: fixed speed cameras are common on the SS113, SS114 and the A19, usually signed but sometimes only 150 m ahead. The A18 uses average-speed enforcement in sections. Rental fines are passed through automatically.
raw.Car rental & cross-border: Sicily is an island, so cross-border is a non-issue, but **ferry permission is not automatic** — taking a rental to the Aeolians or to the mainland usually requires written consent. One-way PMO-to-CTA drops are typically €40–€90; book the one-way explicitly at reservation, not at the counter. Sicilian rental desks are notorious for aggressive insurance upselling and for pre-existing damage disputes: photograph every panel and the roof before leaving.
raw.Fuel: widespread and rarely a problem, but many rural stations are **self-service only after 19:30** and some inland stations close entirely on Sunday. "Servito" pumps cost €0.20–€0.25/litre more than "fai da te". Expect ~€1.80–€1.95/litre for petrol.
raw.Driving hazards specific to Sicily: unsignalled roadworks with no taper; scooters filtering on both sides; livestock on the SP roads of the Madonie and the Iblei; and unlit single-bore tunnels on the SS624 and older SS113 sections. Right of way at roundabouts is treated as advisory.

sources.verified: Scala dei Turchi access status — the white cliffs remain partly restricted with sections off-limits since 2019, the site is privately owned, and there is no free parking (private lots on the SP68); the A20 Messina–Palermo is tolled while the A19 Palermo–Catania is toll-free; Sicilian ZTL enforcement practice and typical fine levels; Rifugio Sapienza at 1,910 m as the SP92 road head.
sources.confidenceNotes: Scala dei Turchi is the most volatile item in this file — access has been opened, restricted and re-restricted repeatedly and is subject to ongoing legal and erosion disputes; re-verify within days of publishing. Etna's SP92 and the cable car close without notice during eruptive episodes; INGV bulletins are the source of truth. ZTL hours and boundaries in Cefalù, Noto and Ragusa are set municipally and change seasonally — always confirm against the comune's own site rather than a travel blog. A20 toll totals and Etna cable car prices are revised annually. Rental one-way drop charges and ferry-permission policies vary by company and should be confirmed in the booking terms, not at the desk.

provenance.sourceFormat: md with '## Metadata' bullet block (one file per trip)

trips.title: The Rhine Alpine Triangle — Vaduz, the Silvretta and Graubünden
trips.subRegion: Alpine Rhine valley, Vorarlberg and Graubünden

bestPeriod.note: The Silvretta Hochalpenstrasse and Furkajoch open in June and close in late October; everything below 1,700 m works from May.

trips.gatewayAirport: Zürich (ZRH)
trips.summary: One base in Vaduz, six day loops into three countries — the Silvretta, the Bregenzerwald, the Ruinaulta gorge and the Graubünden passes.
trips.hook: Liechtenstein is 25 km long and has one mountain road. That is not a limitation here — it is the reason the trip works. From a single base in Vaduz you can be on an Austrian toll pass at 2,032 m or above a Swiss river gorge within ninety minutes, and be back for dinner in a country with no motorway at all.

snapshot.Country: Liechtenstein (with Austria and Switzerland day loops)
snapshot.Base(s): Vaduz, 6 nights; one optional night in Malbun
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 1,230 km; valley motorway plus alpine passes, gradients to 12%, max altitude 2,032 m
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Zürich (ZRH), 120 km; Friedrichshafen (FDH) and Innsbruck (INN) are alternatives
snapshot.Who It Suits: Drivers who prefer one unpacked suitcase and six different countries' worth of road

itinerary.title: Zürich to the Fürstentum
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at Zürich airport. A Swiss-registered rental almost always carries the **Autobahnvignette** already; check the windscreen or, for the e-vignette, that your plate is registered. Take the A3 along the Zürichsee and the Walensee — an hour of lake and limestone wall.
itinerary.afternoon: Leave the motorway at Sargans, cross the Rhine at Trübbach and enter Liechtenstein. No border post, no formalities, no Liechtenstein road charge — the country has no motorway to charge for. Settle in Vaduz, 455 m.
itinerary.evening: Walk the Städtle: the Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein and Hilti Art Foundation share a black basalt cube, the Landesmuseum is opposite, and the castle sits on its rock above, closed to visitors but photogenic from the vineyard path. Park in the underground Städtle garage; surface bays are short-stay blue-zone.
itinerary.dayStats: 120 km · 1h30 driving · no passes · max altitude 455 m.

itinerary.title: The one mountain road
itinerary.morning: Drive Liechtenstein's only alpine road: Vaduz to **Triesenberg** (884 m) on tight switchbacks with a 10% average, then through the Gnalp–Steg tunnel to **Steg** (1,300 m) and up to **Malbun** at 1,600 m. Fifteen kilometres, 1,150 m of climb, and a dead end — Malbun has no through route to anywhere.
itinerary.afternoon: Take the Sareis chairlift to 2,000 m for the ridge view into Austria, then drive down and south to **Balzers**, where Burg Gutenberg stands on a free-standing knoll above the Rhine.
itinerary.evening: Back in Vaduz, book a tasting at the **Hofkellerei des Fürsten von Liechtenstein**, the princely wine estate on the slope below the castle. Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, and a short walk from the Städtle.
itinerary.dayStats: 60 km · 1h30 driving · 1 climb (Malbun, dead end) · max altitude 1,600 m.

itinerary.title: Silvretta Hochalpenstrasse
itinerary.morning: North into Austria via Feldkirch. You need the **Austrian digital Vignette** for the A14 Rheintalautobahn and the S16 — around €13 for ten days, bought from the ASFINAG app, valid immediately. Run the Walgau to Bludenz, then over the **Arlbergpass**, 1,793 m, on the free B197 rather than the tolled S16 tunnel, into Landeck.
itinerary.afternoon: South up the Paznaun through Ischgl to Galtür for the **Silvretta Hochalpenstrasse**: 34 hairpins, gradients to 12%. The lower Partenen ramp on the Vorarlberg side is shut for rockfall barrier works until summer 2030, so in 2026 the road is driven as a toll-free there-and-back from Galtür (open from 4 June) as far as the Vermuntsee. The **Bielerhöhe** at 2,032 m sits on the dam wall of the Silvretta-Stausee, with the Piz Buin behind it and a large car park that is the only easy parking on the whole road.
itinerary.evening: Retrace through Ischgl and Landeck, back over the Arlbergpass and down the Klostertal to Bludenz and home.
itinerary.dayStats: 230 km · 4h15 driving · 2 passes (Arlbergpass, Bielerhöhe) · max altitude 2,032 m.

itinerary.title: Furkajoch and the Bregenzerwald
itinerary.morning: Feldkirch, then Rankweil and up the Laternsertal to the **Furkajoch**, 1,761 m — a narrow, unfenced Vorarlberg pass, closed from November to May, with passing places rather than two full lanes. Not for wide vehicles. Over to **Damüls**, one of the highest villages in the region.
itinerary.afternoon: Down the **Faschinajoch** (1,486 m) or straight on to Au and the Bregenzerwald proper: Schwarzenberg, Bezau and Andelsbuch, where contemporary timber architecture sits next to 300-year-old farmhouses. The Werkraum Bregenzerwald in Andelsbuch shows what the local joiners actually make.
itinerary.evening: Over the **Bödele** (1,140 m) to Dornbirn, then Bregenz for the Bodensee at dusk. Back to Vaduz on the A14.
itinerary.dayStats: 210 km · 4h00 driving · 3 passes (Furkajoch, Faschinajoch, Bödele) · max altitude 1,761 m.

itinerary.title: Ruinaulta and the Viamala
itinerary.morning: South on the Swiss A13 to Chur, then up to **Flims**. Park at Flims Waldhaus and walk 40 minutes to **Conn** and the **Il Spir** viewing platform, a cantilevered timber spiral hanging over the **Ruinaulta** — the Rhine gorge cut through the debris of a prehistoric landslide.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive the gorge's southern rim through Ilanz and down the hairpins to **Versam-Safien**, then out at Bonaduz. Stop at **Reichenau**, where the Vorderrhein and Hinterrhein meet under a covered bridge and become the Rhine.
itinerary.evening: Continue to Thusis for the **Viamala** gorge — 359 steps down between walls 300 m high on the old road to Italy. Return north on the A13. If you have time and light, the **San Bernardino** pass at 2,065 m is another 40 minutes south and worth the detour.
itinerary.dayStats: 210 km · 3h40 driving · no passes on the core loop · max altitude 1,100 m.

itinerary.title: Prättigau, Wolfgangpass and Davos
itinerary.morning: A13 to Landquart and up the **Prättigau** through Schiers and Klosters, a long, steady valley climb with the Silvretta chain on the left.
itinerary.afternoon: Over the **Wolfgangpass**, 1,633 m — one of the few Graubünden passes open all year — past the Davosersee into **Davos** at 1,560 m, Europe's highest town of its size. Continue over the **Flüelapass** (2,383 m) only if it is open; it is a summer road, closed roughly November to May, and the Vereina car-train through the mountain is the winter alternative.
itinerary.evening: Loop back via Filisur and the **Lenzerheide** (1,549 m) to Chur, then the Rhine valley home. Detour to see the Landwasser viaduct near Filisur if the light holds.
itinerary.dayStats: 235 km · 4h10 driving · 2 passes (Wolfgangpass, Lenzerheide) · max altitude 1,633 m.

itinerary.title: Rhine valley and out
itinerary.morning: Cross to **Werdenberg** at Buchs, a lakeside cluster of medieval timber houses below a castle, then **Bad Ragaz** and the **Taminaschlucht**, the gorge where the thermal spring emerges. The last kilometre to the old baths is closed to private cars; a shuttle runs from the valley station.
itinerary.afternoon: North on the A3 along the Walensee to Zürich. Refuel in Liechtenstein or Austria before leaving; Swiss fuel is the most expensive of the three.
itinerary.evening: Drop the car at Zürich airport. Swiss returns want a full tank and heavy refuelling surcharges if not.
itinerary.dayStats: 145 km · 2h00 driving · no passes · max altitude 520 m.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Gasthof Löwen
accommodationStrategy.description: A 14th-century timber-framed house on the main road through Vaduz, with parking and a walkable position between the Städtle and the vineyards. Six nights in one bed is the whole logic of this trip, and the Löwen puts you five minutes from the motorway ramp at Trübbach.
accommodationStrategy.booking: two months in summer; Liechtenstein has under 1,000 hotel beds in total.

accommodationStrategy.name: Park Hotel Sonnenhof
accommodationStrategy.description: Above the town on the slope below the castle, with its own garden, indoor parking and a view straight down the Rhine valley to the Swiss peaks. Worth it for the last two nights if you want the driving days bracketed by something restorative.
accommodationStrategy.booking: three months.

accommodationStrategy.name: Gorfion Familotel
accommodationStrategy.description: If you want one night at altitude, Malbun at 1,600 m is the only option in the country, and the Gorfion is built for families with outdoor parking and ski-and-hike storage. Waking above the tunnel means the Sareis lift and the ridge paths before anyone drives up from the valley.
accommodationStrategy.booking: six weeks.

logistics.emergency: 112 everywhere. In Liechtenstein and Switzerland: police 117, fire 118, ambulance 144, and **Rega air rescue on 1414**. Austrian alpine rescue is 140.
logistics.money: Liechtenstein uses the Swiss franc and is inside the Swiss customs union, but euros are accepted at many Vaduz counters at an unfavourable rate. Card everywhere; Austrian Gasthäuser still like cash.

other.label: Three road-charge regimes in one week
other.text: Liechtenstein has no motorway and charges nothing. Switzerland requires the **Autobahnvignette** at CHF 40 (approx. €42) — annual only, no short-term option, valid 1 December to 31 January of the following year, now available as a plate-linked e-vignette. Austria requires its own **digital Vignette** for Autobahnen and Schnellstrassen, from about €13 for ten days. Neither covers the other, and neither covers special tolls.

other.label: Special tolls are extra
other.text: The S16 Arlberg road tunnel (approx. €12.50) is charged at its own barrier on top of the Austrian Vignette; the Silvretta Hochalpenstrasse is toll-free while its Vorarlberg side remains shut for construction. The Swiss vignette likewise does not cover the Vereina or Furka car-trains.

other.label: Rentals and cross-border
other.text: There is no meaningful car hire in Liechtenstein itself — rent in Zürich, St. Gallen–Altenrhein or Friedrichshafen. Swiss rentals include the Swiss vignette but not the Austrian one; Austrian and German rentals are the reverse. Cross-border into CH/AT/DE/IT/LI is standard on all three; one-way drops between countries typically run €150–€400.

other.label: Emergencies
other.text: 112 everywhere. In Liechtenstein and Switzerland: police 117, fire 118, ambulance 144, and **Rega air rescue on 1414**. Austrian alpine rescue is 140.

other.label: Driving rules differ by border
other.text: Switzerland and Liechtenstein require dipped headlights in daylight; Austria does not. Swiss speeding fines are income-scaled and severe, and the A13 Rhine valley is heavily camera-monitored. Alcohol limits are 0.5‰ in all three.

other.label: Fuel
other.text: Cheapest in Austria (Feldkirch, Bludenz), then Liechtenstein, then Switzerland. Fill in Vorarlberg on the Silvretta and Bregenzerwald days.

other.label: Opening-hour traps
other.text: Alpine pass roads with gates — Silvretta above all — close overnight. Swiss shops shut at 18:30 and all Sunday; Liechtenstein observes its own national holiday on 15 August, when almost everything closes.

proTips: Get your Liechtenstein passport stamp at the Vaduz tourist office in the Städtle for a couple of francs. It is a souvenir stamp, not a border control, and it is the only one in the country.
Fill the tank at Feldkirch on the way home from Austria every time. Over six days the saving against Swiss prices covers a pass toll.
Drive the Furkajoch eastbound in the morning: the west ramp is the narrow one, and meeting a coach on it downhill is the day's worst moment.
Buy the Austrian ten-day Vignette from the ASFINAG app rather than a reseller — it activates the moment you pay, with no statutory waiting period.
Walk to Il Spir from Flims Waldhaus rather than driving to Conn. The upper road is restricted to residents and buses, and the walk is the flat 40 minutes through the forest.
The Bielerhöhe car park is the only comfortable stop on the Silvretta road. Everything else is a widened bend with room for three cars.
Check the Graubünden pass status page before the Davos day. Flüela and Albula can be closed while Wolfgang and Julier are open, which changes the loop entirely.

typeSpecific.surface: approx. 1,230 km; valley motorway plus alpine passes, gradients to 12%, max altitude 2,032 m
typeSpecific.audience: Drivers who prefer one unpacked suitcase and six different countries' worth of road

packingNotes: Swiss francs in cash, roughly CHF 200, plus €100 for Austrian tolls and Gasthäuser.
A windproof layer for Sareis at 2,000 m and the Bielerhöhe dam wall, which is exposed in any weather.
Walking shoes for Il Spir, the Viamala steps and the Taminaschlucht — all wet stone.
Sunglasses and screen cleaner; the Rhine valley runs into low sun morning and evening.
Offline maps for Vorarlberg's side valleys, where signal drops out completely.
A small daypack — every loop involves at least one 40-minute walk from a car park.
Swimwear for the Bad Ragaz thermal baths on the last morning.
whatCouldGoWrong: **The Furkajoch is still closed in June, or the Silvretta's Galtür approach is shut by snow.** Fallback: run the Arlberg, Flexenpass (1,773 m) and Hochtannbergpass (1,676 m) loop through Lech and the Bregenzerwald instead — all lower, all open earlier.

**You cross into Austria without the Austrian Vignette.** Cameras on the A14 catch it immediately and the on-the-spot substitute toll is far more than the vignette. Fallback: buy it on the app before Feldkirch, or stay on the free B190/B191 valley roads.

**Weather closes the Vaduz–Malbun road.** It is the country's only mountain road and there is no alternative route. Fallback: Malbun's post buses keep running with chains when private cars are turned back.

**Zürich airport drop-off timing.** The A3 through Pfäffikon backs up badly on Sunday evenings and Friday afternoons. Fallback: allow 2h15 rather than 1h30, or route via the A13 and A1 through St. Gallen.

trips.title: The Grand Duchy Loop — Éislek Ridges to Moselle Terraces

bestPeriod.note: Late September puts the Moselle harvest and the Éislek beech colour in the same week.

trips.gatewayAirport: Luxembourg (LUX)
trips.summary: A 620 km loop of a country you can cross in ninety minutes — slate ridges, castle valleys, riverside vineyards and blast-furnace towns.
trips.hook: Luxembourg is 82 km top to bottom, which is exactly why it rewards a slow week. The distances are trivial; the transitions are not. In four days you go from wind-scoured Ardennes plateau to Riesling terraces to the rust-red slag hills of the Minett, and each landscape has its own road manners.

snapshot.Country: Luxembourg, with short hops into Belgium and Germany
snapshot.Base(s): Clervaux (1 night), Vianden (2), Echternach (2), Luxembourg City (2)
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 620 km; plateau ridge roads, tight river-valley CRs, one motorway spine
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Luxembourg-Findel (LUX); rental desks in the terminal, 8 km from the city
snapshot.Who It Suits: Drivers who prefer 100 km of good road to 400 km of any road; castle and industrial-heritage people

itinerary.title: Off the A7 and onto the ridge
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at Findel and take the A7 *Nordstrooss* north — 30 km of new motorway that dives through the Grouft and Stafelter tunnels and spits you out at Schieren. It is free, like every road in Luxembourg.
itinerary.afternoon: At Ettelbruck join the N7, the Éislek ridge road: a long, exposed run over the Oesling plateau through Hoscheid and Marnach with big-sky views either side and a few 8% dips into stream valleys. Pull into the crest layby above Hoscheid for the first proper look north.
itinerary.evening: Clervaux, 78 km from the airport. Walk up to the château for *The Family of Man*, Edward Steichen's 1955 photographic exhibition, permanently installed here and inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World register.
itinerary.dayStats: 78 km · 1 h 15 drive · no passes, one plateau crest · max altitude 510 m at Hoscheid

itinerary.title: The Upper Sûre and the fuel-price border
itinerary.morning: West on the CR324 and N15 to the Upper Sûre lake (*Stauséi*). Park at the Burfelt viewpoint above Insenborn for the aerial view of the flooded valley, then drive the shoreline loop through Lultzhausen and Bavigne — narrow two-lane CRs with blind crests and constant cyclists.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross into Belgium at Martelange, where the N4 through the village is a wall of filling stations. Fuel is cheaper on the Luxembourg side of that strip than anywhere in Belgium, France or Germany, because Luxembourg's excise duty is lower. Return via Boulaide and Esch-sur-Sûre, where the road tunnels through solid rock into a village wrapped in a meander.
itinerary.evening: Drop south-east to Vianden via Wiltz on the N26 and CR322. The château sits floodlit above the Our; the village has one main street and a chairlift.
itinerary.dayStats: 118 km · 2 h 20 drive · no passes · max altitude 545 m near Bavigne

itinerary.title: Our valley, pumped storage and the castle road
itinerary.morning: Ride the Vianden chairlift for the castle-from-above view, then drive the hairpin road up to Mont Saint-Nicolas, upper reservoir of the SEO pumped-storage plant — a 1960s engineering set-piece with a gallery inside the mountain and a lake on the summit.
itinerary.afternoon: Take the CR324 north along the Our to Stolzembourg and Dasbourg, a slow shaded frontier road where the German bank is fifteen metres away. Turn back south for Bourscheid castle on its spur 150 m above the Sûre; the approach from Bourscheid-Moulin is a 12% climb with tight switchbacks.
itinerary.evening: Diekirch for the National Museum of Military History — the Ardennes offensive told through vehicles and dioramas — then back to Vianden.
itinerary.dayStats: 96 km · 2 h 05 drive · no passes · max altitude 505 m at Mont Saint-Nicolas

itinerary.title: Into the Mullerthal sandstone
itinerary.morning: East to Beaufort, where two castles share one site: the medieval ruin and the Renaissance château, which has produced blackcurrant liqueur for generations and pours tastings in the afternoon.
itinerary.afternoon: The CR121 to Berdorf, then a twenty-minute walk to the Schiessentümpel, the triple-arched waterfall on every poster of "Little Switzerland". The lane down to Echternach through the sandstone defile is genuinely narrow, with laybys used as passing places.
itinerary.evening: Echternach: the Basilica of St Willibrord, the abbey square and the lake on the edge of town. Use the Parking Charly car park rather than the old-town squares.
itinerary.dayStats: 74 km · 1 h 45 drive · no passes · max altitude 415 m near Berdorf

itinerary.title: The Route du Vin
itinerary.morning: Follow the Sûre down to Wasserbillig, then south on the N10, the Moselle wine road. Grevenmacher first: the Bernard-Massard cellars have made bottle-fermented Crémant de Luxembourg since 1921 and run guided tours with a tasting.
itinerary.afternoon: Machtum, Ahn and Wormeldange, where vineyards climb off the road at an alarming angle. The Musée du Vin at Ehnen is small and unfashionable and explains the terroir better than any tasting room. End at Remich and the Caves St Martin galleries cut into the rock.
itinerary.evening: Schengen, 8 km on, for the European Museum by the bridge. If you plan to taste properly, leave the car in Remich: all buses, trams and second-class trains nationwide are free for everyone, with no ticket at all.
itinerary.dayStats: 82 km · 1 h 50 drive · no passes · max altitude 320 m above Wormeldange

itinerary.title: The Minett: iron, slag and reclaimed ground
itinerary.morning: South-west on the free A13 to Fond-de-Gras, a preserved industrial site where the Train 1900 steam service and the narrow-gauge *Minièresbunn* mine railway both run on summer weekends. Check operating days first.
itinerary.afternoon: Rumelange's National Mine Museum takes you into the gallery by mine train — 12°C underground, year-round. Then Esch-sur-Alzette and Belval, where two preserved blast furnaces stand over a university campus and a concert hall.
itinerary.evening: Walk the Prënzebierg–Giele Botter reserve above Differdange at dusk: former open-cast workings, now orchid meadows and red-rock cliffs, with the Titelberg Celtic oppidum on the next ridge. Drive into Luxembourg City for the last two nights.
itinerary.dayStats: 132 km · 2 h 30 drive · no passes · max altitude 420 m at Prënzebierg

itinerary.title: Fortress city, then home
itinerary.morning: Leave the car parked and walk: the Bock casemates, the Chemin de la Corniche above the Alzette, then the Pfaffenthal panoramic lift down into the Grund.
itinerary.afternoon: Kirchberg for the architecture — Mudam by I.M. Pei (2006) on the ramparts of Fort Thüngen, with the Philharmonie by Christian de Portzamparc (2005) alongside.
itinerary.evening: Return the car at Findel, fifteen minutes from Kirchberg. Fill the tank on the way; Luxembourg fuel is a parting gift.
itinerary.dayStats: 42 km · 55 min drive · no passes · max altitude 380 m on the Kirchberg plateau

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Belle-Vue
accommodationStrategy.description: On the Grand-Rue facing the castle rock, with its own parking — which matters, because Vianden's street bays fill by mid-afternoon in summer. Two nights here covers the Our valley, Mont Saint-Nicolas and Bourscheid with no repositioning.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 6 weeks ahead in July–August.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Bel Air
accommodationStrategy.description: Parkland on the edge of town, secure off-street parking, and a garden that makes a good decompression stop between the Mullerthal lanes and the Moselle. Fifteen minutes' walk to the basilica.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 2 months ahead for the Whit Tuesday procession.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Parc Beaux-Arts
accommodationStrategy.description: Three converted 18th-century houses on Rue Sigefroi, thirty seconds from the casemates. Book a parking space with the room; the old town is a maze of resident-only bays.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 6 weeks; avoid EU summit weeks, when rates double.

logistics.emergency: 112 for ambulance and fire; 113 for police in Luxembourg. Coverage is near-universal — the deep Our and Sûre valleys are the only weak spots.
logistics.weather: The Oesling plateau at 500 m runs 5–8°C colder and considerably windier than the Moselle on the same day; fog on the N7 crest is common at dawn in autumn.
logistics.money: Cards are accepted almost everywhere, including small wineries, but a few village parking meters and rural bakeries still want coins. Tipping is rounding up, not a percentage.
logistics.transportRules: Use it for the Moselle wine day and the capital, where parking is the only real cost. Alcohol limit is 0.5 g/l, and 0.2 g/l for licences under two years old.

other.label: Tolls: there are none
other.text: Luxembourg charges nothing for any road, motorway included, and requires no vignette — nor do Belgium or Germany for cars. Budget zero for road charges.

other.label: Low-emission zones
other.text: Luxembourg has none. Brussels, Antwerp and Ghent all run LEZs that require foreign plates to be registered online in advance, and German cities with an *Umweltzone* need a Feinstaubplakette (approx. €6). Neither applies on this loop; both bite if you extend it.

other.label: Fuel strategy
other.text: Fill inside Luxembourg, always: the gap with neighbours is worth 15–25% on a tank. Border stations at Wasserbillig, Schengen, Dudelange and Martelange open late and take foreign cards.

other.label: Winter tyres are a legal requirement
other.text: in wintry conditions, not a recommendation. Rentals collected October–April should carry them; confirm at the desk.

other.label: Opening-hour traps
other.text: Most museums and castles close Mondays; several Minett sites run weekends only outside July–August, and Sunday afternoons in small towns are genuinely shut.

other.label: Cross-border rental
other.text: Cars from Findel can be driven freely into Belgium, Germany and France, but one-way drops abroad typically add €150–€400, and the border is 20 km away in three directions.

proTips: Buy the **LuxembourgCard** (approx. €13–€28 per person per day, cheaper for multi-day) on the morning of the Minett day: the mine museum, Fond-de-Gras, Vianden château and Clervaux together beat its cost in one afternoon.
Vianden castle is quietest **before 10:30**, when the coach groups arrive from the Moselle river cruises.
On the Moselle, ask for **Auxerrois** rather than Riesling — it is what the growers drink here, rarely exported and priced accordingly.
**Park at P+R Bouillon** on the capital's south-west edge and ride the free tram in. It saves €20–€30 a day and skips the one-way system.
The **Schiessentümpel** has roadside parking for about a dozen cars. Arrive before 09:30 or leave the car in Berdorf and walk the extra 25 minutes.

raw.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 620 km; plateau ridge roads, tight river-valley CRs, one motorway spine
raw.Who It Suits: Drivers who prefer 100 km of good road to 400 km of any road; castle and industrial-heritage people

typeSpecific.surface: approx. 620 km; plateau ridge roads, tight river-valley CRs, one motorway spine
typeSpecific.audience: Drivers who prefer 100 km of good road to 400 km of any road; castle and industrial-heritage people

packingNotes: Offline maps for the CR network; satnavs route you onto farm tracks between Bavigne and Boulaide.
A small stash of €2 coins for older village parking meters that still refuse cards.
Wind shell and warm mid-layer for the plateau, plus something lighter for the Moselle.
Grippy shoes for Mullerthal sandstone, which is slick after rain and often wet regardless.
A jacket for the Rumelange mine gallery — a constant 12°C.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Rain turns the Mullerthal into a sponge** and the sandstone paths hold water for days. Swap Day 4 and Day 5; the Moselle works in any weather.
**Industrial heritage runs on a weekend timetable.** Train 1900 and the Minièresbunn may not operate midweek or off-season. The Rumelange mine museum and Belval keep longer hours year-round.
**Vianden's parking saturates** on summer weekends and during the early-August medieval festival. Use the riverside lots by the campsite and walk up in ten minutes.

**Straying into a Belgian LEZ unregistered** brings an automatic fine by post plus the rental company's admin fee. Registering a foreign plate online is free — do it before any detour toward Antwerp or Brussels.
**The A7 tunnels close for maintenance** overnight and occasionally at weekends, diverting traffic onto the old road through Mersch. Allow an extra 25 minutes on airport days.

trips.title: Three Corniches and the Road to Turini

bestPeriod.note: Avoid the Grand Prix build, which closes central Monaco streets from early April to late June.

trips.gatewayAirport: Nice Côte d'Azur (NCE)
trips.summary: Sea-level Riviera in the morning, 1,600 m rally hairpins by mid-afternoon — a week of driving out of a two-square-kilometre base.
trips.hook: Monaco makes an absurd basecamp and an excellent one. You can be on the Grande Corniche in six minutes and at the Col de Turini in ninety, and every evening the car goes back underground while you walk. The driving here is not about distance. It is about camber, surface, and knowing which of three parallel roads to take at which hour.

snapshot.Country: Monaco, with all driving days in France and one border crossing to Italy
snapshot.Base(s): Monaco (7 nights, no relocation)
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 710 km; corniche ledges, stacked hairpins, one high alpine col, gorge road
snapshot.Getting There: Nice Côte d'Azur (NCE); rental desks in the Terminal 2 car park, 30 km from Monaco
snapshot.Who It Suits: Drivers who want technique over mileage; anyone who enjoys rally history

itinerary.title: Sea-level arrival
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at NCE and take the Basse Corniche (D6098) rather than the A8: Villefranche-sur-Mer, Cap Ferrat, Beaulieu, Èze-sur-Mer, Cap d'Ail. It is 32 km and takes an hour, often more.
itinerary.afternoon: Park and stop driving. Monaco's public underground car parks are the only realistic option — Chemin des Pêcheurs under the Rocher, Casino, Louis II, Fontvieille. Most give the first hour free, then charge hourly with cheaper night rates. Check the height barrier: many are 1.80–2.00 m and refuse an SUV with a roof box.
itinerary.evening: Walk. The public lifts and escalators between Fontvieille, the Rocher and Monte-Carlo are free and run late. Sunset from the Jardin Exotique terrace or the ramparts by the Palais.
itinerary.dayStats: 32 km · 1 h drive · no passes · max altitude 60 m at Cap d'Ail

itinerary.title: All three corniches in one figure of eight
itinerary.morning: Out west on the Basse Corniche before 08:30, when it is still a road rather than a queue. At Beaulieu turn up to the Moyenne Corniche (D6007) and take it back east through the tunnels to Èze village, parking in the paid lot below the medieval gate.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb to the Grande Corniche (D2564), which follows the Roman Via Julia Augusta along the ridge at 450–500 m. Stop at the Parc départemental de la Grande Corniche below Fort de la Revère — free parking, and the whole coast from Cap Ferrat to Bordighera in one sweep.
itinerary.evening: La Turbie and the Trophée des Alpes, the Augustan monument of 6 BC that still marks the old frontier. Drop back to Monaco down the D53 hairpins.
itinerary.dayStats: 68 km · 2 h 15 drive · Col d'Èze (507 m) · max altitude 550 m at La Revère

itinerary.title: Madone, Gorbio, Castillon
itinerary.morning: East to Menton, then up the D22 to Sainte-Agnès and the Col de la Madone (925 m) — a narrow, well-surfaced climb of about 13 km at 6–7%, the village clinging to a limestone crag at the top.
itinerary.afternoon: Traverse to Gorbio on the D50, an exposed balcony lane with no barrier in places, then back down to Menton for lunch in the old port.
itinerary.evening: Take the D2566 north over the Col de Castillon (707 m) to Sospel for a first look at the Bévéra valley and the road you will drive tomorrow. Return the same way.
itinerary.dayStats: 92 km · 2 h 40 drive · Col de la Madone (925 m), Col de Castillon (707 m) · max altitude 925 m

itinerary.title: Braus, Saint-Roch, Turini, Authion
itinerary.morning: Sospel first, then the D2204 west over the **Col de Braus (1,002 m)** — the most photographed hairpin stack in France, six tiers of switchbacks on the L'Escarène side, roughly 8% and consistently narrow. Descend to L'Escarène.
itinerary.afternoon: North through Lucéram on the D2566, over the **Col Saint-Roch (990 m)**, then the long forested climb to the **Col de Turini (1,607 m)**: about 15 km at an average 7% with pitches near 10%, the surface good, the corners tightening on exit. This is the Monte-Carlo Rally's night stage; the pass is nominally open all year but closes without warning after snowfall between December and March.
itinerary.evening: If it is between late May and October, add the D68 Authion loop above Turini — a one-lane military road to the Pointe des Trois Communes at about 2,080 m, with unguarded drops and passing places. Then the descent to Sospel and back to Monaco.
itinerary.dayStats: 138 km · 4 h drive · Braus, Saint-Roch, Turini, Authion · max altitude 2,080 m

itinerary.title: Up the Roya to the Merveilles
itinerary.morning: Cross into Italy at Ventimiglia and take the RD6204/SS20 north up the Roya. Storm Alex destroyed much of this valley in October 2020; sections remain single-lane under traffic lights, and the Tende road tunnel reopened in 2025 with alternating one-way traffic on a published timetable. Check it before you set off.
itinerary.afternoon: At Saint-Dalmas-de-Tende turn onto the D91 toward Castérino. Tarmac ends at the Lac des Mesces car park — there is no road into the Vallée des Merveilles and never has been. Walk in toward the Refuge des Merveilles for the Bronze Age engravings; leaving the marked path in the Mercantour National Park core zone requires an accredited guide, and jeep-taxis run from Castérino.
itinerary.evening: Back down the Roya, with a ten-minute detour to Saorge, stacked on its cliff, in evening light.
itinerary.dayStats: 186 km · 4 h 20 drive · Col de Tende tunnel approach · max altitude 1,400 m at Mesces

itinerary.title: Gorges du Loup and the Col de Vence
itinerary.morning: A8 west to Cagnes-sur-Mer — this is a toll motorway, roughly €3–€5 for the run, cards accepted in the manned and automatic lanes. Then the D2210 to Tourrettes-sur-Loup and Pont-du-Loup.
itinerary.afternoon: North on the D6 into the Gorges du Loup: rock overhangs, unlit single-lane tunnels and two paid stopping places at the Saut du Loup and the Cascade de Courmes. Loop back over the D3 to Gourdon, a perched village with parking for very few cars.
itinerary.evening: The D2 over the **Col de Vence (963 m)** crosses a bare karst plateau with no shade and no barriers, then drops into Vence. Return on the A8.
itinerary.dayStats: 172 km · 3 h 30 drive · Col de Vence (963 m) · max altitude 963 m

itinerary.title: Cap d'Ail, then out
itinerary.morning: Leave the car underground. Walk the Sentier du Littoral from Monaco's western edge around Cap d'Ail to Plage Mala — 45 minutes of stepped coastal path below the railway.
itinerary.afternoon: Retrieve the car, fill up in Beausoleil or Cap d'Ail, and take the Moyenne Corniche west for the last time.
itinerary.evening: Return the car at NCE, allowing 75 minutes from Monaco.
itinerary.dayStats: 38 km · 1 h 10 drive · no passes · max altitude 300 m on the Moyenne Corniche

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Columbus Monte-Carlo
accommodationStrategy.description: On the Fontvieille side, facing the Princess Grace rose garden and away from the circuit streets. Its own parking, plus the Fontvieille commercial-centre garage next door, means you never cross the Rocher's restricted zone.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3 months for September, 6 for Grand Prix season.

accommodationStrategy.name: Novotel Monte-Carlo
accommodationStrategy.description: Built into the slope on Boulevard Princesse Charlotte with a secure underground garage, direct lift access and a five-minute walk to the Casino — the most practical Monaco address for a car-based week at a non-palatial rate.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 2 months ahead.

accommodationStrategy.name: Fairmont Monte Carlo
accommodationStrategy.description: On the Grand Prix hairpin itself, over the tunnel, with valet parking that removes the height-barrier problem entirely. Expensive, but the circuit location is the point.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4–6 months for May and September.

logistics.emergency: 112 across the region; in Monaco 17 for police and 18 for fire and rescue. Mountain rescue in the Mercantour goes through 112. Mobile coverage drops out in the Roya gorges and above Castérino.
logistics.weather: Turini can be 15°C colder than Larvotto and holds ice in shaded hairpins into April. The Authion loop opens only when the snow clears, typically late May, and closes with the first serious fall.
logistics.money: Monaco uses the euro; cards are universal, cash is for parking meters in French villages. Restaurant service is included, and rounding up is enough.

other.label: Parking is the whole logistics problem
other.text: Public underground car parks are cheap by Riviera standards (roughly €2–€3 per hour, €20–€30 for 24 hours), but on-street bays are effectively resident-only, and the Rocher is closed to all but Monaco and Alpes-Maritimes (06) plates. Everyone else parks at the Chemin des Pêcheurs and uses the free public lifts.

other.label: French tolls
other.text: The A8 has barriers at Nice-Saint-Isidore and La Turbie; short hops cost €2–€5, contactless cards work, and the orange-*t* lanes are badge-only.

other.label: Crit'Air
other.text: France's air-quality sticker costs about €3.80, is ordered online with the registration document and arrives by post — order three weeks ahead. It is required in the Nice low-emission zone and during pollution peaks.

other.label: Cross-border rental
other.text: Italy is 12 km east; most Nice suppliers permit it, some prohibit it outright, others add a €30–€60 cross-border fee — declare it at the desk. One-way drops elsewhere in France run €150–€300, in Italy far more.

other.label: Fuel
other.text: Monaco has only a handful of filling stations. Fill in Beausoleil, Cap d'Ail or on the A8 services, and never start a mountain day below half a tank — there is nothing between Sospel and Turini.

other.label: Opening-hour traps
other.text: Perched villages shut between 12:30 and 15:00, including their only fuel pump. The Trophée des Alpes closes Mondays.

proTips: Drive the **Grande Corniche eastbound in the late afternoon**. The sun sits behind you, the sea goes metallic, and the Vistaëro laybys above Roquebrune are empty after the tour coaches turn back at 17:00.
The Col de Braus hairpins photograph properly **from the D2204 pull-off above the third tier**, mid-morning.
Book the **Tende tunnel timetable into the day**, not around it. Alternating traffic means fixed windows in each direction; missing one costs 45 minutes at the portal.
**Èze village car park fills by 09:45.** Park at Èze-sur-Mer and walk up the Nietzsche path, or drive through and stop at La Revère instead.
On rally weekends in late January the **Turini stage road closes overnight**; the spectator tradition is to drive up the day before and stay in Sospel or Moulinet.

raw.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 710 km; corniche ledges, stacked hairpins, one high alpine col, gorge road
raw.Who It Suits: Drivers who want technique over mileage; anyone who enjoys rally history

typeSpecific.surface: approx. 710 km; corniche ledges, stacked hairpins, one high alpine col, gorge road
typeSpecific.audience: Drivers who want technique over mileage; anyone who enjoys rally history

packingNotes: Offline mapping: the Roya and Bévéra valleys lose signal entirely.
Driving shoes with a thin sole; the Turini descent is 25 minutes of continuous braking and modulation.
A fleece and windproof for the Authion at 2,000 m, even in July.
Walking shoes with real tread; the Merveilles path above Mesces is loose granite.
whatCouldGoWrong: **The Grand Prix build closes Monaco.** Grandstands and barriers go up from early April and come down through late June, shutting circuit streets and some car park entrances. Check the calendar before booking that window.

**The Roya is still a rebuilt road.** Single-lane sections, temporary bridges and tunnel timetables all change. If the RD6204 is shut, reach the Merveilles from the Vésubie side via Saint-Martin-Vésubie, or substitute the Col de la Couillole day.
**Turini closes for snow** at short notice from December to March, and the Authion for half the year. Fallback: the Braus–Saint-Roch–Castillon triangle stays open and gives most of the hairpins.

**Your car will not fit.** Height barriers of 1.80 m in Monaco's older car parks eliminate most SUVs and every roof box. Book a compact, and confirm the garage clearance with the hotel before arrival.

trips.title: The Grand Loop: Cliff Monasteries, the Prut and the Deep South by Car
trips.subRegion: Dniester cliffs, the northern Prut, Ștefan Vodă and Gagauzia

bestPeriod.window: the second half of September — harvest in the vineyards, dry clay tracks, and the Prut floodplain still green
bestPeriod.avoid: March–April and any wet spell (village clay roads become impassable), and mid-July to mid-August (35 °C, dust)

accommodation.note: €200–€360 (€29–€51/night, village guesthouses and small-town hotels)

activities.note: €90–€160 (fortress, reserves, cellar tours, guides)

profile.difficultyNote: Easy–Moderate

trips.gatewayAirport: Chișinău International (KIV). Collect the car at the airport; Moldovan-plated rentals need no road vignette. Iași (IAS) in Romania is a viable alternative entry, 2 h 30 from Chișinău, but a cross-border hire costs more.
trips.summary: Roughly 1,050 km around a country the size of Belgium, on roads that change character every twenty minutes: fresh EU-funded asphalt, then broken Soviet concrete slab, then a clay farm track with a horse cart on it.…
trips.hook: Roughly 1,050 km around a country the size of Belgium, on roads that change character every twenty minutes: fresh EU-funded asphalt, then broken Soviet concrete slab, then a clay farm track with a horse cart on it. In between are rock-hewn monasteries cut into Dniester limestone, a circular Genoese-plan fortress at Soroca, a hundred hills on the Prut floodplain that geologists still argue about, and the best wine you have never been offered.

snapshot.Start / End: Chișinău → Chișinău (loop, ~1,050 km)
snapshot.Getting there: Chișinău International (KIV). Collect the car at the airport; Moldovan-plated rentals need no road vignette. Iași (IAS) in Romania is a viable alternative entry, 2 h 30 from Chișinău, but a cross-border hire costs more.

itinerary.title: Out of the city to the Răut meander
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at KIV and take the M2 north, then the R20 down into the Răut valley. Traffic thins within twenty minutes of the ring road.
itinerary.afternoon: **Orheiul Vechi**: the cave monastery cut into the limestone spur above Butuceni, a working hermitage reached through a rock passage, with the Răut wrapping the promontory below. Entry **20 MDL** adult, 10 MDL reduced; the Butuceni information point runs 08:00–18:00 weekdays and to 20:00 at weekends. A guide for 1–10 people is 200 MDL in Romanian, 300 MDL in English.
itinerary.evening: Stay in **Butuceni** or **Trebujeni**. Dinner is *plăcinte*, *zeamă* and house wine from a plastic jug, and the sky over the meander is very dark.

itinerary.title: Two cliff monasteries
itinerary.morning: North to **Saharna** via Rezina. The monastery complex sits at the mouth of a gorge; the marked path upstream past the cascades to the **Grimidon** rock and the old rock-hewn skete is about 3 km each way, easy but slippery on wet limestone.
itinerary.afternoon: South-east to **Țipova** — the **largest rock-hewn monastery in Eastern Europe**, three levels of cells and a church carved into the cliff perhaps 250 m above the Dniester, with a steep stair down to the water and a waterfall gorge behind the village.
itinerary.evening: Sleep at the Saharna monastery guesthouse or a Lalova pension. Neither has a card machine [VERIFY: current Saharna and Țipova monastery guesthouse rates].
itinerary.dayStats: 95 km / 2 h 20 driving, 6 km walking

itinerary.title: To the fortress
itinerary.morning: North on the R20 and M2 through Rezina, Șoldănești and Florești. This stretch shows the road spectrum in one morning: new asphalt, then a slab section, then new asphalt again.
itinerary.afternoon: **Soroca fortress**, the best-preserved castle in Moldova — a **perfect circle** with five towers, rebuilt in stone in the 1540s under Petru Rareș on a Genoese-influenced plan, standing directly on the Dniester bank with Ukraine 300 m across the water.
itinerary.evening: Walk up to the hill of **Roma mansions** above the town — a genuinely strange skyline of self-built palaces with Bolshoi and Capitol domes — then eat by the river [VERIFY: current Soroca fortress entry fee and hours].

itinerary.title: The Prut floodplain
itinerary.morning: West through **Bălți**, Moldova's second city — a place to refuel and buy provisions rather than to sightsee — then south-west to Glodeni.
itinerary.afternoon: **Pădurea Domnească**, the "Princely Forest": the country's largest floodplain oak forest on the Prut, arranged through **Moldsilva** in advance (+373 22 27 23 06). Five **European bison** live in a fenced enclosure reachable only with a warden, and the established route "Pe un picior de plai pe-o gură de rai" runs through the old oaks. No published tariff — it is settled in cash on arrival [VERIFY: current Pădurea Domnească visit fee].
itinerary.evening: The **Suta de Movile** — the "Hundred Hills" — near Cobani: a field of several hundred low mounds spread across the Prut terrace, origin still disputed between reef remnants and landslip. Best at low sun from the R16 above the village.

itinerary.title: South again, and underground
itinerary.morning: The long run back down the R16 and M14 through Ungheni to Chișinău. Fuel in Ungheni; the north has real gaps in the network.
itinerary.afternoon: **Castel Mimi** at Bulboaca, a restored 1893 château of the last governor of Bessarabia, now a working winery with gardens and a restaurant [VERIFY: current Castel Mimi tour and tasting prices]; or **Cricova**, 15 km from the capital, 120 km of galleries toured **by vehicle** — Matinal 250 MDL, tasting tours 400–3,100 MDL, reservation mandatory.
itinerary.evening: A night in Chișinău, laundry, and an ATM stop before the south.
itinerary.dayStats: 175 km / 3 h + 40 km / 45 min

itinerary.title: Ștefan Vodă and the deep south
itinerary.morning: East and south to **Purcari** in the **Ștefan Vodă** appellation, Moldova's most decorated estate, founded 1827. Advance booking is required: château tour 300 MDL, Classic tasting 450 MDL, Reserve Exclusive 600 MDL, with minimum party sizes on the higher tastings. Note the road east of Căușeni runs close to the de facto line — stay on the signed M3 and do not improvise a shortcut.
itinerary.afternoon: West across the southern steppe to **Slobozia Mare** on the Prut. This is the emptiest driving of the week: long straight roads, sunflower to the horizon, villages of geese.
itinerary.evening: **Prutul de Jos** reserve HQ (tel 062122295): two set routes — a **3 km, 2-hour walking route** to the Beleu viewing platform, and a **boat route through the Manolescu channel** onto **Lake Beleu**, run only when water levels allow and in small groups. Binoculars are lent; there is camping and a dining pavilion at HQ. Arrange by phone at least a day ahead.

itinerary.title: Beleu, Gagauzia, home
itinerary.morning: Dawn on **Lake Beleu**, the largest natural lake in Moldova and the core of a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve on the lower Prut — pelicans, glossy ibis, herons, and in autumn migrating waterfowl in numbers.
itinerary.afternoon: North-east to **Comrat**, capital of **Găgăuzia**. The Gagauz National History and Ethnography Museum and a plate of *gözleme* and *kıvırma* are a good last stop before the motorway-grade run home.
itinerary.evening: M3 north to Chișinău, 100 km and 1 h 45. Refuel before returning the car — Moldovan rentals are full-to-full and airport fuel is dearer.

accommodationStrategy.name: Butuceni village guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: five minutes from the Orheiul Vechi cave monastery on the reserve side of the river, with secure yard parking, home-cooked half board, and the Belvedere platform for sunrise before any day-tripper arrives from the capital.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 2–4 weeks ahead; the village has only a few dozen beds and the capital's weekend traffic takes them.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel in Soroca centre
accommodationStrategy.description: the only proper hotel base in the north, five minutes' walk from the fortress and the river promenade, with off-street parking — which matters, because street parking near the fortress is informal and unlit.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 1–2 weeks ahead; midweek is always available.

accommodationStrategy.name: Prutul de Jos reserve accommodation / Slobozia Mare pensions
accommodationStrategy.description: puts you at the lake for the dawn boat window rather than driving two hours to reach it, with camping and a dining pavilion at the reserve HQ and a warden who can tell you at 06:00 whether the channel is navigable.
accommodationStrategy.booking: by phone with the reserve (062122295 / 062122289) at least a few days ahead; there is no online system.

logistics.connectivity: Moldova is **not** in EU roaming — buy an Orange or Moldcell SIM at KIV. Coverage is good on the M-roads and adequate in villages; download offline maps, because satnav routing on the R-roads will confidently send you down a clay track.
logistics.emergency: **112** nationwide, with English usually available. Give your position by village name and R-road number. Recovery from a soft clay track is a tractor and a negotiation, not a service call — budget 500–1,000 MDL and expect it to take two hours.
logistics.weather: The whole plan pivots on rain. A single heavy shower closes the clay legs for 24–48 hours; check the forecast the night before each dirt section and use the alternatives above without regret. Summer heat over 35 °C is normal in the south, where there is no shade at all.
logistics.bookingWindows: Purcari, Cricova and Castel Mimi are reservation-only, several days out. The Moldsilva and Prutul de Jos reserve visits need a phone call days ahead. Village guesthouses 2–4 weeks in season.
logistics.money: Moldovan leu, roughly 19–20 MDL to the euro. Cards work in Chișinău, Bălți, Soroca and Comrat and at the named wineries; village guesthouses, monastery donations, reserve fees and roadside melon stalls are **cash**. Carry 3,000–5,000 MDL. ATMs exist in every raion centre, not in villages.
logistics.transportRules: **Zero-tolerance drink-driving — the legal limit is effectively 0.00 and enforcement is routine.** Dipped headlights outside built-up areas. Seatbelts front and rear. Speed 50 in villages, 90 rural, 110 on the few dual sections. **Livestock and horse carts roam free** and are at their worst at dusk when herds return to the village — an unlit cart on an unlit road is the single most likely accident on this trip. Do not drive rural roads after dark if you can avoid it.
logistics.permits: No permits for ordinary roads. **The scientific reserves — Codrii, Pădurea Domnească, Prutul de Jos — are not walk-up sites**; access is by prior arrangement with each administration and fees are settled in cash. Orheiul Vechi charges 20 MDL. Foreign-plated cars need the **vinieta**; Moldovan-plated rentals do not.

proTips: **Treat rain as a routing decision, not an inconvenience.** Check the forecast each evening and reorder the next day around it — Țipova, Suta de Movile and the Beleu dyke are all wet-weather no-gos, and all three have a dry-foot alternative.
**Fuel above half a tank north of Bălți.** Stations thin out towards Glodeni and Cobani, several close at 20:00, and a few village pumps take cash only.
**Leave the rental in Chișinău for Transnistria.** Your insurance almost certainly excludes it; a rutieră from Gara Centrală costs about 50 MDL and removes the entire problem.
**Ask the guesthouse to phone ahead for you.** Reserve wardens, monastery guesthouses and small wineries answer a Romanian call from a local number far more reliably than an email in English.

**Buy directly from the small producers you drive past.** Moldova's best-value bottles are sold at the gate for a third of the Chișinău restaurant price, and *vin de casă* in a refilled plastic bottle is a genuine local institution — just remember rule 6 below.
**Nobody drinks and drives here, at all.** With a zero limit and frequent checks, the practical answer is one driver who tastes nothing, or a night in the village where the winery is.
**Do Beleu at dawn and Suta de Movile at dusk.** Both are low-relief landscapes that only read in raking light; in flat midday sun they photograph as nothing at all.

raw.Driving legs, km and time: Chișinău → **Orheiul Vechi (Trebujeni/Butuceni)** 60 km / 1 h 15. Orheiul Vechi → **Saharna** 60 km / 1 h 20 via Rezina. Saharna → **Țipova** 35 km / 1 h (the last 6 km is track). Țipova → **Soroca** 110 km / 2 h 15. Soroca → **Bălți** 45 km / 1 h. Bălți → **Pădurea Domnească** (Cuhnești/Branişte) 55 km / 1 h 15. Pădurea Domnească → **Suta de Movile** (Cobani/Braniște) 15 km / 30 min. Cobani → Chișinău 175 km / 3 h. Chișinău → **Castel Mimi** (Bulboaca) 40 km / 45 min. Castel Mimi → **Purcari** 80 km / 1 h 30. Purcari → **Slobozia Mare (Lake Beleu)** 165 km / 3 h. Slobozia Mare → **Comrat** 110 km / 2 h. Comrat → Chișinău 100 km / 1 h 45.
raw.Road reality — the core of this trip: Moldova has three road surfaces and you will meet all of them daily. **M-roads** (M2 Chișinău–Soroca, M3 south, M14) are mostly resurfaced two-lane asphalt at 90 km/h and are fine. **R-roads** run the full range: recently rebuilt EU- and EBRD-funded asphalt on some sections, and **unrepaired Soviet concrete slab** on others — the slab is the worst surface here, with 3–5 cm joints every few metres that will shake the car apart above 50 km/h. **Village *drum de țară*** are unsealed clay: perfectly drivable when dry in a normal hatchback, and **genuinely impassable within an hour of rain**, when the clay turns to grease and even 4x4s slide off camber. Plan every dirt leg with an alternative.
raw.Wet-weather alternatives for each dirt l: *Țipova approach:* the direct descent from Horodiște is clay — in wet weather park in Horodiște village and walk the 2 km down, or approach from Lalova on the river road. *Saharna gorge track:* leave the car at the monastery car park on asphalt and walk the waterfall gorge; do not drive the upper track. *Suta de Movile:* the field tracks between the mounds are pure clay — in the wet, view them from the R16 above Cobani and skip the interior. *Pădurea Domnească:* the forest roads are the warden's problem, not yours; the reserve visit is by warden vehicle or on foot. *Beleu:* the Manolescu channel access is a dyke road that softens badly; ask the reserve HQ before driving it.
raw.Rental cross-border rules: **Romania is normally permitted** with advance notice, a **Green Card** and a cross-border fee. **Ukraine is normally excluded** from Moldovan rental insurance, and so is **Transnistria** — critical, because the direct Chișinău–Tiraspol road crosses the de facto line and your CDW and third-party cover typically lapse the moment you do. If you intend to enter Transnistria by car you must buy the entity's own local insurance at the crossing; most travellers take a rutieră instead and leave the rental in Chișinău [VERIFY: current cross-border authorisation fee and Green Card charge at Chișinău desks].
raw.Road tax for foreign-plated cars: A **Moldovan-plated rental needs nothing** — road tax is already in the registration. A **foreign-plated car** must buy the ***vinieta***, an electronic road-use charge sold at the border crossings, at fuel stations and online at the state portal, in periods from seven days upward. It is checked by camera and by the border on exit; there is no sticker [VERIFY: current vinieta tariff bands].
raw.Viewpoints and laybys: The **Belvedere platform** above Butuceni over the Răut meander; the cliff terrace at **Țipova** above the Dniester with Ukraine on the far bank; the **Saharna** gorge above the 22 cascades; the **Soroca** riverfront below the fortress and the "Gypsy Hill" of mansions above the town; the R16 rise above **Cobani** for the Suta de Movile; the levee at **Slobozia Mare** over Lake Beleu at sunset.
