trips.title: Two Roads Over the Carpathians: The Transfăgărășan and Transalpina Loop from Sibiu

bestPeriod.window: late June to mid-September, when both DN7C and DN67C are certain to be open end to end
bestPeriod.avoid: May and early June (Transfăgărășan still shut above Bâlea Cascadă), and the 15 July–20 August weekend crush at Bâlea Lac

accommodation.note: €300–€520 (€45–€75/night, doubles in guesthouses and cabanas)

transport.note: €270–€400 (compact rental €35–€55/day + ~65 L fuel + rovinietă)

activities.note: €45–€90 (Poenari, Vidraru boat, cable car, museums)

profile.difficultyNote: Moderate

trips.gatewayAirport: Sibiu International (SBZ), 5 km out; Cluj (CLJ) 3 h; Bucharest Otopeni (OTP) 4 h. CFR rail from Brașov 2 h 40.
trips.summary: You climb out of the Făgăraș foothills in second gear, and past the eleventh hairpin the beech forest quits: nothing left but granite, snowmelt and hot brakes. A week of two mountain crossings — one famous, one…
trips.hook: You climb out of the Făgăraș foothills in second gear, and past the eleventh hairpin the beech forest quits: nothing left but granite, snowmelt and hot brakes. A week of two mountain crossings — one famous, one better — stitched together by monasteries, a Vlad Țepeș ruin up 1,480 steps, and valley roads where 60 km takes ninety minutes. For confident drivers who would rather stop twenty times than arrive early.

snapshot.Start / End: Sibiu → Sibiu (loop, ~610 km)
snapshot.Getting there: Sibiu International (SBZ), 5 km out; Cluj (CLJ) 3 h; Bucharest Otopeni (OTP) 4 h. CFR rail from Brașov 2 h 40.

itinerary.title: Sibiu, and the paperwork that saves the week
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at Sibiu airport, then do the boring things properly: photograph every panel and the tyre tread, confirm the rovinietă is active on the plate, and get the cross-border annex emailed to you. Ask explicitly whether Moldova/Ukraine/Serbia are excluded — they almost certainly are.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk Piața Mare and Piața Mică, cross the Podul Minciunilor, and climb the Turnul Sfatului for the tin-roofed eye-windows that make Sibiu's rooftops famous. The Brukenthal National Museum on Piața Mare holds the best old-master collection in Romania [VERIFY: current hours].
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Crama Sibiul Vechi on Strada Papiu Ilarian — cellar vaults, ciorbă de burtă, bulz. Then fill the tank at the Petrom on Șoseaua Alba Iulia, because tomorrow's first proper station is 100 km away.
itinerary.dayStats: 0 km driving

itinerary.title: Foothills, Cistercians and the first ramp
itinerary.morning: DN1 east through Avrig to **Cârța**, where the roofless Cistercian abbey of 1202 sits behind a Saxon fortified church — twenty minutes, and the only Gothic ruin on the route.
itinerary.afternoon: Făgăraș for the moated brick **Cetatea Făgărașului**, then turn south onto DN7C at Cârțișoara. Stop at the Bădea Cârțan museum, then run the easy lower section to **Bâlea Cascadă** (1,234 m). The road narrows and the temperature drops six degrees in fifteen minutes.
itinerary.evening: Sleep at the Bâlea Cascadă chalet by the cable-car station, or drop back to a Cârțișoara guesthouse if beds are gone. Walk the twenty minutes to the waterfall itself before the light goes. Cash only at several kiosks up here.
itinerary.dayStats: 100 km / 2 h 15 driving

itinerary.title: The Transfăgărășan, north to south
itinerary.morning: Be at the Bâlea Cascadă barrier by 07:15 — the restricted sector opens at 07:00 and the coach traffic arrives around ten. Twelve kilometres of stacked hairpins lift you to **Bâlea Lac, 2,034 m**, a glacial tarn in a rock cirque. Coffee at **Cabana Bâlea Lac** on the shore.
itinerary.afternoon: Through the **884 m Bâlea tunnel** — unlit, wet, single lane each way, headlights on — and out onto the Argeș side, which is the better half: longer sightlines, fewer people, the Piscul Negru switchbacks unwinding for 20 km. Then the **Vidraru dam**, 166 m of concrete arch across the Argeș gorge [VERIFY: Vidraru dam crossing status during rehabilitation works].
itinerary.evening: **Poenari Citadel** — 1,480 concrete steps up the ridge to Vlad Țepeș's real fortress, roughly 45 minutes up in the cool of the evening [VERIFY: current hours and any bear-related closure]. Sleep in Curtea de Argeș.
itinerary.dayStats: 75 km / 3 h 30 driving with stops

itinerary.title: Curtea de Argeș to the Parâng gate
itinerary.morning: The Curtea de Argeș Episcopal Cathedral, 1517, with its twisted turrets and the royal tombs of the Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen kings. Breakfast of covrigi from the bakery on Bulevardul Basarabilor.
itinerary.afternoon: DN7 west to Râmnicu Vâlcea, then DN67 along the Subcarpathian shelf through **Horezu** — UNESCO-listed Brâncovenesc monastery and the ceramics workshops on the main road, where the cockerel motif is genuinely local, not imported. Lunch at **Casa Argeşeană** if you leave late enough to still be near Argeș [VERIFY: current hours].
itinerary.evening: Arrive **Novaci** at the foot of the Parâng. Refuel here — this is the last reliable pump before Sebeș, 140 km of mountain later. Guesthouse dinner: tochitură and țuică from the plum orchards below town.
itinerary.dayStats: 180 km / 3 h 40 driving

itinerary.title: The Transalpina, and Pasul Urdele at 2,145 m
itinerary.morning: Climb DN67C to **Rânca** (1,600 m), a scrappy ski hamlet that exists because of the road. Then keep going: the treeline falls away and the Transalpina turns into the thing people come for — a ribbon on open alpine grass with shepherds' flocks crossing without warning.
itinerary.afternoon: **Pasul Urdele, 2,145 m**, Romania's highest paved pass. Park at the saddle and walk fifteen minutes onto the ridge for the Parâng panorama. Descend past Pasul Ștefanu and Pasul Dengheru to **Obârșia Lotrului**, a road junction with two cabanas and no phone signal.
itinerary.evening: North on DN7A/DN67C down the Sebeș valley — long, narrow, unlit, and slower than the map claims. Sleep in **Sebeș** or push the extra 15 km to **Alba Iulia** for a better dinner.
itinerary.dayStats: 72 km / 2 h 20 driving

itinerary.title: Alba Iulia and a rough-road monastery
itinerary.morning: **Cetatea Alba Carolina**, Romania's largest Vauban star fort, seven bastions and the 1918 Union Hall. Walk the Gate III sally-port carvings and the Orthodox Coronation Cathedral.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Râmeț detour**: Teiuș, then a narrowing county road to Râmeț Monastery in its limestone gorge — 45 km and 1 h 15 each way, last kilometres rough but fine in a normal car when dry. (**Cheile Bicazului** is 330 km each way in the Eastern Carpathians: a two-day add-on, not an afternoon.)
itinerary.evening: Back to Alba Iulia. Dinner at Pub 13 inside the bastion walls, then the 20:00 changing of the guard in period Habsburg uniform [VERIFY: 2026 guard-change schedule].
itinerary.dayStats: 90 km / 2 h 30 with the detour

itinerary.title: Saxon fringe and the drop back to Sibiu
itinerary.morning: A10 and A1 south-east, then peel off to **Cisnădioara** for the 12th-century Romanesque church on its conical hill — ten minutes' walk up, the oldest intact church in Transylvania.
itinerary.afternoon: **Cisnădie**'s fortified church tower, then back into Sibiu. Refuel and clean the car before drop-off; Carpathian tar and grit will otherwise appear on the damage sheet.
itinerary.evening: Last dinner at Kulinarium on Piața Mică, then the walls at Strada Cetății. Fly out or take the 06:40 IR to Bucharest.
itinerary.dayStats: 75 km / 1 h 30 driving

accommodationStrategy.name: Cabana Bâlea Lac
accommodationStrategy.description: the lake at dawn and dusk without the day-trippers, and your car is already above the 07:00 barrier. Basic, cold, shared bathrooms, cash preferred [VERIFY: current rate].
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct by phone/Facebook, 4–8 weeks ahead for July–August weekends.

accommodationStrategy.name: Bâlea Cascadă chalet
accommodationStrategy.description: the fallback when the tunnel sector is shut or the lake cabana is full, and the base station for the **Bâlea cable car**, which runs when the road above is closed — the winter way to the **Hotel of Ice**, rebuilt each December from lake ice [VERIFY: 2026 cable car tariff, hours and Hotel of Ice build].
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct, 2–3 weeks ahead.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Kronprinz / Casa Luxemburg
accommodationStrategy.description: real parking rather than street roulette, walkable to both squares, and luggage held on your rental-return morning.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–4 weeks ahead; Sibiu fills for the June Jazz and August Medieval festivals.

logistics.connectivity: Orange and Vodafone cover the valleys; nothing between Piscul Negru and Vidraru, nothing at Obârșia Lotrului. Download offline maps for the whole loop.
logistics.emergency: 112 for everything. Mountain rescue is Salvamont, reachable via 112 or the Salvamont app; the Sibiu and Gorj county teams cover this route.
logistics.weather: Afternoon storms build over Bâlea and Urdele from mid-July; fog can drop the tunnel sector to walking pace in an hour. Snow is possible at 2,000 m in any month.
logistics.bookingWindows: Bâlea Lac and Rânca beds 4–8 weeks for summer weekends; Sibiu 3–4 weeks; the car 6–8 weeks (automatics are scarce and cost 30–40% more).
logistics.money: Romanian leu (RON), roughly 5 RON to €1. Cards work in towns; carry €40–€60 in RON for cabanas, the Poenari kiosk and shepherd cheese stalls.
logistics.transportRules: 50 km/h in towns, 90 on DN roads, 130 on motorway. Zero-tolerance alcohol limit (0.00‰). Dipped headlights compulsory outside towns, day and night. Winter tyres required on snow-covered roads 1 November–31 March.
logistics.permits: Rovinietă mandatory; DN7C's Bâlea Cascadă–Piscul Negru sector is 07:00–21:00 only, with extra restrictions on cyclists and pedestrians in peak weeks. Do not feed the bears on DN7C — it carries a fine and causes the closures.

proTips: Drive the Transfăgărășan **south-bound and early**: barrier at 07:00, Bâlea Lac by 08:15, through the tunnel before the coaches. Northbound afternoon traffic queues 40 minutes at the tunnel on August weekends.
Sleep at Bâlea Lac midweek, not on a Saturday. The same cabana bed costs less and you get the tarn to yourself at 06:00.
Climb Poenari's 1,480 steps at 17:30, not midday — the stairway is shaded and the ridge light on Vidraru is better.
Fill up in Novaci before the Transalpina and in Făgăraș before the Transfăgărășan. There is no fuel between Novaci and Sebeș.
The Transalpina is the better road and almost nobody outside Romania knows it. If weather forces a choice, drive DN67C.
Learn *"Un plin, vă rog"* (fill it up) and *"Se poate cu cardul?"* (can I pay by card?) — the second saves you at every cabana till.
If DN7C is shut for weather, take the **Bâlea cable car** from the Cascadă chalet — it runs year-round and gets you to the lake anyway.

raw.Driving legs (km + realistic time): Sibiu→Cârța 40 km/50 min (DN1); Cârța→Făgăraș 25 km/30 min; Făgăraș→Bâlea Cascadă 35 km/55 min; Bâlea Cascadă→Bâlea Lac 13 km/40–55 min (the hairpin ladder); Bâlea Lac→Piscul Negru 20 km/45 min; Piscul Negru→Vidraru 25 km/40 min; Vidraru→Poenari 4 km/10 min; Poenari→Curtea de Argeș 25 km/30 min; Curtea de Argeș→Novaci 155 km/3 h 05 (DN7, then DN67 via Horezu); Novaci→Rânca 18 km/35 min; Rânca→Pasul Urdele 20 km/45 min; Urdele→Obârșia Lotrului 34 km/1 h; Obârșia Lotrului→Sebeș 85 km/1 h 50 (Valea Sebeșului, narrow and pot-holed); Sebeș→Alba Iulia 15 km/20 min; Alba Iulia→Sibiu 70 km/1 h 10 (A10/A1).
raw.Named passes and closure dates: Transfăgărășan DN7C: high point at the Bâlea tunnel, 884 m long, portal at roughly 2,040–2,050 m; **reopened Friday 12 June 2026 at noon** for the season, and the **Bâlea Cascadă (Sibiu) ↔ Piscul Negru (Argeș) sector is open to traffic 07:00–21:00 only** — outside those hours barriers drop. Typical annual closure runs late October/1 November to mid-June; never plan on it before mid-June. Transalpina DN67C: **reopened 29 May 2026** with traffic restrictions; high point **Pasul Urdele, 2,145 m**, the highest road pass in Romania.
raw.Car rental cross-border rules: Take a compact with real torque, not the cheapest 1.0 petrol — you pull 8–12% gradients loaded. The Green Card (Carte Verde) is standard for EU travel, but almost every Romanian rental **restricts or forbids entry to Moldova, Ukraine and Serbia**; going there needs prior **written authorisation** plus an extended Green Card, arranged days ahead and charged (€30–€60). Bulgaria and Hungary are normally permitted with notice. An unauthorised crossing voids CDW entirely.
raw.Vignette: The **rovinietă** is Romania's electronic vignette, mandatory on all national (DN) roads including DN7C and DN67C. Buy at any OMV/Petrom/Rompetrol till, at roviniete.ro or via the eRovinieta app; plates are scanned, no sticker. There is no 7-day product: category A (cars up to 8+1 seats) runs **1 day €3.50 (about 18 RON), 10 days €6 (about 31 RON), 30 days €9.50 (about 50 RON), 60 days €15 (about 79 RON), 12 months €50 (about 263 RON)** — the 2026 tariff, set in euro and billed in lei at the CNAIR monthly rate, so a fortnight's driving costs the price of a coffee stop. A Euro-emissions-banded tariff has been drafted to replace it but was not yet in force at the start of September 2026. Most rentals include it — confirm in writing.
raw.Viewpoints and laybys: Poarta Raiului above Rânca; the Cârțișoara-side terrace on DN7C over the hairpin ladder; the Vidraru dam crest under the Prometheus statue; the Piscul Negru switchbacks; the Urdele saddle car park; the Bâlea Cascadă chalet terrace.

trips.title: Julian Alps Passes: Vršič, Predel & Mangart
trips.subRegion: Gorenjska & Primorska — Upper Sava, Trenta and the Soča Valley

bestPeriod.window: Mid-June–early July & September–early October (all three passes reliably open)
bestPeriod.avoid: November–mid-May — Vršič is closed or chained-only, Mangart and Predel shut entirely; August brings Vršič shuttle-season congestion
bestPeriod.raw: Mid-June–early July & September–early October (all three passes reliably open)

accommodation.note: Bovec and Kranjska Gora mid-range; one splurge night in Bohinj

food.note: Gostilna dinners €25–€40; Soča trout is the local extravagance

transport.note: Rental, fuel, weekly e-vinjeta €16, Mangart toll €10, parking

activities.note: Vintgar, Kobarid Museum, Boka viewpoint, optional rafting

profile.difficultyNote: 2 — mostly driving, with a 1 h 30 Vintgar gorge boardwalk and a 40-minute walk to the Mangart Saddle

trips.gatewayAirport: LJU — Ljubljana Jože Pučnik; 62 km / 50 min to Kranjska Gora via A2 and Route 201
trips.summary: Slovenia packs three genuinely serious alpine roads into an area you can cross in ninety minutes, and this week drives all of them properly rather than ticking them off. Vršič is the headline — 1,611 m, fifty numbered hairpins, several of them still surfaced in the original 1915 Russian-laid cobbles — but Mangart is the one that stays with you, a 12 km toll road drilled through five unlit tunnels to the highest asphalt in the country. Between the passes you get the Soča itself, a river the colour of glacier milk running past Trenta, Bovec and Kobarid, and a Predel crossing into Italy that takes twenty minutes and feels like a different century. It suits drivers who enjoy technical roads for their own sake, and who are content to spend an entire afternoon covering 40 km.

itinerary.title: Ljubljana to Kranjska Gora, and Zelenci at dusk
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at LJU. Buy the weekly e-vinjeta before you leave the airport forecourt — the A2 begins immediately and enforcement is camera-based. Run the A2 to Jesenice, then Route 201 up the Sava valley.
itinerary.afternoon: Settle in Kranjska Gora and walk or drive the 4 km to the Zelenci nature reserve, where the Sava Dolinka rises out of an emerald spring pool. There is a small paid car park at the trailhead.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Gostilna Pri Martinu in Kranjska Gora — a proper valley inn; order the ričet with smoked pork, or the beef goulash with buckwheat žganci.
itinerary.dayStats: 62 km / 50 min; weekly e-vinjeta €16; A2 is fully vignette-covered; Zelenci parking €3.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Kotnik, Kranjska Gora — small, family-run, free parking on site.

itinerary.title: Vršič: fifty hairpins and the Russian Chapel
itinerary.morning: Leave by 08:00 to have the cobbles to yourself. The 24 northern hairpins are numbered on stone markers; bend 8 carries the Russian Chapel, built in 1916 by prisoners of war who died in an avalanche while constructing this road. Park in the layby just past it.
itinerary.afternoon: At the 1,611 m summit, walk ten minutes up toward the Poštarski dom for the Prisojnik "window" view. Then descend the 26 southern hairpins into Trenta — this is where cobbles alternate with new asphalt and the drop-offs are unguarded. Stop at the Trenta source of the Soča (Izvir Soče), a 20-minute scramble with fixed cables.
itinerary.evening: Down the Soča road (Route 206) to Bovec. Eat at Gostilna Sovdat for Soča trout, or Thirsty River Brewery for a post-drive beer.
itinerary.dayStats: 52 km / 4 h with stops; 50 hairpins; summit 1,611 m; max gradient 12%; no toll; ~1,100 m of descent into Trenta.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Sanje ob Soči, Bovec — designer rooms, generous free parking, five minutes from town.

itinerary.title: Mangart, the highest asphalt in Slovenia
itinerary.morning: Drive Bovec to Log pod Mangartom, then onto the Mangartska cesta. Pay the €10 toll at the barrier. The five tunnels are unlit, unsigned and single-lane — headlights on, horn before entry, and give way to anything descending. Ascend in second gear.
itinerary.afternoon: Park at the km 9 lot (90 spaces; arrive before 10:00 in July–August or you will be turned back at the automatic barrier). Walk the 40 minutes to the Mangart Saddle at 2,055 m, with Jôf di Montasio and the Italian Julians filling the horizon. Descend using engine braking only; riding the brakes for 9 km will fade them.
itinerary.evening: Back in Bovec, walk to the Boka waterfall viewpoint layby on the road toward Žaga — Slovenia's highest falls, best in late afternoon when the west light hits the cliff face.
itinerary.dayStats: 46 km / 3 h 30; Mangart toll €10; 12 km climb, 980 m ascent; 5 unlit tunnels; saddle 2,055 m; road open mid-June to November.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Sanje ob Soči, Bovec (second night).

itinerary.title: Predel into Italy, and back over the border
itinerary.morning: Take Route 203 up to the Predel Pass at 1,156 m — a short, well-surfaced climb past the ruined Predel fort and the Log pod Mangartom war cemetery. Cross into Italy at Cave del Predil.
itinerary.afternoon: Drop to Tarvisio on the SS54, then loop back via the SS13 and the Rateče border into Slovenia — a 90 km circuit that crosses two national borders without a single passport check. Stop at Lago del Predil for lunch on the water.
itinerary.evening: Return to Bovec via Vršič or the Soča road (choose the valley road if it has rained — the cobbles are slick). Dinner at Martinov Hram in Kobarid if you extend the loop south.
itinerary.dayStats: 95 km / 2 h 45; Predel 1,156 m; Italian autostrade not used, so no Telepass needed; Slovenian vignette still required on return to A-roads.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Hvala, Kobarid — moving base south; paid garage under the hotel.

itinerary.title: Kobarid, the Soča gorge and the Napoleon Bridge
itinerary.morning: The Kobarid Museum on the Isonzo Front is the best small war museum in the Alps — two hours, and it recontextualises every fortification you have driven past. Then walk the Kozjak waterfall loop from the Napoleon Bridge car park.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive the Route 102 south along the Soča toward Tolmin, stopping at the Tolmin gorges (Tolminska korita) — the lowest point of Triglav National Park at 180 m, and a striking contrast to yesterday's 2,055 m.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Hiša Franko in Staro Selo, 3 km from Kobarid — Ana Roš's three-Michelin-star restaurant. Book months ahead, or eat superbly for a fifth of the price at Gostilna Breza in Kobarid.
itinerary.dayStats: 55 km / 1 h 20; Tolmin gorge entry €8; Kobarid Museum €8; Kozjak loop 3.5 km / 1 h.

itinerary.title: Over the Soriška planina to Bohinj
itinerary.morning: Take Route 403 from Podbrdo over the Soriška Planina saddle (1,277 m) — a quiet, wide, beautifully graded road with about a dozen open bends and no traffic. It drops you into the Selška valley.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross to Lake Bohinj via Bohinjska Bistrica. Drive the north shore road to Ukanc; the Savica waterfall car park is at the road's end. In peak summer Bohinj closes the Ukanc road to non-residents from mid-morning — arrive before 09:30 or use the Bohinj park-and-ride.
itinerary.evening: Sunset from the Church of St John the Baptist at the lake's eastern outlet, then dinner at Gostilna Rupa in Srednja vas for žlikrofi and Bohinj cheese.
itinerary.dayStats: 78 km / 1 h 50; Soriška Planina 1,277 m; Bohinj parking €10–€15/day; Savica entry €4.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Bohinj, Bohinjsko jezero — lakeside, underground parking included.

itinerary.title: Vintgar gorge and the run to Ljubljana
itinerary.morning: Drive to Zgornje Gorje for the Vintgar Gorge. Entry is timed-slot only and must be booked online; the 1.6 km boardwalk hangs over the Radovna river and ends at the Šum waterfall. First slot at 08:00 is the one worth having.
itinerary.afternoon: Bled for coffee at Slaščičarna Zima and a kremšnita, then the A2 south to Ljubljana. If you have time, stop at Radovljica's medieval core — the free car park sits just outside the walls.
itinerary.evening: Return the car at LJU with a full tank. Fuel at the Petrol station on the airport approach road.
itinerary.dayStats: 82 km / 1 h 30; Vintgar €20 adult, timed entry; Bled parking €3/h; A2 vignette-covered.
itinerary.sleep: Departure, or Vander Urbani Resort, Ljubljana old town.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Kotnik
accommodationStrategy.description: Twelve rooms above one of the valley's better pizzerias, with free off-street parking directly outside — a real advantage in a resort where hotel garages cost €15 a night. It sits 400 m from the Vršič turn-off, so you can be on the first hairpin eight minutes after breakfast. €95–€135 a double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Sanje ob Soči
accommodationStrategy.description: Two nights here cover both the Vršič descent and the Mangart day without moving. Large gravel car park with room for a roof box, drying space for wet gear, and breakfast from 07:30 which is early enough to beat the Mangart barrier queue. €120–€180.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Hvala
accommodationStrategy.description: The Soča valley's grande dame, on the main square, with a covered garage — a genuine consideration in Kobarid where the square fills with tour coaches by 10:00. Walking distance to the Kobarid Museum and the Napoleon Bridge trailhead, and Hiša Franko is a nine-minute drive. €130–€190.

logistics.connectivity: Slovenia is in the EU roaming zone — your EU plan works at domestic rates. Coverage is good in the valleys and drops entirely in the Mangart tunnels and the Vršič north face. Download offline maps; nav apps routinely mis-time these roads.
logistics.emergency: 112 for everything, including the Slovenian Mountain Rescue Association (GRZS). Rescue is not free for non-members; a €30 GRZS card or comprehensive alpine cover is strongly advised. Road assistance is 1987 (AMZS).
logistics.weather: The Soča valley gets Mediterranean moisture funnelled into alpine terrain, producing some of Europe's highest rainfall. Afternoon thunderstorms are near-daily in July. A **foehn** wind can lift temperatures 10°C in an hour, and autumn fog fills the Trenta valley below 800 m while the passes sit in sunshine.
logistics.bookingWindows: Vintgar Gorge requires a timed online ticket — book 3–7 days ahead in summer. Hiša Franko takes reservations 2–3 months out. Bovec and Kobarid hotels fill for the late-July Soča festivals. Vršič itself needs no booking.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are accepted essentially everywhere, including the Mangart toll booth and mountain huts. Keep €20 in coins for parking meters and gorge turnstiles. Tipping is 5–10%, rounded.
logistics.transportRules: The e-vinjeta is plate-registered and mandatory on all motorways and expressways — verify your rental already has one and that it is registered to the correct plate. Headlights are mandatory 24/7. Winter equipment (winter tyres or chains carried) is legally required 15 November–15 March and any time there is snow. Alcohol limit 0.05%.
logistics.permits: Most of this route lies inside Triglav National Park. Wild camping and campervan overnighting are banned within the park and actively fined. Drones require permission from the park authority and are prohibited over Vintgar, Bohinj and Vršič. Off-road driving on forest tracks is illegal.
logistics.health: Tap water is excellent throughout and free at village fountains. **Tick-borne encephalitis is endemic in Slovenia** — it is one of Europe's highest-incidence countries; consider vaccination if you plan forest walking. The Soča is 8–12°C even in August; cold shock is the real swimming risk. Altitude on this route tops out at 2,055 m on foot, which needs no acclimatisation.

proTips: Drive Vršič **north to south, before 09:00**. The cobbled bends are in shade and the descent hairpins into Trenta open toward the light. After 10:00 the pass fills with motorcycle groups and the free shuttle, and passing on the cobbles becomes genuinely unpleasant.

Reach the Mangart barrier before 10:00. The km 9 car park has 90 spaces and an automatic barrier that simply stops admitting cars when full — arriving at midday in August can mean a wasted €10 and a turnaround on a single-track road.
Descending Mangart and Vršič, select second gear and stay off the brake pedal. Brake fade on a 980 m descent is the single most common cause of rental damage claims in this region.
Check promet.si the morning of each pass day. It carries live status for Vršič, Mangart and Predel — including the "chains required" flag that appears surprisingly often in September.

Buy the weekly e-vinjeta rather than the monthly even for a nine-day trip if you can stay off motorways for the extra days: €16 versus €32. Confirm the rental's existing vignette expiry date before you assume you are covered.

Vršič's summit parking has been restricted through the 2026 season. Park at the Erjavčeva koča layby just below the summit on the north side, or use the free shuttle from Kranjska Gora and drive the pass on a different day.
The Predel loop into Italy is the cheapest way to add a country: fuel is often €0.10–€0.15/litre cheaper on the Italian side at Tarvisio, and the Tarvisio Saturday market is worth timing for.
In Bohinj, the Ukanc road closes to non-resident traffic on peak days. Park at the Bohinjsko jezero lot and take the free Bohinj Card shuttle instead of circling.
If it has rained, take the valley road back from Trenta rather than re-crossing Vršič. Wet historic cobbles on a 12% gradient offer roughly half the grip of the adjacent asphalt.

raw.Total distance: ~620 km over 7 days. Deliberately short. The Vršič day is 52 km and takes four hours; treat any nav estimate on these roads as roughly 60% of reality.
raw.Vršič Pass (Route 206), 1,611 m: Slovenia's highest road pass. 50 numbered hairpins — 24 on the Kranjska Gora side, 26 on the Trenta side — with several still cobbled in the original Russian-prisoner masonry, notably bends 8, 17 and 22. Gradients reach 12%, the road is 5 m wide in places with no barrier, and the cobbles are treacherous when wet or when leaf-covered in October. Free to drive; no toll, no vignette required (it is a regional road).
raw.Vršič 2026 traffic regime: control barriers monitoring flow were introduced 15 June 2026 but do **not** charge a toll — through traffic remains free for cars, motorcycles and bicycles. Summit parking was suspended for part of the 2026 season, with a managed 117-space lot reopening 1 September. A free shuttle runs Kranjska Gora–Bovec over the pass 1 June–30 September, with higher frequency 26 June–31 August.
raw.Mangart Saddle road (Mangartska cesta): 12 km, ~980 m of ascent, five unlit tunnels hacked straight into rock, some barely single-vehicle. Toll €10 per car (motorbikes and coaches up to 35 seats included; trailers banned). Typically open mid-June to November depending on snow. In 2026 rockslide damage means vehicles reach only the km 9 car park (90 spaces, automatic barrier), from which the saddle at 2,055 m is a waymarked 40-minute walk.
raw.Predel Pass (Route 203 / Italian SS54),: the quiet one. A 20-minute climb from Log pod Mangartom to the Italian border above Cave del Predil, past the Predel fort. Open year-round in principle but frequently snow-closed. Crossing into Italy is a Schengen non-event — no booth, no check.
raw.Vignette & tolls: Slovenia requires an **e-vinjeta**, registered to the plate — no windscreen sticker since 2022. 2026 prices: weekly €16, monthly €32, annual €117.50 for a standard car under 1.3 m front-axle height; taller vehicles and camper vans pay double. Buy at evinjeta.dars.si or any petrol station. Fines run to €300. The Karavanke tunnel to Austria is €9 extra and is not covered by the vignette.
raw.Car rental & cross-border: Slovenian and Italian rentals both work. Crossing into Italy on the Predel is routinely permitted, but a Green Card and written cross-border permission are still needed for Croatia, Bosnia, Serbia or Montenegro; Ljubljana agencies charge €30–€80. One-way LJU-to-Venice or LJU-to-Trieste drops start at €150. Take a manual with real engine braking — an underpowered automatic on the Vršič descent will cook its brakes.
raw.Fuel: last fuel before Vršič northbound is Kranjska Gora; southbound it is Bovec. Nothing between. Bovec's station closes around 20:00 and is closed Sunday afternoons out of season.

sources.verified: Vršič Pass altitude (1,611 m), ~50 hairpins, partly cobbled surface, and the 2026 traffic regime — control barriers from 15 June 2026 with no toll, free Kranjska Gora–Bovec shuttle 1 June–30 September, summit parking suspended until 31 August with a 117-space lot reopening 1 September; Mangart road 2026 €10 toll, five unlit tunnels, 12 km / 980 m ascent, mid-June to November season, and vehicles limited to the km 9 car park (90 spaces) after rockslide damage; Slovenian e-vinjeta 2026 prices (weekly €16, monthly €32, annual €117.50) and the €9 Karavanke tunnel charge.
sources.confidenceNotes: The Mangart km 9 restriction is a live rockslide consequence and could either extend to the saddle or tighten further — re-verify on tnp.si and promet.si before publishing. Vršič's 2026 parking arrangement and shuttle schedule are a new scheme and likely to change for 2027. Mangart and Predel have no fixed opening dates; both are snow-dependent and the "mid-June" figure reflects the 2026 opening only. Vintgar Gorge pricing and timed-entry rules are revised annually. Hiša Franko's status and booking window should be re-checked. Mangart Saddle altitude is cited variously as 2,055 m (road/saddle) and 2,072 m in older sources — the 2,055 m figure is the current one.

trips.title: Nosferatu to the Silver Town: An Orava, Tatra and Spiš Castle Loop
trips.subRegion: Orava, the Tatras, Spiš and the Slovak Karst

bestPeriod.window: the second half of September — clear air over the Orava, castles still open, no Tatra traffic
bestPeriod.avoid: mid-December to mid-March unless you are equipped for snow; several castles and the Orava Village Museum run reduced winter access

activities.note: €80–€140 (castle and cave entries, museums)

profile.difficultyNote: Easy

trips.gatewayAirport: Fly Poprad-Tatry (TAT) or Košice (KSC) and rent there; return the car in Bratislava (one-way fee applies). Alternatively start and end in Bratislava and add 340 km to reach Orava.
trips.summary: Slovakia's castles are absurdly good and almost nobody drives between them. This loop starts under the cliff-top keep Murnau filmed as Count Orlok's lair in 1922, crosses the Orava's empty uplands, slips along the…
trips.hook: Slovakia's castles are absurdly good and almost nobody drives between them. This loop starts under the cliff-top keep Murnau filmed as Count Orlok's lair in 1922, crosses the Orava's empty uplands, slips along the Tatra foot on the Polish border, climbs the largest castle complex in central Europe, drops into caves under the Karst, and ends in a silver town inside a volcano. About 750 km, seven days, and one of them entirely on unhurried mountain road.

snapshot.Start / End: Poprad → Bratislava (point-to-point, ~750 km total)
snapshot.Getting there: Fly Poprad-Tatry (TAT) or Košice (KSC) and rent there; return the car in Bratislava (one-way fee applies). Alternatively start and end in Bratislava and add 340 km to reach Orava.

itinerary.title: To the castle on the rock
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at Poprad, confirm the e-vignette status at the desk, and take the D1 west to Ružomberok.
itinerary.afternoon: Road 59 north up the Orava to **Oravský Podzámok**. **Orava Castle** rises 112 m straight out of the rock above the river; F. W. Murnau shot it as Count Orlok's castle for *Nosferatu* in 1922, and the exterior is unchanged. The tour climbs through five levels [VERIFY: current Orava Castle tour times and price].
itinerary.evening: Stay in the village or in Dolný Kubín. Eat trout, and look at the castle floodlit from the road bridge.

itinerary.title: Log houses and the Roháče
itinerary.morning: West to **Zuberec-Brestová** and the **Múzeum oravskej dediny**, an open-air museum of relocated Orava log houses, a wooden church and a whole street of farmsteads on a forested slope [VERIFY: current Orava Village Museum hours].
itinerary.afternoon: Drive to the head of the **Roháče** valley below the Western Tatras and walk an hour up towards the Roháčske plesá — the road ends and the tarns are a genuine mountain walk, not a stroll.
itinerary.evening: North to **Oravská Priehrada**. The reservoir drowned five villages in 1953; **Slanický ostrov umenia** is the church hill of one of them, left as an island and now an art gallery reached by boat [VERIFY: current Slanický Island boat season and fare].
itinerary.dayStats: 75 km / 2 h

itinerary.title: The border and into the Tatra foot
itinerary.morning: East along the reservoir shore to **Suchá Hora** and the **Chochołowska** border area — high, open moorland peat bog with the Western Tatras filling the southern horizon.
itinerary.afternoon: Either cross to Poland at Chochołów and run through **Zakopane** on road 47/49, or stay Slovak on 66 through Trstená and Liptovská Teplička. The Polish option adds scenery and traffic in equal measure.
itinerary.evening: Arrive in **Ždiar**, a Goral village of painted timber houses strung along road 66 under the Belianske Tatry. Sleep here; the passes are better in the morning light.
itinerary.dayStats: 95 km / 2 h

itinerary.title: Podspády and Kežmarok
itinerary.morning: Drive the **Podspády** saddle at around 1,081 m, the highest road point on this loop, with the Belianske limestone wall on one side and Poland on the other.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to **Kežmarok** — the castle, the burgher square, and the 1717 **wooden articular church**, UNESCO-listed, built entirely without nails under Habsburg restrictions on Protestant building [VERIFY: current articular church opening times].
itinerary.evening: Short drive to Levoča or stay in Kežmarok. Either way, eat early.
itinerary.dayStats: 35 km / 45 min

itinerary.title: The largest castle in central Europe
itinerary.morning: **Spiš Castle (Spišský hrad)**, UNESCO-listed, sprawling over a travertine hill above **Spišské Podhradie** — approach from the west so it fills the road ahead. There is no shade in the upper ward [VERIFY: current Spišský hrad season and entry fee].
itinerary.afternoon: Cross the valley to **Spišská Kapitula**, the walled canons' town of one street and two gates, with the Romanesque St Martin's Cathedral. Then on to **Levoča** and Master Pavol's 18.6 m limewood altar in the Basilica of St James.
itinerary.evening: Levoča's square at dusk, with the Cage of Shame and the free-standing Renaissance town hall.

itinerary.title: Karst, manor and ruin
itinerary.morning: South to the **Slovak Karst** and the **Domica** cave — UNESCO-listed, geologically continuous with Hungary's Baradla across the border, with a boat section on the underground Styx when the water is high enough [VERIFY: current Domica tour times and boat availability].
itinerary.afternoon: North to **Betliar**, the Andrássy manor with its English park, library and hunting trophies, then ten minutes to **Krásna Hôrka**, the hilltop castle badly burned in 2012 and restored in stages — check what is open before you drive up [VERIFY: current Krásna Hôrka reopening status].
itinerary.evening: Sleep in Rožňava or push on towards Brezno.

itinerary.title: Donovaly and the silver town
itinerary.morning: West through Brezno to **Banská Bystrica**, then the climb over **Donovaly at 960 m** — a wide, well-graded pass with a summit car park and a genuine panorama into the Veľká Fatra.
itinerary.afternoon: South-west to **Banská Štiavnica**, UNESCO-listed, sitting inside a collapsed volcanic caldera. Trojičné námestie, the plague column, the Old and New Castles, and the **Calvary** on its cone above the town.
itinerary.evening: Swim in a *tajch* — Klinger or Počúvadlo, the 18th-century mining reservoirs now used as lakes — then drive the last 190 km to Bratislava, or sleep and drive it in the morning.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Odboj
accommodationStrategy.description: secure off-street parking under the castle rock, so you can walk to the first tour of the day rather than fight the coach park, and it is on the right side of town for the Zuberec run next morning.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct, 3–4 weeks ahead [VERIFY: current nightly rate].

accommodationStrategy.name: Penzión Kamzík
accommodationStrategy.description: right on the pass road with its own parking, half-board, and a drying room — useful because Ždiar sits at 900 m and the weather here changes faster than in the Spiš. Good base for the Podspády drive in morning light.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct or Booking.com, 3 weeks ahead; earlier for the ski season.

accommodationStrategy.name: Penzión Kachelman
accommodationStrategy.description: parking in a town where the streets are 1:8 gradients and the historic core is close to impassable for a stranger; from here you walk to everything and only touch the car to leave for Bratislava.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct, 4 weeks ahead; sold out for the Salamander festival weekend in September.

logistics.connectivity: Good 4G on all main roads. Weakest in the upper Orava valleys, on the Suchá Hora moor and in the Karst below Domica. Download offline maps for the Orava.
logistics.emergency: 112. Mountain rescue **HZS 18 300** if you leave the car for the Roháče or the Belianske foot — Slovak mountain rescue is chargeable to the rescued person without insurance. Motorway assistance is via your rental's number, not 112.
logistics.weather: Donovaly and Podspády get snow from November and hold it into April. Autumn fog sits in the Orava basin until 10:00. Summer thunderstorms build over the Tatras from early afternoon and the road 66 surface floods in dips.
logistics.bookingWindows: Guesthouses 3–4 weeks. Castle tours are guided and timed: Orava, Spiš and Betliar sell out mid-morning slots in July and August. **Almost every Slovak museum and castle closes Monday** — build the loop so Monday is a driving day.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards everywhere for fuel and hotels; carry €80–€120 cash for castle kiosks, cave tickets and village parking. Fuel is roughly on a par with Czechia and cheaper than Austria.
logistics.transportRules: **E-vignette mandatory on D/R roads**, plate-registered, from eznamka.sk. **Blood alcohol 0.0‰ — absolute zero tolerance.** Headlights on at all times, year-round. **Winter tyres legally required in winter road conditions** (unlike Poland, where they are not). Reflective vest reachable from inside the car, not the boot. Speed: 50 in towns, 90 out, 130 on motorway, 90 on expressway in built-up areas.
logistics.permits: No permits. Fuel is the real Orava issue — stations thin out badly between Trstená, Zuberec and the Suchá Hora border, and again between Rožňava and Brezno. Fill at half a tank, not a quarter. Cross-border: Czechia, Austria, Hungary and Poland are routinely permitted on Slovak rentals; **Ukraine is excluded**.

proTips: Shoot Orava Castle from the road-59 layby on the far bank in the late afternoon, when the sun comes round onto the rock face. Murnau's exterior shots are recognisably from this side.
Book the first castle tour of the day everywhere. Slovak castles run guided groups only, capped, in Slovak with an English text sheet — the 09:00 slot is a handful of people, the 11:00 is fifty.
Buy the **10-day e-vignette**, not the 1-day. The difference is a few euros and this route drops on and off the D1 four times.
Take the Slovak side from Suchá Hora to Ždiar rather than routing through Zakopane in July and August. The Polish resort adds an hour of traffic for scenery you can get from road 66.
Fill up in Dolný Kubín before the Roháče and in Rožňava before Brezno. Both are the last reliable stations before long empty stretches.
If it is Monday, drive Donovaly and walk the Banská Štiavnica **Calvary** — both open, both free, both better than a closed castle.
Check Krásna Hôrka's status before committing the detour. Restoration since the 2012 fire has proceeded in phases and the accessible parts have changed repeatedly.

notes: Poprad → **Oravský Podzámok** — 130 km, 1 h 50 (D1 to Ružomberok, then road 59 up the Orava valley).
Oravský Podzámok → **Zuberec-Brestová** and the Roháče → **Oravská Priehrada** (Slanická Osada) — 75 km, 2 h with stops.
Oravská Priehrada → **Suchá Hora** border area → **Ždiar** via Poland or the Slovak side — 95 km, 2 h.
Ždiar → **Podspády** → **Kežmarok** — 35 km, 45 min.
Kežmarok → **Spiš Castle** and **Spišská Kapitula** → **Levoča** — 55 km, 1 h 15.
Levoča → **Domica** (Slovak Karst) → **Betliar** → **Krásna Hôrka** — 165 km, 3 h 15.
Krásna Hôrka → **Banská Bystrica** via **Donovaly** → **Banská Štiavnica** — 190 km, 3 h.
Banská Štiavnica → Bratislava — 190 km, 2 h 30.
raw.Named passes and altitudes: **Donovaly, 960 m** — the Ružomberok–Banská Bystrica saddle on road 59, gritted and open year-round but genuinely snowy from November. **Podspády / Ždiarske sedlo, ~1,081 m** on road 66/67 between the Belianske Tatry and the Polish border. **Huty and the Orava passes** on the Zuberec–Liptov link, around 800–900 m. **Vrchslatina and Šturec** on the older Banská Bystrica approaches. None of these close routinely, but all can shut for hours in a blizzard [VERIFY: current winter closure practice on the Zuberec–Huty link].
raw.The e-vignette: Slovak motorways (D and R roads) require an **electronic, plate-registered vignette** from **eznamka.sk** — no sticker, no windscreen anything. For vehicles up to 3.5 t the tiers are a 1-day, a 10-day, a 30-day and a 365-day product, roughly €5 / €12 / €17 / €60 [VERIFY: 2026 e-vignette tariff — re-check at eznamka.sk before travel]. Buy it before you drive; enforcement is by camera and fines are heavy. Rental cars usually come with an annual one — confirm at the desk rather than assuming.
raw.Winter tyres are legally mandatory: in Slovakia when there is compacted snow, ice or frost on the road — a real contrast with Poland, where winter tyres are not legally required at all. Cross the border at Suchá Hora in November and the legal obligation changes underneath you. Slovak law also requires a full winter set on vehicles up to 3.5 t in those conditions, not just two wheels.
raw.Rental cross-border rules: Slovak rentals routinely permit **Czechia, Austria, Hungary and Poland** with no more than a note on the contract. **Ukraine is excluded** by essentially every major desk, and so, usually, are Moldova, Serbia, Albania and Belarus. Declare a Polish leg — this route touches it — and check whether the Green Card and breakdown cover extend [VERIFY: current cross-border fee at Slovak rental desks].
raw.Viewpoints and laybys: The layby on road 59 at **Oravský Podzámok**, opposite the castle rock, is the Nosferatu shot. **Slanický ostrov umenia** jetty at Oravská Priehrada. The **Ždiar** laybys on road 66 looking into the Belianske Tatry. The **Spišské Podhradie** approach from the west, where Spiš Castle fills the windscreen. The **Donovaly** summit car park.

trips.title: Andorra High Route: Comapedrosa, Juclà and the Madriu Valley
trips.subRegion: Vall del Madriu-Perafita-Claror & Parc Natural Comunal de les Valls del Comapedrosa

bestPeriod.window: Late June–early October, with the staffed refuge window roughly 1 June–12 October
bestPeriod.avoid: November–May — the staffed refuges close, the high colls hold snow and the Madriu valley path ices in its lower gorge
bestPeriod.raw: Late June–early October, with the staffed refuge window roughly 1 June–12 October

accommodation.note: Staffed refuge half board €55.80 at Comapedrosa; valley hotels €70–€120

food.note: Borda dinners €25–€35, mountain lunches €12–€18, refuge packed lunch €10–€12

transport.note: Toulouse or Barcelona coach, Andorran bus network, two taxis to trailheads

activities.note: Caldea spa €45–€55, Sorteny natural park, luggage transfers between valleys

profile.difficultyNote: 4/5 — a 2,942 m summit plus three consecutive days of 800–950 m ascent crossing colls above 2,700 m

trips.gatewayAirport: TLS Toulouse-Blagnac, 3 h to La Massana by bus or car; BCN Barcelona 3 h 15 min; LEU Andorra-La Seu d'Urgell 40 min
trips.summary: Andorra is 468 km² and nearly all of it is above 1,000 m, which makes it the densest walking country in the Pyrenees. This week takes its two defining landscapes: the granite bowl beneath **Pic de Comapedrosa, 2,942 m**, the country's high point, and the **Vall del Madriu-Perafita-Claror**, a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape covering nine per cent of the national territory with no road into it at all. Between them the route crosses the Sorteny and Juclà lake basins on the Coronallacs circuit. You sleep in a mixture of staffed refuges with cooked dinners and free unstaffed stone shelters. It suits confident hikers who like high, empty, lake-strewn granite country and do not need a village every night.

itinerary.title: La Massana, Ordino and the Sorteny valley
itinerary.morning: Arrive by coach from Toulouse or Barcelona (3 h–3 h 15 min) into **Andorra la Vella**, then the local bus up to **La Massana, 1,230 m**. Buy gas, maps and anything you forgot; Andorra's sports shops are duty-free and genuinely cheap.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive or bus to **Ordino** and walk into the **Parc Natural de la Vall de Sorteny**, an easy 8 km loop through the botanical meadows — over 700 plant species — to the **Borda de Sorteny refuge at 1,970 m** and back.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Borda Xixerella** near Pal, a converted stone barn doing wood-grilled meats, *trinxat* and Andorran cheese, or at Molí dels Fanals in Sispony.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km / 450 m ascent / La Massana 1,230 m / Sorteny refuge 1,970 m / 3 h realistic / duty-free gas canisters available
itinerary.sleep: Hotel in La Massana or Arinsal

itinerary.title: Arinsal to the Comapedrosa refuge
itinerary.morning: Start from **Arinsal at 1,550 m**, following the Riu de Comapedrosa past the **Cascada de la Roca del Cabirol** on a steadily steepening path through pine to the open cirque.
itinerary.afternoon: Reach the **Refugi del Comapedrosa, 2,260 m**, after **685 m of ascent**, then spend the afternoon walking up to the **Estany Negre** and the Estanys de les Truites beneath the summit wall — good acclimatisation and the best light of the day on the granite.
itinerary.evening: Half board at the refuge (€55.80): soup, a stew, cheese, and a warden's briefing on tomorrow's snow and wind. Forty-five places, so it books out on August weekends.
itinerary.dayStats: 5.5 km / 710 m ascent / Arinsal 1,550 m / refuge 2,260 m / 2 h 45 min–3 h realistic / half board €55.80, bed only €21.90

itinerary.title: Pic de Comapedrosa, 2,942 m
itinerary.morning: Leave at 07:00 for the country's high point. Steep switchbacks to the **Portella de Sanfons**, then a stony ridge and a short easy scramble to the **summit of Pic de Comapedrosa, 2,942 m**, with France, Spain and the whole of Andorra laid out — the "roof of the Principality".
itinerary.afternoon: Descend by the Sanfons route or reverse the ascent, collect gear at the refuge, and continue down to **Arinsal**. Transfer across to **Ordino** or **Canillo** for the eastern half of the week.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Ordino's Plaça Major; Restaurant Armengol or the terrace at Coma. Andorran *escudella* and a Costers del Segre red.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km / 700 m ascent / 1,400 m descent / summit 2,942 m / 6 h 30 min–7 h 30 min realistic

itinerary.title: Sorteny to the Estanys de Juclà
itinerary.morning: Return to the **Borda de Sorteny refuge, 1,970 m**, and climb the Coronallacs stage east over the **Collada dels Meners at roughly 2,713 m**, a long grass-and-scree pull with old iron-mine workings near the top.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend into the Juclà basin and the **Estanys de Juclà**, the largest natural lake in Andorra, and check into the **Refugi de Juclà** at about 2,300 m on its shore.
itinerary.evening: Trout-coloured light on the lake at dusk, dinner in the refuge, and no phone signal to speak of. The Coronallacs stages are exactly this: one coll, one lake basin, one bed.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km / 900 m ascent / 550 m descent / Collada dels Meners approx. 2,713 m / 5 h 30 min–6 h 30 min realistic

itinerary.title: Vall d'Incles and the crossing to Refugi de l'Illa
itinerary.morning: South-west from Juclà, dropping toward the **Vall d'Incles** — a summer-shuttle-only valley of *bordes* and grazing — then climbing again past the Estanys de Cabana Sorda.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross the high ground around the **Coll de Vall Civera (approx. 2,550 m)** into the head of the Madriu and reach the **Refugi de l'Illa, 2,488 m**, a modern staffed refuge beside the Estany de l'Illa with the Riu Madriu starting at its door. It sits inside the UNESCO valley, whose tariffs are approved as public prices by the Andorran government.
itinerary.evening: The refuge's terrace faces east down the entire Madriu. Order tomorrow's packed lunch — it is a long, foodless day out.
itinerary.dayStats: 14 km / 800 m ascent / 650 m descent / Coll de Vall Civera approx. 2,550 m / refuge 2,488 m / 6–7 h realistic

itinerary.title: The full Madriu: Perafita, Ràmio and Escaldes
itinerary.morning: Walk the length of the **Vall del Madriu-Perafita-Claror**, past the **Pla de l'Ingla** and the side turn to the free, unstaffed **Refugi de Perafita** — worth the detour to see how the unguarded system works: bunks, a table, a stove, nobody in charge.
itinerary.afternoon: The long stone-pitched descent past the **bordes de Ràmio**, the *fangars* charcoal platforms and the old irrigation channels, through a hanging beech gorge to **Entremesaigües** and out at **Escaldes-Engordany, 1,100 m**. There is no road the entire way, which is the point.
itinerary.evening: **Caldea** thermal spa in Escaldes (€45–€55) is precisely engineered for legs that have just lost 1,400 m. Dinner afterwards at Can Manel in Andorra la Vella.
itinerary.dayStats: 18 km / 250 m ascent / 1,400 m descent / Madriu valley 42 km², 9% of Andorra / 7–8 h realistic / no vehicle access anywhere in the valley
itinerary.sleep: Hotel in Escaldes-Engordany or Andorra la Vella

itinerary.title: Escaldes, the customs run and out
itinerary.morning: Walk the Madriu interpretation centre and the Romanesque **església de Sant Miquel d'Engolasters** above Escaldes, then the easy Rec del Solà balcony path over Andorra la Vella.
itinerary.afternoon: The duty-free shop before you leave is a national institution — but **Andorra is outside the EU customs union and allowances are enforced at both the French and Spanish frontiers**, typically around 1.5 litres of spirits, 300 cigarettes and a €900 goods value for adults. Do not over-buy.
itinerary.evening: Coach or drive out: 3 h 15 min to Barcelona, 3 h to Toulouse, or 40 minutes to the small La Seu d'Urgell airport.
itinerary.dayStats: 6 km of town walking / Escaldes 1,100 m / customs allowance approx. €900 goods, 1.5 L spirits / BCN 3 h 15 min
itinerary.sleep: Barcelona, Toulouse, or the outbound flight

accommodationStrategy.name: Refugi del Comapedrosa
accommodationStrategy.description: Forty-five places directly beneath Andorra's highest peak, open continuously 1 June–12 October, booked online at reserves.refugicomapedrosa.ad or on +376 327 955 between 09:00 and 19:00. Half board is €55.80 and a bed alone €21.90. Staying here turns the Comapedrosa summit from a 1,400 m valley slog into a comfortable morning.

accommodationStrategy.name: Refugi de l'Illa
accommodationStrategy.description: The only bed at the head of the UNESCO Madriu valley, modern, warm and with government-approved public tariffs. It is the hinge of any Madriu crossing, since the alternative is walking the whole valley in one day from Grau Roig. Book through the Coronallacs portal or the refuge's own site.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel base in La Massana or Ordino
accommodationStrategy.description: Andorra's compact bus network means one valley hotel covers the western half of the week: parking, drying rooms, luggage storage while you are at the refuges, and dinner options that a refuge cannot match. Roughly €70–€120 double, cheaper outside the ski season.

logistics.connectivity: **Andorra is outside the EU roaming zone.** Andorra Telecom is the sole operator and EU SIMs roam at non-EU rates that can be punitive — check your tariff, or buy a local prepaid Mobiland SIM. Coverage is good in the valleys and on the Juclà basin, poor in the Madriu gorge. Download offline maps.
logistics.emergency: **112** reaches the Bombers d'Andorra, who operate mountain rescue and the helicopter. **Andorra is not in the EU and EHIC/GHIC is not valid here** — treatment is charged. Buy insurance that names Andorra explicitly (many policies list it separately from "Europe") and covers mountain rescue and repatriation. Nearest hospital: Meritxell in Escaldes-Engordany.
logistics.weather: Afternoon storms build over the high colls from around 14:00 in July and August; the Collada dels Meners is the exposed one. Autumn fog fills the Madriu quickly. Andorra sits on the Mediterranean–Atlantic divide, so weather can differ completely between Arinsal and Encamp on the same day. Check meteo.ad.
logistics.bookingWindows: Comapedrosa and l'Illa 3–6 weeks for July and August, longer for weekends; the Coronallacs circuit is booked as a package through its own portal. Unstaffed refuges cannot be booked at all. Valley hotels 2–4 weeks in summer.
logistics.money: Andorra uses the **euro** despite being outside the EU. Cards work everywhere in the valleys; carry €200 for refuges and mountain bars. Tipping is not customary beyond rounding up. Prices for fuel, alcohol, tobacco and sports equipment are markedly lower than in France or Spain because of the tax regime.
logistics.transportRules: **Andorra is not in Schengen** and both frontiers have customs posts — passports and vehicle documents are checked, and goods allowances are enforced on exit. Hire cars from Spain or France usually permit entry but confirm the insurance green card covers Andorra. Andorra has no railway; coaches run from Barcelona, Barcelona airport and Toulouse. The domestic bus network is cheap, frequent and reaches every parish.
logistics.permits: No permit is needed to walk, and the refuges and GRP are free to use. The **Vall del Madriu-Perafita-Claror is closed to motor vehicles** and managed under a UNESCO plan; camping is restricted, fires prohibited, and the *bordes* and irrigation channels are protected heritage. Drones require authorisation. Dogs must be leashed near grazing flocks.
logistics.health: Lake and stream water is plentiful but grazed above — filter or treat. Altitude is modest; the real risks are afternoon lightning on the colls and the cumulative knee damage of the Madriu descent. Livestock guardian dogs work the Perafita and Claror pastures — walk around flocks, do not run.

proTips: Book the **Comapedrosa refuge for a weeknight**. Forty-five places against a national high point on a Saturday in August is the tightest bed in the Principality.

Buy your gas canisters, map and any missing kit in **La Massana or Andorra la Vella on day one** — duty-free pricing makes Andorra the cheapest gear shopping in the Pyrenees, and there is nothing to buy above 2,000 m.
Check whether your travel insurance names **Andorra** rather than just "Europe" or "EU". This is the single most commonly missed thing about walking here.
Turn off data roaming at the border and use a **Mobiland prepaid SIM** if you need connectivity. Andorra is outside the EU roaming rules and the bill surprises people.
Walk the **Madriu downhill from l'Illa**, not up from Escaldes. You get the whole World Heritage valley unfolding in front of you and finish at a thermal spa instead of starting at one.

Detour the 20 minutes to the unstaffed **Refugi de Perafita** even if you are not sleeping there. It is the clearest illustration of how the unguarded network functions, and a useful bad-weather option to have seen in daylight.
Use the **Vall d'Incles summer shuttle** rather than driving in — private vehicles are restricted in high season and the shuttle drops you closer to the Cabana Sorda path.
Order the refuge packed lunch the night before on the l'Illa stage. There is no food, no shop and no bar between the refuge and Escaldes-Engordany, seven hours away.
Keep the Caldea spa booking for the evening of the Madriu descent, not a rest day. Sixteen hundred metres of stone-pitched descent is exactly what the thermal circuit is for.

raw.Hut-to-hut booking path: **Refugi del Comapedrosa (2,260 m, 45 places)** → **Refugi de Borda de Sorteny (1,970 m)** → **Refugi de Juclà (approx. 2,300 m, beside Andorra's largest lake)** → **Refugi de l'Illa (2,488 m)**, with the unstaffed **Refugi de Perafita** as a shelter on the final descent. These are among the country's small handful of **refugis guardats** (staffed refuges), and the **Coronallacs** circuit is the official five-stage route linking them. **Comapedrosa books online at reserves.refugicomapedrosa.ad or by phone on +376 327 955 between 09:00 and 19:00**, and runs **continuously from 1 June to 12 October** with out-of-season bookings by arrangement. Its published rates are **€55.80 half board (bed, dinner and breakfast) and €21.90 for the bed alone**. Refugi de l'Illa's tariffs are set as **public prices approved by the Govern d'Andorra** and it books through its own site and the Coronallacs reservation portal. Expect **€50–€60 half board across the staffed network**. Cards are accepted at Comapedrosa and l'Illa but the connection fails in bad weather — carry €200. **Bring a sleeping-bag liner**; blankets are provided.
raw.Staffed versus unstaffed refuges — the s: Alongside the staffed huts, Andorra maintains **roughly two dozen *refugis no guardats*** — free, permanently unlocked stone or metal shelters with bunks or sleeping platforms, a table, sometimes a stove, and **no warden, no food, no water supply and no booking**. They operate strictly first-come, first-served, cannot be reserved, and can be full when you arrive. **Refugi de Perafita** in the Madriu is one. Plan around the staffed huts and treat the unstaffed ones as a bonus or a bad-weather bail-out, carrying a stove and food if you intend to use one. **If a staffed refuge is full**, the practical answers are the nearest unstaffed refuge, a descent to the valley (Andorra is small — nothing is more than 4 hours from a road), or the Coronallacs booking office rerouting your stage order.
raw.Safety markers and waymarking: Andorra uses the **French/Spanish GR system — red-over-white horizontal stripes** on the **GRP (Gran Recorregut del Perímetre / Gran Ruta d'Andorra)**, a roughly **120 km circular route** around the country's edge with an official stage structure, and **yellow-over-white** for PR local routes. The **Coronallacs** stages carry their own logo alongside the GRP marks. Above the tree line the marking becomes **cairns (*fites*) and painted dots**, which are unreliable in cloud on the Collada dels Meners and the Coll de Vall Civera. There are **no via ferratas on this itinerary**; the Vall del Riu and Canillo ferratas are separate excursions.
raw.Elevation and gear essentials: Cumulative ascent across the five walking days is roughly **4,000 m**. High points: **Pic de Comapedrosa 2,942 m**, Collada dels Meners approx. 2,713 m, Coll de Vall Civera approx. 2,550 m, Refugi de l'Illa 2,488 m, Estany de Juclà approx. 2,300 m. **North-facing snow patches on the Comapedrosa summit couloir and the high colls persist into early July**; microspikes are worth carrying before 10 July and an ice axe for a June crossing. No ferrata set required. Poles matter — the Madriu descent loses 1,400 m on stone-pitched mule path.
raw.Water, food resupply and rubbish: This is granite country with lakes everywhere, so water is far more available than in the limestone Pyrenees, but **every basin is grazed** — filter or treat. Staffed refuges sell water and packed lunches (€10–€12, ordered the previous evening). Resupply only in **Arinsal, La Massana, Ordino, Encamp and Escaldes-Engordany**; there is no shop on the high route. **Pack everything out.** The Madriu is a World Heritage site with an active management plan and litter is taken very seriously; fires are prohibited outside refuge hearths.
raw.Bail-out options, rescue and insurance: No point on this route is more than about four hours from a road, which makes Andorra unusually forgiving. Comapedrosa bails to Arinsal (2 h), Juclà to the Vall d'Incles (2 h), l'Illa to Grau Roig or down the Madriu. **112 reaches the Bombers d'Andorra, who run the mountain-rescue and helicopter service.** Andorra is **outside the EU**, so **EHIC/GHIC does not apply** — Andorran healthcare is charged and reimbursement is a private matter. **Travel insurance explicitly covering Andorra (not "EU") plus mountain rescue and repatriation is essential**; many policies list Andorra separately and some omit it entirely.
raw.UNESCO valley rules: The **Vall del Madriu-Perafita-Claror** was inscribed in 2004 as a cultural landscape covering about **42 km², nine per cent of Andorra**, and it is **closed to motor vehicles**. Access is on foot only, principally from **Entremesaigües and Ràmio above Escaldes-Engordany**, from the Vall d'Incles, or over the colls from Grau Roig. Wild camping is restricted, grazing and the *bordes* (stone barns) are living heritage rather than ruins, and dogs must be under control around livestock.
raw.Realistic walking times: Andorran signposts are reasonably honest by Pyrenean standards but still assume a light pack. Add **20–30%**. Arinsal to the Comapedrosa refuge is signed 2 h–2 h 30 min for 685 m; plan 2 h 45 min–3 h with a full pack.

The **Coronallacs** stages carry their own logo alongside the GRP marks. Above the tree line the marking becomes **cairns (*fites*) and painted dots**, which are unreliable in cloud on the Collada dels Meners and the Coll de Vall Civera. There are **no via ferratas on this itinerary**; the Vall del Riu and Canillo ferratas are separate excursions.

trips.title: The Berliner Höhenweg — Zillertal Alps Hut Chain

bestPeriod.note: The Mörchenscharte and Lapenscharte hold old snow into early July; go after mid-July for the cleanest rock on the cabled sections.

trips.gatewayAirport: Innsbruck (INN)
trips.summary: A hut-to-hut week from Mayrhofen along the Berliner Höhenweg, crossing the cable-secured Mörchenscharte beneath the Zillertal's glaciers.
trips.hook: The Berliner Höhenweg is the classic hut chain of the Zillertal Alps: four days of glacier-rimmed saddles between the 1879 Berliner Hütte and the Kasseler Hütte, bookended by an approach through the Zemmgrund and an easier finish on the Tuxer side. Mayrhofen, at the head of the Zillertal, supplies the buses in and the schnitzel out.

snapshot.Base(s): Mayrhofen (start/finish), five huts en route
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 55–65 km, 5,200 m ascent / 5,200 m descent; glacier-moraine paths, cable-secured rock steps, T3–T4
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Innsbruck (INN), then rail to Jenbach and the Zillertalbahn to Mayrhofen (about 1.5 hours total)
snapshot.Who It Suits: Experienced hut hikers comfortable with fixed cable and glacier-adjacent exposure; not a beginner's first hut trip

itinerary.title: Mayrhofen to Furtschaglhaus
itinerary.morning: Bus from Mayrhofen up the Zemmgrund to Breitlahner (1,290 m), the roadhead. The valley narrows fast once you're on foot, following the Zemmbach upstream through larch forest.
itinerary.afternoon: Beyond the Grüne-Wand-Hütte the path steepens toward the Schlegeis reservoir side-valley, climbing to Furtschaglhaus (2,295 m), a large Deutscher Alpenverein hut with the Furtschaglspitze and Großer Möseler filling the head of the valley.
itinerary.evening: Book Furtschaglhaus through the DAV/Alpenvereinshütten online portal — it also serves day visitors who drive to the Schlegeis dam, so beds go fast on clear-forecast weekends.
itinerary.dayStats: 16 km, 1,000 m ascent, negligible descent, 5.5–6.5 hours. Grade T2–T3, well-built valley path, no exposure.

itinerary.title: Furtschaglhaus to Berliner Hütte via the Zsigmondyweg
itinerary.morning: The Zsigmondyweg leaves Furtschaglhaus as a high balcony path, contouring well above the Waxeggkees glacier's tongue rather than crossing it — the non-glacier alternative most hikers take.
itinerary.afternoon: Rock steps and one short cabled section lead over a shoulder before the path drops to Berliner Hütte (2,042 m), the grandest building on the whole circuit — a genuine 1879 alpine hotel in miniature, with the Waxeggkees and Hornkees glaciers framing the view from its terrace.
itinerary.evening: Berliner Hütte is the trip's showpiece and its busiest bed — reserve it as early as the ÖAV calendar allows, by phone if the online system shows no space, since wardens hold back a few beds for exactly that call.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km, 650 m ascent, 850 m descent, 5–6 hours. Grade T3, one short fixed-cable rock step, moderate exposure on the balcony traverse.

itinerary.title: Berliner Hütte to Greizer Hütte via the Mörchenscharte
itinerary.morning: The signature day. Climb steadily to the Mörchenscharte (2,872 m), a narrow gap between the Mörchner and the Wildgerlosspitze where the final 150 m of ascent is on fixed steel cable bolted to slabby rock.
itinerary.afternoon: The descent on the far side is equally cabled and equally exposed before easing into the upper Floitengrund, where Greizer Hütte (2,227 m) sits below the Floitenkees glacier.
itinerary.evening: This is the crux day of the week; arrive with daylight and appetite to spare rather than cutting it fine. Cash only for the bar tab here.
itinerary.dayStats: 11 km, 850 m ascent, 700 m descent, 6–7 hours. Grade T4, sustained fixed-cable sections both sides of the scharte, real exposure — the trip's mandatory via-ferrata set (harness, lanyard, karabiners) earns its weight here even though the cable itself is continuous handrail rather than a full via ferrata course.

itinerary.title: Greizer Hütte to Kasseler Hütte via the Lapenscharte
itinerary.morning: Climb out of the Floitengrund to the Lapenscharte (2,701 m), a broader and less technical saddle than the Mörchenscharte but still with a short cabled step near the top.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend into the Stilluppgrund, where Kasseler Hütte (2,177 m) looks back at the Reichenspitze group across a wide glacial cirque — quieter than Berliner or Greizer, and a good place to slow down.
itinerary.evening: Kasseler Hütte's kitchen does a proper Kaspressknödelsuppe; the terrace catches the last sun of the day.
itinerary.dayStats: 10 km, 700 m ascent, 750 m descent, 5–6 hours. Grade T3–T4, one short cabled step below the scharte, moderate exposure.

itinerary.title: Kasseler Hütte to Ginzling
itinerary.morning: A long, steady descent through the Stilluppgrund, dropping through larch and spruce forest as the valley opens toward the Zillertal floor.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive in Ginzling by early-to-mid afternoon — a genuine break from altitude, with a chance to wash kit and eat something that isn't hut soup. A family-run gasthof in the village is the standard overnight for hikers finishing this stage.
itinerary.evening: Ginzling has small grocers for restocking snacks before the final Tuxer-side day; nothing stays open much past 19:00, so shop early.
itinerary.dayStats: 14 km, 100 m ascent, 1,650 m descent, 4.5–5.5 hours. Grade T1–T2, forest track and farm road, no exposure.

itinerary.title: Ginzling to Gams Hütte and back
itinerary.morning: A regional bus (or a taxi if timing is tight) runs from Ginzling to Finkenberg, from where the path climbs through forest to Gams Hütte (2,048 m) on the Tuxer Alps side of the valley — a deliberate change of scenery from the glaciated Zillertal peaks.
itinerary.afternoon: From the hut's meadow terrace the whole Berliner Höhenweg horseshoe is visible across the valley, a proper vantage on the week just walked. Descend the same way, or loop via the Wanglalm for variety.
itinerary.evening: Return to Ginzling or continue straight to Mayrhofen if the day started early enough.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km, 950 m ascent, 950 m descent, 5–6 hours. Grade T2, wide forest and alpine meadow path, no exposure.

itinerary.title: Ginzling to Mayrhofen and the Ahornbahn
itinerary.morning: An easy valley walk or short bus ride down to Mayrhofen along the Zillertal floor, following the Ziller river.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride the Ahornbahn cable car above town for a last panoramic look back at the peaks the week has crossed, without the boots.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Mayrhofen — the town has no shortage of Gasthöfe serving Tiroler classics for a returning hut party.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km walking plus cable car, 250 m ascent (lift-assisted), 250 m descent, 2–3 hours on foot.

accommodationStrategy.name: Furtschaglhaus, Berliner Hütte, Greizer Hütte, Kasseler Hütte
accommodationStrategy.description: Book the four-hut chain as one block through the Alpenvereinshütten online reservation system the day each hut's calendar opens; Berliner Hütte is the hardest bed on the whole route, given its fame and its car-accessible-ish approach from the Schlegeis dam.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 6–8 weeks ahead for August, sooner for Berliner Hütte.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: €25–€40 half-board for Alpenverein members, €45–€60 for non-members

accommodationStrategy.name: Family-run gasthof in Ginzling
accommodationStrategy.description: Ginzling has several small, long-running gasthöfe used to hikers coming off the Stilluppgrund; ask about drying rooms for wet boots and packs before the Tuxer-side day.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–4 weeks ahead.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel or apartment in Mayrhofen
accommodationStrategy.description: Mayrhofen has a deep hotel base built for exactly this kind of trip; ask about secure gear storage for the days you're on the huts.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4–6 weeks ahead in August.

logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European; Austrian alpine rescue (Bergrettung) direct on **140**. Every hut on this chain has radio contact even where mobile signal drops in the Zemmgrund and Stilluppgrund.
logistics.weather: Storms build over the Zillertal peaks from early afternoon in high summer; cross the Mörchenscharte and Lapenscharte in the morning.
logistics.bookingWindows: Berliner Hütte and Furtschaglhaus fill first, both reachable by strong day visitors as well as trekkers; book them the moment the season's calendar opens.

other.label: Via-ferrata set is genuinely needed
other.text: for Day 3's Mörchenscharte — the cable is continuous and the exposure real, even though it isn't marketed as a formal via ferrata route. Rent one in Mayrhofen if you don't own one; several outdoor shops on the main street do daily hire.

other.label: Hüttenschlafsack mandatory
other.text: at every hut on the chain.

other.label: Cash for huts
other.text: Carry €300–€350 in small notes; card acceptance is patchy above Breitlahner.

other.label: Snow on the saddles
other.text: Both cabled scharten hold old snow into early July on their shaded sides — confirm conditions with the warden the evening before.

other.label: Camping is prohibited
other.text: outside designated sites in this alpine zone.

proTips: Book Berliner Hütte first and build the rest of the chain around its availability — it is the one bed that can force a re-route.
Hire the via-ferrata set in Mayrhofen before the bus to Breitlahner; nothing sells it on the trail itself.
Cross the Mörchenscharte before midday — the cabled rock warms and the traffic (this is a popular crossing) thins in the early morning.
Detour to the Grüne-Wand-Hütte terrace on Day 1 for a coffee stop; it is the last easy espresso before four days of hut filter coffee.
Ask the Kasseler Hütte warden about the Wanglalm loop variant on Day 6 — it adds little distance but avoids retracing the direct ascent path.
Buy the Zillertalbahn ticket as a return from Jenbach; it is a heritage narrow-gauge line and worth timing to catch a steam-hauled service if one is running that week.
Ride the Ahornbahn on the last afternoon rather than the first — the view means more once you recognise the ridgeline you've just crossed.
