trips.title: Orla Perć and the Five Lakes: A Polish Tatra Hut Week from Zakopane
trips.subRegion: Tatry Wysokie & Tatry Zachodnie, Tatrzański Park Narodowy

bestPeriod.window: the first three weeks of September — Orla Perć dry and empty, hut floors free, Morskie Oko without the queue
bestPeriod.avoid: the 1–3 May and 15 August long weekends, and any period with fresh snow on the chains (usually before late June and after mid-October)

transport.note: €45–€85 (PLN 195–365; buses, Palenica shuttle, Kasprowy cable car)

activities.note: €20–€45 (PLN 85–195; TPN entry fees, Gubałówka funicular)

profile.difficultyNote: Hard

trips.gatewayAirport: Kraków Balice (KRK), then 2 h by FlixBus/Szwagropol to Zakopane, or the PKP IC "Tatry" train 3 h 30.
trips.summary: Poland owns barely a fifth of the Tatra range and behaves as though it owns all of it. The Orla Perć is the proof: chains, iron rungs and a knife of ridge that kills people most years. A week of PTTK huts where…
trips.hook: Poland owns barely a fifth of the Tatra range and behaves as though it owns all of it. The Orla Perć is the proof: chains, iron rungs and a knife of ridge that kills people most years. A week of PTTK huts where nobody is turned away and half the room sleeps on the floor, glacial lakes at 1,700 m, and a 2,499 m summit reached by ladder. It rewards experience and punishes bravado.

snapshot.Start / End: Zakopane → Zakopane (loop, ~70 km, ~5,200 m ascent)
snapshot.Getting there: Kraków Balice (KRK), then 2 h by FlixBus/Szwagropol to Zakopane, or the PKP IC "Tatry" train 3 h 30.

itinerary.title: Zakopane, and reading the boards
itinerary.morning: Arrive, and go straight to the TPN information point at Kuźnice for the trail-condition board — closures, snow on the chains, and any Orla Perć restriction are posted there, not online.
itinerary.afternoon: Krupówki, then the Pęksowy Brzyzek cemetery and Willa Koliba, Stanisław Witkiewicz's 1893 prototype of the Zakopane Style. The Gubałówka funicular gives the whole Tatra wall in one look.
itinerary.evening: *Kwaśnica* and *oscypek* with cranberry at a Krupówki side-street *karczma*, then pack: everything you carry for six days, nothing you do not.
itinerary.dayStats: 0 km

itinerary.title: Up to Hala Gąsienicowa
itinerary.morning: From Kuźnice take the blue trail over Boczań and **Skupniów Upłaz** — an open ridge meadow with Giewont opposite — rather than the dull green forest road. Two hours.
itinerary.afternoon: **Schronisko Murowaniec** at 1,500 m, granite and timber, built 1921–25. Drop the pack and walk 40 minutes to **Czarny Staw Gąsienicowy** under Kościelec to check tomorrow's weather from the water.
itinerary.evening: Hut dinner, then bed early. Tomorrow needs a 06:00 start and full daylight from end to end.

itinerary.title: Zawrat, Orla Perć, Kozi Wierch
itinerary.morning: Blue trail past Zmarzły Staw and up the scree gully to **Zawrat, 2,159 m** — chains on the last 150 m, three hours from the hut. Assess honestly at the saddle: wet rock or building cloud means turn left and descend, not right onto the ridge.
itinerary.afternoon: **Orla Perć**, one-way eastward: Mały Kozi Wierch, Zmarzła Przełęcz, the ladders, and **Kozi Wierch (2,291 m)**, the highest summit lying wholly inside Poland. Four to five hours of continuous hands-on ground.
itinerary.evening: Yellow trail down the Dolina Pięciu Stawów headwall to **Schronisko w Dolinie Pięciu Stawów Polskich (1,671 m)**. Soup, dry socks, and the satisfaction of not having become a statistic.

itinerary.title: Szpiglasowa Przełęcz to Morskie Oko
itinerary.morning: A slow start by the Wielki Staw, then the yellow trail up to **Szpiglasowa Przełęcz (2,110 m)** on chains, with the optional ten-minute spur to **Szpiglasowy Wierch (2,172 m)**.
itinerary.afternoon: The chained descent to **Morskie Oko** is the best-known staircase in Poland — steep, polished, and slow when busy. Two hours down to the lake at 1,395 m.
itinerary.evening: **Schronisko przy Morskim Oku**, the 1908 timber hut on the shore. Once the day-trippers leave at 17:00 the lake is a different place entirely. Beds are 140 PLN (~€33) per person from 1 July to 30 September and 120 PLN the rest of the year in the Nowe Schronisko and Gazdówka, 90 PLN year-round in the Wozownia, plus a 2.50 PLN climate fee; the kitchen runs 07:00–21:00 in July and August and 09:00–18:00 otherwise, and the hut takes cash only (2026 tariff).

itinerary.title: Rysy from the Polish side
itinerary.morning: Red trail past **Czarny Staw pod Rysami**, then the long chained ramp up the north face. Four to five hours to the **Polish summit of Rysy at 2,499 m** — the highest point in Poland, with the Slovak main summit at 2,503 m a few metres along the border ridge.
itinerary.afternoon: The descent is slower than the climb: same chains, tired legs, and a queue on the narrow sections from midday. Allow three to four hours back to the lake.
itinerary.evening: Second night at Morskie Oko. Eat *pierogi ruskie* and a plate of *placki* and do not apologise for either.

itinerary.title: Out by the road, in by the valley
itinerary.morning: The 9 km asphalt road down to **Palenica Białczańska** is closed to private cars. Walk it in two hours or take the **electric shuttle**, 80 PLN (~€19) per person uphill from Palenica Białczańska to Włosienica and 60 PLN back down. The *fasiąg* horse carts no longer run to Włosienica: from 1 September 2026 a TPN pilot cut them back to the 2.9 km between Palenica Białczańska and Wodogrzmoty Mickiewicza, at roughly 100 PLN up and 50–60 PLN down (2025–26 rates).
itinerary.afternoon: Bus to Zakopane, then on to **Siwa Polana** and up the **Dolina Chochołowska**, the longest valley in the Polish Tatras at around 10 km, on a broad track you may legally cycle.
itinerary.evening: **Schronisko na Polanie Chochołowskiej (1,146 m)** — the biggest PTTK hut in the range, on a meadow that turns purple with crocuses in early spring; around 70 PLN (~€16) for a dormitory place and 125–130 PLN per person in a double, though these come from a comparison table rather than the hut's own price list [VERIFY: Chochołowska rate direct from the hut].

itinerary.title: The western rim, then out
itinerary.morning: Green trail up **Trzydniowiański Wierch (1,758 m)** for the Western Tatra grass ridges — a different mountain range from Tuesday's granite, and empty by comparison.
itinerary.afternoon: Back down and out to Siwa Polana. The alternatives from Zakopane, if legs and weather allow, are **Giewont (1,895 m)** with its 15 m iron cross of 1901 and its lightning record, or the **Czerwone Wierchy** traverse over Kopa Kondracka, Małołączniak (2,096 m), Krzesanica and Ciemniak.
itinerary.evening: Thermal water at Chochołów or Bukowina Tatrzańska, then the last bus to Kraków.

accommodationStrategy.name: Schronisko w Dolinie Pięciu Stawów Polskich
accommodationStrategy.description: the only bed between Orla Perć and Morskie Oko, and Poland's highest hut. It turns the ridge into a same-day finish instead of an epic. No showers worth the name; wood stove; strict quiet hours.
accommodationStrategy.booking: online through the hut's own system as soon as the window opens — this is the hardest bed in the Polish Tatras.

accommodationStrategy.name: Schronisko przy Morskim Oku
accommodationStrategy.description: base for Rysy without the 9 km road at either end of the day, plus the lake to yourself before 09:00 and after 17:00.
accommodationStrategy.booking: by telephone only — the hut runs no online system — during reception hours 09:00–21:00, 2–3 months ahead for summer; expect floor space otherwise, and bring cash.

accommodationStrategy.name: Schronisko na Polanie Chochołowskiej
accommodationStrategy.description: 100+ places means walk-in is realistic, the valley approach is flat enough for a tired last night, and it opens the Western Tatras without returning to Zakopane.
accommodationStrategy.booking: online where possible, 2–4 weeks ahead; walk-in usually works midweek.

logistics.connectivity: Play, Orange and Plus cover Zakopane, the ridges and most huts; the Chochołowska and Pięciu Stawów valley floors are patchy. Download the *Ratunek* app before you go — it works where a voice call struggles.
logistics.emergency: **TOPR 601 100 300 or 985**, or 112. Rescue is not billed to you in Poland, but insurance for evacuation and hospital care still matters.
logistics.weather: Storms build over the ridge from early afternoon in July and August. Orla Perć, Rysy and Giewont are all lightning traps with iron in the rock — be off them by 14:00.
logistics.bookingWindows: Pięciu Stawów and Morskie Oko 2–3 months for July–August; Murowaniec 4–6 weeks; Chochołowska 2–4 weeks. Palenica Białczańska parking must be pre-booked and sells out by 06:00 in season.
logistics.money: Polish złoty (PLN), roughly 4.3 to €1. Huts take cards but the machines fail when the signal drops — carry PLN 400–500 (about €95–€115) in cash for the week.
logistics.transportRules: No private cars on the Palenica Białczańska–Morskie Oko road: walk or take the e-bus — the *fasiąg* now covers only the first 2.9 km to Wodogrzmoty Mickiewicza. Zakopane–Kuźnice and Zakopane–Palenica minibuses run from ul. Kościuszki roughly every 20 minutes in season.
logistics.permits: TPN entry fee at every gate. Marked trails only; no wild camping, bivouacking or drones, dogs banned throughout the park. Orla Perć's one-way sections are enforced, and high trails close for chamois breeding or rockfall — check the Kuźnice board.

proTips: Do Orla Perć on a **weekday in September**. Weekend traffic on a one-way ridge means standing on exposed ground waiting for a party of twelve, which is exactly when people fall.
Book Pięciu Stawów the hour its window opens. Everything else on this itinerary can flex; that hut cannot.
Walk *up* the Palenica road at 05:30 on a Rysy day if you cannot get the hut. You will pass the first e-bus and reach Morskie Oko in silence.
Say *"Czy są wolne miejsca?"* and expect *"tylko na podłodze"* — only on the floor. Say yes; a mattress at Pięciu Stawów beats descending at dusk.
Skip the Kasprowy cable car unless you buy a timed slot online days ahead. The queue at Kuźnice regularly outlasts the walk to Hala Gąsienicowa.
Carry two litres and refill at the huts only. The high ridge from Zawrat to Kozi Wierch has no water at all, and Rysy's last source is Czarny Staw.
Keep Giewont as the weather-window spare, not the plan. Its chains are the single most lightning-struck spot in the Polish Tatras.

raw.Hut chain and booking channel: Every hut here is **PTTK**-run, and the tradition holds: **nobody is turned away in the mountains** — but that means a mattress in a corridor or under a dining table, not a bed. Booking channels differ hut by hut and this is the detail that catches people out. Chain: **Schronisko Murowaniec, Hala Gąsienicowa** (1,500 m; dormitory around 90 PLN/€21, a figure from a hut-price comparison table rather than PTTK's own tariff) [VERIFY: Murowaniec rate direct from the hut] → **Schronisko w Dolinie Pięciu Stawów Polskich** (1,671 m, Poland's highest hut; its **own online reservation system**, 140 PLN/€33 per person in multi-bed rooms, and it opens two months at a time on published dates — 5 October 2026 for April–May 2027, 11 January 2027 for June–July) → **Schronisko przy Morskim Oku** (1,410 m; **telephone booking only, no online system**) → **Schronisko na Polanie Chochołowskiej** (1,146 m, the largest PTTK hut in the Tatras; walk-in realistic midweek).
raw.Orla Perć, stated honestly: The Eagle's Path, cut in 1903 on Franciszek Nowicki's initiative, is **the most dangerous marked trail in Poland**: via-ferrata-grade terrain — chains, staples, ladders, long unprotected exposure — walked **without** a harness by most people, and it kills hikers most years. Long sections are **one-way, in the Zawrat → Krzyżne direction**. The section here is **Zawrat (2,159 m) → Kozi Wierch (2,291 m)**: roughly 2.5 km of ridge, four to five hours, no water, no shelter, no bail-out between the ends. Do not attempt it on wet rock, with a storm forecast, with a heavy pack, or with anyone new to exposed scrambling.
raw.Waymarks: Polish blazes match the Slovak system: a horizontal three-band mark, white–colour–white. **Red** carries the main ridge lines (including Orla Perć), **blue**, **green**, **yellow** and **black** the approaches and connectors. TPN junction boards give times in hours each way.
raw.Daily ascent/descent: Day 2 +490 m. Day 3 +850/−620 m (Zawrat, Orla Perć, Kozi Wierch). Day 4 +500/−780 m over Szpiglasowa Przełęcz. Day 5 +1,105/−1,105 m to Rysy and back. Day 6 −250/+380 m plus 9 km of road. Day 7 +610/−610 m on the Chochołowska rim.
raw.Park entry and quotas: **TPN** charges a per-entry fee at every manned gate — Kuźnice, Palenica Białczańska, Siwa Polana, Łysa Polana — 11 PLN (~€2.55) per adult, 5.50 PLN reduced, with a seven-day ticket at 55 PLN/27.50 PLN — payable at the gate, online at tpn.gov.pl or by the QR codes posted at each entry point (2026 tariff). The **Kasprowy Wierch cable car** is capped at **180 passengers an hour uphill in the summer season** (a little over 3,000 people a day) with timed slots that sell out days ahead; a return is 165 PLN (~€38) at the ticket office, 129 PLN reduced, and 99–165 PLN online depending on the slot, in the high season running to 30 September 2026. It is **not** covered by the Tatry Super Ski winter pass.
raw.Rescue: **TOPR — Tatrzańskie Ochotnicze Pogotowie Ratunkowe**, founded 1909: **601 100 300** or **985**, plus 112 and the free *Ratunek* app, which sends your GPS position. Unlike Slovakia, TOPR rescue is publicly funded and not billed to the casualty — insurance for evacuation and hospital care is still essential.
raw.Gear tied to altitude: Stiff-soled boots, hardshell, warm layer, gloves for the chains, headtorch, 2 L water, and a **sleeping bag liner** (huts give blankets, not linen). A via ferrata set is optional on Orla Perć and used by a minority; if you would want one, that is a signal to skip the ridge.

typeSpecific.hutBooking: Every hut here is **PTTK**-run, and the tradition holds: **nobody is turned away in the mountains** — but that means a mattress in a corridor or under a dining table, not a bed. Booking channels differ hut by hut and this is the detail that catches people out. Chain: **Schronisko Murowaniec, Hala Gąsienicowa** (1,500 m; dormitory around 90 PLN/€21, a figure from a hut-price comparison table rather than PTTK's own tariff) [VERIFY: Murowaniec rate direct from the hut] → **Schronisko w Dolinie Pięciu Stawów Polskich** (1,671 m, Poland's highest hut; its **own online reservation system**, 140 PLN/€33 per person in multi-bed rooms, and it opens two months at a time on published dates — 5 October 2026 for April–May 2027, 11 January 2027 for June–July) → **Schronisko przy Morskim Oku** (1,410 m; **telephone booking only, no online system**) → **Schronisko na Polanie Chochołowskiej** (1,146 m, the largest PTTK hut in the Tatras; walk-in realistic midweek).

trips.title: The Red Stripe: Seven Days on the Făgăraș Ridge, Suru to Sâmbăta
trips.subRegion: Munții Făgăraș, Southern Carpathians (Sibiu, Argeș and Brașov counties)

bestPeriod.window: the last week of August and the first three weeks of September — snow gone from the couloirs, storms less frequent, springs still running
bestPeriod.avoid: before mid-July (old snow in Strunga Dracului and the Călțun couloirs) and after early October (first snowfalls, refuges unusable)

accommodation.note: €120–€280 (cabana beds €15–€30; refuges free; tent nights free)

food.note: €130–€200 (mostly carried; cabana dinners €10–€15)

transport.note: €90–€170 (Sibiu transfers, Bâlea cable car, taxi off the mountain)

activities.note: €40–€90 (bear spray bought locally, maps, one guided day)

profile.difficultyNote: Expert

trips.gatewayAirport: Sibiu (SBZ) or Bucharest (OTP, 4 h by train to Sibiu/Brașov). Local train or taxi Sibiu → Turnu Roșu, 30 km. Exit by taxi from Mănăstirea Brâncoveanu to Făgăraș or Victoria, then rail to Brașov.
trips.summary: This is the most serious walking in the Carpathians. Seventy kilometres of granite and schist crest above 2,000 metres, with two thousand-metre cirques on both sides, a chained chimney that kills people most summers,…
trips.hook: This is the most serious walking in the Carpathians. Seventy kilometres of granite and schist crest above 2,000 metres, with two thousand-metre cirques on both sides, a chained chimney that kills people most summers, Romania's highest summit as a side trip, and huts spaced not four hours apart but a day and a half. Several of the shelters are unstaffed tin boxes with no water and no warden. You carry the week, or you do not do the week.

snapshot.Start / End: Turnu Roșu (Sebeșu de Sus) → Sâmbăta de Sus (point-to-point, ~75 km, ~6,500 m ascent)
snapshot.Getting there: Sibiu (SBZ) or Bucharest (OTP, 4 h by train to Sibiu/Brașov). Local train or taxi Sibiu → Turnu Roșu, 30 km. Exit by taxi from Mănăstirea Brâncoveanu to Făgăraș or Victoria, then rail to Brașov.

itinerary.title: Out of the forest onto the western crest
itinerary.morning: Taxi from Sibiu to **Sebeșu de Sus** above **Turnu Roșu**, the western terminus of the ridge. Buy **bear spray in Sibiu the day before** — it is legal, sold in outdoor and hunting shops, roughly 100–350 RON (€20–€70), and **it cannot be carried on any flight**, so it is a buy-on-arrival item.
itinerary.afternoon: The red stripe climbs relentlessly through beech, then spruce, then juniper. Six to seven hours to the **Suru** shelter and **Șaua Suru** below **Vârful Suru (2,283 m)**. Water in the last forest stream — fill everything.
itinerary.evening: Camp or squeeze into the refuge. This is the least-visited end of the Făgăraș and you may have the whole western crest to yourself.

itinerary.title: The long empty crest to Negoiu
itinerary.morning: Over Vârful Budislavu and **Șaua Scărișoara**, then the grassy 2,400 m dome of **Vârful Ciortea**. In cloud this is the section where people lose the line — bearings, not instinct.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue over Șaua Gropilor and the Serbota flank, then drop north on the marked descent to **Cabana Negoiu (1,546 m)**, the historic Sibiu-side hut, for a bed, a shower and a hot meal [VERIFY: current Cabana Negoiu rates and whether it is staffed for the full 2026 season].
itinerary.evening: Eat *ciorbă de burtă* and drink one beer, not three. Tomorrow is the crux and it starts early.

itinerary.title: Negoiu, the crux, and Călțun
itinerary.morning: Leave by 06:30. Back up to the ridge and along **Custura Sărății** — narrow, airy and chained in places — to **Șaua Cleopatra**. Here the route splits.
itinerary.afternoon: **Take the Strunga Doamnei.** Reach **Vârful Negoiu (2,535 m)**, the second-highest in Romania and the finest summit on the ridge, with the Argeș cirques falling away south. Then the descent to **Lacul Călțun** and **Refugiul Călțun** at about 2,135 m — glacial tarn, boulder field, and a metal refuge with no warden and no water beyond the lake.
itinerary.evening: Filter lake water. Cook early: storms on this section reliably build from mid-afternoon and the refuge is the only shelter for hours in either direction.

itinerary.title: Over Lespezi to Bâlea Lac
itinerary.morning: The chained climb out of Călțun onto **Vârful Lespezi (2,522 m)** — steep, exposed, the second-hardest passage of the week — then Paltinu and the long crest east.
itinerary.afternoon: **Vârful Vânătoarea lui Buteanu (2,507 m)**, then down to **Șaua Capra** and **Lacul Bâlea** at 2,034 m, the glacial lake sitting at the top of the **Transfăgărășan (DN7C)**.
itinerary.evening: **Cabana Bâlea Lac** — a real bed, hot food, phone signal and, if you need to bail, the **telecabina** down to Bâlea Cascadă and the road. Note that the Transfăgărășan's restricted sector, **Bâlea Cascadă to Piscu Negru, is open only 07:00–21:00** and the road itself only opened for the 2026 season on **12 June**; it is typically shut from late October until mid-June [VERIFY: 2027 Transfăgărășan opening date].

itinerary.title: Fereastra Zmeilor and Podragu
itinerary.morning: East over **Vârful Iezerul Caprei** and Vârful Netedu on broad grassy crest — fast walking, poor navigation in cloud, and the best bear-viewing ground of the trip at dawn on the northern slopes.
itinerary.afternoon: Past **Fereastra Zmeilor**, the Dragons' Window, with its unstaffed refuge, then over Arpașu Mare and down to **Cabana Podragu (2,136 m)** beside Lacul Podragu — the highest staffed hut on the ridge and the logistical hinge of the whole traverse [VERIFY: current Podragu rates and 2026 staffing dates].
itinerary.evening: Podragu is cash-only and runs on a generator. Book by phone days ahead in August; in September you can usually walk in.

itinerary.title: Moldoveanu, 2,544 m
itinerary.morning: Leave the pack at Podragu and go light. The red stripe runs east over Vârful Podu Giurgiului and Ucea Mare to the saddle below **Vârful Viștea Mare (2,527 m)**.
itinerary.afternoon: From Viștea Mare, a fifteen-minute connecting ridge — narrow, rocky, easy in dry conditions — leads to **Vârful Moldoveanu (2,544 m)**, the **highest point in Romania**. Nine to eleven hours round trip from Podragu. Turn around at 13:00 regardless of where you are; the afternoon build here is not negotiable.
itinerary.evening: Back at Podragu, dry everything. Tomorrow is the descent and it is long.

itinerary.title: Dara, and down the Sâmbăta valley
itinerary.morning: North-east over **Vârful Dara (2,500 m)** and Vârful Hârtopu, one of the quietest and most spectacular stretches of crest, with the Podragu and Sâmbăta cirques below on either hand.
itinerary.afternoon: Down through **Fereastra Mare a Sâmbetei** into the **Valea Sâmbetei** — steep, wooded, wet underfoot — past **Cabana Valea Sâmbetei (1,401 m)** for a last meal, then out to the trailhead.
itinerary.evening: **Mănăstirea Brâncoveanu** at Sâmbăta de Sus — a Brâncovenesc-style monastery founded by Constantin Brâncoveanu, with a guesthouse and, more to the point, a road. Taxi to Victoria or Făgăraș, then rail to Brașov or Sibiu.

accommodationStrategy.name: Cabana Podragu
accommodationStrategy.description: the only staffed bed high enough to make Moldoveanu a day trip rather than a two-day expedition. Dormitory bunks, hot food, drying space, generator power, cash only.
accommodationStrategy.booking: by phone, direct, a week ahead in September and two to three weeks in August [VERIFY: current phone booking channel].

accommodationStrategy.name: Cabana Bâlea Lac
accommodationStrategy.description: the mid-route reset. Real showers, a shop, phone signal, cable car down, and the only point on the traverse where you can resupply, post a bag ahead, or abandon the walk with dignity.
accommodationStrategy.booking: online or by phone, 3–4 weeks ahead — it fills with Transfăgărășan road tourists, not hikers.

accommodationStrategy.name: Refugiul Călțun
accommodationStrategy.description: it splits the hardest 25 km of the ridge into two survivable days. No warden, no booking, no water tap, no food, 10–20 places on a first-come basis.
accommodationStrategy.booking: you cannot. Carry a tent and treat the refuge as a bonus, not a plan.

logistics.connectivity: Orange and Vodafone reach much of the crest — surprisingly good on the summits, absent in every cirque. Bâlea Lac and Podragu have signal. Download offline maps before Day 1; there is no data in the Sâmbăta and Podragu valleys.
logistics.emergency: **Salvamont 0725 826 668** and **112**. Give your position as a named summit or saddle plus your waymark colour. Response time from the crest is hours. Tell someone your route and your bail-out points before you start.
logistics.weather: The Făgăraș makes its own weather. **Convective storms build from 13:00–14:00 on most summer days**, and the ridge is the highest metal-free lightning conductor for a hundred kilometres — you are the tallest thing on it. Be off exposed crest by early afternoon. Cloud can drop visibility to twenty metres in minutes, which is the real argument for the compass.
logistics.bookingWindows: Staffed cabanas 1–3 weeks ahead by phone; refuges cannot be booked at all. August weekends are the only genuine crowding. Bear spray needs no permit but must be bought in Romania.
logistics.money: The leu, roughly 5.0–5.1 RON to the euro. **Podragu, Negoiu and Valea Sâmbetei are cash-only** — carry 800–1,200 RON (€160–€240) in small notes for the week. ATMs at Sibiu, Victoria and Făgăraș only.
logistics.transportRules: A rental car needs a **rovinietă** e-vignette, category A: €3.50 for one day, €6 for ten days, €9.50 for thirty — **there is no seven-day product**. Do not park a car at Turnu Roșu and expect to reach it; this is a point-to-point walk and the finish is 90 km from the start by road.
logistics.permits: No entry fee and no permit for the Făgăraș ridge, and **wild camping on the crest is tolerated** in practice outside strictly protected reserves — pitch on grass, never in a refuge doorway, carry out everything. Fires are prohibited above the treeline. Sheepdogs at the summer *stâne* are a genuine hazard: walk round the flock, do not run, and carry a pole.

proTips: **Take the Strunga Doamnei and do not apologise for it.** The Dracului is the famous line; the Doamnei is the one that gets you to Călțun with a heavy pack and both ankles. Guides make the same choice with clients.

**Bears are the reason your food goes in a dry bag, hung, twenty metres from the tent.** Romania holds the **largest brown bear population in Europe outside Russia**, and the Făgăraș has real density on the northern slopes and in the Sâmbăta and Podragu valleys. Cook away from where you sleep, never leave rubbish at a refuge, make noise on wooded descents at dawn and dusk, and if you meet one: do not run, back away slowly, keep the spray on your hip belt where you can reach it, not inside the pack.

**Post a resupply bag to Cabana Bâlea Lac.** It is the only road-accessible point mid-traverse, and it turns a seven-day food carry into two four-day carries — worth several kilos over the hardest days.
**Do Moldoveanu from Podragu, not from the south.** The Argeș-side approaches involve a long forest road and a bivouac; from Podragu it is a single long day with a light pack and a hot meal waiting.

**Water is the limiting factor, not distance.** There is **no water on the crest itself** — you drop to Lacul Călțun, Lacul Bâlea, Lacul Podragu, or the springs 50–150 m below the ridge on the northern side. Fill at every one, and carry four litres over the dry sections.
**Learn *"Unde este apă?"*** — where is water? — and *"Cât mai e până la refugiu?"* Shepherds know both answers and are the only people you will meet for hours.

**Go in the second week of September.** Old snow is gone from the couloirs, the storm frequency drops sharply, the August refuge scrum is over, the springs are still running, and the light on the northern cirques is the best of the year.

raw.The chain of huts and refuges — and the: Staffed and bookable: **Cabana Bâlea Lac** (2,034 m, staffed year-round, own phone/site booking, reached by road and cable car), **Cabana Bâlea Cascadă** (1,234 m, road-served), **Cabana Negoiu** (1,546 m, staffed, phone booking), **Cabana Podragu** (2,136 m, staffed in summer only, phone booking, generator power, cash), **Cabana Valea Sâmbetei** (1,401 m, staffed, phone). **Unstaffed, unbookable, first-come, no water on site, no warden, no food, no rescue on hand: Refugiul Călțun** (by Lacul Călțun, ~2,135 m), **Refugiul Fereastra Zmeilor**, and the **Suru** shelter — the original **Cabana Suru** burned down in 2003 and what stands is a small emergency refuge, not a hut [VERIFY: current status and capacity of the Suru refuge]. Refuges hold roughly 10–20 people and fill on August weekends. **Plan for a tent.** [VERIFY: current 2026 bed rates at Bâlea Lac, Negoiu, Podragu and Valea Sâmbetei]
raw.Waymarking: The main ridge is the **bandă roșie** — a red horizontal stripe between two white bands — running the full traverse from Turnu Roșu to Plaiul Foii. Descents to the north (Transylvanian) side use **blue stripe**, **red triangle** and **yellow stripe** according to valley. Be blunt about the quality: **above 2,000 m the paint is patchy, the cairns are inconsistent, and in cloud on the broad grassy summits — Ciortea, Iezerul Caprei, Podragu — the line is genuinely hard to hold.** Carry a paper map (Muntii Nostri or Dimap Făgăraș), a compass, and the GPX on two devices.
raw.Daily ascent and descent: Day 1 +1,650/−100 m. Day 2 +1,150/−900 m. Day 3 +900/−800 m. Day 4 +950/−1,050 m. Day 5 +900/−800 m. Day 6 +1,000/−1,000 m (Moldoveanu out-and-back). Day 7 +450/−1,900 m. Roughly **6,500 m of climbing** in seven days with a full pack.
raw.Strunga Dracului versus Strunga Doamnei: The classic line onto **Vârful Negoiu (2,535 m)** from Șaua Cleopatra goes through the **Strunga Dracului**, the Devil's Gully: a steep chained chimney, exposed, polished, holding old snow into July, funnelling every stone dislodged above you onto the party below. It has a fatality record. The **Strunga Doamnei** is the marked alternative on the northern side — longer, still chained in places, but far less exposed and far less prone to rockfall. **With a seven-day pack on your back, take the Strunga Doamnei.** Reserve the Dracului for a dry day, light, early, with a helmet, and only if the party is genuinely comfortable on unprotected scrambling.
raw.Gear for 2,500 m without huts: Tent or bivi bag and a bag rated to **−5 °C comfort** (September nights on the crest go below freezing). B-rated boots, helmet for the Negoiu and Călțun sections, 40 m of nothing — this is not a roped route, but gloves for the chains are essential. **4 litres of water capacity** and a filter. Full hardshell, warm layer, hat and gloves in every month. Stove and four days of food minimum, because there is no resupply between Bâlea and Sâmbăta. Headtorch, spare batteries, powerbank, and a whistle.
raw.Rescue and insurance: **Salvamont national dispatch: 0725 826 668**, plus **112**. Install the *Salvamont* and *DSU* apps, which transmit GPS. Salvamont teams operate county by county — Sibiu, Argeș and Brașov all cover parts of this ridge, and response from the crest is measured in hours, not minutes. Carry EHIC plus a policy with mountain-rescue and helicopter cover.

trips.title: Kungsleden North: Abisko to Nikkaluokta
trips.subRegion: Lapland, Norrbotten — Abisko and Kebnekaise massif

bestPeriod.window: Late June to mid-September, matching the STF staffed-hut season and the boat services. July has mosquitoes and midnight sun; the first half of September has autumn colour, no insects and the first frosts
bestPeriod.raw: Late June to mid-September, matching the STF staffed-hut season and the boat services. July has mosquitoes and midnight sun; the first half of September has autumn colour, no insects and the first frosts

accommodation.note: STF mountain huts €45–70 per night for members; Kebnekaise Fjällstation €70–140; Abisko Turiststation €60–110

food.note: €35–60 per day — hut shops sell freeze-dried meals and staples at mountain prices; carry your own for the middle stages

transport.note: €200–320: night train or flight to Kiruna/Abisko, lake boats, Nikkaluokta bus

activities.note: Included; optional guided Kebnekaise summit €150–250

profile.difficultyNote: Moderate–hard. About 105 km over 6 walking days on a well-marked, bridged trail; one pass at 1,150 m; the difficulty is distance, weather and remoteness rather than technicality

trips.summary: A seven-day hiking & alpine trekking itinerary in Lapland, Norrbotten — Abisko and Kebnekaise massif, Sweden.

itinerary.title: Abisko: arrival and the Abisko canyon
itinerary.morning: Arrive by the Stockholm–Narvik night train to Abisko Turiststation (about 17 h, and one of Europe's best rail journeys), or fly to Kiruna and take the bus.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the Abisko canyon where the Abiskojåkka river cuts a gorge through red rock, and see the Lapporten — the U-shaped glacial gate that is the symbol of Swedish Lapland. Weigh your pack, buy last gas canisters at the station shop.
itinerary.evening: Abisko Turiststation. Brief yourself on the route board and register your plan.
itinerary.dayStats: 6 km

itinerary.title: Abisko to Abiskojaure
itinerary.morning: The trailhead arch at Abisko is the northern terminus of the Kungsleden, the King's Trail. Birch forest, boardwalk over wet ground, the river always to your left.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive Abiskojaure hut on the lake — a group of red-painted cabins with a sauna by the water.
itinerary.evening: Sauna and a lake swim at 8 °C. **Water:** the river and its tributaries the entire way; Swedish mountain water is drinkable untreated above the treeline and generally safe here.

itinerary.title: Abiskojaure to Alesjaure
itinerary.morning: Climb out of the birch into open fell. The valley widens; the trail is stony but clear, marked with cairns and red-painted rocks.
itinerary.afternoon: Alesjaure sits above a lake chain with Sámi settlements nearby — this is a working reindeer-herding landscape, not a wilderness in the empty sense. The hut has one of the best saunas on the trail, on a hill with a view down the valley.
itinerary.evening: Sámi-operated boat services run on the Alesjaure lakes in season and can shorten this stage significantly if weather or blisters demand it. `verify: true`

itinerary.title: Alesjaure to Tjäktja and over the pass to Sälka
itinerary.morning: Gentle climb up the Tjäktjavagge valley — a classic glacial trough, wide, treeless and enormous.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Tjäktja pass** at about 1,150 m is the highest point of the Kungsleden and the watershed of the trip. There is an emergency shelter at the top. Descend into the long valley to Sälka.
itinerary.evening: Sälka hut, with a shop and a sauna. If the day is too long, break it at Tjäktja hut before the pass. **Water:** streams throughout; the pass itself is dry for about 4 km.

itinerary.title: Sälka to Singi and Kebnekaise Fjällstation
itinerary.morning: Down the valley to Singi, where the Kungsleden continues south and our route turns east into the Kebnekaise massif.
itinerary.afternoon: The Ladtjovagge valley approach to Kebnekaise Fjällstation, with the massif rising ahead. The station is a full mountain centre — restaurant, shop, sauna, guides.
itinerary.evening: Proper food and a bed. Book the guided summit day now if you want it.

itinerary.title: Kebnekaise south summit
itinerary.morning: Sweden's highest mountain. The **eastern route** is the standard non-glaciated ascent — long, steep, rocky, and hard but unguided-feasible for fit, experienced walkers. The **western route** crosses the Björling glacier and requires a guide, rope and crampons.
itinerary.afternoon: The south summit is a glacier-capped peak whose height changes measurably from year to year as the ice cap melts — it has now dropped to roughly the same height as the ice-free north peak, which is itself a lesson in what is happening up here.
itinerary.evening: Back at the station. Sauna. This is the hardest day of the week by a wide margin — treat the weather forecast as a veto, not a suggestion. **Water:** streams to about 1,400 m only; carry 2 litres.
itinerary.dayStats: 18 km return, 1,700 m, 10–14 h

itinerary.title: Kebnekaise to Nikkaluokta and out
itinerary.morning: The exit valley to Nikkaluokta, a Sámi village and the road head. A boat across Ladtjojaure lake cuts about 6 km off the walk when it is running.
itinerary.afternoon: Bus Nikkaluokta–Kiruna (about 1 h 20), then flight or the night train south. Eat a reindeer burger at the Nikkaluokta café; it is a tradition and it is earned.
itinerary.dayStats: 19 km, mostly descending

accommodationStrategy.name: STF mountain huts
accommodationStrategy.description: Small clusters of red cabins with bunk dormitories, a shared kitchen with gas, a wood-fired sauna at most of them, and a warden. Several have a small shop selling freeze-dried food, chocolate, gas and basic supplies. **No advance booking for the mountain huts** — beds are allocated on arrival and the STF principle is that nobody is turned away, with floor mattresses as the overflow. STF membership gives a meaningful discount. `verify: true`

accommodationStrategy.name: Kebnekaise Fjällstation
accommodationStrategy.description: The big mountain station at the foot of the massif: rooms and dormitories, a restaurant serving proper Lapland cooking, a shop, and the guide office for the western-route summit. Two nights here is the correct shape for Days 5–6.

accommodationStrategy.name: Abisko Turiststation
accommodationStrategy.description: Trailhead base with rooms, dorms, a shop, a restaurant and the Aurora Sky Station chairlift. It sits on the railway, so your travel day ends at the door.

logistics.emergency: 112. Mountain rescue is coordinated by the police and is slow by mountain-range standards — this is a genuinely remote area. Hut wardens have radio contact. Carry a whistle, and consider a satellite messenger for the Kebnekaise day.
logistics.weather: Snow is possible in any month; the Tjäktja pass in a whiteout is serious. Fjällsäkerhetsrådet (the Swedish mountain safety council) publishes conditions and warnings in English.

other.label: Season boundaries matter absolutely
other.text: Outside the staffed season the huts close, the lake boats stop and — critically — some **bridges are removed for the winter**, which changes river crossings from trivial to dangerous. Check the STF season dates before booking any transport. `verify: true`

other.label: Allemansrätten
other.text: Sweden's right of public access allows wild camping for a night or two on unenclosed land, which is what makes the Kungsleden flexible. You may camp beside huts and pay a reduced fee to use the service building and sauna.

other.label: Reindeer herding
other.text: This is Sámi land in active use. Do not disturb reindeer, do not fly drones over herds, keep to the trail near corrals, and treat herding fences and gates as working infrastructure.

other.label: Mosquitoes
other.text: Mid-July in the birch zone is severe. A head net weighs nothing and will change your trip. Late August onward they are gone.

other.label: Gear essentials
other.text: Four-season shell and trousers, insulated jacket, hat and gloves, boots with ankle support, gaiters, sleeping bag rated to at least 0 °C plus a liner, stove and fuel (canisters are sold at huts, not carried on planes), water bottles, headtorch from mid-August when the nights return.

other.label: Payment
other.text: Sweden is effectively cashless and the huts take cards, but connectivity is intermittent — carry two cards and expect offline processing.

proTips: Go in the **first two weeks of September**. Autumn colour on the fells is extraordinary, the mosquitoes are gone, the huts are quiet, and the northern lights return at night while the huts are still staffed.
Use the **lake boats** without guilt. Alesjaure and Ladtjojaure boat services remove about 15 km of flat lakeside walking and let you spend the saved day on Kebnekaise instead.
Book **two nights at Kebnekaise Fjällstation** so the summit day has a weather reserve. A single-night plan means summiting in whatever conditions arrive.
Take the **night train** rather than flying. It arrives at the trailhead itself, saves a hotel night, and the run along the Torneträsk lake at dawn is the trip's overture.
Every hut has a **sauna**, usually with a lake or river beside it and a booking sheet on the door. Sign up on arrival; the evening slots go first.
Send a resupply parcel? No — but do plan on hut shops for the middle three days and carry only two days' emergency food. It is the single biggest pack-weight saving available.

trips.subRegion: Julian Alps & Triglav National Park — Vrata, Kredarica, Triglavska jezera, Bohinj

bestPeriod.window: Mid-July–mid-September, with the huts fully staffed roughly 20 June–30 September
bestPeriod.avoid: October–June — the Mali Triglav ridge holds verglas and old snow, Kredarica's reservation system is closed and Hribarice is a snow slope
bestPeriod.raw: Mid-July–mid-September, with the huts fully staffed roughly 20 June–30 September

accommodation.note: Hut beds €22–€38 with PZS discount, €40–€60 without; Bohinj hotel €90–€130

food.note: Hut dinners €12–€18, breakfast €8–€10, a litre of hut water €3–€4

transport.note: Airport transfer, Mojstrana shuttle, Bohinj bus, Vogel cable car €25–€30 return

activities.note: Ferrata set hire €12–€18/day, PZS membership €40–€65, Savica waterfall €4–€6

profile.difficultyNote: 5/5 — a 1,500 m ascent day followed by an exposed cabled ridge at 2,864 m, then four more walking days above 1,500 m

trips.gatewayAirport: LJU Ljubljana Jože Pučnik, 55 min to Mojstrana; KLU Klagenfurt 1 h 40 min; TRS Trieste 2 h
trips.summary: Triglav is a national obsession compressed into one mountain, and this week climbs it the honest way — up the Vrata valley from 1,015 m, over the summit at 2,864 m, then away from the crowds south across the Hribarice plateau into the Valley of the Seven Lakes and down to Bohinj. Day two is the hardest day's walking in Slovenia outside a rope; day three is a cabled ridge with 800 m of air on the left. After that the week softens into high karst, larch, glacial tarns and a lake swim. It suits fit hikers who are comfortable with exposure and clipped into a self-belay kit, not first-time mountain walkers.

itinerary.title: Mojstrana, the Peričnik waterfall and Vrata
itinerary.morning: Transfer to **Mojstrana** and spend an hour in the **Slovenski planinski muzej**, the Slovenian Alpine Museum, which explains why this mountain sits on the flag. Hire the ferrata set here and check the lanyard's date stamp.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive or walk 12 km up the **Vrata valley** to **Aljažev dom, 1,015 m**, stopping at the **Peričnik waterfall** — the path passes behind the 52 m upper fall. In the valley head, the **Triglav north face** rises 1,000 m in one sweep, and the **Aljaž memorial piton** stands opposite the hut.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Aljažev dom: *jota*, *ričet*, sausage and buckwheat *žganci*. Pack tonight, because tomorrow starts at 05:30.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km valley road / Aljažev dom 1,015 m / Peričnik upper fall 52 m / north face 1,000 m of relief / ferrata hire €12–€18 per day

itinerary.title: Tominškova pot: 1,500 metres to Kredarica
itinerary.morning: Leave at 05:30 on the **Tominškova pot**, the steeper and more spectacular of the two Vrata routes, cabled and pegged from roughly 1,300 m across slabs beneath the north face. Helmet on from the first cable — this route has rockfall.
itinerary.afternoon: Above the cables the path joins the **Prag** route at the Kredarica plateau and grinds up scree and old snow to **Triglavski dom na Kredarici, 2,515 m**, the highest building in Slovenia, with the meteorological station beside it and the shrunken Triglav glacier below.
itinerary.evening: Hut dinner at 18:00 sharp, lights out at 22:00, and the best sunset in the country off the terrace. Show your PZS card at check-in or pay the full rate.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km / 1,500 m ascent / 7–8 h realistic (signed 5–6 h) / cables from ~1,300 m / hut 2,515 m / water sold at €3–€4/litre

itinerary.title: Mali Triglav, the summit at 2,864 m, and down to Planika
itinerary.morning: Start at 06:00 to beat the queue. Up the scree to **Mali Triglav, 2,725 m**, then the **cabled summit arête** — narrow, continuously exposed, and where the entire kit earns its hire fee. Sign the book in the **Aljažev stolp**, the 1895 tin tower on the 2,864 m summit.
itinerary.afternoon: Reverse the ridge and descend south past the Kredarica cirque to **Dom Planika pod Triglavom, 2,401 m**, a short but real day. Strong parties continue to Koča na Doliču.
itinerary.evening: Planika is smaller and quieter than Kredarica, with the same rationed water and better soup. Watch the last summit parties come off the ridge at dusk and be glad you are not among them.
itinerary.dayStats: 7 km / 400 m ascent / 500 m descent / summit 2,864 m / 4–5 h realistic including cable queues / ridge drops 500–800 m

itinerary.title: Dolič, Hribarice and the crossing to Prehodavci
itinerary.morning: Traverse west and down to **Tržaška koča na Doliču, 2,151 m** in the saddle between Triglav and Kanjavec, with a possible 1 h 15 min detour up **Kanjavec, 2,568 m** for the view back at the whole massif.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb the stony **Hribarice plateau at 2,358 m**, a lunar karst pavement of sinkholes and snow patches, then descend to **Zasavska koča na Prehodavcih, 2,071 m**, above the two highest of the Triglav lakes.
itinerary.evening: Sunset from the Prehodavci saddle over Jezero v Ledvicah. This is the emptiest hut of the week and the one that most feels like the old Julian Alps.
itinerary.dayStats: 11 km / 550 m ascent / 900 m descent / Hribarice 2,358 m / 5–6 h realistic / snow patches on the plateau into mid-July

itinerary.title: The Valley of the Seven Lakes
itinerary.morning: Descend past **Jezero v Ledvicah** ("kidney lake") and the **Rjavo jezero**, then the long larch-and-limestone staircase through the **Dolina Triglavskih jezer** to **Koča pri Triglavskih jezerih, 1,685 m**, beside the Dvojno jezero.
itinerary.afternoon: A short, deliberately easy day. Walk the extra hour up **Mala Ticarica, 2,071 m** or simply lie on the slabs. Swimming in the lakes is prohibited — this is the strictest rule in the park and it is enforced.
itinerary.evening: The Lakes hut has the best kitchen at altitude in Slovenia: *štruklji*, blueberry *žganje* and trout when it is flown in. Book it — it is the most sought-after hut in TNP after Kredarica.
itinerary.dayStats: 7 km / 150 m ascent / 550 m descent / Dvojno jezero 1,669 m / 3–4 h realistic / swimming banned park-wide

itinerary.title: Komna and the drop to Bohinj
itinerary.morning: Climb gently south-west over the **Komna plateau** — WW1 Isonzo Front mule roads, gun emplacements and the **Dom na Komni, 1,520 m**, where the Slovene partisan hospital operated.
itinerary.afternoon: The knee-punishing 1,000 m descent on the old military switchbacks to **Slap Savica** and **Ukanc** at the west end of **Lake Bohinj** (526 m). Swim; it is the only legal one of the week.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Gostilna Rupa in Srednja vas or Pri Hrvatu in Bohinjska Bistrica — Bohinj cheese, *ričet*, trout — and a Union on a terrace with dry socks.
itinerary.dayStats: 14 km / 300 m ascent / 1,300 m descent / Komna 1,520 m / 6–7 h realistic / Bohinj 526 m / Savica entry €4–€6
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Bohinj or Penzion Gasperin, Bohinjska Bistrica

itinerary.title: Vogel, Ribčev Laz and out
itinerary.morning: Take the **Vogel cable car** from Ukanc to 1,535 m (roughly €25–€30 return) for the classic head-on view of the Triglav massif you have just crossed, and an easy ridge walk toward Šija.
itinerary.afternoon: Bus or bike the lakeshore to **Ribčev Laz** for the stone bridge and the frescoed **church of St John the Baptist**, then the Mostnica gorge at Stara Fužina if legs allow.
itinerary.evening: Return the ferrata set in Mojstrana or Bled on the way out, and finish with dinner in Bled or Ljubljana. Airport is 55–75 minutes.
itinerary.dayStats: Vogel top station 1,535 m / cable car €25–€30 return / lakeshore 12 km / LJU 75 min from Bohinj
itinerary.sleep: Bled or Ljubljana, or the outbound flight

accommodationStrategy.name: Triglavski dom na Kredarici
accommodationStrategy.description: The pivot of the whole week: 300-plus places, the only bed close enough to make a dawn summit realistic, and the only one bookable through a proper online system with an immediate card charge. Show your PZS card at the desk. Expect noise, thin air and rationed water, and accept it as the price of position.

accommodationStrategy.name: Koča pri Triglavskih jezerih
accommodationStrategy.description: The most attractive hut in the park, at the lakes, below the tree line, warm enough to sleep properly and with a genuinely good kitchen. It is also the most contested bed after Kredarica — email or phone the managing *planinsko društvo* as soon as the season's dates are published.

accommodationStrategy.name: Aljažev dom v Vratih
accommodationStrategy.description: Road-accessible, so you can arrive with a full bag, eat a large dinner and leave anything you do not want on the ridge. Directly under the Triglav north face, with the Aljaž piton monument opposite, and cheap. Its 05:00 breakfast arrangement is what makes Day 2 possible.

logistics.connectivity: Slovenia is in the EU roaming zone. Signal is good at Kredarica (the meteorological station sits there), patchy in Vrata, and absent on Hribarice and in the lakes valley. Download the PZS mapping or the 1:25,000 Triglav sheet offline.
logistics.emergency: 112 reaches GRZS mountain rescue. State the hut and path name, not just coordinates. PZS membership includes rescue and repatriation cover in Slovenia and abroad; without it, a helicopter lift is billed to you and EHIC/GHIC will not pay. Nearest hospital: Jesenice, 30 min from Mojstrana.
logistics.weather: Afternoon thunderstorms over the massif are near-daily in July and August and the summit ridge is the worst possible place for one — the cables are a lightning path. Aim to be off the arête by 11:00. The **foehn** can push the freezing level up and destabilise snow patches; autumn *burja* squalls hit the Komna plateau. Check meteo.si and the ARSO mountain forecast.
logistics.bookingWindows: Kredarica's 2026 online system runs 10 June–30 September; book the moment your dates are fixed, since August Saturdays fill first. The Lakes hut and Planika need 4–8 weeks. Ferrata hire 3–5 days in high summer. PZS membership takes a few days to issue a card — do it before you book.
logistics.money: Euro. Huts prefer cash and card terminals fail at altitude; €200–€300 for the week. Tipping is not expected; round up.
logistics.transportRules: A Slovenian e-vinjeta (€16 weekly) is required for the A2 to Jesenice. The Vrata valley road has a seasonal parking charge at Aljažev dom and fills by 08:00. Bohinj runs a summer shuttle to Savica and Ukanc; buses take bikes for a small fee.
logistics.permits: No permit is needed to walk in TNP, and there is no entry fee, but **wild camping and bivouacking are prohibited throughout the park**, as are fires, drones without authorisation, swimming in the Triglav lakes, and picking flowers. Off-path travel on the karst plateaus damages protected habitat.
logistics.health: Hut water is rainwater and is sold, not free; do not assume potability from streams below pastures. Rockfall on Tominškova pot is real — helmet from the first cable. Altitude at 2,515 m causes poor sleep rather than sickness in most people, but allow for it. Ticks and TBE are a genuine risk in the valley forests up to about 1,500 m; Slovenia has one of Europe's highest incidences.

proTips: Take PZS membership **before** booking Kredarica. The discount is applied inside the booking flow by selecting your affiliation — you cannot claim it retrospectively at the desk.
Book Kredarica for a **Sunday to Thursday night**. Slovenes climb Triglav at weekends, and the cable queue on a Saturday morning can add 90 minutes to the ridge.
Reverse the usual plan and sleep at Planika, not Kredarica, on summit night if you want a quieter hut — you lose 100 m of altitude and gain a great deal of sleep.
Carry 2.5 litres from Aljažev dom. Water at Kredarica is sold by the litre and the Day 2 ascent is the thirstiest of the week.
Check the hire lanyard's inspection date and that it is an energy-absorbing set, not an old rope-and-carabiner rig. Shops near Bled still rent obsolete kit.
Ask at Kredarica whether the **zimska soba** is open before you plan a late arrival. It is the difference between shelter and a very long night if the hut is full.
Do the Kanjavec detour from Dolič on Day 4. It is 75 minutes for the only view that shows both the north face and the lakes valley at once.
Save the Vogel cable car for Day 7 rather than Day 1. Looking at the ridge you climbed is worth far more than looking at the ridge you are about to.

raw.Hut-to-hut booking path: Aljažev dom v Vratih (1,015 m, PD Dovje-Mojstrana) → **Triglavski dom na Kredarici** (2,515 m, PD Ljubljana-Matica) → Dom Planika pod Triglavom (2,401 m, PD Ljubljana-Matica) → Zasavska koča na Prehodavcih (2,071 m, PD Zasavje) → Koča pri Triglavskih jezerih (1,685 m, PD Ljubljana-Matica) → Dom na Komni (1,520 m, PD Ljubljana-Matica). Almost every hut here belongs to a **planinsko društvo** affiliated to the **Planinska zveza Slovenije (PZS)**. **Kredarica books exclusively online at triglavskidom.si**, with the **2026 reservation window running 10 June to 30 September** and the full amount charged to a Visa or Mastercard at the moment of booking; the exact staffed opening date is announced a few days beforehand. Free cancellation is allowed **up to two days before arrival** via the link in the confirmation email, with automatic refund; after that there is no refund, but the reservation may be **modified up to three times** subject to space. Other huts take email or phone bookings and several use the PZS-wide reservation pages on pzs.si. **A sleeping-bag liner or personal clean sheet is compulsory and full sleeping bags are prohibited** at Kredarica; single-use linen can be rented for a few euros. Huts prefer cash — carry €200–€300, since the card link at 2,515 m is not dependable. **If a hut is full**, Slovenian mountain custom and PZS house rules require the warden to shelter you rather than turn you out, but that means a mattress in the *zimska soba* or the dining room; the practical fallbacks are Dom Planika and Koča na Doliču for Kredarica, and Koča na Prehodavcih or Koča pri Triglavskih jezerih for each other.
raw.PZS membership and reciprocity: An annual PZS membership (roughly €40–€65 depending on category) is selected during the Kredarica booking flow and **must be proved with a valid physical or digital card on arrival, or you pay the full rate**. Members under 17 get a further reduction. Membership typically halves the overnight fee, so over five hut nights it pays for itself, and it carries **reciprocal rights in CAI, ÖAV, DAV and other UIAA-affiliated huts** across the Alps. It also bundles mountain-rescue and repatriation insurance valid in Slovenia and abroad.
raw.Safety markers and waymarking: Slovenia uses the **Knafelc blaze** — a red circle with a white centre, painted on rock and tree — plus wooden signposts with the destination and hours. Route numbers appear on the signposts rather than the blazes. TNP paths are graded on signposts as **lahka pot** (easy), **zahtevna pot** (demanding, some cable) and **zelo zahtevna pot** (very demanding, sustained cable and exposure). The Vrata approaches and the summit ridge are *zelo zahtevna*.
raw.Via ferrata reality on Triglav: The **Tominškova pot** from Vrata and the **Prag** route both carry fixed cables and pegs from around 1,300 m. The **Kredarica → Mali Triglav → Triglav** ridge is a sustained, narrow, cabled arête with 500–800 m drops on both sides — a **helmet, harness and full via ferrata lanyard set are the standard of care**, and TNP, PZS and every local guide treat them as required equipment rather than a suggestion. Slovenian mountain rescue statistics are dominated by unprotected falls on exactly this ridge. Hire in Mojstrana at Slovenski planinski muzej's shop or in Bled and Bohinj, €12–€18 a day; expect a €100–€200 deposit.
raw.Elevation and gear essentials: Cumulative ascent is roughly **3,000 m and 3,500 m of descent** over six walking days. High points: **Triglav 2,864 m**, Mali Triglav 2,725 m, Kredarica 2,515 m, Hribarice 2,358 m, Prehodavci 2,071 m. **Snow lingers in the Triglav north-face couloirs, on the Hribarice plateau and in the Kredarica cirque well into July** — before roughly 15 July carry microspikes, and an ice axe with the skill to use it if you go in June. Full-shank B/C boots, gloves for the cables, and a helmet that fits over a hat.
raw.Water, food resupply and rubbish: The Julian Alps are limestone and the high route is effectively **waterless between huts**. Kredarica and Planika collect rainwater and melt: drinking water is sold, often **€3–€4 per litre**, showers may be unavailable, and washing water is rationed. Fill 2 litres at Aljažev dom and carry 2.5–3 on the ascent day. Resupply in Mojstrana, and again only in Ukanc/Bohinj on Day 6. **Everything is flown or cable-hauled up, so all rubbish comes back down with you** — huts will not take your packaging.
raw.Bail-out options, rescue and insurance: From Kredarica the fastest escape is south to Dom Planika and down to **Vodnikov dom na Velem polju (1,817 m)** and the Pokljuka road. From Prehodavci you can drop east to Trenta in 3–4 h. **112 reaches GRZS (Gorska reševalna zveza Slovenije)**; helicopter rescue for a Slovenian resident or PZS member is covered through the membership package, but a foreign walker without cover is billed. EHIC/GHIC does not pay for helicopter evacuation. Nearest hospital: Jesenice.
raw.Realistic walking times: Slovenian signpost hours are calculated for a fit, unladen local and are among the tightest in Europe. Add **30–40%**. Vrata to Kredarica is signed 5–6 h; plan 7–8 h with a pack. Kredarica to the summit and back is signed 3 h; plan 4–5 h if the ridge is busy, because on an August morning you queue at the cables.

trips.title: Chains and Chata Beds: A High Tatras Hut-to-Hut Week from Starý Smokovec

bestPeriod.window: the first three weeks of September — high routes still open, huts quieter, stable anticyclonic weather
bestPeriod.avoid: before 16 June (TANAP high-route closure), and July–August weekends when Téryho and Zbojnícka are full months ahead

accommodation.note: €230–€380 (€30–€55/night in huts, half-board extra)

food.note: €210–€300 (€30–€43/day — hut meals are expensive because every crate is carried up)

transport.note: €60–€110 (TEŽ trains, Hrebienok funicular, Lomnica cable car)

activities.note: €0–€250 (TANAP entry is free; a licensed guide day is the variable)

profile.difficultyNote: Hard

trips.gatewayAirport: Poprad-Tatry (TAT) airport, 15 min to Poprad station; Košice (KSC) 1 h 40. Then the **TEŽ** electric railway to Starý Smokovec (35 min).
trips.summary: The High Tatras are the smallest true alpine range in Europe and they do not care. Six days of granite, chained slabs and glacial tarns, sleeping at 2,015 m where the beer arrived on a man's back, crossing a saddle…
trips.hook: The High Tatras are the smallest true alpine range in Europe and they do not care. Six days of granite, chained slabs and glacial tarns, sleeping at 2,015 m where the beer arrived on a man's back, crossing a saddle you are legally allowed to climb in only one direction, and finishing on Rysy at 2,503 m with Poland spread out below. For hikers with a head for exposure and no need for a shower.

snapshot.Start / End: Starý Smokovec → Štrbské Pleso (point-to-point, ~60 km, ~5,600 m ascent)
snapshot.Getting there: Poprad-Tatry (TAT) airport, 15 min to Poprad station; Košice (KSC) 1 h 40. Then the **TEŽ** electric railway to Starý Smokovec (35 min).

itinerary.title: Up to the treeline
itinerary.morning: Fly to Poprad, TEŽ to Starý Smokovec, and buy a multi-day Tatra transport ticket at the station [VERIFY: current TEŽ multi-day fare]. Leave anything you do not need at your hotel — you carry everything else for six days.
itinerary.afternoon: Take the Hrebienok funicular (or walk the green trail up, 1 h 15), then the yellow trail past the Studenovodské vodopády waterfalls to **Zamkovského chata** at 1,475 m, about an hour.
itinerary.evening: Eat *bryndzové halušky* and *kapustnica* on the terrace, get an early night, and check the hut's weather board — the 06:00 forecast is the one that matters.

itinerary.title: Into Malá Studená dolina
itinerary.morning: The green trail climbs the Malá Studená dolina on boulder and slab, past the Obrovský vodopád. Steady rather than steep for the first hour, then a chained ramp.
itinerary.afternoon: **Téryho chata** at 2,015 m, built in 1899, sits among the five **Spišské plesá** in a granite bowl. Drop the pack and wander the tarns; the water is drinkable and shockingly cold.
itinerary.evening: Cash only up here, and the price of a beer reflects that a *nosič* carried it. Watch the light on Široká veža, then a bunk-room night with twenty strangers.

itinerary.title: Priečne sedlo, upward only
itinerary.morning: The crux of the week. **Priečne sedlo (2,352 m)** is a **one-way trail: ascent only** from the Téryho side, marked and enforced — chains, staples and a chimney with real exposure. Start by 07:30, before anyone above kicks stones down.
itinerary.afternoon: Over the notch and down chained slabs into the Veľká Studená dolina to **Zbojnícka chata (1,960 m)**, four to five hours end to end. If it is wet, do not attempt it — reverse to Hrebienok and take the valley trail instead.
itinerary.evening: Zbojnícka is the friendliest hut on the route: soup, goulash, a wood stove, no signal, no card machine [VERIFY: current bed and half-board rates].

itinerary.title: Prielom, then a repositioning day
itinerary.morning: A morning out-and-back to **Prielom (2,288 m)** on chains above the Zbojnícke plesá — two hours up for the Bielovodská panorama — then back to the hut for the pack.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend the Veľká Studená dolina to Hrebienok, TEŽ line 184 to Tatranská Lomnica, and the cable car to Skalnaté pleso [VERIFY: current Lomnica cable-car fare].
itinerary.evening: The red-marked traverse over **Veľká Svišťovka (2,037 m)** — chains, then a long zigzag descent to **Chata pri Zelenom plese (Brnčalova chata, 1,551 m)** under the Kežmarský štít wall. Three hours; do not start it after 16:00.

itinerary.title: Down, across, and back up to Sliezsky dom
itinerary.morning: The blue trail down the Dolina Zeleného plesa and Biela voda to Tatranské Matliare — long, forested, easy on the legs after two chained days.
itinerary.afternoon: TEŽ to Tatranská Polianka, then the magistrála-linked blue trail up Velická dolina, 1 h 45, to **Sliezsky dom (1,670 m)** — a full hotel with hot showers, laundry and a card machine.
itinerary.evening: Walk fifteen minutes to Velické pleso and the Kvetnica hanging meadow for the sunset on Gerlachovský štít, at 2,655 m the highest peak in the whole Carpathian chain [VERIFY: current Sliezsky dom rates].

itinerary.title: To the highest hut in Slovakia
itinerary.morning: Down to Vyšné Hágy, TEŽ to Štrbské Pleso, then the red magistrála around the lake and up to **Popradské pleso (1,494 m)** — about 1 h 15 — past the Symbolický cintorín, the cemetery of empty plaques for those the mountains kept.
itinerary.afternoon: The red trail up the Mengusovská dolina, then chained ground to **Chata pod Rysmi at 2,250 m**, three to four hours. Everything in this building — gas, flour, beer, your dinner — came up on a *nosič*'s frame.
itinerary.evening: Bunks are tight, water is rationed and it is cash only. Set an alarm for 04:45.

itinerary.title: Rysy at 2,503 m, then down
itinerary.morning: Forty-five minutes of chained slab to the summit of **Rysy** — 2,503 m on the Slovak side, the Polish summit 2,499 m, the border running over the top. Morskie Oko sits directly below to the north.
itinerary.afternoon: Reverse to Popradské pleso for lunch at the Horský hotel, then the easy path out to **Štrbské Pleso**.
itinerary.evening: TEŽ back to Poprad. Eat *pirohy* and drink Tatratea somewhere with chairs that are not benches.

accommodationStrategy.name: Téryho chata
accommodationStrategy.description: the only bed on the Priečne sedlo side, so it turns the crux into a fresh-legs morning rather than the end of a long day. Bunk rooms, blankets, cold water.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct with the hut by email or phone, 3–6 months ahead for July–August weekends.

accommodationStrategy.name: Chata pod Rysmi
accommodationStrategy.description: puts you 45 minutes below Rysy for a summit before the day-hikers arrive from Štrbské Pleso. Season is short and weather-dependent.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct, as early as the season opens; carry cash.

accommodationStrategy.name: Sliezsky dom
accommodationStrategy.description: the mid-week reset — showers, laundry, real beds, a card machine and drying space, all at altitude so you do not lose acclimatisation.
accommodationStrategy.booking: online, 4–6 weeks ahead.

logistics.connectivity: Orange/Telekom cover the resort strip and most ridges; Téryho, Zbojnícka and Chata pod Rysmi have patchy-to-none. Huts post the morning forecast on a board — treat it as the authority.
logistics.emergency: **HZS 18 300**, or 112. Give your position by hut name and trail colour. Rescue is chargeable — carry proof of a mountain-rescue policy.
logistics.weather: Tatra storms build fast from 13:00 in summer. On chains, wet granite doubles your time; a lightning cell over Priečne or Rysy is a genuine emergency. Turn around early and without argument.
logistics.bookingWindows: High huts 3–6 months for peak weekends, 3–6 weeks midweek in September. Book the whole chain before you book flights — the beds, not the flights, are the constraint.
logistics.money: Slovakia uses the euro. **Téryho, Zbojnícka and Chata pod Rysmi are cash-only**; carry €250–€350 in notes for the week. Sliezsky dom and Zamkovského take cards.
logistics.transportRules: TEŽ narrow-gauge lines link Poprad, Starý Smokovec, Tatranská Lomnica and Štrbské Pleso every 30–60 minutes; validate before boarding. The Hrebienok funicular and the Lomnica cable car are separate tickets.
logistics.permits: No permit or entry fee for TANAP, but the rules bind: marked trails only, **high routes closed 1 November–15 June**, **Priečne sedlo is one-way upward**, no wild camping anywhere in the park, no drones, dogs banned above the treeline.

proTips: Book Téryho and Zbojnícka **first, by email, in one message**, and ask for consecutive nights. Huts hold a small manual allocation and a clear two-night request gets priority over two separate ones.
Go in the first three weeks of September. The high trails are open until 31 October, the queues on Priečne are gone, and hut beds appear at three weeks' notice instead of three months.
Carry €300 in €10 and €20 notes. There is no ATM above the resort line, and a hut that cannot change a €50 will simply say no.
Learn *"Máte voľné miesto?"* (do you have a free bed?) and *"Koľko hodín?"* (how many hours?). Junction times in Slovak huts are quoted in hours and everyone will answer that second question.
Start every chained section by 08:00. The stone-fall risk on Priečne and Rysy is other hikers, and the crowd arrives mid-morning.
Buy the mountain-rescue policy at the airport or online before you land. It is a few euros a day, and HZS bills for the helicopter.
If weather kills the Priečne day, drop to Hrebienok and use the TEŽ to jump forward to Zelené pleso. Losing one saddle is better than losing the week.

raw.Hut chain and booking channel: Slovak Tatra huts are booked **directly with each hut** — email, phone or the hut's own web form — not through any central system. There is no PTTK-style network here. July and August weekend beds go **months ahead**; a September midweek bed usually takes 3–6 weeks. Chain: **Zamkovského chata** (1,475 m, own web form) → **Téryho chata** (2,015 m, direct, email/phone only) → **Zbojnícka chata** (1,960 m, direct, email/phone only) → **Chata pri Zelenom plese / Brnčalova chata** (1,551 m, direct) → **Sliezsky dom** (1,670 m, hotel-grade, online) → **Chata pod Rysmi** (2,250 m, Slovakia's highest hut, direct; short season) [VERIFY: current bed rates at each hut] [VERIFY: Chata pod Rysmi 2026 opening and closing dates].
raw.Waymarks: The **KST** (Klub slovenských turistov) system: a horizontal three-band blaze, white–colour–white, on rock and trees. **Red** is the main long line — the *Tatranská magistrála* traverse; **blue**, **green** and **yellow** are connectors and valley approaches. Junction posts (*rázcestník*) give times in hours, not kilometres, and those times are for an unladen, fit walker.
raw.Daily ascent/descent: Day 1 +180 m. Day 2 +540/−0 m. Day 3 +390/−445 m over Priečne sedlo. Day 4 +330/−1,100 m plus mechanical assist, then +490/−410 m on the Svišťovka traverse. Day 5 −700/+520 m. Day 6 −520/+760 m to Chata pod Rysmi. Day 7 +253/−1,150 m over Rysy. Total roughly 5,600 m up.
raw.Seasonal closure: TANAP closes the high trails **1 November to 15 June** every year, without exception and regardless of snow conditions. Valley trails and the magistrála's lower sections stay open. Do not plan this itinerary in early June.
raw.Guide rule: Marked trails are free to walk. Anything **off the marked trail, or on climbing terrain**, legally requires a licensed Slovak mountain guide (*horský vodca*) — this covers Prostredný hrot, Slavkovský štít's ridge variants, and every summit not served by a blaze. Guides run €200–€300 a day for a party of two [VERIFY: current guiding day rate].
raw.Rescue and insurance: **Horská záchranná služba (HZS)**, emergency **18 300** or 112. Critically: **mountain rescue in Slovakia is chargeable to the rescued person** — helicopter and ground callouts both. Standard EHIC does not cover it. Buy a Slovak mountain-rescue policy (Union, Generali or the HZS-partnered products) or an alpine club card with rescue cover; it costs a few euros a day against a five-figure bill.
raw.Gear tied to altitude: Above 2,000 m expect near-freezing dawns in September and lightning risk from 13:00 in July. Non-negotiable: B-rated stiff-soled boots, hardshell, warm layer, headtorch, 2 L water capacity, gloves for the chains (the steel is cold and greasy), and a **sleeping bag liner** — most huts supply blankets, not bedding.

typeSpecific.hutBooking: Slovak Tatra huts are booked **directly with each hut** — email, phone or the hut's own web form — not through any central system. There is no PTTK-style network here. July and August weekend beds go **months ahead**; a September midweek bed usually takes 3–6 weeks. Chain: **Zamkovského chata** (1,475 m, own web form) → **Téryho chata** (2,015 m, direct, email/phone only) → **Zbojnícka chata** (1,960 m, direct, email/phone only) → **Chata pri Zelenom plese / Brnčalova chata** (1,551 m, direct) → **Sliezsky dom** (1,670 m, hotel-grade, online) → **Chata pod Rysmi** (2,250 m, Slovakia's highest hut, direct; short season) [VERIFY: current bed rates at each hut] [VERIFY: Chata pod Rysmi 2026 opening and closing dates].
